_readme: Known symbols for DBSIM.EXE: confirmed address -> meaning mappings, applied to the Ghidra project by ES2ApplySymbolNames.java.
Schema, confidence rules and run order: tools/ghidra_scripts/README.md, 'Known symbols'.
Entries are in address order. tools/scripts/es2_naming.py insert and edit keep it, and check that it holds.

entries.name: Cam_IsAttachedTo
entries.description: True when the camera is in mode 2 (attached) on the given object.

entries.name: Cam_AttachOrbit
entries.description: Unless locked (+0x4a): orbit centre to +0x38, object to +0x32, zeroes distance +0x22, the orbit pitch, roll and heading +0x26/+0x28/+0x2a, all three rates +0x2c/+0x2e/+0x30 and the zoom rate +0x24, and sets mode 1.

entries.name: Cam_AttachEye
entries.description: Unless locked (+0x4a): eye offset to +0x3e, object to +0x32, mode 2.

entries.name: Cam_SetMode
entries.description: Stores 0-3 into CAM+0x36 unless the camera is locked (+0x4a).

entries.name: Cam_Update
entries.description: CAM's once-a-frame placement, called from the main loop (Sim_Run) with ViewObjectPtr between Sim_MainTick and the render. First records LocalPlayerMech's +0x26 position, +0x0c euler triple and Math_IntegrateRateOverTick(0x400) into the 50-entry chase ring at 004a7c80/004a7ed8/004a8004 (cursor 004a80cc), then places by CAM+0x36: 0 free camera, 1 orbit, 2 attached to the object's +0x24 node, 3 chase (8000 back along the ring).

entries.name: Cam_ApproachRate
entries.description: Math_RateLimitedMoveToward(rate, Q8(0x800, axis), 0xc0): Cam_Steer's heading and pitch rates.

entries.name: Cam_ApproachZoom
entries.description: Math_RateLimitedMoveToward(rate, Q8(0x400, axis), 0x50): Cam_Steer's zoom rate and free-camera speed.

entries.name: Cam_Steer
entries.description: Cam_Steer(cam, steer, throttle, trigger): nothing while the lock CAM+0x4a is set, and nothing outside modes 0 and 1 (CAM+0x36). Through Cam_ApproachRate and Cam_ApproachZoom, the heading rate +0x30 moves toward Q8(0x800, steer) in mode 1 and Q8(0x800, -steer) in mode 0 at step 0xc0; with the trigger set, +0x24 (zoom in mode 1, speed in mode 0) moves toward Q8(0x400, throttle) (-throttle in mode 0) at 0x50 and the pitch rate +0x2c toward 0 at 0xc0, and without it +0x24 moves toward 0 and the pitch rate toward Q8(0x800, throttle). Callers found by es2_xref: Sim_PollPlayerInput, ViewChain_PlayerDeathCamera and PreferencesPanel_OrbitViewHook, the last with (-0x40, 0, 0).

entries.name: Cam_StaticInit
entries.description: Static initialiser of the camera module (Borland _INIT_ entry 004a7a5c, priority 0x20): Rtl_VectorNew on ChaseTrail_Positions (50 x 12 bytes, maybe_Point3I_Ctor) and ChaseTrail_Rotations (50 x 6 bytes, maybe_Point3S_Ctor).

entries.name: RegisterSubsystemLoader
entries.description: Appends (funcPtr, id) to a global registration table (DAT_004a80d0, 6-byte entries: 4-byte function pointer + 2-byte id) at the slot indexed by a global counter (DAT_00497074) that it then increments. Confirms whatever registers itself here -- e.g. Mech_LoadResources via the 00420654 thunk -- is walked and invoked by DBSIM's generic subsystem-init driver rather than being dead code.

entries.name: Subsystem_RunPhase
entries.description: Walks the registration table RegisterSubsystemLoader fills (DAT_004a80d0, 6-byte entries, count at DAT_00497074) and calls every entry whose 2-byte id equals the argument. Seven call sites: phases 0, 1, 3, 4 and 6 from the session setup/teardown at 0045f144, phase 2 from Sim_InitMissionSession, and PHASE 5 FROM THE TOP OF Sim_RenderFrame -- so phase 5 runs once per frame. NOTE FOR SEARCHES: a function reached only through this table has no E8/E9 caller and no static data reference, because the table is populated at runtime; neither a call scan nor a raw dword scan of the image can find it.

entries.name: Vcr_Checkpoint
entries.description: (ptr, size, label): recording appends size bytes of ptr to the buffer 004a8580 (cursor 00497078, total 0049707c); playback freads size bytes from the -d .dmp (004d2562), memcmps against ptr and sets 00497080 on a mismatch. Module vcr.cpp. No caller found by es2_xref.

entries.name: Vcr_FlushCheckpoints
entries.description: Phase-6 subsystem, run every frame: while recording with the -d handle set, appends the checkpoint buffer's total bytes to <stem>.dmp (mode ab, Assert vcr.cpp:47) and resets cursor and total. Registered by Vcr_StaticInit.

entries.name: Vcr_StaticInit
entries.description: Static initialiser (Borland init table 004a7a64): RegisterSubsystemLoader(6, Vcr_FlushCheckpoints).

entries.name: TinyObj_GetPosition
entries.description: TINY_OBJ vtable +0x04 (00497321, also TS_TINY_OBJ's): copies this+0xc and this+0x10 into the static triple at 00497098 and returns it; the third dword (004970a0) is zeroed once, on the first call, under the latch at 004970a4. A tiny object stores only two position components, and every caller shares the one static buffer.

entries.name: TinyObj_InstallModelTransform
entries.description: TINY_OBJ vtable +0x00 (00497321): takes the position from its own vtable +0x04, builds a Q14 rotation from the Euler triple (0, 0, this+0x14) with BuildEulerRotationMatrixQ14 and installs it with Raster_SetModelTransform -- a heading-only transform. TSTinyObj_Draw runs it before drawing.

entries.name: Raster_SetModelTransformFromPose
entries.description: (obj): builds a transform from the Euler angles at obj+0x1c (BuildEulerRotationMatrixQ14) with the translation obj+0x10/+0x14/+0x18 and installs it with Raster_SetModelTransform. REG_OBJ's vtable +0x00 (004972d5); TSRegObj_Draw runs it before drawing.

entries.name: SimObject_InstallModelTransform
entries.description: Builds the object's Q14 euler rotation matrix at obj+0x12 when the dirty flag at obj+0x32 is clear, then installs it as the current model transform. Called twice by Shape_DrawAtDetailLevel, around the LOD pick.

entries.name: TSTinyObj_Ctor
entries.description: (this, shape): constructor of TS_TINY_OBJ (vtable 00497301, RTTI 'TS_TINY_OBJ', 0x1a bytes). Installs DRAWABLE (004a14bc), then TINY_OBJ (00497321) with +0xc, +0x10 and the short at +0x14 zeroed, then TS_TINY_OBJ, and stores a new 0xc-byte TSShapeInstance for shape (TSShapeInstance_Ctor) at +0x16.
entries.source: DBSIM decompile at 0040201c; RTTI at 00497301 and 00497321

entries.name: TSRegObj_Ctor
entries.description: (this, shape): constructor of TS_REG_OBJ (vtable 004972a9, RTTI 'TS_REG_OBJ', 0x26 bytes). Installs DRAWABLE (004a14bc); constructs a second base at +0xc with View_CtorBase(this+0xc, zero triple, zero triple); installs REG_OBJ (004972d5, secondary table 004972f1 at +0xc), then TS_REG_OBJ (secondary 004972c5); and stores a new 0xc-byte TSShapeInstance for shape at +0x22.
entries.source: DBSIM decompile at 004020b8; RTTI at 004972a9 and 004972d5

entries.name: SimObjectBase_Constructor
entries.description: Constructor of TS_OBJ (TSObjVtable, 004a0b98, RTTI 'TS_OBJ', 0x41 bytes), (this, shape). Installs DRAWABLE (004a14bc), then MAT_OBJ (00497289) with +0xc, the short at +0x10, +0x26..+0x31 and the short at +0x32 zeroed, then TSObjVtable; stores a new 0xc-byte TSShapeInstance (TSShapeInstance_Ctor) for a non-null shape at +0x34, and zeroes +0x38..+0x3f. A derived class's constructor runs it first and installs its own table after. SimObjectBase_ConstructShaped is the variant that allocates a 0x42-byte animated shape instance instead.

entries.name: SimObjectBase_ConstructShaped
entries.description: (this, shape): installs the DRAWABLE vtable (004a14bc, RTTI 'DRAWABLE'), then MAT_OBJ's (00497289), then TSObjVtable (004a0b98, RTTI 'TS_OBJ'); zeroes +0xc, +0x10 and +0x26..+0x33; when shape is given allocates a 0x42-byte shape instance (ShapeInst_Construct) for +0x34; zeroes +0x38..+0x3f and sets +0x39, the byte SimObject_ApplyRootMotionIfEnabled tests. SimObjectBase_ConstructAnimated and SimObjectBase_ConstructWithDetailTable run it.

entries.name: ShapeInst_AddThread
entries.description: Builds one animation thread on an object's shape instance (obj+0x34): allocates 0x52 bytes, binds it to the shape's animation list, cuts it to the given sequence at frame 0 (AnimThread_SetSequence), sets its playback rate to zero and registers it on the instance (ShapeInst_RegisterThread). A caller that wants the thread running sets the rate itself. Called by Mech_Constructor for a HERC's three threads and by Base_Construct for a structure's two.

entries.name: AnimObj_Dtor
entries.description: ANIM_OBJ vtable +0x08 (004973ac): the deleting destructor, (this, flags). Reinstalls ANIM_OBJ's table; when the owns-animated-instance byte +0x39 is set, takes every thread off the shape instance at +0x34 (ShapeInst_RemoveThread on its first slot, +0x1a, until empty), Mem_Deletes each, deletes the instance through its own vtable +0x18 with flags 3 and clears +0x34. Then installs TSObjVtable, deletes +0x34 if still set, and Mem_Deletes this on flags bit 0. Every ACTOR-derived destructor (SimObject_Dtor, Mech_Dtor, Flyer_Dtor, the five structure destructors) and DetAnimObj_Dtor call it with flags 0 after their own levels.

entries.name: SimObject_ApplyRootMotion
entries.description: Seeds the shape root node to identity, advances the animation by dt, reads node 0 world transform back, and applies it: pos = objRotation * delta.translation + pos, euler += eulerOf(delta.rotation). Then resets the root. The only source of Herc translation and turn-in-place rotation.

entries.name: SimObject_ApplyRootMotionIfEnabled
entries.description: Forwards to SimObject_ApplyRootMotion(obj, obj+0x34, arg) when obj+0x39 is set, and does nothing otherwise. Mech_ConfigureLoadout calls it as (mech, 0) ahead of its per-hardpoint loop. It has nothing to do with hardpoint visibility: the placeholder parts are replaced at draw time by Mech_SpliceHardpointShapes.

entries.name: SimObject_PushTransform
entries.description: Saves the object transform, position and the whole animated node hierarchy into globals at 004a8d54. Paired with SimObject_PopTransform.

entries.name: SimObject_PopTransform
entries.description: Restores what SimObject_PushTransform saved. Used by Mech_MovementTick to undo a blocked move.

entries.name: SimObject_ConformToTerrain
entries.description: Sits an object on sloped ground. Samples Terrain_HeightQuery at +/-r forward and +/-r right (r from vtable +0x10, the shape's own radius), takes pitch from Math_Atan2Bam(2r, front - back) and roll from the left/right pair -- Math_Atan2Bam's argument order is (x, y), so the span is the x -- and writes Z as the mean of the four samples (sum >> 2). Clears the rotation-valid flag so the matrix rebuilds. Two callers: GroundVehicle_ThinkTick, which makes it the only thing in the simulation that writes a structure's pitch and roll, and FlatObj_Draw, which conforms every ground shape it draws.

entries.name: SimObject_StaticInit
entries.description: Static initialiser of the sim-object module (Borland _INIT_ entry 004a7a68, priority 0x20): vector-constructs the three save buffers SimObject_PushTransform fills and SimObject_PopTransform restores -- SimObjectSave_AnimThreads (10 x 0x52, AnimThread_ElementCtor), SimObjectSave_NodeLocals (30 x 12, maybe_Point3SPair_Ctor) and SimObjectSave_NodeTransforms (30 x 0x20, Transform_Ctor).

entries.name: AnimThread_ElementCtor
entries.description: (thread): returns its argument -- the per-element constructor Rtl_VectorNew runs over an array of 0x52-byte ANThread records (class record at 00402c41, size 0x52); the LEA of +0x2e is an inlined empty member constructor. SimObject_StaticInit builds SimObjectSave_AnimThreads with it.

entries.name: MatObj_GetPosition
entries.description: MAT_OBJ vtable +0x04 (00497289): returns this+0x26. MAT_OBJ's own copy of what SimObject_GetPosition (0046b801) does for TS_OBJ and every class below it.

entries.name: TSRegObj_Draw
entries.description: TS_REG_OBJ vtable +0x00 (004972a9): Raster_SetModelTransformFromPose(this), then draws the shape instance at +0x22 through its own vtable +0x1c.

entries.name: RegObj_GetPosition
entries.description: REG_OBJ vtable +0x04 (004972d5, also TS_REG_OBJ's): returns this+0x10, the translation Raster_SetModelTransformFromPose reads.

entries.name: TSRegObj_Dtor
entries.description: TS_REG_OBJ vtable +0x08 (004972a9): the deleting destructor, (this, flags). Reinstalls TS_REG_OBJ's two tables, deletes the shape instance at +0x22 through its own vtable +0x18 with flags 3, runs TSContext_Dtor(this+0xc, 0) on the second base, and Mem_Deletes this on flags bit 0.

entries.name: TS_REG_OBJ_DtorThunk
entries.description: The this-adjusting thunk at primary vtable +0x1c of TS_REG_OBJ's vtable block, in the table for its TSContext subobject at +0xc: subtracts 0xc from this and jumps to TSRegObj_Dtor.

entries.name: RegObj_Dtor
entries.description: REG_OBJ vtable +0x08 (004972d5): the deleting destructor, (this, flags). TSContext_Dtor(this+0xc, 0) on the second base, then Mem_Delete(this) on flags bit 0.

entries.name: REG_OBJ_DtorThunk
entries.description: The this-adjusting thunk at primary vtable +0x1c of REG_OBJ's vtable block, in the table for its TSContext subobject at +0xc: subtracts 0xc from this and jumps to RegObj_Dtor.

entries.name: TSTinyObj_Draw
entries.description: TS_TINY_OBJ vtable +0x00 (00497301): TinyObj_InstallModelTransform(this), then draws the shape instance at +0x16 through its own vtable +0x1c.

entries.name: TSTinyObj_Dtor
entries.description: TS_TINY_OBJ vtable +0x08 (00497301): the deleting destructor, (this, flags). Reinstalls TS_TINY_OBJ's table, deletes the shape instance at +0x16 through its own vtable +0x18 with flags 3, and Mem_Deletes this on flags bit 0.

entries.name: TinyObj_Dtor
entries.description: TINY_OBJ vtable +0x08 (00497321): the deleting destructor, (this, flags). Two RTL destructor-count decrements (TINY_OBJ, DRAWABLE), then Mem_Delete(this) on flags bit 0.

entries.name: ShapeInstance_CtorCellFrames
entries.description: Two-field shape-instance holder: stores the shape at +0, then allocates +4 as a PRIVATE copy of the shape's per-sequence cell-frame array (shape+0x1c, shape+0x24 entries), or null when the shape carries no sequence. Element 0 of that copy is the cell a TSCellAnimPart draws, which is what lets two mounts carrying the same weapon flash independently.

entries.name: HeapBlockOwner_Dtor
entries.description: (owner, flags): Mem_Delete of the block whose pointer is at owner+4, then of owner itself when flags bit 0 is set. Several TSBase-derived destructors (00411969, 004119c3, 00420730) run it on the member at their +0x10 with flags 0.

entries.name: MechType_BindHardpointSlots
entries.description: Builds one root's hardpoint slot list: for each hardpoint bone id, resolves the shape's vtable +0x24 to the ADDRESS of the part slot holding the part whose TSBasePart id number (+6) is that id, storing null for the -1 the invisible mounting emits. Writes a {void **slots; short count} pair, which MechType_InitOne keeps per LOD root at typeRec+0xe6 with the count at +0xea.
entries.signature: void __cdecl MechType_BindHardpointSlots(void *slotList, void *shapeRoot, short hardpointCount, short *boneIds)

entries.name: Mech_SpliceHardpointShapes
entries.description: Walks a root's hardpoint slot list against the machine's mount array and overwrites each slot: the mount's weapon shape when one is fitted, else the next 0x18-byte blank from typeRec+0xec. The replacement inherits the placeholder's TSBasePart transform (+4) and id number (+6). This is why a machine's own .DTS placeholder geometry is never drawn, fitted or not.

entries.name: ConfigPart_Render
entries.description: CONFIG_PART vtable +0x1c (0049a494): draws the shape bound in the part's SHAPE_INST member. When +0x10 holds a shape: makes shape+0x26 the current DBA context (g_CurrentShapeDbaContext), TSGroup_BindNodeTransform(this, local), makes the part's own cell-frame copy (+0x14) g_CellAnimFrames, TSPartList_Render(shape), restores both globals and calls Render_NoOp. The private frame copy is what lets each mount's weapon model play its own flipbook.

entries.name: ConfigPart_CreateArray
entries.description: (array, source, shapes): stores source at array+6 and its short count (source+4) at array+4, allocates count pointers (Mem_NewArray) at array+0, and fills each with a new 0x18-byte CONFIG_PART built inline -- ClassItem, TSBase, TSPartBase, then ShapeInstance_CtorCellFrames(part+0x10, *shapes++), then CONFIG_PART's table (0049a494).

entries.name: ConfigPartArray_StepFrame
entries.description: (array, index): steps the index'th CONFIG_PART of the array (array+0 holds the part pointers ConfigPart_CreateArray allocates) one cell on: the first word of the part's cell-frame copy (*(part+0x14)) becomes (word + 1) modulo the word *(*(shape+0x20)) of the part's shape (+0x10), and it returns 1 when that wrapped to 0, else 0. No caller found by es2_xref.

entries.name: SimObjectBase_ConstructAnimated
entries.description: The animated-shape structure base constructor: SimObjectBase_ConstructShaped, then the same shape-drawing vtable SimObjectBase_ConstructStatic installs. SimObjectBase_ConstructShaped allocates a real 0x42-byte TSShapeInstance at obj+0x34 and sets the root-motion-enabled byte at obj+0x39, which is what lets SimObject_ApplyRootMotionIfEnabled step the object's threads. Base_Construct uses it for the Radar and Armed cases, which draw from dts\BASES_AN.DTS.

entries.name: SimObjectBase_ConstructStatic
entries.description: The static-shape structure base constructor: SimObjectBase_Constructor, then installs the shape-drawing vtable. The shape holder it leaves at obj+0x34 is the two-field cell-frames form (ShapeInstance_CtorCellFrames, 00402fc0) and obj+0x39 stays clear, so no animation thread can be built on it and SimObject_ApplyRootMotionIfEnabled does nothing. Base_Construct uses it for the Plain, transport and GroundVehicle cases, which draw from dgs\BASES.DGS.

entries.name: SimObjectBase_ConstructWithDetailTable
entries.description: The shape-drawing base constructor that takes a LOD detail table: same body as SimObjectBase_ConstructAnimated, but builds the shape holder from roots[0] and stores the table itself at obj+0x41, where the other two base constructors null that field. Its only caller is Mech_Constructor, which is why a machine is the only class that selects a root.

entries.name: Shape_DrawAtDetailLevel
entries.description: Picks which root of a multi-root shape to draw, per frame, from projected size ((radius << DAT_006c60ac) / max(dist - radius, 1), floored at 1) scaled by Q10 g_ShapeDetailSizeScaleQ10, against the descending threshold table the type record's +0xe2 points at. THE TWO INDICES DIFFER: the root index starts at g_ShapeDetailBias, the threshold cursor starts at 0, and both advance together -- so a nonzero bias is a floor on how fine the shape is ever drawn, not an offset into the table. Installs the transform, calls the shape instance's vtable +0x1c, then restores roots[0]. The detail table at obj+0x41 is installed only by SimObjectBase_ConstructWithDetailTable, whose sole caller is Mech_Constructor, so only a machine selects; a structure reaches here with it null and just draws. ENDS AT 004034f2 -- Structure_DrawWithDetailBias at 004034f4 is a separate function Ghidra has not defined, so a containment-based cross-reference reports its calls as coming from inside this one.

entries.name: Structure_DrawWithDetailBias
entries.description: The Draw slot (+0x00) of all five structure vtables -- Structure, StructureRadar, StructureArmed, StructureEmplacement and StructureType0x22. Pushes g_TSDetailBiasFromStructureDetail into the TSDetailPart bias via TSDetailPart_SetBias, calls Shape_DrawAtDetailLevel, then restores the bias to 0. This is how the STRUCTURE DETAIL preference reaches TSDetailPart level selection. Ghidra has not defined it as a function, so it appears as Shape_DrawAtDetailLevel+0x110 in containment-based cross-references.

entries.name: Base_GetAimPoint
entries.description: The structure class's vtable +0x30 -- where on a structure anything aiming at it should aim. Calls SimObject_GetAimPointZero (00411a74) to clear both out triples, then writes BASES.DAT +0x2c into the offset triple's Z. Every caller adds the offset to the object's position unrotated, so this is a height up the structure's side. All 65 retail types state one, 1000 to 2000 world units. This settles BASES.DAT +0x2c, the last unread field of the record besides +0x00 and the six bytes at +0x18.

entries.name: Base_GetAimNodeTransform
entries.description: Structure vtable +0x24, installed by all five Base_Construct tables: fills the static record at 004a9650 with a fixed matrix and the translation (0, 0, BASES.DAT +0x2c), the type's aim-point height. Detection_LineOfSight reads its +0x1c as the sight height; the homing and HUD aim paths read its +0x14.

entries.name: Base_GetTurretAngle
entries.description: Structure vtable +0x3c: returns the short at structure+0x20f, the aim offset the sensor and target-selection arcs are measured from on top of the heading. Only StructureArmedVtable (004978ac) and StructureGroundVehicleVtable (00497818) install it; the plain building, the radar mast and the flyer all keep the shared 00411a5c zero stub. Which class installs this is what separates a structure that aims from one that does not.
entries.source: tools/ghidra_scripts/known_vtables.json; slot diff across the five Base_Construct tables

entries.name: Base_GetBodyRadius
entries.description: Structure vtable +0x5c: returns BASES.DAT +0x2a. The type's own stated body radius -- what the blast sweep subtracts from a candidate's distance -- distinct from the shape's bounding radius at shape+8 (SimObject_GetShapeRadius, vtable +0x10). The two disagree by up to a fifth on retail data and four types state 0 here. Base_GetCollisionRadius (+0x7c) returns the same field under a condition.

entries.name: Base_GetCollisionRadius
entries.description: Structure vtable +0x7c: the radius at which this structure blocks a walking machine, read by Mech_CollisionTest of the object being walked into, and by Mech_AiObstacleAvoidance through the same vtable slot to decide whether a candidate is worth sweeping. Returns BASES.DAT +0x2a only for an ANIMATED type (typeRec+0x06 nonzero) that is not a wreck-with-hulk; 0 otherwise, and 0 means walk through me. The static types it returns 0 for are the ones Structure_GatherWalkCandidates's collision-volume sweep covers instead, so the two sets are exact complements.

entries.name: Base_ComponentPresent
entries.description: Structure vtables +0x84, the structure's Mech_ComponentPresent, over structure+0x201.

entries.name: Base_NextTargetableComponent
entries.description: Structure vtables +0x80, the structure's Mech_NextTargetableComponent: the same walk over its type's whole component list (count at type+0x12, occupancy at structure+0x201) with the component id equal to the cursor. Not reached in retail -- a targeting pod's lock is set to -1 for every target whose target class (obj+0x1a8) is not 0, the same fence damage-system.md records for vtable +0x58.

entries.name: Base_EveryPartGone
entries.description: Whether the STRUCTURE, and not just this part, has gone: walks the type's components and passes one whose fire shape is -1 or whose damage has reached its maximum. It is what makes the last part to collapse use the type's whole-structure explosion and fire in place of its own, and what gates the hulk swap.

entries.name: Base_CollapseExplosion
entries.description: One collapse explosion and the stage hold that follows it, both out of the four-entry death sequence tables: the EXPLOS.DAT type from 004973fc, placed at the structure's own origin when 0049740c says so and at the offset put through its frame otherwise, then the component's stage timer reloaded from 00497404.
entries.signature: void __cdecl Base_CollapseExplosion(int *structure, int *state, int sequence, short *point)

entries.name: Base_ThrowDebris
entries.description: The wreckage a collapsing structure part throws: installs g_DebrisStructure (BASE_DEB) as the alternate database and throws the component record's +8 group from the part's emission point put through the structure's frame. A group above 5 -- i.e. one that resolves into BASE_DEB rather than the shared default -- also throws the fixed groups 10 and 12, which is why the big structures come apart in more pieces than the small ones.

entries.name: Base_FinishDependents
entries.description: Finishes off every structure part naming this one at component record +0x1c, recursively and through the ordinary damage path so each starts its own death sequence. The structure equivalent of a machine's .DMG bone group.

entries.name: Base_DeathSequenceTick
entries.description: Steps every structure part that is coming down through the next stage of its death sequence, counting the stage number DOWN from the count Base_ApplyDamage seeded. Stage above 1 scatters one smoke explosion at a random point inside the part's own spread box and reloads the timer to 300, and stage exactly 4 also runs Base_FinishDependents. Stage 1 is the collapse: Base_CollapseExplosion, Base_ThrowDebris, then either the part's sequence (component +2) steps to its rubble cell and Base_FinishDependents runs, or -- once Base_EveryPartGone passes, for a type that leaves a wreck (typeRec+0x04 >= 0), whatever the fires -- the object's model instance shape pointer is switched to g_HulkShapes[typeRec+0x04]. Stage 0 lights a fire (the type's once every part is gone when the type and the part both state one, else the part's own), or drops a one-part type with no wreck and no part sequence to -100000 on its Z.

entries.name: Base_ThinkTick
entries.description: StructureVtable's and StructureRadarVtable's +0x18 tick slot -- the plain building's whole per-tick behaviour. Base_DeathSequenceTick, then while standing: if typeRec+0x24 >= 0, step cell sequence typeRec+0x24 by one modulo that sequence's own frame count, on a countdown at +0x1f6 reloaded from typeRec+0x26 (milliseconds); and if typeRec+0x06 is non-zero, SimObject_ApplyRootMotionIfEnabled(this, 100), which steps the structure's animation threads. Eight retail types state a cell sequence but only types 9 and 0x1a reach this function; of the rest, the Armed types step the same array as a muzzle flash instead, the transport (0x22) never steps it, and 0x0a is never built. The flipbook is NOT what turns a radar dish -- all four radar types state -1 for it and spin a free-running thread instead.

entries.name: Base_TurretSeek
entries.description: The structure turret seek, two axes. Axis 0 is the ELEVATION and takes Math_EulerToward's X straight; axis 1 is the TRAVERSE and takes its Z NEGATED. Per axis: clamp(angle >> 3) to +/-0x100, a square-law gain Q8(Q8(|in|, in), gain), Math_RateLimitedMoveToward into the per-axis rate at +0x209, accumulate that into the angle at +0x20d clamped between the per-axis stops, then AnimThread_SeekToPosition(thread[axis], axis, (unsigned)angle >> 2). Tails into SimObject_ApplyRootMotionIfEnabled(this, 100), which re-poses the nodes. Gain 004973e4 = {2000, 2500}; rate limit 004973e8 = {200, 800}; lower stop 004973ec = {-4000, -32768}; upper stop 004973f0 = {4000, 32767} -- so the traverse is unlimited and only the elevation is held, to +/-4000. Same mechanism as the HERC turret: the angle seeks a position in a full-sweep animation rather than rotating a node.

entries.name: Base_AimTurret
entries.description: Transforms an aim point into a structure turret's own frame -- the object's world transform inverted, then shape PART 2's (transform 2 on all four armed BASES_AN roots, the barrel node hanging off the traversing base at transform 1) inverted -- takes the aim error from Math_EulerToward into DAT_004a9670, and hands it to the turret seek (00403d5c). Returns DAT_004a9670, a static triple, so the result is not reentrant.

entries.name: Base_ArmedThinkTick
entries.description: StructureArmedVtable's +0x18 tick slot (BASES.DAT types 8, 0x0b, 0x20, 0x23). A structure that has already fallen hands the whole tick to Base_ThinkTick. While standing: retargets every 10000 ms via Ai_SelectTarget(this, 0x30, 0) and drops a target past 60000; steps the muzzle-flash cell on the +0x1f6 countdown while that countdown's own value at +0x1f7 is still non-zero, reloading it only while the cell has not wrapped back to 0, so the flash plays through once and stops; leads the target by range*targetSpeed/PROJ-record-2 speed inside 40000, which only a GUN tower does because the launcher form never looks the speed up; aims through Base_AimTurret; and fires both barrels from (+/-300, 400, 0) in the turret node's frame on a 1500 ms countdown at +0x211. typeRec+0x2e is the ARMAMENT CLASS read as a value: 2 fires Rocket_Fire(0,..) and everything else Bullet_Fire(2,..). The LAUNCHER, not the gun, rolls rand & 0x1f == 0 -- for barrel 0 and, only if that failed, for barrel 1 -- so it puts at most one round up per opportunity. The countdown at +0x86 is a FIRING WINDOW, not a barrel selector: each expiry flips the flag at +0x21b and reloads from the pair at 004973e0 (both 10000), so the tower fires for ten seconds and holds for ten. Fire is gated on that flag, on aim error inside +/-1000 on both axes, and on range inside 40000.

entries.name: Base_TransportThinkTick
entries.description: StructureTransportVtable's +0x18 tick slot (class LC_BASE), BASES.DAT type 0x22 alone -- the TRANSPORT (its MFD name, STRINGS0.STR group 23 entry 24 via BASES.DAT +0x28), a landed drop pod with three fixed weapon stations; nothing on the model moves. A fallen one hands the tick to Base_ThinkTick. Otherwise runs Base_DeathSequenceTick, then fires THREE weapon stations from one object by rewriting its own heading field: heading += 0x1555, three passes 0x5554 (120 degrees) apart, original heading restored at the end. Unless +0xa5 is set it first sets +0xa5 when every component after the first is at full damage. Each station's 0x1f-byte record at +0x209+s*0x1f holds three 8-byte slots, a retarget countdown at +0x18 (Ai_SelectTarget(this, 0x10, 0x3000) on a 10000 reload) and a target at +0x1b. Slots read g_LcWeaponSlots (dat\LC_WPNS.DAT); slot k is live while component 2s+(k!=0)+1 is short of full damage, steps a firing window (reload 004973f4[open] + Math_RandomBelow(004973f8[open]), both pairs 5000) and fires when its refire countdown is out, the window open, the aim error (from the origin, against this station's heading) inside the slot's arcs and the range under the slot's. Slot 0 fires Rocket_Fire(3, muzzle, own euler, this, 0) with the target installed on +0x1a4 across the call and cleared after, purely to give the round a lock; slots 1-2 fire Bullet_FireBurst(3, frame aimed at the target, template+0x30, this, template+0x38) with WeaponMountTemplate_GetByWeaponId(8). Muzzle = position + Rotate2D(heading, offset.xy) + offset.z. Refire reloads from the slot's +0x14.

entries.name: Structure_GatherWalkCandidates
entries.description: Gathers the structures a walking machine can be blocked by and hands them to Structure_WalkCollisionTest. Walks the structure list at g_StructurePool, skipping the excluded object, and includes a candidate when it is a static type OR an animated one that has fallen to a wreck-with-hulk -- exactly the complement of what Base_GetCollisionRadius returns nonzero for -- unless the structure is gone entirely (destroyed, no hulk, one component).
entries.signature: void __cdecl Structure_GatherWalkCandidates(int *point, unsigned short radius, int excluded)

entries.name: Sim_RaycastShapeList
entries.description: (out, ray, side): gathers Sim_RaycastShapes' candidates from the structure pool (g_StructurePool), oldest first through Pool_Prev, into a stack array, then calls Sim_RaycastShapeVolume over them and returns its hit flag. Machines are not in the pool. A non-negative side skips a structure whose group team byte differs. The filter is Base_GetCollisionRadius's test read the other way round: typeRec+0x06 zero -- a STATIC structure -- always counts, and an animated structure counts ONLY once it passes the wreck test (typeRec+4 != -1, component 0 stages left <= 1, obj+0x99). No group-action test. So among structures this probe sees exactly the set whose collision radius is zero, and the machine sweep sees the rest.

entries.name: Sim_RaycastShapes
entries.description: (out, from, to, clearance, side): ray from one world point to another against the structures' collision volumes. Builds a ray record on the stack -- frame from Math_EulerToward(to, from) and BuildEulerRotationMatrixQ14 with from as translation, length Math_DistanceBetweenPoints, clearance at +8, world-to-ray inverse at +0x0a -- then Sim_RaycastShapeList. On a hit out[0] is the distance and out[1] the struck structure's obj+0xc; the hit flag returns in AX (the decompile drops it). Three callers, all clearance 0 and side -1: Mech_AiObstacleAvoidance twice and Ai_LineOfSightBlocked.

entries.name: Base_ApplyDamage
entries.description: Structure vtable +0x74. Writes one component's damage against its BASES.DAT template max. Past half the maximum it rolls once per tenth of health the shot moved through, each a ~10% chance (rand & 0xfff <= 0x199) of destroying the component outright. On a kill it clears the alive flag, records the attacker at state+7, and if Base_DamageFraction reads 0x100 marks the structure destroyed (obj+0x99), activates its mission action (obj+0x1b6) and credits the kill through attacker vtable +0x60. Returns early when typeRec+0x1e (invulnerable) is set.

entries.name: Base_ApplyExplosiveDamage
entries.description: Structure vtable +0x70, the blast counterpart of Base_ApplyDamage. Returns early for an invulnerable type, for a wreck that leaves a hulk, and -- the gate that matters -- for a type with no BASECOL.DAT model installed at typeRec+0x38, which makes 40 of the 65 retail types immune to explosions while still vulnerable to direct fire. For every live component it draws and compares (rand & 0xfff) < 0x1004, a ceiling one above the largest value that mask can produce, so THE ROLL NEVER FAILS and every component is measured; the draw only advances the generator. Measures the blast point against the component's own position via vtable +0x58 and applies (blastRadius - distance) * damage / blastRadius through vtable +0x74. No shields, no facing.
entries.signature: void __cdecl Base_ApplyExplosiveDamage(StructureObject *this, short damage, int *hitPoint, short blastRadius, int *attacker)

entries.name: Bullet_StashDirectFireDamage
entries.description: Writes the two globals (DAT_004a9676 armour, DAT_004a9678 shield) that Base_DirectFireHitTest reads back when a shot arrives with zero on both counts. Called only from Bullet_TickUpdate's subtype-9 (plasma) branch, which stashes the round's damage here and then zeroes it in the shot record before the raycast.

entries.name: Base_DirectFireHitTest
entries.description: Structure vtable +0x20 -- all five type-switched vtables Base_Construct installs (00497784/97818/978ac/97940/979d4) point this slot here. Hit test and damage in one call. Branches on typeRec+0x38 (installed when BASES.DAT +0x30 is nonzero): non-null runs Mech_SelectStruckComponent against the type's BASECOL.DAT sphere model and names the struck component, null runs Sim_RaycastShapeVolume against the shape's collision height field and always reports component 0. A destroyed type with a hulk (typeRec+4 != -1) is forced to the volume path. Spawns the shot's armour impact effect (shot effects base +0x10). See docs/retail/simulation/hit-detection.md.

entries.name: Base_DamageFraction
entries.description: Structure vtable +0x40. (sum of component damage << 8) / (sum of component max) -- a ratio of sums, not a count of destroyed components, so a type with one large core component is effectively destroyed by killing the core alone. 0x100 means the structure has fallen.

entries.name: Base_BearingInSensorArc_Always
entries.description: Vtable +0x44 of all five structure tables (BASE, RADAR_BASE, GUN_BASE, VEHICLE, LC_BASE): returns 1 in AX for any bearing, where the ACTOR base, mech and flyer share SimObject_BearingInSensorArc's +/-78.75 degree arc, so the arc test always passes for a structure.

entries.name: Base_Construct
entries.description: Builds a structure from a script.dat block-9 record: switches on the type index to pick one of five vtables, allocates the per-component alive-flag array (obj+0x201) and state array (obj+0x205, 11 bytes/entry), seeds each component's damage from the mission record's health percentage (param_1[0x19]: <0 or 100 = intact, 0 = spawned destroyed), and stores the BASES.DAT type record at obj+0x1f2. Its tail then builds one animation thread per sequence from 0 up, for as many as BASES.DAT +0x06 states (0-2): each is registered on the shape instance by ShapeInst_AddThread (00402374), started at the rate in the +0x20 short pair, and thread 1 is additionally seeded with AnimThread_SeekToPosition(thread, 1, 6000). So +0x06 is a THREAD COUNT, not merely a library selector -- the library is picked per case in the switch (the four Radar and four Armed cases take dts\BASES_AN.DTS, every other case dgs\BASES.DGS) and the two agree on all retail data. +0x20 is the per-thread playback rate pair.

entries.name: BaseFormation_GetSlotOffset
entries.description: Base equivalent of Formation_GetSlotOffset (004205cc), but reading a variable-length, file-backed table instead of a flat one: DAT_004a9630[formationId] is a per-formation record whose +4 field is a pointer to that formation's slot-offset array (10 bytes/slot: two int32s X,Y then a trailing int16), indexed as ptr + (slot-1)*10 -- i.e. slot N uses the (N-1)-th entry, so slot 1 (the group's first follower) uses entry 0. Returns {x, y} as two int32s (z is a one-time-zeroed static, never written per-call -- bases take no Z offset). DAT_004a9630 is populated by Base_LoadResources (00405fac) from dat\BFORMS.DAT -- unlike the mech table, this load site IS confirmed.

entries.name: Base_ApplyFormationOffset
entries.description: Vtable +0x78 for every base subtype (confirmed identical across all five base vtables: 0x497940/0x4979d4/0x4978ac/0x497784/0x497818, each layered on the common base vtable 0x49a54c) -- the structural match for Mech_ApplyFormationOffset (00417898). No-ops when the object's group-relative slot (+0x49) is 0 (the group's first-claimed member); otherwise looks up BaseFormation_GetSlotOffset(group's formation id, slot) via BaseFormation_GetSlotOffset and hands the offset to Formation_RotateAndAddOffset (00411d64).

entries.name: Base_AttachToGroup
entries.description: Base/structure equivalent of Mech_AttachToGroup (00417aa8), called from DBSim_BuildGroupRecord (00423b34) for discriminator 2. Stores the group pointer at +0x45 and the member's slot index within the group's member-ref array at +0x49. Fills heading only if unset (-0x8000 sentinel), applying a per-slot heading nudge from a formation-indexed table when the slot is nonzero. Fills position only if unset: reads the group's own coordinate pointer (group+0x18) or falls back to its route (Route_WaypointAt), then -- only when the adjustAnchor arg (the raw block-11 record's own 0x06 paints-ground flag) is nonzero -- replaces that shared point's position within its terrain tile with the formation's own fixed fraction of it, from BFORMS.DAT record +0x14 (map dimension), +0xc and +0x10 (the fraction in 256ths). This is what puts the group on the pad Base_ApplyFormationTerrain (00405db0) paints over the same tile; the two are gated by the same flag. It then unconditionally calls the object's own vtable +0x78 (Base_ApplyFormationOffset, Base_ApplyFormationOffset) with the position, then Terrain_MarkStructureFootprint (00470dc8) with that position and the object's SimObject_GetShapeRadius, then a terrain height query. Mechs have no equivalent: Mech_AttachToGroup takes no such flag and contains none of this arithmetic.
entries.signature: void __cdecl Base_AttachToGroup(void *structure, void *group, short slot, int adjustAnchor)

entries.name: Base_ApplyFormationTerrain
entries.description: Repaints the ground under one base group with its formation's own material -- what puts a retail base on a marked concrete pad instead of open terrain. Called from DBSim_SpawnMissionObjects (004253d8) immediately after DBSim_BuildGroupRecord, for discriminator-2 groups whose block-11 paints-ground flag (0x06) is set, passing the group's first-attached member. Reads that object's group pointer (+0x45) -> formation id (+2) -> the BFORMS.DAT record at DAT_004a9630, and returns without doing anything when the record's material index (+8) is -1, which is exactly the six formations that carry no layout map. Otherwise hands Terrain_PaintFormationPad (00471260) the object's position (+0x26), that material index, the record's row-pointer array (+0x18) and its map dimension (+0x14). Sibling of Base_AttachToGroup (00405c3c), which snaps the group onto the tile this paints under the same flag.

entries.name: Structure_InitPool
entries.description: (count): g_StructurePool = a new 0x12-byte pool of count 0x26d-byte elements (Pool_Init), the pool Base_Construct draws every structure class from, and g_StructureDeleteQueue = a new 8-byte list {Mem_NewArray(100), int16 count 0 at +4, int16 capacity 0x19 at +6}. Caller found by es2_xref: DBSim_LoadScriptDat.

entries.name: Structure_FlushDeletes
entries.description: ObjectPool_FlushDeleteQueue(g_StructureDeleteQueue, g_StructurePool). Base_StaticInit registers it as the base module's subsystem phase-5 stub.

entries.name: BaseType_LoadShape
entries.description: The whole of a structure type's model selection, indexing dat\BASES.DAT's table at typeIndex * 0x3c: the field at +6 picks the library (0 -> dgs\bases via BaseType_ResolveShape with classId 0x2bc0001, else dts\bases_an via the animated-library path with 0x1e0003) and the field at +2 is the shape index within it; the field at +0x32 picks the texture bank (0 -> basetex, else vehtex, except type 0x34 which borrows RAZOR's mech bank). Cross-check: exactly eight types select the animated library and BASES_AN.DTS holds exactly eight roots, numbered as those eight reference them. The 0x2bc0001/0x1e0003 constants are ClassItem registry classIds, not recordSize<<16|version, and 0x2bc0001 is literally BASES.DGS's own leading 4 bytes. See dgs-hd0-notes.md.

entries.name: Base_LoadResources
entries.description: base.cpp's resource-load sequence for the base/structure subsystem: streams dat\bforms (-> DAT_004a9630, formation offsets; see BaseFormation_GetSlotOffset), dat\lc_wpns (-> g_LcWeaponSlotCount and g_LcWeaponSlots, the transport's weapon slots), dat\bases (-> DAT_004a9620, the BASES.DAT type table BaseTypeTable.cs also reads; this is the only reader of it -- do not look for a Bases_LoadTypeTable, which is a name 0043a2e0 has carried on the strength of loading the BASES sprite bank, and which is really MfdStatusScreen_Ctor), dat\basecol (collision), dat\bhulks, dat\basetex and dat\vehtex (texture banks) via a shared plain-file-read helper (VolRStream_CtorFromPath open / VolRStream_Read read via a vtable+0x18 dispatch / VolRStream_Dtor close -- no container header, first bytes of each file are its own content, confirmed against BASES.DAT's independently-verified byte-exact parse). BFORMS.DAT's per-formation record is fully variable-length: int32 slot count N, N*10 bytes of slot data, an int32 material index (-1 for the six formations with no layout) and two more int32s (where the group's anchor sits in its tile, in 256ths), an int32 buffer count M, then M {1 length byte + that many data bytes} buffers -- confirmed byte-exact: walking the retail file this way consumes all 3186 content bytes with 17 formations (matching the block-11 formation id field's documented 0-16 range) and nothing left over.

entries.name: Base_ComponentPosition
entries.description: Structure vtable +0x58: the world position of one destructible part, which is what the blast falloff measures from. Builds the object's rotation from its euler triple if the +0x32 dirty flag is set, then puts the component's own point at BASES.DAT component record +0x10 through the object transform at obj+0x12. No node resolution -- a structure's parts do not move -- and NOT the BASECOL.DAT sphere geometry a shot is tested against.

entries.name: Base_FirstLiveComponent
entries.description: Base vtable +0x54. With a null second argument returns the first component index whose alive flag (+0x201 array) is non-zero, which is what Ai_AimAndFire asks for. With a pose (Rocket_Fire passes the round's +0xc block: euler triple, position at +0x1a) it walks the same live components and returns the one whose bearing from that position is nearest the pose's pitch and heading in |dpitch| + |dheading|, as Mech_ComponentNearestAim does; -1 when none is live.

entries.name: Base_StaticInit
entries.description: Static initialiser of the base (structure) module (Borland _INIT_ entry 004a7a6e, priority 0x20): registers Base_LoadResources at subsystem phase 2 and Structure_FlushDeletes at phase 5, nulls g_StructurePool and counts one live destructor (*Rtl_DtorCountPtr += 1). Base_StaticDtor is its _EXIT_ counterpart.

entries.name: Base_StaticDtor
entries.description: Base_StaticInit's _EXIT_ routine (Borland _EXIT_ entry 004a7be2): decrements *Rtl_DtorCountPtr and Mem_Deletes g_StructurePool.

entries.name: TransportStation_ElementCtor
entries.description: Rtl_VectorNew's per-element constructor for the three 0x1f-byte weapon-station records Base_Construct builds at LC_BASE+0x209 for BASES.DAT type 0x22, the transport: runs Rtl_VectorNew over the record's three 8-byte weapon slots with TransportSlot_ElementCtor, and initialises nothing itself.

entries.name: StructureComponentState_ElementCtor
entries.description: Rtl_VectorNew's per-element constructor for a structure's 11-byte component-state records (StructureComponentState), which Base_Construct allocates at structure+0x205, one per BASES.DAT component (PUSH 0x4069e5 at 00405a6a, element size 0xb, mode 1). An empty body that returns its argument, so each record starts as the zeroed memory Mem_NewArray hands back.

entries.name: BaseFormation_ElementCtor
entries.description: (record): returns its argument -- the per-element constructor Base_LoadResources hands Rtl_VectorNew for the BFORMS.DAT formation array (0x1c bytes each, count 004a962c).
entries.source: DBSIM disassembly at 00406a5c and its vector-new site 00406046

entries.name: BaseFormationSlot_ElementCtor
entries.description: (record): returns its argument -- the per-element constructor Base_LoadResources hands Rtl_VectorNew for each BFORMS.DAT formation's slot array (10 bytes each).
entries.source: DBSIM disassembly at 00406a64 and its vector-new site 00406081

entries.name: LcWeaponSlot_ElementCtor
entries.description: (record): returns its argument -- the per-element constructor Base_LoadResources hands Rtl_VectorNew for g_LcWeaponSlots (LC_WPNS.DAT, 0x16 bytes each); the LEA of +8 is the inlined empty constructor of the muzzle-offset member.
entries.source: DBSIM disassembly at 00406a6c and its vector-new site 00406206

entries.name: BaseType_ElementCtor
entries.description: (record): returns its argument -- the per-element constructor Base_LoadResources hands Rtl_VectorNew for the BASES.DAT type table (0x3c bytes each, count 004a961c); the LEAs of +0xa and +0x18 are inlined empty member constructors.
entries.source: DBSIM disassembly at 00406a77 and its vector-new site 004062de; docs/retail/formats/bases-dat.md

entries.name: BaseComponent_ElementCtor
entries.description: (record): returns its argument -- the per-element constructor Base_LoadResources hands Rtl_VectorNew for each BASES.DAT type's component array (0x1e bytes each, count type+0x12, pointer stored at type+0x14); the LEAs of +0xa, +0x10 and +0x16 are inlined empty member constructors.
entries.source: DBSIM disassembly at 00406a85 and its vector-new site 004063a8; docs/retail/formats/bases-dat.md

entries.name: TransportSlot_ElementCtor
entries.description: Rtl_VectorNew's per-element constructor for a transport weapon station's 8-byte weapon slot (refire countdown +0, firing-window countdown +3, window-open flag +6), passed by TransportStation_ElementCtor. An empty body that returns its argument.

entries.name: LoosePool_BASE_Dtor
entries.description: LoosePool<BASE>'s destructor, the dtor its class record (0x8 bytes, at 00406aa0) names: (pool, flags): decrements *Rtl_DtorCountPtr; when the pool is not null, Mem_Delete of its buffer at +0, then Mem_Delete of the pool when flags bit 0 is set.

entries.name: Base_TransportDtor
entries.description: LC_BASE vtable +0x08 (00497784, BASES.DAT type 0x22): the deleting destructor, (this, flags). Four RTL destructor-count decrements (LC_BASE, BASE, ACTOR, DET_ANIM_OBJ), AnimObj_Dtor(this, 0), then on flags bit 0 ObjList_SwapRemove(&maybe_GlobalLiveObjectList, this) instead of a Mem_Delete.

entries.name: Base_ReassessTickNoOp
entries.description: Vtable +0x1c (the reassess slot) of all five structure tables: returns 0 and does nothing. A structure's whole behaviour runs from its +0x18 think.

entries.name: GroundVehicle_Dtor
entries.description: VEHICLE vtable +0x08 (00497818): the deleting destructor, (this, flags). Five RTL destructor-count decrements (VEHICLE, GUN_BASE, BASE, ACTOR, DET_ANIM_OBJ), AnimObj_Dtor(this, 0), then on flags bit 0 ObjList_SwapRemove(&maybe_GlobalLiveObjectList, this).

entries.name: Base_ArmedDtor
entries.description: GUN_BASE vtable +0x08 (004978ac): the deleting destructor, (this, flags). Four RTL destructor-count decrements (GUN_BASE, BASE, ACTOR, DET_ANIM_OBJ), AnimObj_Dtor(this, 0), then on flags bit 0 ObjList_SwapRemove(&maybe_GlobalLiveObjectList, this).

entries.name: Base_Dtor
entries.description: BASE vtable +0x08 (00497940): the deleting destructor, (this, flags). Three RTL destructor-count decrements (BASE, ACTOR, DET_ANIM_OBJ), AnimObj_Dtor(this, 0), then on flags bit 0 ObjList_SwapRemove(&maybe_GlobalLiveObjectList, this).

entries.name: Base_RadarDtor
entries.description: RADAR_BASE vtable +0x08 (004979d4): the deleting destructor, (this, flags). Four RTL destructor-count decrements (RADAR_BASE, BASE, ACTOR, DET_ANIM_OBJ), AnimObj_Dtor(this, 0), then on flags bit 0 ObjList_SwapRemove(&maybe_GlobalLiveObjectList, this).

entries.name: LightManager_Construct
entries.description: Effect light manager constructor: Rtl_VectorNew of 20 slots at +0x6c, stride 0x23, each flagged free with a null light pointer; embeds a light object at +0x328 and zeroes the two free-list counts at +0x35c and +0x3b0. Its own LightManager_SetFalloffConstants(mgr, 2000, 3000) call is dead -- LightManager_InitSubsystem overwrites it immediately.

entries.name: LightManager_SetFalloffConstants
entries.description: Stores the manager's two falloff constants SHIFTED RIGHT BY 5: mgr+0x10 = A = param>>5, mgr+0x14 = B = param>>5. The live call is (10, 2000), so A=0 and B=62 -- not 10 and 2000.

entries.name: LightManager_SetSlotFalloff
entries.description: (mgr, slot, a, b): the per-slot form of LightManager_SetFalloffConstants -- stores a >> 5 at the slot's A (+0x0f) and b >> 5 at its B (+0x13), slot = mgr + 0x6c + index * 0x23, then LightManager_RecomputeCullRadius on it. No caller found by es2_xref.

entries.name: LightManager_ClaimSlot
entries.description: Claims the first free effect-light slot for a world point: marks it busy, copies the position, seeds intensity 0xff, copies A/B from the manager, appends the slot to the live array at mgr+0x1c and recomputes the cull radius. Returns the slot index. NO FULL-TABLE GUARD -- with all 20 busy it writes the slot record through the caller's own worldPoint pointer and returns 0x14; unreachable in retail: EffectLightPool holds three handles.

entries.name: LightManager_ReleaseSlot
entries.description: Frees a slot: sets the free flag, swap-removes its pointer from the live array, and recycles its attached light object through LightManager_RecycleLight.

entries.name: LightManager_SetSlotPosition
entries.description: Writes a slot's world position (slot+1/+5/+9). Reached only through EffectLight_SetPosition; nothing in retail moves an effect light.

entries.name: LightManager_SetSlotIntensity
entries.description: Writes a slot's intensity to BOTH +0x0d (int16) and +0x1b (int32) and recomputes the cull radius. ClaimSlot leaves +0x1b alone; +0x1b is what the per-object selection reads, +0x0d what the cull radius reads.

entries.name: LightManager_SetCameraPosition
entries.description: Copies the view object's position into mgr+0x00..+0x08 once a frame from Sim_RenderFrame. Read by nothing on the live path -- its only consumer, LightManager_SelectLightsUnconditional, has zero callers.

entries.name: LightManager_SelectLightsForObject
entries.description: Called once per depth-sorted render entry from ObjList_DrawEntryRender, with the entry's position and its SimObject_GetShapeRadius. Per live slot: cull past slot+0x17; else Math_Atan2Guarded(dist>>5, radius>>5) < 8000 picks a DIRECTIONAL approximation (distance-attenuated intensity, direction rebuilt at length 0x800) and otherwise a POINT light (unattenuated, falloff constants handed to the shade path as light+0x34=0 and light+0x38=1984). Far is directional, near is point -- the helper takes (x, y), so the angle is the object's angular size. See docs/retail/formats/effect-lights.md.

entries.name: LightManager_SelectLightsUnconditional
entries.description: No reference found by es2_xref. A cull-by-fixed-distance variant of LightManager_SelectLightsForObject that always builds a point light, with no directional approximation.

entries.name: LightManager_RecomputeCullRadius
entries.description: slot+0x17 = (slot.intensity * B * 0x20) / 10 + A * 0x20. With A=0 and B=62 that is intensity * 198.4, so a full-intensity light is culled past ~50,592 world units.

entries.name: Light_GetOrCreateDirectional
entries.description: Pooled-object getter/constructor for a type=1 (directional) light: recycles from a small free-list at param_1+0x35c/+0x360 if available, otherwise allocates+constructs (vtable &PTR_LAB_0049f8d8, type field at +0x16 set to 1), then registers it via Light_Register (FUN_0048bd44). Called by LightManager_SelectLightsForObject.

entries.name: Light_GetOrCreatePoint
entries.description: Same pooled-object pattern as Light_GetOrCreateDirectional (FUN_00407388) but for a type=2 (point) light (vtable &PTR_LAB_00497ac8, type field +0x16 set to 2). Called by LightManager_SelectLightsForObject and LightManager_SelectLightsUnconditional.

entries.name: LightManager_RecycleLight
entries.description: Unregisters a synthesised light and pushes it back onto the manager's directional (+0x35c) or point (+0x3b0) free list by its type field +0x16.

entries.name: LightSlot_ElementCtor
entries.description: (slot): returns its argument -- the per-element constructor LightManager_Construct hands Rtl_VectorNew for the manager's twenty 0x23-byte slots at +0x6c; the LEA of +1 is the inlined empty constructor of the slot's position.
entries.source: DBSIM disassembly at 00407548 and its vector-new site 00406e4c

entries.name: TSOmniLight_Dtor
entries.description: TSOmniLight vtable +0x00 (00497ac8, RTTI 'TSOmniLight', 0x40 bytes, derived from TSLight), the destructor named by its class record: (light, flags). Two RTL destructor-count decrements, TSContext_Dtor(light+0x1e, 2), TSContext_Dtor(light, 0), then Mem_Delete on flags bit 0 -- TSSunLight_Dtor's body.
entries.source: DBSIM disassembly at 004075c1; class record at 0040756d

entries.name: EffectLight_Construct
entries.description: Attaches an effect light: claims a manager slot at the world point, stores the index at handle+0x0c, and sets the slot intensity to the EXPLOS.DAT row's frame intensity [0]. Called only by Explosion_Construct, gated on the row's light mode being nonzero.

entries.name: EffectLight_Destruct
entries.description: Releases the handle's manager slot and optionally frees the handle.

entries.name: EffectLight_SetIntensity
entries.description: Sets the handle's slot intensity. Explosion_TickUpdate calls it with the row's frame intensity [frame] & 0xff on each flipbook step.

entries.name: EffectLight_SetPosition
entries.description: Sets the handle's slot position. No retail caller moves an effect light.

entries.name: LightManager_InitSubsystem
entries.description: Builds the effect light manager singleton DAT_004a968c (0x404 bytes, LightManager_Construct), then overrides the constructor's falloff constants with LightManager_SetFalloffConstants(mgr, 10, 2000) -- the pair that actually reaches every frame, giving A=0 and B=62 after the setter's >>5. Also builds the effect-light handle pool EffectLightPool.

entries.name: EffectLightPool_FlushDeletes
entries.description: ObjectPool_FlushDeleteQueue(004a9686, EffectLightPool).

entries.name: Light_AddPersistent
entries.description: (light): appends to Light_PersistentList and increments Light_PersistentCount, with no bound check. Light_CreateMissionSun adds the sun after Light_Register.

entries.name: Light_RemovePersistent
entries.description: (light): finds the light in Light_PersistentList and shifts the later entries down over it and decrements Light_PersistentCount.

entries.name: Light_ReregisterPersistent
entries.description: Light_Register on every entry of Light_PersistentList. ObjList_DrawEntryRender calls it when DAT_004cfa08 is set.

entries.name: LightManager_RegisterSubsystem
entries.description: Static-init registrar for the effect light manager (Borland _INIT_ entry 004a7a74, priority 0x20): registers LightManager_InitSubsystem at phase 2 and EffectLightPool_FlushDeletes at phase 5, and nulls EffectLightPool. Its entry precedes Explosion_RegisterSubsystem's, so the light flush runs first in phase 5.

entries.description: LightSource vtable +0x00 (00497b8a, RTTI 'LightSource', 0xe bytes, derived from DRAWABLE): push ebp / mov ebp,esp / pop ebp / ret. An effect light draws nothing.

entries.description: LightSource vtable +0x04 (00497b8a): returns 0 -- a null position pointer.

entries.name: LightManager_Dtor
entries.description: LightManager's destructor, the dtor its class record (0x404 bytes, at 00407a6d) names: (manager, flags): when manager is not null, decrements *Rtl_DtorCountPtr three times, TSContext_Dtor(manager+0x346, 2) and TSContext_Dtor(manager+0x328, 0), the embedded objects, then Mem_Delete when flags bit 0 is set.

entries.name: Explosion_GetTypeRecord
entries.description: g_ExplosionTypeTable + obj[+0x41] * 0x28 -- the impact effect's own EXPLOS.DAT type row.

entries.name: ExplosionPool_FlushDeletes
entries.description: ObjectPool_FlushDeleteQueue(g_ExplosionDeleteQueue, g_ExplosionPool). A phase-5 subsystem hook registered by Explosion_RegisterSubsystem, after EffectLightPool_FlushDeletes.

entries.name: Explosion_LoadResources
entries.description: EXPLO.CPP subsystem init. Loads the fifteen EXPLO0..EXPLO14 DBA banks (name template 'explo666' at 00497ba0), the EXPLOS.DTS shape file and the EXPLOS.DAT table; binds each shape to the DBA its EXPLOS.DAT shape row names. With CockpitArt_LoadOnDemand set it uses the 13-bank EXPLO<n>S / EXPLOS2 low-memory set instead.

entries.name: Explosion_Destruct
entries.description: Explosion vtable +0x08: queues the effect's ground shape (+0x4f) on g_FlatObjDeleteQueue and its light (+0x53) on the queue at 004a9686, then as FlatObj_Destruct: restores TSObjVtable, deletes the shape instance at +0x34 (flag 3), frees on the flag's low bit.

entries.name: Explosion_Construct
entries.description: Builds one impact effect: (obj, typeId, worldPoint, ownerObject, playSound). Resolves the EXPLOS.DAT type row's shape, resets that shape's cell-animation frame counter to 0, loads the frame countdown from the row's frame interval, and optionally attaches a light source and a trail object. playSound gates the row's sound id + 10.

entries.name: Explosion_ProximityTest
entries.description: (effect, point): returns 1 when the effect's type row has light mode exactly 2 and the distance from the effect to the point is under the row's proximity radius (+0x20). Unreferenced: no rel32 branch, stored pointer or vtable slot reaches it, and the effect class's vtable (00497d4c) has six slots.

entries.name: Explosion_TickUpdate
entries.description: Impact-effect tick, called directly by Sim_MainTick (the effect vtable's +0x14 is a shared stub). Counts the frame timer down; on expiry steps the shape's cell-animation frame modulo the shape's own frame count, drives the attached light from the type row's per-frame intensity, and reloads the timer. Returns finished on the step that wraps the frame back to 0, so the flipbook plays exactly once.

entries.name: Explosion_GetOwnerDrawCell
entries.description: Returns owner+0x1e8 (the owner's cached draw-table cell pair) for an impact effect that has an owner (effect+0x57), else 0. Scene_SubmitFrameObjects files the effect under that cell instead of the one its own position falls in.

entries.name: Explosion_IsHiddenFromOwnerCockpit
entries.description: Returns 1 (skip drawing) when the effect has an owner (effect+0x57) the cockpit camera is attached to (Cam_IsAttachedTo(ViewObjectPtr, owner)) and its type id (effect+0x41) is not 2 or 11-14; else 0.

entries.name: Explosion_RegisterSubsystem
entries.description: Static-init registrar for EXPLO.CPP (Borland _INIT_ entry 004a7a7a, priority 0x20): registers Explosion_LoadResources at phase 2 and ExplosionPool_FlushDeletes at phase 5, and nulls g_ExplosionPool.

entries.name: Explosion_StaticDtor
entries.description: Explosion_RegisterSubsystem's _EXIT_ routine (Borland _EXIT_ entry 004a7bee): decrements *Rtl_DtorCountPtr and Mem_Deletes g_ExplosionPool when it is set.

entries.name: ObjPool_EXPLOSION_Dtor
entries.description: ObjPool<EXPLOSION>'s destructor, the dtor its class record (0x8 bytes, at 0040835e) names: (pool, flags): decrements *Rtl_DtorCountPtr; when the pool is not null, Mem_Delete of its entry buffer at +0 when that is set, then Mem_Delete of the pool when flags bit 0 is set.

entries.name: Debris_FreeResources
entries.description: debris.cpp phase-5 teardown: frees the debris object pool and its free list.

entries.name: Debris_LoadPieceList
entries.description: Reads one debris group out of an open _DEB.DAT stream: a throw count, a piece count, and that many 14-byte pieces. Multiplies both of a piece's angle fields by 182 (degrees to BAM) unless the raw value is the -1 sentinel, and accumulates the group's total piece weight into the group record, which the file does not store. Returns the largest shape index the group names.

entries.name: Debris_ThrowGroupAt
entries.description: Debris_ThrowGroup from a point rather than a frame: builds an identity rotation with the point in its translation and forwards. Every spawn site but a machine's own component destruction uses this one. The fourth argument is forwarded and read by nothing; all six call sites pass 0.
entries.signature: void __cdecl Debris_ThrowGroupAt(short *group, int shapeArray, int *point, int unused)

entries.name: Debris_Throw
entries.description: Places and launches one piece of a debris group. A piece stating either angle has its own yaw composed onto the spawn frame and the composed attitude read back as Euler angles, but only one stating an orientation yaw keeps it; the position is the spawn frame's own translation either way, the composed transform being a temporary. Then Debris_ThrowAtBearing, or Debris_ThrowRandomBearing when the piece states no throw yaw.

entries.name: Debris_ThrowGroup
entries.description: Throws one debris group at a transform. A group whose throw count is zero throws every piece it holds once each; any other throws exactly that many pieces drawn at random and weighted -- a draw under the group's total weight, then each piece's weight subtracted off it in file order until one covers the remainder, so the same piece can be thrown twice. Ghidra infers three parameters; the call site pushes four and cleans 0x10, and the fourth is unused.
entries.signature: void __cdecl Debris_ThrowGroup(short *group, int shapeArray, int transform, int unused)

entries.name: Debris_LoadDatabase
entries.description: Loads one debris database into a 12-byte struct {group* groups; int16 groupCount; TSShape** shapes; int16 shapeCount}: dts\<name>.DTS for the shapes and dat\<name>.DAT for the groups, read by Debris_LoadPieceList. A non-zero third argument is written into every loaded shape's bound-bank pointer (shape+0x26), which is how a chassis' wreckage is painted in the chassis' colours. Three call sites: def_deb at startup, base_deb from Base_LoadResources, and one per HERC chassis from MechType_InitOne into that type's record at +0x212.

entries.name: Debris_LoadResources
entries.description: debris.cpp phase-2 subsystem init: allocates the 150-entry debris pool at g_DebrisPool and its 40-entry draw list, loads DEF_DEB into g_DebrisDefault, nulls g_DebrisAlternate, and seeds the three throw parameters to their first-throw values (6000, 16000, 420).

entries.name: Debris_Construct
entries.description: Builds one thrown piece on a shape: position at +0x26, child debris group at +0x41 (signed char, -1 = never bursts and the gate on the whole death branch), EXPLOS.DAT death effect at +0x59, a burst countdown of RandomBelow(30000)+2000 at +0x55, and the currently installed alternate database captured at +0x5d so a burst reads its child group against the same table its parent came from.
entries.signature: int * __cdecl Debris_Construct(int *debris, int shape, int *position, char childGroup, short deathEffect)

entries.name: Debris_Resolve
entries.description: Splits a debris group index into the database that owns it, in place: below g_DebrisDefault's group count it reads the default, at or above it subtracts that count and returns g_DebrisAlternate, whatever the calling site installed a moment earlier. Retail DEF_DEB holds 6 groups, so 0-5 are shared and 6 upward reach the installed table.

entries.name: Debris_Launch
entries.description: Gives one piece its launch velocity and tumble. speed = (g_DebrisSpeedScale << 10) / mass; the pitch splits it into a horizontal part and a vertical one and the yaw spreads the horizontal onto X and Y, all Q14 against the cosine table. Adds the carrier velocity at DAT_004a96e4, which only Flyer_ComponentDamageWrite ever sets. The spin is Math_Q10Multiply(-1700, rand & 0x3ff) - 800, so always negative: every piece tumbles the same way at 800-2500 BAM a second.
entries.signature: void __cdecl Debris_Launch(int *debris, int mass, short pitch, short yaw)

entries.name: Debris_ThrowAtBearing
entries.description: Draws the launch pitch between g_DebrisPitchMin and g_DebrisPitchMax and forwards to Debris_Launch on the given bearing.

entries.name: Debris_ThrowRandomBearing
entries.description: Debris_ThrowAtBearing on a wholly random bearing -- what a piece stating no throw yaw gets, which is every DEF_DEB piece.

entries.name: Debris_TickUpdate
entries.description: Debris vtable +0x14. Spin into euler X and gravity (-0x20, or -10 in theater 4, the Moon) into the vertical speed; Math_Q10Multiply(30, v) drag on the two horizontal axes only; then the move, by the AVERAGE of the speed before and after this tick and added UN-INTEGRATED, so a debris velocity is per-tick where a flyer's is per-second. Below terrain + Math_Q10Multiply(500, shapeRadius) the piece snaps up and bounces at -Math_Q10Multiply(450, vz), clearing its countdown; a rebound under 0x2d has stopped. A piece with a child group then bursts -- the countdown is ticked only while it is still flying, so ground contact bursts it either way -- spawning its death effect, re-installing the database at +0x5d and throwing the child group at a tightened window (3000, 8000, 320).

entries.name: Debris_Draw
entries.description: Debris vtable draw slot: installs the piece's model transform and renders its shape.

entries.name: Debris_RegisterSubsystem
entries.description: Registers Debris_LoadResources as a phase-2 subsystem loader and Debris_FreeResources as phase 5, and nulls the pool pointer.

entries.name: Debris_StaticDtor
entries.description: Debris_RegisterSubsystem's _EXIT_ routine (Borland _EXIT_ entry 004a7bf4): decrements *Rtl_DtorCountPtr and Mem_Deletes g_DebrisPool when it is set.

entries.name: SmokeBall_FlushDeletes
entries.description: ObjectPool_FlushDeleteQueue(g_SmokeBallDeleteQueue, g_SmokeBallPool). Smoke_FlushDeletes calls it after flushing the emitter queue.

entries.name: Smoke_FlushDeletes
entries.description: ObjectPool_FlushDeleteQueue(g_SmokeDeleteQueue, g_SmokePool), then SmokeBall_FlushDeletes. Smoke_RegisterSubsystem registers it as the smoke module's subsystem phase-5 stub.

entries.name: SmokeBall_LoadResources
entries.description: Builds g_SmokeBallPool (Pool_Init: 200 entries of 0x4c bytes, the SMOKE_BALL size) and g_SmokeBallDeleteQueue (8-byte list header, capacity 0x19, over Mem_NewArray(100)); loads the smoke shapes into g_SmokeShapes with Shape_LoadAllRoots and the smoke DBA bank into g_SmokeTextures with Resource_Load, and points every loaded root's +0x26 DBA context at g_SmokeTextures. Called at the end of Smoke_LoadResources.

entries.name: Smoke_LoadResources
entries.description: The smoke module's phase-2 subsystem loader (registered by Smoke_RegisterSubsystem): builds g_SmokePool (Pool_Init: 20 entries of 0x2a bytes, the SMOKE size) and g_SmokeDeleteQueue (8-byte list header, capacity 0x19, over Mem_NewArray(100)), then SmokeBall_LoadResources.

entries.name: SmokeBall_Construct
entries.description: SMOKE_BALL (TS_OBJ, vtable 00498084) constructor: shape from g_SmokeShapes[variant], position from the argument, frame timer 200.

entries.name: Effect_DriftAndAnimate
entries.description: (obj): adds the int16 velocity +0x41/+0x43/+0x45 to the position +0x26/+0x2a/+0x2e; when Timer_CountDown(+0x47) expires, reloads +0x48 with 200 and steps the shape's frame counter (*(shape(+0x34)+8)) on modulo the frame count, returning 1 when it wraps to 0. Sim_MainTick runs it on every object of the pool 004a96f2 and queues those returning 1 for delete.

entries.name: Smoke_Construct
entries.description: SMOKE (DRAWABLE, vtable 00498064, 0x2a bytes) constructor: owner +0x15, component +0x19, smoke type +0x28, first shape variant +0x26 = type*4 + (Math_RandomNext(0x4d268f) & 3). es2_xref finds nothing reaching it.

entries.name: Smoke_Tick
entries.description: Called from Sim_MainTick. Every 200 ticks while the count +0x24 lasts, places a SMOKE_BALL at the owner component's point (or a fixed offset) and steps +0x26 to the next of the type's four variants.

Smoke_StaticDtor is its _EXIT_ counterpart.

entries.description: SMOKE vtable +0x04 (00498064): returns 0 -- a null position pointer.

entries.description: SMOKE vtable +0x08 (00498064), the destructor its class record names: (this, flags). Two RTL destructor-count decrements (SMOKE, DRAWABLE), then Mem_Delete(this) on flags bit 0.

entries.name: SmokeBall_Dtor
entries.description: SMOKE_BALL vtable +0x08 (00498084), the destructor its class record names: (this, flags). Installs TSObjVtable, deletes the shape instance at +0x34 through its own vtable +0x18 with flags 3, and Mem_Deletes this on flags bit 0.
entries.source: DBSIM decompile at 0040970d; class record at 00409633

entries.name: FlatObj_LoadResources
entries.description: Loads a DTS shape set and binds a matching DBA to it, choosing base name 'flat' when param_1 == 0 and 'flat2' otherwise; the same base name is used for both 'dts\<name>' and 'dba\<name>'. Stores the loaded shape list at 004a971c with its count at 004a9720, then loops over every loaded shape writing the bound-DBA pointer into each instance's +0x26 -- the SAME bound-active-DBA field confirmed for mech texturing in docs/retail/formats/dts-texture-binding.md. Called at the end of World_LoadTheater. Retail data has FLAT2.DBA (a single 64x54 frame). Named 'maybe_' because what the flat/flat2 shapes are actually drawn as (ground plane, distant filler, skirt) was not determined.

entries.name: Sim_FlushDeleteQueue
entries.description: One-line wrapper running ObjectPool_FlushDeleteQueue(g_FlatObjDeleteQueue, g_FlatObjPool). Registered at subsystem phase 5, which Sim_RenderFrame runs at the start of every frame's draw, and called again at the end of Mech_ComponentDamageWrite, which commits the ground shapes a lost leg or a vanishing chassis queued during the damage write.

entries.name: FlatObj_Draw
entries.description: FlatObj vtable slot 0: SimObject_ConformToTerrain, SimObject_InstallModelTransform, then the shape instance's (obj+0x34) own vtable +0x1c draw.

entries.name: FlatObj_RegisterSubsystem
entries.description: Static-init registrar for the FlatObj pool: registers Sim_FlushDeleteQueue at phase 5 and nulls g_FlatObjPool.

entries.name: Meteor_FlushDeletes
entries.description: ObjectPool_FlushDeleteQueue(g_MeteorDeleteQueue, g_MeteorPool). Meteor_RegisterSubsystem registers it as the meteor module's subsystem phase-5 stub.

entries.name: Meteor_LoadResources
entries.description: Startup loader for the METEOR (drop pod) subsystem, registered into DBSIM's subsystem-loader table by Meteor_RegisterSubsystem: allocates the object pool at g_MeteorPool and its free list, loads the dts\meteor shape group and the dba\impact texture bank, and binds that bank into every shape it loaded.

entries.name: Meteor_Construct
entries.description: Builds a drop pod aimed at a picked ground point. It is NOT dropped straight down: it draws a random heading and a HORIZONTAL RUN-IN of 70000 plus up to 25000 units, starts that far short of the target along that heading, and flies in at a flat 2000 units per tick. The launch height is derived from the run-in -- n = runIn/2000 ticks, height = (n*n>>1)*50, so 30600 to 55200 units up -- and both axes are then flown at constant velocity, so the descent is a straight line. Reading the 70000-95000 figure as an altitude puts the pod at twice the height it belongs at. Velocity at +0x45, landed flag +0x4b and open-animation counter +0x4d cleared, delivered group at +0x55. It never writes the type tag at +4, so a pod keeps the zero Pool_Init left: tag 0, which ObjList_IsBeyondDrawDistance gives its own draw distance.

entries.name: Meteor_Render
entries.description: Draws a drop pod: while falling, the plain shape; once landed (+0x4b set), builds its rotation matrix from its euler triple if stale and draws the opening-animation shape instance at +0x41 instead.

entries.name: Meteor_Tick
entries.description: The drop pod's per-tick update, called from Sim_MainTick (0045f5fb is the one call es2_xref finds). Falling phase (+0x4b clear): integrates position by the velocity at +0x45, pitches the shape to Math_Atan2Bam(2000, vz) and zeroes +0x32, plays sound 0x2f (podin2) once (latch +0x51) below absolute height 50000, and on ground contact (Terrain_HeightQuery) sets the landed flag, zeroes the pitch, snaps to ground, plays sound 0x30 (podland) and calls Damage_ExplosiveBlastSweep(pos, 3000, 10000, 0, null), setting +0x4c if that answers non-zero. Both sounds go through Sound_PlayAt at ViewObjectPtr + 4, the camera's own position, not the pod's. Landed phase: while +0x4d >> 10 is below the opening shape's (+0x41) frame count, writes it as the shape's frame and advances +0x4d by Math_IntegrateRateOverTick(0x5dc). Once it reaches the count, when the pod carries a group (+0x55): unless +0x4c is set, copies its position onto the group's leader and clears the group's +0x14 (the moment the group enters the mission); then, either way, allocates a FlatObj from g_FlatObjPool (004a9711) on g_FlatShapes root 3 at its position, without checking the allocation before writing the position. Then destroys the shape instance at +0x41 and returns 1; otherwise returns 0.

entries.name: Meteor_RegisterSubsystem
entries.description: Static-init registrar for the METEOR subsystem (Borland _INIT_ entry 004a7a92, priority 0x20): registers Meteor_LoadResources at phase 2 and Meteor_FlushDeletes at phase 5, and nulls g_MeteorPool. Meteor_StaticDtor is its _EXIT_ counterpart.

entries.name: Bullet_Draw
entries.description: The Bullet class's vtable slot 0. Sets DAT_004a5b1c = 0 for the duration of the call, which is what makes a projectile's textured polys draw unlit (see TSTexture4Poly_Render), installs the object's frame as the model transform, renders the shape instance at obj+0x34, and restores DAT_004a5b1c from DAT_004a5b20.

Projectile_StaticDtor is its _EXIT_ counterpart.

entries.name: Rocket_GetTypeRecord
entries.description: getType() accessor: returns the instance's 14-byte ROCKETS.DAT record, maybe_RocketTypeTable_Unguided + instance.typeIndex (byte @ +0x41) * 0xe.

entries.name: Rocket_HomingSteer
entries.description: Missile seeker. Steers only with a target (+0x56) and, when the owner is locally piloted (owner+0xa3), only while that target is still the owner's selected target (owner+0x1a4). Subtype 2 (ARM) steers only while the target emits (target +0x96 scanner or +0xa1 jammer). The lead is the target's component +0x5a through target vtable +0x58 when non-negative, else the aim point (vtable +0x24) or the origin; Math_EulerToward(lead, self) less the round's euler gives the pitch and heading errors. Subtype 3 sets owner+0xb5 to suppress AI weapon selection for a tick; subtypes 0, 1 and 4, while the FIRING owner's +0x9c spoof flag is set (ECM), move each error in [-0xc00, 0xbff] by 0xc00 toward the opposite sign. Each error then goes through Math_RateLimitedMoveToward at 0x500 and Math_IntegrateRateOverTick onto pitch (+0xc) and heading (+0x10).

entries.name: Rocket_PlayerSteer
entries.description: The electro-optical missile's player steer, not a ballistic variant. Gate input+0x0d is the fire trigger (0x4d2357). Held: reads the two axes the block's camera-axis pointers +0x22 and +0x26 address (the steering and throttle axes while DAT_004d25aa routes the controls to the round), subtracts Math_IntegrateRateOverTick(Math_Q8Multiply(0x500, *+0x22)) from the heading (+0x10) and adds the same of *+0x26 to the pitch (+0x0c), with no rate limit or deadband, marks the frame stale (+0x32 = 0) and zeroes the trigger and both axes, so the player's fire path never sees the trigger while a round is flown. Released: drops the round's target (+0x56) and rewrites its subtype id (+0x41) to 0. See docs/retail/simulation/rockets.md.

entries.name: Rocket_TickUpdate
entries.description: Per-tick launcher-round update, vtable +0x14. Steps the shape cell-anim frame on ROCKETS.DAT +0x08/+0x0a (the exhaust flame, NOT a seeker reacquire); age +1 vs record +0x02 in ticks; damped burn speed += Math_IntegrateRateOverTick(record +0x04) averaged with the opening speed, capped at PROJ.DAT Speed; Rocket_PlayerSteer for a locally-simulated subtype 3, raising DAT_004d25aa, else Rocket_HomingSteer; Sim_RaycastObjectList over this tick step with record +0x06 as slack. When the round ends (lifetime or hit): a locally-simulated subtype 3 round calls Input_LatchButton(1, 1) and clears the trigger 004d2357; the round in DAT_0049c394 ending before its lifetime raises DAT_0049c398. Last, on every tick: for a round whose owner is not locally piloted (owner+0xa3 clear), sound 0x32 within 40000 of ViewObjectPtr, latched at round+0x06 and re-armed when the round leaves that range.

entries.name: Rocket_LoadTypeTable_Unguided
entries.description: rocket.cpp. Loads the Type-0 rocket type table (14-byte/0xe stride, confirmed via IMUL-style indexing).

entries.name: Rocket_Construct
