entries.description: The movement half the patrol, search-and-destroy and guard thinks share: Ai_DriveToPoint at mech+0x240 under a standing squad order, Ai_FollowRoute for the group leader, Ai_KeepFormation for everyone else -- so ONLY THE LEADER READS THE ROUTE. Then Ai_UpdateWeaponsFree and Mech_CenterTorsoTick.

entries.name: Mech_AiEnterCombat
entries.description: Thin wrapper that calls Mech_AiCombatReassess; the entry point other AI paths use to force a machine into the combat decision.

entries.name: Ai_NavigationStepThunk
entries.description: A bare tail call to Ai_NavigationStep. Named by no behaviour descriptor.

entries.name: Mech_BehaviourSearchDestroyThink
entries.description: Behaviour state 12, search/destroy. Mech_BehaviourPatrolThink's shape and the same leader gate, differing in that what it acquires must pass Group_IsOrderTarget -- the group fights only what its order names.

entries.name: Mech_BehaviourPatrolThink
entries.description: Behaviour state 8, patrolling. Ai_NavigationStep, drop the target, then a gate that returns for any machine that is neither the group leader nor under a standing squad order -- so only the leader ever acquires. Past it, on the 10000-count (about 4.9 s) block-scratch timer at mech+0x5a: a machine out of action takes fleeing, otherwise it acquires (mask 1) only when the group order verb is 3 or the squad verb is 2, and hands the result to Mech_AiEnterCombat.

entries.name: Mech_BehaviourTravelThink
entries.description: Behaviour states 9 and 11, travelling and bulldog travel. Calls Ai_FollowRoute DIRECTLY rather than through Ai_NavigationStep, so every member reads the route and every member can advance the shared cursor. Then drops the target and, on the mech+0x5a timer, acquires into mech+0x5f -- a turret look-at, never written to mech+0x1a4.

entries.name: Mech_BehaviourFollowThink
entries.description: Behaviour state 10, following. Mech_BehaviourTravelThink with the route replaced by Group_OrderTargetObject's position and a 25000-unit stop, that stop being a 3D Math_DistanceBetweenPoints range rather than the ground one every steer uses. Touches no route cursor, while verb 6's completion test is a route test -- so a following order can only complete on a group whose route was empty to begin with.

entries.name: Mech_AiGoalPosition
entries.description: Resolves the point a machine is working to: a squad order's target object or its stored point for verbs 3, 5 and 6, otherwise the mission group's current order target via Group_OrderTargetPosition.

entries.name: Ai_LineOfSightBlocked
entries.description: Line of sight from this machine to its selected target, both endpoints lifted to their aim-node origins or by 500 units when there is no node: 0 clear; 1 blocked by something the machine cannot get past (a shape, via Sim_RaycastShapes, or ground too steep to walk); 2 blocked only by ground it could walk over. The trigger for the skirting state.

entries.name: Mech_AiOnLineOfFireBlocked
entries.description: Mech vtable +0x64. Copies the selected target's position to mech+0x31e and sets mech+0xad, which makes the next combat think enter skirting. Its one caller is the tail of Sim_RaycastObjectList: a shot that stopped nearer than the shooter's target and within 0x2000 of the same bearing. The base and flyer classes leave the slot empty.

entries.name: Mech_BehaviourSkirtThink
entries.description: Behaviour state 14 (skirting). Walks an arc around whatever blocked the line of fire, at a point 90 degrees off the line to the position stashed at mech+0x31e, re-testing Ai_LineOfSightBlocked every 5000 ms and restoring the stashed descriptor from mech+0x5a when it comes back clear. A terrain block (reading 2) gets no arc.

entries.name: Ai_BeginSkirtIfBlocked
entries.description: The gate at the top of every combat think. When mech+0xad is set it stashes the current descriptor at mech+0x5a, installs skirting (descriptor 0x499708), records the 3D range to mech+0x31e at mech+0x67, and returns true so the think does nothing else.

entries.name: Mech_BehaviourDriveOffThink
entries.description: Behaviour state 16 (driving off en). Ai_BeginSkirtIfBlocked, then Mech_BehaviourFaceOffThink verbatim. The states differ only in their descriptors: this one holds a place and reassesses through Mech_AiSelectBehaviour.

entries.name: Ai_SelectDefenceTarget
entries.description: Picks the HERC threatening a defended point: over GlobalMechList, candidates passing Ai_IsTargetable and not crippled, scored (limit - distance to the point) / (holders + 1), where limit is 90000, or 980000 when the group's current order names no object. Preferring live candidates, it returns the best. Used by Mech_AiOnTakingFire for the guarding and driving-off states.

entries.name: Mech_BehaviourGuardThink
entries.description: Behaviour state 15, guarding. A player squadmate with no standing order holds formation instead; everything else works a standoff ring on Mech_AiGoalPosition -- approach past 30000, hold facing OUTWARD (the -0x8000 in the steering term) between 10000 and 30000, walk away below 10000. Targets through Ai_SelectDefenceTarget, installing driving off en (16) or fleeing (18).

entries.name: Mech_BehaviourRamTick
entries.description: The per-tick MOVE slot of one AI behaviour state, NOT a death throe: block 00499b5c's +0x0c, whose think slot Mech_BehaviourRamThink (0041e570) charges the machine's selected target at full throttle and calls this three times a tick once its charge timer fires. Integrates motion, snaps the machine to terrain height + typeRec+0x16, places its legs, and runs Mech_CollisionTest; on a block (or once mech+0xb1 is latched) it detonates Damage_ExplosiveBlastSweep(pos, 3000, 2000, 0, self) and then finishes off every one of its own 29 components with a flat 32000 through vtable +0x74 -- a guaranteed self-destruction, no roll and no falloff. Ghidra's function boundary starts one prologue late at 0041e48e. The mech+0xb1 arm is the 'something ran into me' latch Mech_CollisionTest raises through vtable +0x68 (SimObject_SetRunInto, 0042200c) on whatever blocked it; that byte has exactly one writer and this one reader in the image and is NEVER cleared, so a machine bumped earlier in the mission detonates on its first tick in the state.

entries.name: Mech_BehaviourInertThink
entries.description: Behaviour states 20 (dead) and 21 (disabled). Mech_LocomotionTick(mech, 0, 0, 0) and nothing else.

entries.name: Mech_BehaviourRamThink
entries.description: The think slot (+0x00) of AI behaviour state block 00499b5c, the ramming attack. Acquires a target through Ai_SelectTarget(this, 6, 0) into mech+0x1a4 every 10000 ms (timer at mech+0x5a), maintaining its +0x1a2 refcount, then steers with Mech_LocomotionTick(turn = (bearing - heading) >> 8, throttle 0x100) -- a QUARTER the steer gain every other state uses. A two-phase flag at mech+0x5f over a countdown at mech+0x62, each phase arming the timer it ENTERS: approaching (0) lasts 8000 + rand(4000), charging (1) lasts 3000 + rand(1500). Charging, it calls Mech_BehaviourRamTick TWICE, interleaved with two more steers -- three RamTicks a tick counting the move slot's own. Both fields start zeroed by Behaviour_SetState, so entering the state charges immediately. Always returns 0.

entries.name: Ai_BuildCombatGeometry
entries.description: Fills the 0x18-byte block every combat think passes down: +0x00 bearing to target, +0x02 bearing error, +0x04 its magnitude, +0x06 the target's aspect (bearing back to me in its turret frame), +0x08 its magnitude, +0x0a 3D range, +0x0e approach flag, +0x10/+0x14 the 15000/30000 standoff pair. The states steer on the aspect, and the copy Ai_AimAndFire is handed has one reader, Ai_ChooseWeapon's shield-facing test.

entries.name: Ai_CombatMoveStep
entries.description: The combat states' movement: sets the block's approach flag from the range against the standoff pair -- choosing the sign so the machine opens or closes the range whichever way it is facing -- stashes it at mech+0x5a, and drives Mech_LocomotionTick with the bearing error >> 6 and +/-0x100. The range arms read the magnitude Ai_BuildCombatGeometry left, before the caller's own steering override is folded in.

entries.name: Mech_CenterTorsoTick
entries.description: The [Backspace] 'Center Turret' command, run every tick while g_CenterTurretMode is latched. Drives each torso tick with -clamp(Q10(0xfa, angle), +/-0x100) and snapTarget 0 with the snap enabled, so the turret runs home and stops exactly on centre. Nothing clears the mode on arrival; the input path clears it the moment either turret axis is non-zero.

entries.name: Ai_AimAndFireAtMech
entries.description: Ai_AimAndFire's machine branch. Refuses the shot and centres the turret when the bearing error exceeds the chassis' torso-twist limit (typeRec+0x22: 14000 on 20 of the 21 chassis; PITBULL's 32767 passes every error but 0x7fff and -0x8000). Aims at the chosen component (mech+0x2a2) only when the 3D range is in [5000, 20000); otherwise at the target's aim node origin. Ends in Ai_FireAtPoint.

entries.name: Ai_AimAndFire
entries.description: The aim-and-fire tail every combat think ends on, and which travelling/following call against their look-at object -- so a walking machine shoots at what it watches without selecting it. Switches on the target's class (obj+0x1a8) to pick the aim point: class 0 goes to Ai_AimAndFireAtMech, class 1 to the structure's first live component (vtable +0x54 with a null second argument, then +0x58), anything else to the object's position plus its own aim offset (vtable +0x30). A null third argument means mech+0x1a4.

entries.name: Mech_AiSelectBehaviour
entries.description: Picks and installs the next AI behaviour state. Three mutually exclusive paths: the local player (mech+0xa3) takes 'player fly' or 'player' on the type record's flyer flag typeRec+0x50; a machine in the player's own group with a standing squad order (mech+0x23e) maps verbs 1/2 to 'patrolling', 4 to Mech_AiEngageOrderedTarget against the order target at mech+0x248, and 6 to 'guarding'; anything else reads its mission group's current order (mech+0x45, array at group+0x44 indexed by group+0x6c, verb = the entry's first short) and maps 0-6 to search/destroy, ramming, guarding, patrolling, sleeping, travelling-or-bulldog-travel (split on typeRec+0x22 vs 0x7d01) and following. A null order entry substitutes verb 0x0b, which matches no case. Every path releases mech+0x1a4, decrements the target's +0x1a2 refcount and sets mech+0x9d, so a state change always drops the target.

entries.name: Mech_ComputeCombatRating
entries.description: Writes the combat rating at mech+0x29e and latches the cache flag mech+0x94, which Mech_DirectFireHitTest (00418ba8) clears on a hit and Mech_PerTickSystemsUpdate tests to recompute. Rating = (typeRec+0x44 base + each live weapon mount's value scaled by its condition, for the mounts whose vtable +0x54 answers non-zero -- an ammunition mount only above an eighth of its magazine + each of 19 components' maximum scaled by its condition - a penalty per system over 70% damaged) >> 4, so it falls as the machine is shot apart or runs low.

entries.name: Cockpit_TargetAnglesFromCameraBone
entries.description: Transforms a world point into the pilot eye's frame and returns its azimuth/elevation. The camera part id (typeRec+0x0c) is a shape PART id: the shape find-by-id vtable slot (+0x20) returns the part, its TSBasePart.Transform (+4) is a transform id, and that indexes the per-node transform array at shapeInst+0x16 (0x20 bytes per entry). Composes the inverse of the mech transform (mech+0xc) then the inverse of that node transform, and subtracts typeRec+0x66. The cockpit eye rides the same node, which is where the retail cockpit bob comes from -- no dedicated bob code exists. Chain is uniform across the fleet: part 5 -> transform 11 -> 4 -> 1 for 16 of 18 HERCs, node 1 being the one the walk cycle animates.

entries.name: Ai_ChooseWeapon
entries.description: Scores every mount and returns the best above a floor mapped from mech+0x2aa (fear) through [0,0x400] -> [150,-100]; nothing above the floor means the machine aims and does not shoot. A mount whose vtable +0x5c answers non-zero (destroyed; an ammunition mount also when empty; a pod always) is passed over first. Score is Q10(100, damage credit) - Q10(1000, template+0x34) plus rand(35)*rand(35), where the credit is the armor damage with no shield, the shield damage when the shield holds, and the armor damage + 10000 on the shot that breaks it. Gates launchers on manager+0x0a lock, turns the radar on for an in-range SARH launcher, and latches mech+0xa5 -- no weapons left -- when every mount is absent or spent.

entries.name: Ai_FireAtPoint
entries.description: The AI's fire decision. Reuses the latched mount at mech+0x2ac while it is ready and in range, else spends mech+0xb5 or runs Ai_ChooseWeapon. Aims the turret through Cockpit_TargetAnglesFromCameraBone whether or not anything fires. Leads the point by range*targetSpeed/projectileSpeed along the target's heading, adds the difficulty aim scatter for a Cybrid group only, and fires -- a launcher immediately, a gun only inside 1000 BAM in both axes. Latches ELF and ELF2 back into mech+0x2ac.

entries.name: Mech_AiFriendlyFireComplaint
entries.description: Posts squad message 8 when the player shoots a machine in the player's own group, on a 40000-count (about 19.5 s) cooldown at mech+0x278.

entries.name: Mech_AiOnTakingFire
entries.description: Mech vtable +0x50, called with (attacker, damage) when something hits this machine. Applies no damage. Shares the attacker as a contact through Detection_ShareContact, opens the 30000-count (about 14.6 s) under-fire window at +0x27d, and for a machine in the player's group accumulates the damage at +0x281 and ignores it until the total passes 8000. Otherwise, on a 10000-count (about 4.9 s) retarget cooldown at +0x273, it reacts by the current state's descriptor flag bits: bit 2 (guarding, driving off en) defends the post via Ai_SelectDefenceTarget around Mech_AiGoalPosition (a verb-4 squad order replaces the pick unless the pick is shooting at it; failing both, the attacker), bit 3 (sleeping, ramming, bulldog travel) ignores fire entirely, and anything else re-acquires with Ai_SelectTarget(this, 0x24, 0). Also posts squad message 3, and Mech_AiFriendlyFireComplaint when the player is the shooter.

entries.name: Ai_DriveToPoint
entries.description: The AI's one steering primitive: Mech_LocomotionTick(mech, (Math_HeadingToward(point, mech) - mech.heading) >> 6, speed, 0) with speed = mech+0x252 or 0xaa when that is zero, and a Turbo Pod sprint at 0x100 past 30000 units that only a standing squad order can reach. Returns whether the GROUND-PLANE range is under 10000 -- arrival, which is what Ai_FollowRoute steps the route cursor on.

entries.name: Ai_FollowRoute
entries.description: Drives at the waypoint AFTER the group's route cursor, advancing the cursor through Route_AdvanceCursor when Ai_DriveToPoint reports arrival, and standing still with the throttle at zero when the route has run out. One of four callers of Route_AdvanceCursor, with Mech_BehaviourPlayerThink, Flyer_LeadRouteStep and GroundVehicle_LeaderSteer; all four step the group+0x04 of the group they belong to.

entries.name: Ai_KeepFormation
entries.description: Holds this machine's formation slot on the group leader (group+0x0c slot 0): the post is the leader's position through this machine's vtable +0x78 (Mech_ApplyFormationOffset), so the formation rotates with the leader, and dist is Math_GroundDistanceBetweenPoints to it. Under 2000: turn -((heading - leader heading) >> 6), speed 0. Otherwise, at or under 25000 with the leader's +0x28e outside [-25, 24] (unsigned +0x19 > 0x31): when |heading - leader heading| is under 0x2000 it takes the delta from the post into the leader's frame (the leader's Q14 matrix at +0x12, built from +0x0c when +0x32 is clear, first four shorts through Math_TransposeRotation2D and Math_Rotate2DPoint) and drives turn -((headingError >> 6) + (-lateral >> 5)), speed leader +0x28e + (-longitudinal >> 5); at 0x2000 or more it turns +-0x100 (0x100 when the error is under 1) at speed -0x100. Every other case steers (bearing to the post - heading) >> 6 at dist >> 7, or 0x100 from 25000.

entries.name: MechAi_StaticInitNoOp
entries.description: Static initialiser of the mech AI behaviour module (Borland _INIT_ entry 004a7ad4, priority 0x20): a lone RET. It follows Ai_KeepFormation, the last of that module's Mech_Behaviour*/Ai_* functions, and precedes Mech_LoadResources (mechsys.cpp).

entries.name: Mech_LoadResources
entries.description: mechsys.cpp's resource-load sequence for the mech subsystem -- the mech-side twin of Base_LoadResources (00405fac). Resets the mech-type-slot table (memset &DAT_004a9d8c, 0xff, 0x55), then streams dat\mforms (string 'mforms' at 0049a46b, joined with the shared 'dat' folder-prefix helper ResourcePath_BuildFolderName): reads a 2-byte record count into DAT_004a9dec, allocates that many 28-byte vector elements (Rtl_VectorNew(..., 0x1c, count, ...) -- 7 (x,y) int16 pairs/formation, matching Formation_GetSlotOffset's stride), stores the vector pointer into g_MechFormationTable (g_MechFormationTable), then reads count*28 bytes straight from the file into the buffer. Afterwards loads the 7 mech texture groups (g_MechTextureGroupNames/g_MechTextureGroupSlots) via Resource_Load/BitmapArray_PackToAtlas, unrelated to formations. Auto-analysis does not disassemble it on its own: it sits directly after another function's RET with no call-graph edge, so it is found only by scanning for the 'mforms' string's address as a PUSH-immediate operand. Registered into DBSIM's subsystem-loader table via a thunk at 00420654 (RegisterSubsystemLoader(Mech_LoadResources, 2)), so the game runs it.

entries.name: maybe_MechTypeSlot_GetIndex
entries.description: Trivial accessor, returns (&DAT_004a9d8c)[param_1] -- a per-slot byte, 0xff sentinel meaning 'unused', otherwise the allocated dense index used by MechType_InitOne. Not independently cross-checked beyond its two callers (Mechs_InitAllTypes, MechTypeSlot_Allocate).

entries.name: maybe_MechTypeSlot_Allocate
entries.description: Assigns the next dense allocation index (DAT_004a9d8a, post-incremented) to slot param_1's (&DAT_004a9d8c)[param_1] entry the first time it's requested; on the very first allocation overall, also caches GunLayout_Reserve(1)'s result, the first gun-layout table slot, into _DAT_004a9df4. Not independently cross-checked beyond call-site usage.

entries.name: Shape_RemapTransformId
entries.description: (idRef, map): when the int16 at idRef is non-negative, replaces it with the signed byte map[*idRef] -- which is -1 for an id the map leaves unset. Shape_RemapTransformIds' per-field step.

entries.name: Shape_RemapTransformIds
entries.description: (part, map, nodeCount): rewrites the transform ids in a shape's part tree through a byte map, the remapping counterpart of Shape_StampTransformId with the same class-tag switch on vtable +0 (tags from the GetClassTag bodies). TSGroup (0x140014): Shape_RemapTransformId on part+4 and returns without visiting children. TSCellAnimPart (0x14000b): Shape_RemapTransformId on part+4, then the children. TSBSPPart (0x140015): each int16 of the per-node array at +0x1c (count ushort +0x16) that is above 0, below nodeCount and maps to a non-negative byte is remapped; then the children. TSPartList (0x140007), TSShape (0x140008), TSDetailPart (0x14000c) and ANShape (0x1e0003): the children. Children are the part-pointer array at +0x12, count ushort +0x10, recursed with the same map and count. TSPartBase (0x140005/0x140006) and any other tag: returns. MechType_RemapDetailRootTransforms calls it once per root after the first.

entries.name: MechType_RemapDetailRootTransforms
entries.description: (detailSet, partIds): renumbers every LOD root after the first into root 0's transform numbering. detailSet is the type record's root set at typeRec+0xde (root array +0, root count int16 +0xc); partIds is typeRec+0x30, bytes 46-65 of the mech .DAT. With more than one root: fills a 400-byte stack table (eight 50-byte rows, one per root 1-8) with 0xff; for each part id, up to 50 or the first negative byte, finds the part in root 0 through the root's vtable +0x20 (TSPartList_FindPart) and takes its transform id (part+4, read without a null check), then for each root L >= 1 finds the same part id and, when found, sets row L[that part's transform id] = root 0's transform id. Then Shape_RemapTransformIds(root L, row L, int16 +0x10 of root 0's +0x2a record) for each L >= 1, so a transform id whose row entry is still 0xff becomes -1 at a TSGroup or TSCellAnimPart. MechType_InitOne calls it at 004202b6, right after Shape_LoadAllRoots and the CONNECT_INFO allocation. Retail .DAT lists: 1,2,3,4,5,12-17 on most chassis; HEADHUNT adds 44, MONGOOSE 10,88,99, PITBULL 18-25, SPIDER 1-4,12,14,15,18-23, RAZOR 12; each -1-terminated within the 20 bytes.

entries.name: MechType_InitOne
entries.description: Per-mech-type init, called once per valid slot (0-0x54) by Mechs_InitAllTypes. Opens the per-mech-type resource files (name built from the mech's own code string + several folder-prefix globals), reads a 0xd8-byte fixed record into the MECH_TYPE_DATA[typeIndex] struct (0x21e bytes/entry) at record offset 2, initializes hit-zone/collision/debris sub-resources, and -- the confirmed answer to 'how does DBSIM pick a mech's texture' -- for every mesh sub-component of this mech type, sets TSShapeInstance+0x26 (bound active DBA, see docs/retail/formats/dts-texture-binding.md) to '&g_MechTextureGroupSlots + typeRecord[0x96]*8'. typeRecord+0x96 is MechType_TextureGroupIndex (see that entry); the 0xd8-byte record it lives in is read directly from simvol0/dat/<MECHNAME>.DAT at record offset 2, so record offset 0x96 is file offset 148, the texture-group index.

entries.name: Mechs_InitAllTypes
entries.description: Creates the 'mechs' object pool (string xref confirmed) sized DAT_004a9d8a*0x21e (the MECH_TYPE_DATA record size), then loops mech-type slot 0..0x54 calling MechType_InitOne (004201a8) for every slot MechTypeSlot_GetIndex (0041ff00) reports as in-use (!= 0xff).

entries.name: Mechs_FreeAllTypes
entries.description: Tears down the mech-type table: Rtl_VectorDeleteCounted(004a9de8, 0x29, 0x21e, 0, 0x19, MECH_TYPE_DATA_Dtor) -- the exception-aware wrapper over Rtl_VectorDelete, mode 0x19 taking the count from the array's prefix -- then resets the 0x55-byte slot-index map 004a9d8c to 0xff and the allocated-type count 004a9d8a to 0, the same two resets Mech_LoadResources opens with. No caller found by es2_xref.

entries.name: Formation_GetSlotOffset
entries.description: Returns a static 3-short {x, y, 0} formation offset: table[formationId * 0x1c + slot * 4 - 4] and the short after it. So a formation is 28 bytes = seven (x, y) short pairs, covering follower slots 1-7. The table pointer g_MechFormationTable is written by Mech_LoadResources (0041fdb0), which reads dat\MFORMS.DAT -- 142 content bytes = count + five 28-byte formations, byte-exact.

entries.name: Mech_GetGunLayout
entries.description: GunLayout_GetBySlot(mechTypeRecord[0] + _DAT_004a9df4) -- this machine's hardpoint list. Its return value is what Mech_ConfigureLoadout hands MechLoadout_ConstructWeaponMounts as the record array and count.

entries.name: Mech_RegisterLoader
entries.description: Thunk that registers Mech_LoadResources (0041fdb0) into DBSIM's subsystem-loader table via RegisterSubsystemLoader(Mech_LoadResources, 2), then vector-constructs the mech-texture-group vector, 8 slots of 8 bytes (Rtl_VectorNew(&g_MechTextureGroupSlots, 8, 8, 1, ...)), of which Mech_LoadResources fills 7. Found by raw dword-scanning DBSIM.EXE for Mech_LoadResources' address used as a PUSH-immediate operand (68 B0 FD 41 00).

entries.name: ConfigPart_Ctor
entries.description: (part): CONFIG_PART's constructor: stamps the ClassItem, TSBase, TSPartBase and CONFIG_PART (0049a494) vtables in turn, counting three live destructors, and runs ShapeInstance_CtorCellFrames(part+0x10, 0) on the SHAPE_INST member; returns part. MECH_TYPE_DATA_Ctor runs it over the ten 0x18-byte config parts at typeRec+0xec, the blank records Mech_SpliceHardpointShapes falls back on.

entries.name: ConfigPart_GetClassTagZero
entries.description: CONFIG_PART vtable +0x00 (0049a494), kept by GUN_STATE and every weapon-mount class: returns 0, where TSPartBase answers a real class tag.

entries.name: ConfigPart_Dtor
entries.description: CONFIG_PART vtable +0x18 (0049a494, RTTI 'CONFIG_PART', 0x18 bytes; bases TSPartBase and SHAPE_INST at +0x10), the destructor its class record names: (this, flags). HeapBlockOwner_Dtor(this+0x10, 0) on the SHAPE_INST, TSBase_Dtor(this, 0), then Mem_Delete on flags bit 0.
entries.source: DBSIM decompile at 00420730; class record at 004206c9

entries.name: MechFormation_ElementCtor
entries.description: (formation): Rtl_VectorNew(formation, 4, 7, 1, Rtl_ReturnArgCopy) over its seven 4-byte (x, y) slot offsets, returning formation -- the per-element constructor Mech_LoadResources hands Rtl_VectorNew for the MFORMS.DAT table (PUSH at 0041fe43: 0x1c bytes each, count 004a9dec, stored to g_MechFormationTable).

entries.name: CONNECT_INFO_Ctor
entries.description: (info): CONNECT_INFO's constructor (6-byte class record at 004208e3, destructor CONNECT_INFO_Dtor, which decrements twice): zeroes the slot-array pointer at +0 and counts two live destructors. MechType_InitOne runs it through Rtl_VectorNew(buffer, 6, rootCount, 0x211, it) at 00420286 for the per-root {slots, count} pairs it stores at typeRec+0xe6 and MechType_BindHardpointSlots fills.

entries.name: MECH_TYPE_DATA_Ctor
entries.description: (data): MECH_TYPE_DATA's constructor: Rtl_VectorNew(data+0xec, 0x18, 10, 1, ConfigPart_Ctor), counts one live destructor, returns data. Mechs_InitAllTypes hands it to Rtl_VectorNew (PUSH at 004204f1) for the 0x21e-byte type records, count 004a9d8a, mode 0x211.

entries.name: MECH_TYPE_DATA_Dtor
entries.description: MECH_TYPE_DATA's destructor, the dtor its class record (0x21e bytes, at 00420937) names: (data, flags): when data is not null, decrements *Rtl_DtorCountPtr, Rtl_VectorDelete of the ten 0x18-byte config parts at +0xec with ConfigPart_Dtor, then Mem_Delete when flags bit 0 is set.

entries.name: CONNECT_INFO_Dtor
entries.description: CONNECT_INFO's destructor, the dtor its class record (0x6 bytes, at 004208e3) names: (info, flags): when info is not null, decrements *Rtl_DtorCountPtr twice, Mem_DeleteArray of the buffer at +0 when that is set, then Mem_Delete when flags bit 0 is set.

entries.name: ARRAY_TSPartBase_PtrPtr_Dtor
entries.description: ARRAY<TSPartBase * *>'s destructor, the dtor its class record (0x6 bytes, at 004209e3) names: (array, flags): decrements *Rtl_DtorCountPtr; when the array is not null, Mem_DeleteArray of its buffer at +0 when that is set, then Mem_Delete of the array when flags bit 0 is set.

entries.name: Computer_PostMessage
entries.description: Posts a SYSTEM.STR message id to the cockpit computer's ticker -- the port at CockpitView+0x20b -- through its vtable slot 0, as a {short id, int subject} record with a null subject. The sibling for the pilot and squad channel is Ai_PostSquadMessage (00420a98).

entries.name: Ai_PostSquadMessage
entries.description: Posts {messageId, machine} to the pilot-and-squad message port (the object CockpitView_GetSquadMessagePort returns) through its vtable slot 0, suppressed for a destroyed machine unless the third argument forces it. Ids raised by the AI targeting path: 1 enemy sighted, 3 taking fire, 8 friendly fire.

entries.name: Mech_ReceiveSquadOrder
entries.description: Mech vtable +0x28. One machine receiving one transmitted squad order: switches on the record's verb (STRINGS0 group 0, 0-0x11) over twelve jump-table arms covering sixteen verbs (6, 9 and anything above 0x11 take the default) and installs the standing order at mech+0x23e, its destination at +0x240, its target at +0x248, its guard subject at +0x24c and its abandon tier at +0x250. Verbs 0xd/0xe write patrol and move, 0/2/0xb write engage, 0xc writes guard; 3/0xa/0xf clear the order and reinstall patrolling; 4/0x10 and 7/0x11 are the radar pair, writing mech+0xb2 and mech+0x96; 5 and 8 are the FIRE AT WILL / HOLD YOUR FIRE pair, writing mech+0xb6; 1 sets the ignore-the-player's-selection latch at mech+0x9a, which 0, 5 and 0xb clear. Returns 1 when the order was taken. Each case picks a reply id for Ai_PostSquadMessage, posted only when priorReply is 0, or 1 with an accepted order. Args derived from disassembly: [EBP+8], [EBP+0xc], [EBP+0x10]; the vtable call site at 0043164d pushes three and does ADD ESP,0xc.

entries.name: Flyer_GetSpeed
entries.description: Flyer vtable +0x38: Q10(1000, flyer+0x233), where +0x233 is the type record's +0x04 forward speed, copied in by Flyer_Constructor and never written again. A chassis constant, not anything the aircraft is doing.

entries.name: Flyer_FlushDeletes
entries.description: ObjectPool_FlushDeleteQueue(g_FlyerDeleteQueue (004a9e41), g_FlyerPool (004a9e3d)). Flyer_RegisterSubsystem registers it as the flyer module's subsystem phase-5 stub (PUSH 0x4215a8 at 00421fc2). It lies outside every Ghidra function.

entries.name: Flyer_HandleCommandNoOp
entries.description: FLYER vtable +0x2c: loads its second argument into AX, then XOR EAX,EAX and returns 0 without acting on it -- which is why the shield bracket keys do nothing in a RAZOR.

entries.name: Flyer_Draw
entries.description: Flyer vtable +0x00. Sets the shared draw-state global from DAT_004a9e48, calls Shape_DrawAtDetailLevel, clears it again.

entries.name: Flyer_Constructor
entries.description: Flyer class constructor (flyer, FLYERS.NAM index). SimObjectBase_ConstructStatic with the type record's +0x36, then the block every ACTOR constructor writes: SimObjectBaseVtable, +0x1a8 = 0xffff, +0x98 = 1, +0xa7 = 1, ObjectList_Add, +0x1b2 and +0x1b6 = 0, +0x1ba, +0x1bc and +0x1be = 0xffff. Installs FlyerVtable (0049a5e0) and allocates the component-damage header at flyer+0x200 with literal counts of 1 and 1 (one main component, one dependent -- exactly what SKIMMER.DMG ships). Stores the type record at flyer+0x1fa, sets +0x1a8 = 2, zeroes +0x231 and +0x235, copies the record's +0x04 into +0x233, and links the record's .DMG and .COL pointers (+0x2e, +0x32) via Component_LinkMaxRefData. Installs the deciding state, Behaviour_SetState(flyer+0x4d, 00499cf8). Seeds the flight block at +0x243: zeroes its 0x4e bytes, points +0x263 at the euler angles (+0x0c), builds the object's rotation matrix if +0x32 is clear, copies it to +0x267 and transposes it, rotates the negated position through it into +0x27b, and sets +0x247 = 1000 (airspeed) and +0x261 = 0x200 (throttle). Steps the RTL constructor counter at [006cbf74] twice. The stores it makes are the ones listed; its own body writes none of +0x1f4, +0x1f8, +0x21c or +0x23c.

entries.name: Flyer_DispatchMove
entries.description: Flyer vtable +0x14. Calls the installed behaviour descriptor's +0x24 move triple (the descriptor pointer is at flyer+0x4d). The flyer twin of the mech dispatchers; Mech_AiTick (00411cec) is what reaches it.

entries.name: Flyer_DispatchThink
entries.description: Flyer vtable +0x18. Calls the installed behaviour descriptor's +0x18 think triple.

entries.name: Flyer_DispatchReassess
entries.description: Flyer vtable +0x1c. Calls the installed behaviour descriptor's +0x30 reassess triple, which for every flyer state is Flyer_AiSelectBehaviour (00422d00).

entries.name: Flyer_MovementTick
entries.description: The flyer's per-tick move, the +0x24 slot of the four behaviour states that have one. Adds the world velocity at flyer+0x24f to the position RAW -- three plain ADDs at 0042190a, with no Math_IntegrateRateOverTick, so a flyer's world velocity is a per-tick step where Razor_MovementTick's is a rate. Then four terrain probes (two wingtips at (+/-1000,-420,-300) that roll the airframe away, a nose point at (0,1000,0) and a look-ahead at (0,15000,-1500) that pitch it up), a clamp of the origin to terrain+500, and the flyby loop (sound 0x31) started or released at 30000 units from the view object. No damage, no object sweep, and no gate on being wrecked.

entries.name: Flyer_ComponentDamageWrite
entries.description: Flyer vtable +0x74. Thin wrapper over Component_ApplyDamageAndCascade on the header at flyer+0x200: destroying component 0 loses the aircraft -- sets flyer+0x99, credits the kill through the attacker's +0x60, fires the mission action at flyer+0x1b6, and writes -100000 to flyer+0x2e so it falls.

entries.name: Flyer_DirectFireHitTest
entries.description: Flyer vtable +0x20. Coarse reject on SimObject_GetShapeRadius (shape+8), then Mech_SelectStruckComponent against the type's col/<NAME>.COL model (flyerTypeRec+0x32) with the per-component alive flags at obj+0x208. Damage through vtable +0x74; spawns the shot's armour impact effect, or a fixed effect id 10 once the flyer is destroyed. No shields and no collision volume -- the simplest of the three hit tests.

entries.name: Flyer_GetOverallDamage
entries.description: Flyer vtable +0x40: Component_ReadOverallDamage on the health header at flyer+0x200.

entries.name: Flyer_ApplyFormationOffset
entries.description: Flyer vtable +0x78. No-ops for member index 0 (the flight leader); otherwise reads the three-int16 station offset FlyerFormation_GetSlotOffset (00423044) resolves out of dat/FFORMS.DAT and hands it to Formation_RotateAndAddOffset (00411d64), which rotates it by the GROUP LEADER's heading and adds it to the caller's point. Unlike a mech's or a base's, the offset carries a Z, which is what stacks a flight vertically.

entries.name: Flyer_AttachToGroup
entries.description: Attaches a flyer to its mission group: stores the group at flyer+0x45 and the member index at +0x49; with flyer+0x0c holding the -0x8000 sentinel takes the group's heading and zeroes pitch and roll; with the Z position holding the sentinel takes the group's own point (the one group+0x18 points at, else Route_WaypointAt on the group's route at its cursor, group+4), applies the formation offset through vtable +0x78, and finally substitutes 5000 for a Z that came out zero.

entries.name: Flyer_RegisterSubsystem
entries.description: Static-init registrar of the flyer module (Borland _INIT_ entry 004a7ae0, priority 0x20): registers Flyer_FlushDeletes at subsystem phase 5, nulls g_FlyerPool (004a9e3d) and counts one live destructor. Flyer_StaticDtor is its _EXIT_ counterpart.

entries.name: Flyer_StaticDtor
entries.description: Flyer_RegisterSubsystem's _EXIT_ routine (Borland _EXIT_ entry 004a7c18): decrements *Rtl_DtorCountPtr and Mem_Deletes g_FlyerPool when it is set.

entries.name: SimObject_SetRunInto
entries.description: Vtable +0x68 in ALL EIGHT SimObject-shaped tables -- base, mech, flyer and the five structure classes -- with no override anywhere. Two instructions: obj+0xb1 = 1, "something ran into me". TWO call sites through the slot, both collision sweeps calling it on whatever object blocked the move, whatever class that object is: Mech_CollisionTest (0041903a) and GroundVehicle_CollisionTest (0046a581), the sweep inside StructureGroundVehicleVtable's +0x18 tick slot GroundVehicle_ThinkTick. Mech_BehaviourRamTick is the byte's only reader, and NOTHING clears it. Both the write and the read rebase (ADD reg, 0x92) and use displacement 0x1f, so a scalar search for 0xb1 finds neither -- search byte ptr [reg + 0x1f] instead.

entries.name: ObjPool_FLYER_Dtor
entries.description: ObjPool<FLYER>'s destructor, the dtor its class record (0x8 bytes, at 0042201d) names: (pool, flags): decrements *Rtl_DtorCountPtr; when the pool is not null, Mem_Delete of its entry buffer at +0 when that is set, then Mem_Delete of the pool when flags bit 0 is set.

entries.name: Flyer_PitchCommand
entries.description: Elevator command that holds a pitch attitude: Q16(desiredPitch - flyer.pitch, 1500), resolved through cos(roll) at Q14, less Q16(pitchRate, 8000).

entries.name: Flyer_PitchToAltitude
entries.description: Elevator command that flies the aircraft to a world Z: Math_Atan2Guarded(10000, targetZ - flyer.z) into Flyer_PitchCommand. The 10000 is a fixed horizontal run, so the demanded angle depends on the height error alone. When the base object's +0xae is set it asks instead for the current pitch (+0x0c) plus Math_Q8Multiply(flyer+0x23c, 4000), ignoring the target Z. +0xae is a walking machine's unstick-reverse flag; es2_fieldscan finds it written only by Mech_LocomotionTick and Mech_MovementTick. flyer+0x23c is a Flyer field (a mech's +0x23c is a different field of another class); es2_fieldscan and a raw disp32 sweep of the code section find this read and no write of it in flyer code.

entries.name: Flyer_CommandRoll
entries.description: Fills the command array's aileron element with Q16(desiredRoll - flyer.roll, 2500) + Q16(rollRate, -5000) and runs Flyer_ApplyFlightCommand. The arm Flyer_SteerAndFly takes whenever it is holding or limiting a bank rather than commanding one.

entries.name: Flyer_ApplyFlightCommand
entries.description: Hand-off into FlightModel_Step (00466a54). Squares the aileron and elevator elements with their sign kept ((v*v)>>8) and clamps them to +/-0x100, then calls the model with the flyer's flight block at +0x243, the .FM record at typeRecord+0x3a, and a stack array of four zeros as the wing-damage argument, which is why a Flyer never takes the model's lost-wing or lost-nacelle arms.

entries.name: Flyer_FormationThrottle
entries.description: Works a throttle figure out of the station error, the bearing to the leader and the two chassis' +0x233 speeds, folds it into the previous value of flyer+0x21c and clamps the sum to [0x8c,0x100]. es2_fieldscan and a raw disp32 sweep of the code section find no reader of flyer+0x21c in flyer code but this one, and its one caller found by es2_xref, Flyer_FormationStep, discards the return value. The control law leaves FlightModel_Step's throttle element zero on every call, so nothing a Cybrid flyer decides changes its airspeed (the player's RAZOR THROTTLE binding can: FlightModel_Step's position branch then writes the setting to 0).

entries.name: Flyer_SteerAndFly
entries.description: The flyer's steering channel and the function every movement step (route step, station keeping, attack run) ends in. Builds a 16-bit bank command from Q16(-turn,2500) + Q16(bankTurnRate at flyer+0x287, 32000) + Q16(rollRate,-5000); holds the aircraft at +/-(typeRecord+0x0e, the maximum bank angle) with a 1500 hysteresis band when the bank would take it further over; answers a steering command under 2000 with rudder (Q16(-turn,4000)) and level wings instead of a bank, and only if the roll is already under 800. Fills the command array's fifth element with the terrain height under the aircraft, which is FlightModel_Step's ceiling reference. When it is handed a leader it adds a term of Math_Q14Multiply(leader+0x1f8, cos(own heading - leader heading)); no writer of +0x1f8 was found by es2_fieldscan, a decompile grep or a raw disp32 sweep of the code section, and the flyer pool is zero-filled.

entries.name: Flyer_LeadRouteStep
entries.description: The flight leader's route step. Takes the waypoint one past the group's cursor, advances the cursor when it is within 15000 ground units, else falls back to the cursor's own waypoint; holds altitude 30000 through Flyer_PitchToAltitude and steers with Q16(bearingError, 28000) through Flyer_SteerAndFly.

entries.name: Flyer_FormationStep
entries.description: A wingman's station-keeping. The station is the leader's position offset 0x2000 along the leader's heading plus this aircraft's FFORMS.DAT slot; a wingman that is ahead of its station while still aligned with the leader and inside 10000 units has its steering command mirrored (-0x8000 - err) rather than reversed. Ends in Flyer_SteerAndFly and then Flyer_FormationThrottle.

entries.name: Flyer_AttackRun
entries.description: The attack run, and the only place a Cybrid flyer shoots. A two-phase circuit on flyer+0x1fe: phase 0 extends AWAY from the target holding targetZ+10000 until the range passes 90000, phase 1 runs in and inside 65000 aims at the target itself, breaking off again when the bearing leaves +/-0x2000, the height over the target drops under 3000, or the range closes inside 10000. The aim is led along the target's heading by (range>>3)*(targetSpeed*8)/shotSpeed, where shotSpeed becomes PROJ.DAT row 2's speed once the run is close enough to shoot. While running in, a set base-object +0xae swaps the pitch onto the target for Flyer_PitchToAltitude(0). Firing needs phase 1 inside 65000, bearing error and pitch error (elevation to the aim point less flyer+0x0c) both in [-1000, 999], the short at flyer+0x1f4 in [-10, 9] -- the same (ushort)(x + k) < 2k test as the two angle errors -- and the flyer+0x21e countdown expired: while the flyer+0x5a flag is clear and the range is inside 30000 the shot is Rocket_Fire(0) off the (500,200,-100) muzzle and sets the flag, otherwise it is a pair of Bullet_Fire(2) off that point and its mirror; either reloads the countdown with 1500. Every call ends by reloading flyer+0x21c with 0xb4 and handing the bearing error to Flyer_SteerAndFly.

entries.name: Flyer_ClearFormationThrottle
entries.description: Takes one argument, the flyer, zeroes its +0x21c (the accumulator Flyer_FormationThrottle folds into) and returns 0: the shape of a behaviour think that reports not finished. es2_xref finds no rel32 branch, stored pointer or vtable slot holding its address; the same sweep finds the sibling think Flyer_BehaviourScoutThink through its slot block at 00499f50. Its PUSH EBP follows Flyer_AttackRun's RET and two NOP fill bytes, so its entry is not late.

entries.name: Flyer_FollowStep
entries.description: The movement step the three non-combat flyer thinks all open with: Flyer_LeadRouteStep for the group's first member, Flyer_FormationStep for everybody else, then flyer+0x96 (the radar mode) zeroed.

entries.name: Flyer_BehaviourSearchDestroyThink
entries.description: search and destroy's think. Flyer_FollowStep, then for the flight leader only and when the flyer+0x5b countdown reads 0. The sweep reloads it with 10000, but Behaviour_SetState zeroes +0x5a..+0x81 at every reassess, so in practice the sweep runs on the state's first tick and after each 5000-count dwell: Ai_SelectTarget with mask 0x11 (mission target only, reject own class), checked against Group_IsOrderTarget before it is taken, then Flyer_EngageWithFlight.

entries.name: Flyer_BehaviourPatrolThink
entries.description: patrolling's think. The same shape as Flyer_BehaviourSearchDestroyThink with mask 0x10 and no order-target check, so a flight on patrol takes anything it can see that is not another aircraft.

entries.name: Flyer_BehaviourScoutThink
entries.description: scouting's think: Flyer_FollowStep and nothing else.

entries.name: Flyer_EngageWithFlight
entries.description: Puts the whole flight onto the leader's target: installs the attacking descriptor (00499d34) on itself, then for the group's first member only hands every surviving member the same target (obj+0x1a4, with the +0x1a2 counters and the +0x9d changed flag) and recurses into it. The recursion terminates because only the leader takes the loop.

entries.name: Flyer_BehaviourAttackThink
entries.description: attacking's think. Returns finished as soon as the target is immobilised (+0xa4) or destroyed (+0x99), which zeroes the dwell and sends the aircraft back through the reassess; otherwise Flyer_AttackRun for the flight leader and Flyer_FormationStep for everyone else.

entries.name: Flyer_AiSelectBehaviour
entries.description: The reassess slot of the five flyer states that have one (sleeping and dead carry a null triple): maps the group's current order verb onto a descriptor. 0 -> search and destroy (00499dac), 3 -> patrolling (00499d70), 4 -> sleeping (00499de8), 5 -> scouting (00499e24); 4 and 5 also latch flyer+0xa5, the out-of-the-fight byte. Verbs 1, 2 and 6 and an empty order slot match no case and leave ECX unwritten, so Behaviour_SetState is handed ECX as Flyer_DispatchReassess left it: the OR of the reassess triple, which is 00422d00, this function's own address.

entries.name: Flyer_LoadResources
entries.description: The flyer subsystem's loader (flyersys.cpp). Resets the 0x22-entry type-slot table at 004a9e50 to 0xff, then opens dat/fforms, reads a 2-byte record count into DAT_004a9e7c and count*0x12 bytes of formation records into the vector at DAT_004a9e80.

entries.name: FlyerType_RecordIndex
entries.description: Maps a FLYERS.NAM index to its slot in the loaded type-record array, out of the 0x22-entry table at DAT_004a9e50. 0xff means the type is not loaded.

entries.name: FlyerType_Register
entries.description: Claims a type-record slot for a FLYERS.NAM index the mission needs, if it has none yet, bumping the loaded-type count at DAT_004a9e4e.

entries.name: FlyerType_LoadResources
entries.description: Per-flyer-type resource load into a 0x70-byte type record: the dat/<NAME>.DAT stats over the record's first 0x2e bytes, the shape, the .dmg component file (+0x2e), the col/<NAME>.COL hit-sphere model via Collision_RegisterObject (+0x32, which is what the flyer's own vtable +0x20 Flyer_DirectFireHitTest passes to Mech_SelectStruckComponent), and the fm/<NAME>.FM flight model (+0x3a, 0x36 bytes) whose ceiling slope it derives into +0x48. It also binds the shape's texture bank by writing the LITERAL slot address 0x004a9e0e into TSShapeInstance+0x26 -- g_MechTextureGroupSlots + 3*8, texture group 3 (ENEMY) -- so every flyer type shares one bank rather than choosing per chassis the way MechType_InitOne does.

entries.name: FlyerTypes_LoadAll
entries.description: When the flyer type count 004a9e4e is non-zero: 004a9e74 = LoadNameList('flyers', 0x22), 004a9e78 = Rtl_VectorNew of that many 0x70-byte records (element ctor 00423098), then FlyerType_LoadResources for each of the 0x22 name indices whose FlyerType_RecordIndex is not 0xff. DBSim_LoadScriptDat calls it.

entries.name: FlyerFormation_GetSlotOffset
entries.description: dat/FFORMS.DAT slot lookup: DAT_004a9e80 + formationId*0x12 + slot*6 - 6. Three follower slots per formation, three int16 each (x, y, z), and the slot index is one-based: the flight leader takes no offset.

entries.name: FlyerSys_RegisterSubsystem
entries.description: Static-init registrar of flyersys.cpp (Borland _INIT_ entry 004a7ae6, priority 0x20): its whole body is RegisterSubsystemLoader(Flyer_LoadResources, 2).

entries.name: FlyerFormation_ElementCtor
entries.description: (formation): Rtl_VectorNew(formation, 6, 3, 1, maybe_Point3S_Ctor) over its three 6-byte (x, y, z) slot offsets, returning formation -- the per-element constructor Flyer_LoadResources hands Rtl_VectorNew for the FFORMS.DAT records (0x12 bytes each; PUSH at 00422e21).

entries.name: FlyerType_ElementCtor
entries.description: (record): returns its argument -- the per-element constructor FlyerTypes_LoadAll hands Rtl_VectorNew for the 0x70-byte flyer type records (PUSH at 00422fdd, count 004a9e4e); the LEA of +0x3a is an inlined empty member constructor.

entries.name: ActionTimer_Tick
entries.description: One script.dat block-6 action timer per frame -- the second of the four ways a mission action activates. Counts the millisecond countdown at timer+0x2c down through Timer_CountDown, but only while the primary action at timer+0x00 has activated or the record names none (in which case it runs from mission start). On expiry it calls Action_Activate on each of the ten resolved action pointers at timer+0x04..+0x28 and re-arms the countdown with 30000, which through the <<11 in ActionTimer_SetDelay is about seventeen hours -- so a timer effectively activates once. This is why an action carrying no trigger area of its own is ordinary rather than dead.

entries.name: DBSim_BuildActionTimerRecord
entries.description: Small helper called once per row11 (action timer) record inside DBSim_LoadScriptDat: builds a resolved in-memory action timer from a primary-action ref + the delay short + a 10-slot ref array, all already resolved to row10-array pointers by the caller.

entries.name: Route_AdvanceCursor
entries.description: (cursor): steps a route cursor -- a {short index; waypoint-group ptr} pair such as a group's at group+0x04 -- by one, and wraps the index back to zero when the route closes on itself (more than one waypoint, the new index is the last, and the last waypoint's point pointer is the same object as the first's). It writes the index only; the waypoint-group pointer at cursor+0x02 is read. A closed route is a patrol that never ends.

entries.name: Route_NextWaypointClosesRoute
entries.description: Answers 1 when the waypoint after a route cursor is both the route's last and the same point object as its first -- the duplicate a closed patrol circuit ends on, and the one Route_AdvanceCursor would wrap straight off. Only Mech_BehaviourPlayerThink asks; it is what stops a circuit announcing its start point over and over.

entries.name: Squad_BroadcastOrder
entries.description: The MFD FLASH COMM page's transmit: sends one order to the whole of the player's group, best-suited machine first. Each pass scores every member not yet told -- verbs 0/2/5 prefer a machine whose behaviour descriptor +0x09 (committed) is clear, 1/8/0xf one where it is set, 4 and 7 one not already in the radar mode being asked for -- keeps the highest score and breaks ties on range to the issuer, then calls that machine's vtable +0x28 with the reply so far, so only the first recipient or the first to accept says anything. Verbs 0 and 2 stop at the first acceptance; the rest go round until everyone has been told. The score local is not initialised, so for a verb with no case every member carries the same leftover stack value ([EBP-0x1c]): range order when it is -1 or more, nobody told when it is below. Args derived from disassembly: [EBP+8], [EBP+0xc].

entries.name: TriggerArea_Resolve
entries.description: Load-time resolve of one script.dat block-4 (row #9) record into the 10-byte trigger-area record TriggerArea_ContainsPoint reads: type flag at +0, pointer to block-1 coordinate RefA at +2, and at +6 either a pointer to coordinate RefB (type 0) or the record's literal times 10 (other types).

entries.name: TriggerArea_ContainsPoint
entries.description: Tests a position against one resolved block-4 trigger area. Type flag 0: axis-aligned XY box strictly between the two block-1 coordinates the record points at, Z ignored. Non-zero type flag: distance from the single coordinate less than the stored radius (the file literal times 10).

entries.name: Action_Activate
entries.description: Activates one block-5 mission action, once: sets the action runtime activation flag at +0x0a (zeroed at load), then walks ten (counter ref, operation) pairs at +0x0c/+0x20, skipping a pair whose ref is negative and otherwise bumping (op 6) or clearing (op 5) the mission counter array DAT_004a9ef4. The queue of the mission message at +0x34 is INSIDE that loop, so an action naming five counters posts its line five times and one naming none posts it not at all.

entries.name: Action_TestTrigger
entries.description: Tests a position against one action's trigger areas. Returns 1 immediately if the action has already activated (+0x0a set); otherwise offers the position to each resolved block-4 area (count at +0x04, pointer array at +0x06) via TriggerArea_ContainsPoint and calls Action_Activate on the first hit.

entries.name: Action_TestTriggerForGroup
entries.description: Action_TestTrigger applied to every member of a group in turn (member array at group+0x0c, count at group+0x10), stopping at the first that activates it.

entries.name: Deployment_PickPointNearPlayer
entries.description: Picks a clear arrival point for a deploying group or drop pod: offsets from the player position by distance at (player heading + bearing), then steps outward in 2000-unit increments until the point clears three tests in order. (1) Already-deployed objects, within their own vtable +0x7c collision radius plus 5000 -- APPLIED ONLY WHEN avoidDeployedObjects IS NONZERO, which Group_DeploymentCheck passes for the two walk-on verbs and clears for a drop pod, so a pod may come down on top of a machine. (2) Structure_GatherWalkCandidates collision volumes at radius 5000. (3) Terrain_FaceBlocksAt with a zero direction, which reduces to the steepness of the face under the point. The loop is unbounded.
entries.signature: void __cdecl Deployment_PickPointNearPlayer(int *outPoint, int distance, short bearing, int avoidDeployedObjects)

entries.name: Group_DeploymentCheck
entries.description: Per-frame arrival check for a mission group that has not entered the world yet, run by Sim_MainTick for exactly the groups whose record +0x14 action pointer is non-null. No-ops until that action runtime activation flag (action+0x0a) is set. Then the action verb (action+0x02) picks the arrival: 2 or 3 spawn a METEOR drop pod 150000 units from the player (bearing +-90 deg for 2, +-22.5 deg for 3) carrying the group, leaving +0x14 set for the pod to clear on landing and latching group+0x13 so only one pod is ever launched; 4 or 5 place the group leader at 90000 units behind (4) or 150000 ahead (5) facing bearing-0x8000, run every other member through vtable +0x78 for its formation offset, and clear +0x14; any other verb just clears +0x14 so the group goes live where it stands. All arrival points come from Deployment_PickPointNearPlayer.

entries.name: Group_OrderTargetObject
entries.description: The object the group's current order names -- the first member of the group it holds (+0xc == 0), or the object directly (1-3).

entries.name: Group_OrderTargetPosition
entries.description: The position the group's current order works to: the order object's +0x26 origin, falling back to the first waypoint of the group's route (**(*(group+6)+2)), read with no null check, when the slot is empty or names no subject.

entries.name: Group_IsOrderTarget
entries.description: Whether an object is what the group's current order names: for the order's +0xc == 0 the order holds a group and the test is group identity, for 1-3 it holds the object itself.

entries.name: Group_OrderSubjectPtr
entries.description: (group): the current order's +0x0e subject pointer -- the row-15 link at group+0x44 indexed by group+0x6c -- read without testing the slot for null. es2_xref finds no rel32 branch or stored pointer to it.

entries.name: Group_NearestLiveMember
entries.description: (group, obj): the member of group (array +0xc, count +0x10) nearest obj by Math_DistanceBetweenPoints, skipping obj itself and any member with destroyed (+0x99) or immobilised (+0xa4) set; 0 when none is nearer than 100000.

entries.name: Group_IsOrderComplete
entries.description: Whether a mission group's current order is finished, switched on the order's verb (order+0x00). Verb 0: the order subject's condition tier is 4 (destroyed). Verb 2: the order names a subject and either its tier is 4 or Group_NoRivalOrderOnSubject reports nothing hostile still assigned to it. Verbs 3, 5 and 6: the group's route cursor has no waypoint after the current index. Verbs 1 and 4 never complete and can only be ended by the order's action firing.

entries.name: Group_OrderTick
entries.description: Per-frame tick for a group that has entered the mission (the branch Sim_MainTick takes when group+0x14 is null). Runs the group's current order -- the row-15 link at group+0x44 indexed by the current-order index at group+0x6c -- and advances to the next when Group_IsOrderComplete reports it complete or its own action has activated, flagging the finished order in the byte array at group+0x70 and clearing each member's +0x52. Then ticks every member via Mech_AiTick.

entries.name: Route_WaypointAt
entries.description: Reads one waypoint out of a route cursor: null when the cursor has no waypoint group or the index is past its count, otherwise the resolved block-1 point at that index. Every 'is there a waypoint after this one' test in the AI is a call to this with index+1.

entries.name: DBSim_BuildGroupRecord
entries.description: Builds one script.dat block-11 record into a 0x7a-byte in-memory group record: discriminator (record +0x28) at group+0, formation id (+0x2a) at group+2, heading value at group+10, the resolved block-1 coordinate pointer at group+0x18, the resolved row-10 action pointer at group+0x14, and an allocated array of member object pointers at group+0xc. Then attaches every populated member by discriminator -- Mech_AttachToGroup (0/mechs), Flyer_AttachToGroup (1/flyers), Base_AttachToGroup (2/bases) -- passing each its slot index within the group.

entries.name: MissionGroups_Allocate
entries.description: (array, count): array+4 = int16 count; array+0 = Rtl_VectorNew(0, 0x7a, count, 1, 004240e4), count 0x7a-byte group records. DBSim_LoadScriptDat calls it on MissionGroups (004a9e84) with block 11's record count.

entries.name: Group_WriteStatusBlocks
entries.description: (group, stream) Per member in group order: Mech_ReadDamageReadouts into a 42-short buffer, then entries 1-13, 20-29 and 32-41 each written as ((0x100 - r) * 100) SAR 8, then the 6 bytes at mech+0x2a4 -- the member's Herc, Structure and Flyer kill tallies. 72 bytes a member; VSHELL reads the 66 over the machine's status block and the 6 as the pilot's mission counters.

entries.name: Mission_TotalSalvage
entries.description: Sums Mech_SalvageValue over every object on the other side from the player's that is destroyed (+0x99) or immobilised (+0xa4). Called once as the mission writes its results; the total is scaled by Q10(2500) into the campaign salvage pool.

entries.name: Group_ApplyOutnumberedDamage
entries.description: (group): Mech_ApplyOutnumberedDamage on each member of the group's member array (+0xc, int16 count +0x10). Sim_MainTick runs it on the player's group (player+0x45) when Mission_PollStatus answers 3, and raises status 18 instead when the player is destroyed (+0x99) afterwards.

entries.name: Group_ReportIfAllOutOfAction
entries.description: Walks a mission group's member list (group+0xc, count group+0x10) skipping one nominated member; if every other member is immobilised (+0xa4) or destroyed (+0x99) it runs the group's own 10 mission-variable slots (indices at group+0x1c, opcodes at group+0x30) against DAT_004a9ef4 with the opcode set Mech_ReportOutOfAction uses. It does NOT remove the member from the group: a dead machine stays in the roster and keeps being ticked, which is why the inert behaviour states exist. Resolves ai-goals.md's open question on group +0x1c and +0x30.

entries.name: Meteor_Dtor
entries.description: METEOR vtable +0x08 (004982b8), the destructor its class record names: (this, flags). Debris_Dtor's body: installs TSObjVtable, deletes the shape instance at +0x34 through its own vtable +0x18 with flags 3, and Mem_Deletes this on flags bit 0.
entries.source: DBSIM disassembly at 00424034; class record at 00423fe4

entries.name: MissionGroup_ElementCtor
entries.description: Rtl_VectorNew's per-element constructor for MissionGroups_Allocate's 0x7a-byte group records (its only reference is that PUSH at 00423d4b): zeroes the route cursor's index word at group+0x04 and nothing else.

entries.name: Sim_DamageToPlayerDisabled
entries.description: Two-global predicate gating the very first line of Mech_ComponentDamageWrite for the locally piloted machine: if MissionModeFlag is zero the answer is PlayerInvulnerableFlag == 1, otherwise MissionDifficulty == 0. Reads as an invulnerability or practice setting; neither global's writer was traced.

entries.name: Mission_WriteResults
entries.description: (player) Writes data\results.dat -- int16 (Mission_EvaluateObjectives(player) == 9), int32 Q10(2500, Mission_TotalSalvage) + counter 20 * 25000, int16 count and that many {int16 weapon, int16 condition} salvage pairs from DAT_004a9ef0, then Group_WriteStatusBlocks over the player's group -- and then the 2000 bytes of mission counters DAT_004a9ef4 back over data\mission.var. Sim_Shutdown is its one caller.

entries.name: DBSim_LoadScriptDat
entries.description: Pass 1 of DBSIM's two reads of the mission handoff. Opens data\mission.var (0049a9cb), data\player.mec (0049a9f2), data\mission.str (0049aa17) and data\script (0049aa28, extension appended) in that order; a failed open of the first, second or fourth raises a severity-5 Assert_Report (WORLD.CPP lines 0xa5, 0xb2, 0xdc). mission.var: 2000 bytes into the counter array DAT_004a9ef4, then slots 10, 20 and 21-42 zeroed. player.mec: the player's entry index into DAT_004aaae8, the entry count into DAT_004aaae2, then each entry into a 0x7e-byte record at DAT_004aaae4 (pilot +0, type +4, fit +8, ammunition +0x20, the three condition spans after); PilotingRazor is set when entry 0's type is 8. mission.str: StringTable_LoadGroup of up to 0x32 lines into g_MissionStringLines, a trailing newline stripped from each. script.dat: the 20-byte header into ScriptDatHeader (004a9ed2), MissionModeFlag zeroed, World_LoadTheater(&header); block 1 coordinates into DAT_004a9e90 with their XY extent accumulated into Mission_Box; block 2 headings times 0xb6 into DAT_004a9e94; block 3 waypoint groups into 6-byte records at DAT_004a9e9c, refs resolved to block-1 pointers; block 4 areas through TriggerArea_Resolve into DAT_004a9ea4; block 5 actions into 0x3a-byte records at DAT_004a9eac (type, verb, the area count up to the first negative ref and their pointers, counter refs and operations, message minus 1, target; the five text refs read and dropped; activation flag zeroed); block 6 timers through DBSim_BuildActionTimerRecord; blocks 7, 8 and 9 keep just each record's type (+0x28, +0x2c, +0x00); block 10 read and dropped; each block-11 record past the first marks the slots its 20 member refs name live in the mech, flyer or base flag array (004aa7ae, 004aa8da, 004aa93e and 004aaa56) by its discriminator 0, 1 or 2, and record 0 is kept on the stack; block 12 read and dropped; block 13's count and refs into DAT_004a9ec8 / DAT_004a9ecc. Then the slot-to-pool maps: live flyer and base slots numbered in slot order into DAT_004aa90c / DAT_004aa9ca; live mech slots numbered in slot order into DAT_004aa812, then the slot record 0 names at member position k mapped to (live mech count + k), then each player.mec entry k marked live at slot (block-7 count + k) and mapped to (live mech count + k). Registers each live type (maybe_MechTypeSlot_Allocate, FlyerType_Register, BaseType_LoadShape), sizes GlobalMechList (0x36a-byte elements), the flyer pool g_FlyerPool (0x291), Structure_InitPool and the live object list to the live counts, allocates the gun-layout, damage and collision tables, loads every mech and flyer type, calls Terrain_LoadZone(header+2) and copies the training mission number into TrainingMissionNumber. See docs/retail/formats/script-dat.md.

entries.name: Sim_ShutdownNoOp2
entries.description: Empty body. Sim_Shutdown's last call.

entries.name: Mission_ResolveRefByKind
entries.description: Resolves a script.dat ref to a runtime pointer by kind: 0 gives the mission group record at MissionGroups + ref*0x7a; 1, 2 and 3 give Pool_Nth of the mech, flyer or structure pool at the index the slot-to-pool map (DAT_004aa812, DAT_004aa90c, DAT_004aa9ca, signed bytes) holds for that roster slot; any other kind gives 0. The ref is used as an index without a range test. DBSim_LoadScriptDat's mech map sends the slots block 11 record 0 names to the player's squad. DBSim_SpawnMissionObjects, read this session, calls it for each order's subject, each objective's subject and each type 7-10 action's target.

entries.name: DBSim_SpawnMissionObjects
entries.description: Pass 2 of DBSIM's two reads of the handoff, and the pass that builds the mission's objects. Re-opens data\script (string 0049aa3e plus extension), sets the announced mission status DAT_004a9ed0 to 0xffff, skips the header and blocks 1-6 and reads blocks 7-12. Block 7, then the player.mec entries, between WeaponModels_LoadShapeChunks and WeaponModels_FreeShapeChunks: for each slot DBSim_LoadScriptDat marked live it allocates from GlobalMechList and runs Mech_Constructor with the type. A roster record supplies the position ref at +0x3e (Terrain_HeightQuery plus typeRec+0x16, plus 5000 when typeRec+0x50 is set; an unset ref leaves the position sentinel), heading +0x40, fit +0x2a and ammunition +0x6a to Mech_ConfigureLoadout, radar +0x00, cruise speed +0x02 when non-negative, engaged and defeated actions +0x80/+0x82, out-of-action counters +0x42/+0x56 and starting condition +0x84 to Mech_ApplyStartingCondition. A player.mec entry gets the sentinel position and heading, its fit (+8, +0x20), Mech_ApplySquadCondition from its three condition spans and its pilot index at mech+0x29c, and the entry at DAT_004aaae8 becomes PlayerMech with locallyPiloted set. Block 8: Flyer_Constructor with type +0x2c, position +0x28 taken without a height query, heading +0x2a, actions +0x56/+0x58, counters +0x2e/+0x42. Block 9: Base_Construct on the record, position +0x02 registered with Terrain_MarkStructureFootprint and then Terrain_HeightQuery, heading +0x04, actions +0x2e/+0x30, counters +0x06/+0x1a. Block 10 into 0x16-byte order records at DAT_004a9eb4, the subject through Mission_ResolveRefByKind. Block 11 into MissionGroups (stride 0x7a) through DBSim_BuildGroupRecord: record 0's members become the player.mec machines (map entries at block-7 count + k), every other record's refs are remapped through its kind's slot-to-pool map; a group with no heading ref takes Math_HeadingToward from its slot-0 route's second waypoint to its first when that route has two or more; a base group whose paints-ground flag is 1 calls Base_ApplyFormationTerrain on its first member. Block 12 into 0x4c-byte objective records at DAT_004a9ec4: the subject through Mission_ResolveRefByKind, three mission.str line pointers from g_MissionStringLines and the empty string 0049a870. Then Terrain_FlattenStructureFootprints, every structure's height re-queried, and each action's target resolved: types 0-6 cleared, 7, 8 and 9 as mech, flyer and base slots, 10 as a group, any other type left as stored.

entries.name: Sim_ShutdownNoOp1
entries.description: Empty body. Sim_Shutdown calls it after setting the exit code, before Sim_ShutdownNoOp2.

entries.name: Sim_RaycastObjectList
entries.description: Generic ray-vs-live-object-list query. Nine call sites in four functions: Rocket_TickUpdate (1), Bullet_TickUpdate (2), Bullet_FireBurst (1) and Razor_MovementTick (5, the airframe contact probes). Calls each candidate's vtable +0x20 (hit-test) and +0x50 (AI threat-tracking). The shot record's second exclusion at +0x14 is written only by Razor_MovementTick; all three weapon callers leave that stack slot uninitialised.

entries.name: Damage_ExplosiveBlastSweep
entries.description: Radius-based splash-damage entry point. Sweeps the live-object list, skipping an object whose mission group still carries an action and the excluded object; distance - obj[+0x5c] < blastRadius calls that object +0x70. Note it truncates its int blastRadius to a short when handing it on. RETURNS 1 IF ANYTHING WAS IN RANGE, not if anything was damaged -- the flag is set beside the +0x70 call, before that call can decide the target shields swallowed it. Its one reader is the drop pod +0x4c latch. Exactly 3 call sites, all terminal: Meteor_Tick drop-pod landing, the Plasma-cannon bullet type 9 branch in Bullet_TickUpdate, and Mech_BehaviourRamTick. It is NOT the only way +0x70 is reached -- Mech_ApplyDirectFireDamage and Mech_CollisionTest both call it directly.
entries.signature: short __cdecl Damage_ExplosiveBlastSweep(int *hitPoint, int blastRadius, short damage, int *attacker, int *excluded)

entries.name: Salvage_QueueWeapon
entries.description: Appends one {int16 weapon id, int16 condition} to the salvage list at DAT_004a9ef0 (a 200-byte block, room for 50, unchecked), bumping the count at DAT_004a9eee. Two callers: Mech_ApplyDirectFireDamage's mount-destruction roll on a Cybrid machine, and Mech_SalvageValue for each surviving mount of an enemy wreck. Mission_WriteResults writes the list as results.dat's salvage pairs.

entries.name: Detection_ContactScanRange
entries.description: Returns 30000 when DAT_004a9ee2, the scan-range setting, is 1 and 60000 otherwise: the range within which a held contact can still be selected. Its one caller is TargetSelect_CanTarget, and es2_xref.py finds this function as the only reference to DAT_004a9ee2. See docs/retail/simulation/target-selection.md.

entries.name: Damage_ScaleByDifficulty
entries.description: Scales a damage figure in place by a Q10 factor from one of two four-entry tables selected by the firing side -- 0049a73c {3500, 2800, 2100, 1400} for side 0, 0049a744 {300, 600, 800, 1000} for anything else -- indexed by the mission difficulty at MissionDifficulty. So difficulty moves the two sides' damage in opposite directions (3.42x down to 1.37x, versus 0.29x up to 0.98x).

entries.name: ActionTimers_Tick
entries.description: Walks the whole resolved block-6 array at ActionTimer_Array (count ActionTimer_Count, stride 0x31) calling ActionTimer_Tick on each. Sim_MainTick calls it immediately before Actions_EvaluateTriggers and both AFTER the per-group Group_OrderTick/Group_DeploymentCheck pass, so a group waiting on an action arrives on the tick after it activates.

entries.name: Actions_EvaluateTriggers
entries.description: Per-frame mission trigger evaluator, called by Sim_MainTick with the player's mech. Walks the whole block-5 action array and, per action type (+0x00), picks whose position Action_TestTrigger is offered: 0 the player's mech, 1 every member of the player's group, 2/3 every member of every deployed group of side 0 (human) / side 1 (Cybrid), 4/5/6 every deployed mech / flyer / base group, 7/8/9 the action's own resolved target object at +0x36, 10 every member of the action's target group. Groups whose +0x14 action pointer is still set are skipped as subjects -- an undeployed group cannot trip a trigger.

entries.name: World_StaticInit
entries.description: Static initialiser of WORLD.CPP (Borland _INIT_ entry 004a7aec, priority 0x20): StringTable_Ctor on g_MissionStrings (004aa6d4), the table DBSim_LoadScriptDat loads data\mission.str into. World_StaticDtor is its _EXIT_ counterpart.

entries.name: World_StaticDtor
entries.description: World_StaticInit's _EXIT_ routine (Borland _EXIT_ entry 004a7c1e): OwnedArray_Dtor(g_MissionStrings (004aa6d4), 2).

entries.name: DetAnimObj_Dtor
entries.description: DET_ANIM_OBJ vtable +0x08 (004973cc): the deleting destructor, (this, flags). One RTL destructor-count decrement, AnimObj_Dtor(this, 0), then Mem_Delete(this) on flags bit 0.

entries.name: SimObject_Dtor
entries.description: ACTOR vtable +0x08 (0049a54c): the deleting destructor, (this, flags). Two RTL destructor-count decrements (ACTOR, DET_ANIM_OBJ), AnimObj_Dtor(this, 0), then on flags bit 0 ObjList_SwapRemove(&maybe_GlobalLiveObjectList, this) instead of a Mem_Delete.

entries.name: SimObject_OperatorDelete
entries.description: (obj): ObjList_SwapRemove(&maybe_GlobalLiveObjectList, obj). The class-specific operator delete in the +0x14 field of the ACTOR, MECH, FLYER, BASE, RADAR_BASE, GUN_BASE, VEHICLE and LC_BASE class records; their deleting destructors inline the same call.

entries.name: Mech_Dtor
entries.description: MECH vtable +0x08 (0049a282): the deleting destructor, (this, flags). Three RTL destructor-count decrements (MECH, ACTOR, DET_ANIM_OBJ), AnimObj_Dtor(this, 0), then on flags bit 0 ObjList_SwapRemove(&maybe_GlobalLiveObjectList, this).

entries.name: Flyer_Dtor
entries.description: FLYER vtable +0x08 (0049a5e0): the deleting destructor, (this, flags). Three RTL destructor-count decrements (FLYER, ACTOR, DET_ANIM_OBJ), AnimObj_Dtor(this, 0), then on flags bit 0 ObjList_SwapRemove(&maybe_GlobalLiveObjectList, this).

entries.name: ActionTimer_ElementCtor
entries.description: (timer): returns its argument -- the per-element constructor DBSim_LoadScriptDat hands Rtl_VectorNew for the script.dat block-6 action timers (PUSH at 00424b76: 0x31 bytes each, count ActionTimer_Count (004a9eb8), stored to ActionTimer_Array (004a9ebc)).

entries.name: GridShape_HeightAround
entries.description: Column height under a point of a shape's collision height field, the point already shifted by the grid origin. When (1 << (cellShift - 1)) < radius it returns the tallest cell within radius; below that it samples the single cell. Off-grid is 0, which is what makes the volume end at its own edges. Cells hold a byte code into the 256-entry int32 height table at grid+0x34.

entries.name: GridShape_HeightAt
entries.description: GridShape_HeightAround with the grid-origin shift applied for the caller (origin << cellShift, i.e. world units rather than cells). Returns 0 for a shape with no collision volume.

entries.name: GridShape_Raycast
entries.description: Marches a ray, in shape space, through a shape's collision height field. Rejects an empty grid and a ray with BOTH ends above grid+0x430 (the height table's last entry, its ceiling). Step length is (1 << cellShift) + clearance; the direction is rescaled to it by a Q16 divide truncated to 16 bits. Hits when GridShape_HeightAround returns nonzero above the ray's current Z; reports the hit point with the grid origin offset removed.

entries.name: GridShape_Construct
entries.description: ClassItem registry loadFn for classId 0x02bc0001 (dgs\bases/bhulks shape records): allocates a 0x438-byte GridShape (RTTI name, vtable 0049aaa0, base TSShape), installs the vtable, then calls vtable+0xc (GridShape_ReadFromStream). See dgs-hd0-notes.md.

entries.name: GridShape_GetClassTag
entries.description: GridShape vtable 0049aaa0 slot 0: returns 0x2bc0001, GridShape_Construct's class id.

entries.name: GridShape_GetStreamSize
entries.description: GridShape vtable 0049aaa0 slot +4 (shape): TSShape's stream size (00490cdc) plus columns +0x2a times rows +0x2c plus 0x40a -- the five int16 grid scalars and the 1024-byte height table GridShape_ReadFromStream reads after TSShape's fields, then one byte per cell.

entries.name: GridShape_GetMemorySize
entries.description: GridShape vtable 0049aaa0 slot +8: returns 0. It does not call TSShape's slot +8 (00490d08).

entries.name: GridShape_ReadFromStream
entries.description: Field reader for a dgs\bases/bhulks shape record (vtable+0xc for classId 0x02bc0001), on top of the generic ClassItem base-class chain (TSShape_ReadFromStream). Its tail is the shape's COLLISION VOLUME, a coarse height field: int16 columns (+0x2a), rows (+0x2c), origin column (+0x2e), origin row (+0x30), cell shift (+0x32), a 256-entry int32 height table (+0x34, 1024 bytes, last entry addressed as the ceiling at +0x430), then rows*columns height codes (+0x434). The obvious reading, five undecoded scalars and an opaque block followed by sub-record count * sub-record size raw records, spans the same bytes and parses every retail record, but it is not the layout. See docs/retail/simulation/hit-detection.md.

entries.name: GridShape_WriteToStream
entries.description: GridShape vtable 0049aaa0 slot +0x10 (shape, stream): TSShape's write (00490e34), then the stream's +0x14 write of what GridShape_ReadFromStream reads, in the same order: the int16 columns +0x2a, rows +0x2c, origin column +0x2e, origin row +0x30 and cell shift +0x32, the 0x400-byte height table at +0x34, then one columns-byte row per row through the row-pointer array at +0x434.

entries.name: GridShape_RegisterClassItem
entries.description: Static initialiser of the GridShape module (Borland _INIT_ entry 004a7af2, priority 0x20): ClassItem_RegisterBucket(GridShape_ClassItemEntry (0049aa7c), 1), the one-entry bucket {0x02bc0001, GridShape_Construct, 'GridShape'} that lets ClassItem_FindHandler load a GridShape.

entries.name: GridShape_Dtor
entries.description: GridShape vtable 0049aaa0 slot +0x18 (shape, flags): when shape is set, decrements the live-object counter at *006cbf74, calls 00490958 (TSShape vtable 004a6331 slot +0x18) with flags 0, then Mem_Delete when flags bit 0 is set.

entries.name: Terrain_LoadZone
entries.description: terrain.cpp zone/grid loader. Builds a 'zoneNNNN' filename, reads a grid header, allocates a HeightGrid, installs it as ActiveHeightGrid.

entries.name: maybe_SimObject_TransformPointPairToWorld
entries.description: (obj, out): returns 0 when the pointer at obj+0x41 is null. Otherwise builds the object's Q14 rotation (BuildEulerRotationMatrixQ14 from obj+0xc into obj+0x12) when the dirty flag obj+0x32 is clear, and Transform_ApplyToPoint's the two Point3I at *(obj+0x41) and *(obj+0x41)+0xc through the object transform at obj+0x12 into out and out+0xc; returns out. What a pair of points at obj+0x41 is has not been read; maybe_SimObject_TransformPointPairToWorldStatic is the caller found by es2_xref.

entries.name: maybe_SimObject_TransformPointPairToWorldStatic
entries.description: (obj): sets the static-local guard byte 0049ab6e on first use and returns maybe_SimObject_TransformPointPairToWorld(obj, 004aab3c), a static two-point buffer (EAX passes through). No caller found by es2_xref.

entries.name: Structure_WalkCollisionTest
entries.description: The walking-collision half of the structure volume test, called from Structure_GatherWalkCandidates's gather. Per candidate: 2D distance from the point to the structure against shape+8 (the shape read through the model instance, obj+0x34 -> +4), then the offset rotated into shape space by the transposed XY block of the object's rotation, then GridShape_HeightAt(shape, point, 0), which applies the same origin << cellShift GridShape_Raycast applies, so a walker meets the footprint a shot meets. Returns the first nonzero height; the radius argument is not read.
entries.signature: int __cdecl Structure_WalkCollisionTest(int *point, unsigned short radius, int *candidates, short count)

entries.name: Terrain_HeightQueryActive
entries.description: (point): Terrain_HeightQuery(ActiveHeightGrid, point). Debris_TickUpdate calls it.

entries.name: RaycastShapeMinDistance_Clear
entries.description: Sets RaycastShapeMinDistance (004aab54) to 0. Sim_RaycastObjectList calls it twice, once just before Sim_RaycastTerrain.

entries.name: RaycastShapeMinDistance_Get
entries.description: Returns RaycastShapeMinDistance (004aab54) in EAX (the decompile drops the return).

entries.name: Sim_RaycastShapeVolume
entries.description: Ray versus a list of objects' collision height fields. Per object: coarse reject on shape+8 plus clearance plus ray length, then the object centre in muzzle space tested against a box on X and Y only (Z is not tested), then the ray transformed into shape space and marched by GridShape_Raycast. Writes the hit distance back into the ray record's +0x04 and returns early for a hit under 500. Two callers: Base_DirectFireHitTest (one object) and Sim_RaycastShapeList (the shape probe's gathered structures).

entries.name: Sim_RaycastTerrain
entries.description: The ray-versus-terrain query Sim_RaycastObjectList runs before it tests any object. Calls maybe_Terrain_RayWalk(ActiveHeightGrid, origin, endPoint, rayRecord+8 -- the literal 200, as a radius, &hitPoint, 0); on a ground hit the caller measures the distance back to the origin and clips the ray to it. This is what stops a shot passing through a hillside. Its companion RaycastShapeMinDistance_Clear is only a counter reset (RaycastShapeMinDistance), not part of the query.
