entries.name: Terrain_RayHitDistance
entries.description: (&distance, from, to, step): Terrain_RayWalk on ActiveHeightGrid from from to to; when it reports a hit, stores Math_DistanceBetweenPoints(from, hitPoint) in distance. Returns whether it hit. Detection_LineOfSight and Ai_LineOfSightBlocked call it.

entries.name: Scene_DrawTerrain
entries.description: (view): Raster_SetModelTransform(&DAT_004aab08); sets the render context's clip mode +0x208 to 1 while its clip block (+4) holds one region whose first dword is 0; Terrain_DrawVisibleCells(g_TerrainDrawGrid, view); restores +0x208. Called from Scene_DrawTerrainPass in the frame draw and from the heads-down map's terrain pass.

entries.name: Terrain_StaticInitNoOp
entries.description: Static initialiser of the terrain module (Borland _INIT_ entry 004a7af8, priority 0x20): a lone RET. It follows Scene_DrawTerrain and precedes the HeightGrid class record (004281a1).

entries.name: ObjList_DrawTableIndex
entries.description: (a, b): returns the index recorded for the pair in the draw table at 004cf574 (three int16 per entry: a, b, index; count 004cf8f8); a new pair is appended with the next index, asserting 'ObjList::drawTable full' in objlist.cpp once 0x96 entries exist. ObjList_AddToDrawTable and ObjList_DrawCellObjects call it.

entries.name: ObjList_LoadResources
entries.description: The object list's subsystem phase-2 loader, registered by ObjList_RegisterSubsystem: allocates three 0x800-byte pointer arrays to 004cf8fc, 004cf900 and 004cf90c, 512 render entries of 0x36 bytes with ObjList_DrawEntryConstruct to 004cf908, 512 sort-tree nodes through ObjList_AllocSortNodes, and zeroes 0x249f0 bytes at 004aab84 (which ObjList_DrawCellObjects indexes in 1000-byte rows). It lies outside every Ghidra function; es2_xref reports it as the end of ObjList_DrawTableIndex's extent (+0x80).

entries.name: ObjPick_Arm
entries.description: (point): copies the {x, y} pair to 004cf9b5/004cf9b9 and sets the pending flag 004cf9b4, arming the pixel pick ObjList_DrawAfterTerrain and ObjList_DrawEntryRender run. It is the only store of 1 to 004cf9b4; es2_xref finds no reference to it.

entries.name: ObjPick_GetObject
entries.description: Returns 004cf9c0: the last object whose draw changed the pick pixel during an armed pick (ObjList_DrawEntryRender), or 0, which ObjList_DrawAfterTerrain stores before the object pass. Gunsight_UpdateAndPaint hands a non-zero result to TargetSelect_SetObject.

entries.name: ObjPick_IsIdle
entries.description: Returns 004cf9b4 == 0: no pick is pending. Gunsight_UpdateAndPaint tests it, with the byte 0049be74, before ObjPick_GetObject.

entries.name: Scene_SubmitObject
entries.description: (obj): Scene_SubmitObjectWithRadius(obj, obj->vtable[+0x10]()) -- files one object into ObjList::drawTable under the terrain cell its position and its own shape radius pick. Scene_SubmitFrameObjects' submit for ground shapes (FlatObj), projectiles, ownerless explosions, debris, the 004a96f2 pool and drop pods.

entries.name: ObjList_AddToDrawTable
entries.description: Files one object into ObjList::drawTable at DAT_004aab80 (rows of 1000 bytes, row index interned per cell by ObjList_InternCellRow) or, when it resolves to no cell, into the flat DAT_004cf910 bucket that ObjList_DrawAfterTerrain draws after the terrain walk with no depth fade of its own. Asserts carry the objlist.cpp strings 'ObjList::drawTable entry full' and 'ObjList::drawTable full'.

entries.name: Scene_SubmitObjectWithRadius
entries.description: (obj, radius): HeightGrid_PickDrawCell(ActiveHeightGrid, obj->vtable[+0x04](), radius), then ObjList_AddToDrawTable(obj, cell); returns the cell record, which Scene_SubmitFrameObjects' machine walks cache at obj+0x7a/+0x1ea (0xffff when null).

entries.name: Scene_SubmitObjectAtCell
entries.description: (obj, cellXY): HeightGrid_ClaimDrawCell(ActiveHeightGrid, cellXY), then ObjList_AddToDrawTable(obj, cell); returns the cell record. Used where the cell is already known: a machine with a cached cell at +0x1e8, an explosion filed under its owner's cell (Explosion_GetOwnerDrawCell), and every fire.

entries.name: ObjList_RemoveListedObject
entries.description: (obj): searches the pointer array at 004cf8fc (count int16 0049abba) for obj and, at the first match, decrements the count and moves the last entry into the match's slot. No caller found by es2_xref; an absolute-address search of the disassembly finds 004cf8fc read here and written by ObjList_LoadResources, and 0049abba read here and at 00461798 in Sim_InitMissionSession.

entries.name: Scene_SubmitFrameObjects
entries.description: Per-frame scene assembly. Calls HeightGrid_ClearCellScratch(ActiveHeightGrid), then walks the object pools and lists in a fixed order and files each drawable object into ObjList::drawTable by terrain cell: g_FlatObjPool first (only shapes within 30000 of the view object, by Math_DistanceBetweenPoints, through Scene_SubmitObject), then the 004a9624 structure list, GlobalMechList and the 004a9e3d flyer list by body radius (vtable +0x5c), a machine whose mech+0x2b0 names a structure under that structure's cached cell instead (Scene_SubmitObjectAtCell); each skips an object whose group's +0x14 deployment gate is set and caches the cell it filed at obj+0x1e8/+0x1ea (0xffff for the no-cell bucket); then the projectile pool 004a9746, g_ExplosionPool (Explosion_IsHiddenFromOwnerCockpit, then the owner's cell or its own), g_DebrisPool, the smoke-ball pool 004a96f2, g_FirePool (Scene_SubmitObjectAtCell) and g_MeteorPool. It decides no visibility beyond the flat-shape range and the two gates.

entries.name: ObjList_DrawEntryRender
entries.description: Slot 0 of the depth-sorted render entry's vtable (stamped as PTR_FUN_0049ac38 by ObjList_DrawEntryConstruct). Reads the entry's cached position (+4/+8/+0xc) and object pointer (+0x32), calls Raster_SetDepthFadeFromDistance with the entry's own distance (+0x12), then calls the object's vtable slot 0 -- Bullet_Draw for a projectile. This is why every pooled effect is distance-fogged from its own range. After the draw, while the pick flag 004cf9b4 is set, a pick pixel no longer reading 1 records the object at 004cf9c0 and is reset to 1; and while 0049abbc is set and the object is the probed one (004cf9f8), ObjProbe_MarkCorners.

entries.name: ObjList_DrawAfterTerrain
entries.description: (view): runs after the terrain walk in Sim_RenderFrame. Calls slot 0 of every object in the no-cell bucket DAT_004cf910 (count DAT_004cf9b0) that ObjList_AddToDrawTable fills. Then, when LocalPlayerMech's type record (+0x1f2) has the flyer flag +0x50 set (the RAZOR) and Cam_IsAttachedTo(view, player) is 0, Terrain_DrawCellObjects for the player's cached cell (+0x1e8/+0x1ea). Then, while the pick flag 004cf9b4 is set, points the display's source page +0x38 at +0x8c, saves the pixel under the pick point (004cf9b5) at 004cfa00, writes 1 there and clears ObjPick_GetObject's 004cf9c0; ObjList_SetViewObject(view); restores the saved pixel and clears 004cf9b4. Last, ObjProbe_TestCorners when DAT_0049abbc is set.

entries.name: ObjProbe_Arm
entries.description: (obj): projects obj's position (vtable +4) to the screen and sizes a square from its radius (vtable +0x10): half-size = radius << 006c60ac / (eye distance - radius), each step floored at 1. Stores the four corners {x-h, y-h}, {x+h, y-h}, {x+h, y+h}, {x-h, y+h} from 004cf9c4, the object at 004cf9f8, and sets 0049abbc. Each corner's occluded flag 004cf9f4[i] is set when the corner lies outside the render context's +0x210..+0x21c rect, but the loop never advances its point pointer (00428a72), so all four take the first corner's answer. es2_xref finds no reference to it.

entries.name: ObjProbe_IsHidden
entries.description: Returns whether all four of ObjProbe_Arm's corner flags 004cf9f4[0..3] are set. es2_xref finds no reference to it.

entries.name: ObjProbe_MarkCorners
entries.description: Records the display (006c5f54) at 004cf9fc; for each probe corner whose flag 004cf9f4[i] is clear, saves the pixel there (g_RasterRoutines_GetPixel) at 004cf9e4[i] and writes 2 (g_RasterRoutines_PutPixel). ObjList_DrawEntryRender calls it right after drawing the probed object 004cf9f8 while 0049abbc is set.

entries.name: ObjProbe_TestCorners
entries.description: Points the display's source page +0x38 at its +0x8c (through maybe_g_RasterRoutines_SetSourcePage when it is the current display); for each corner with its flag clear, restores the saved pixel when it still reads 2, otherwise sets the flag -- something drawn after the probed object covered it. Clears 0049abbc. ObjList_DrawAfterTerrain's last step while 0049abbc is set.

entries.name: ObjList_SetDrawDistances
entries.description: (radius): the five object draw distances at DAT_004cfa0c, each Math_Q10Multiply(radius, factor) over the int16 table at 0049abb0 = {800, 900, 1000, 800, 1200}. Its one caller, Terrain_SetupVisibleRegion, passes the terrain draw radius in world units (grid+0x10c << cellShift), once a frame. ObjList_IsBeyondDrawDistance reads the result.

entries.name: ObjList_IsBeyondDrawDistance
entries.description: (obj, dist): picks a draw distance from DAT_004cfa0c by the object's type tag at +4 -- tag 0 entry 1, tag 8 entry 2, tag 5 entry 3, or entry 4 when SimObject_GetShapeRadius (vtable +0x10) is 7000 or more, anything else entry 0 -- and returns whether dist exceeds it. Called only by ObjList_DrawCellObjects (00428d92), which drops the object's render entry when it does.

entries.name: ObjList_DrawCellObjects
entries.description: The per-terrain-cell object draw hook (installed at HeightGrid+0x125, invoked by Terrain_DrawCellObjects). Walks the cell's ObjList::drawTable row and branches on each object's type tag at +4: tag 9 (a ground shape) is drawn immediately, in filing order, with the ramp row count DAT_004a5b1c zeroed around the draw and no fade of its own -- its solid faces fog with the one the cell's quad installed; everything else (a Bullet is tag 3, written by Bullet_Construct) is turned into a 0x36-byte render entry carrying its position, LOD short and distance, appended to the list ObjList_DrawSorted then walks. See docs/retail/formats/terrain-drawing.md, 'Objects in the walk'.

entries.name: ObjList_RegisterSubsystem
entries.description: Static-init registrar of objlist.cpp (Borland _INIT_ entry 004a7afe, priority 0x20): registers ObjList_LoadResources (00428230) at subsystem phase 2, then Rtl_VectorNew(004cf9c4, 8, 4, 1, Rtl_ReturnArg).

entries.name: ObjList_DrawEntryConstruct
entries.description: Constructor for the depth-sorted render entry: three successive vtable stamps (base, derived, most-derived), the last being PTR_FUN_0049ac38 whose slot 0 is ObjList_DrawEntryRender.

entries.name: ObjList_SetViewObject
entries.description: (obj): stores its argument at DAT_0049ac3c. ObjList_DrawCellObjects and ObjList_DrawAfterTerrain pass the view object.

entries.name: ObjList_AllocSortNodes
entries.description: (count): ObjList_SortNodes (0049ac40) = Rtl_VectorNew(0, 0x1d, count, 1, ObjListSortNode_ElementCtor) -- the 0x1d-byte depth-sort tree nodes ObjList_SortTreeAddKind12 and ObjList_SortTreeAddOthers hand out. ObjList_LoadResources passes 0x200.

entries.name: ObjList_PointNearSegment
entries.description: (entry, point): whether Point3I_DistanceBetween(entry+4, point) is less than half of Point3I_DistanceBetween(entry+0x18, entry+0x24) -- the point lies inside the sphere on the render entry's position whose diameter is its segment's length. ObjList_SortCompareSegment and ObjList_SegmentEndpointNear (0042933c) call it.

entries.name: ObjList_PointNearSegmentAxis
entries.description: (entry, point): 0 unless ObjList_PointNearSegment(entry, point) and the entry's int16 +0x30 is non-zero. Then builds the rotation facing along the segment (Math_EulerToward from +0x18 to +0x24, BuildEulerRotationMatrixQ14, Transform_TransposeRotation), rotates point by it untranslated (Transform_RotatePoint) and returns 1 when both the x and z components are within +0x30 in magnitude. No caller found by es2_xref.

entries.name: ObjList_SortCompareSegment
entries.description: (node, newNode): ObjList_SortCompare's case where exactly one render entry carries a segment (entry +0x16 of 1 or 2, endpoints at +0x18 and +0x24). When the segment entry is the nearer (+0x12) the answer is plain distance order, and also when 00428f38 accepts neither the camera (0049ac3c + 4) nor the other entry's position (+4) against it. Otherwise it builds, once per entry (flag +0xc), the normal of the plane that contains the segment and faces the camera -- Vec3I_Cross(segment, Vec3I_Cross(segment, camera - start)), each vector halved until Math_FastMagnitude3D is at most 32000 -- at +0x11 with the camera's side of it (Vec3I_DotSign) at +0xd, and returns whether the other entry's position lies on the camera's side.

entries.name: ObjList_SegmentEndpointNear
entries.description: (entryA, entryB): returns entryA+0x18 when ObjList_PointNearSegment(entryB, entryA+0x18), else entryA+0x24 when ObjList_PointNearSegment(entryB, entryA+0x24), else 0 -- the first of A's segment endpoints inside B's segment sphere. ObjList_SortCompareSegments asks it each way round.

entries.name: ObjList_SortCompareSegments
entries.description: (node, newNode): ObjList_SortCompare's case where both render entries carry segments. Asks 0042933c for a point of one against the other, each way round; with none, plain distance order (+0x12). Otherwise it moves that entry's position (+4) to the point and its type (+0x16) to 0 for the call, compares through ObjList_SortCompareSegment with the other entry as the segment, restores both fields, and inverts the answer when the moved entry was node.

entries.name: ObjList_SortCompare
entries.description: (node, newNode): which side of node newNode's render entry (+8) goes on; non-zero is right, drawn later. When both entries' int16 +0x16 is 1 or 2 the answer is 0042937c's; when both are 0 it is whether newNode's distance (+0x12) is less than node's; otherwise 0042900c's.

entries.name: ObjList_SortTreeInsert
entries.description: (node, newNode): descends right (+4) when ObjList_SortCompare(node, newNode) is non-zero and left (+0) otherwise, recursing until it finds the empty child to link newNode into.

entries.name: ObjList_SortTreeAddKind12
entries.description: (entries, count): for each entry whose int16 +0x16 is 1 or 2, fills the next 0x1d-byte node from 0049ac40 (entry at +8, children and byte +0xc cleared) and inserts it under the root with ObjList_SortTreeInsert (the first node is the root). Returns the next free node; the decompile drops it (MOV EAX,ESI).

entries.name: ObjList_SortTreeAddOthers
entries.description: (entries, count, node): ObjList_SortTreeAddKind12's complement: every entry whose int16 +0x16 is neither 1 nor 2 gets the next node from node onwards and is inserted under the root at 0049ac40 with ObjList_SortTreeInsert, unless it is the root itself.

entries.name: ObjList_SortTreeDraw
entries.description: (node): in-order walk of the sort tree: the left subtree, then slot 0 of the render entry at +8 (ObjList_DrawEntryRender), then the right subtree.

entries.name: ObjList_DrawSorted
entries.description: (entries, count): nothing for count 0. Builds a binary tree of the render entries in the 0x1d-byte node pool at 0049ac40 ({+0 left, +4 right, +8 entry}, the first node the root): ObjList_SortTreeAddKind12 adds the entries whose int16 +0x16 is 1 or 2, ObjList_SortTreeAddOthers the rest from the node it returns, both through ObjList_SortTreeInsert; then ObjList_SortTreeDraw walks it from the root. ObjList_DrawCellObjects calls it at the end of a cell with the entries it built, each of which it gave +0x16 = 0, so they order by distance alone: farthest first.

entries.name: ObjListSortNode_ElementCtor
entries.description: (node): returns its argument -- the per-element constructor ObjList_AllocSortNodes hands Rtl_VectorNew for the 0x1d-byte depth-sort tree nodes; the LEA of +0x11 is an inlined empty member constructor.

entries.name: CockpitViewManager_Ctor
entries.description: This 0x37-byte object is the player's own cockpit view manager (MECHVIEW.CPP): it holds the current view index at +0x14, the pending view command at +0x18, the CockpitView widget tree pointer at +0x1f, the owning mech at +0x29 and the herc model name at +0x2d, and it is what CockpitView_SetView/CockpitView_ProcessViewCommand drive. It is small because the heavy state lives in the CockpitView object it builds (see CockpitViewManager_LoadViews -> CockpitView_Ctor -> CockpitViewInstance). Also the site of CockpitPaletteSingleton's first (singleton-guarded) load of dpl\\cockpit.

entries.name: CockpitViewManager_Publish
entries.description: Stores its argument in CockpitViewManagerPublished (004cfa20). One call site: the tail of CockpitViewManager_LoadViews, passing the manager itself.

entries.name: CockpitViewManager_Published
entries.description: Returns CockpitViewManagerPublished (004cfa20) -- the cockpit view manager, or null before the cockpit is built. Sim_PollPlayerInput's HDD VIEW case tests the pointer itself rather than any field of it, which is the retail bug recorded in KNOWN_ISSUES.

entries.name: CockpitViewManager_GetCockpitView
entries.description: (manager): returns manager+0x1f, the CockpitView widget tree (CockpitViewInstance). Sim_DispatchCommand calls it on CockpitViewManagerInstance twice, in the auto-track paths, and discards the result.

entries.name: CockpitViewManager_LoadViews
entries.description: The whole cockpit bring-up, in order: (1) loads vue\\<herc> -- int32 viewCount then viewCount x 32-byte records {int x0,y0,x1,y1, cx, cy, canvasOriginX, canvasOriginY}, all coordinates shifted by VideoMode_X/YCoordShift; every retail .VUE has viewCount=4; (2) allocates 4 slots for canopy bitmaps, 4 x 0x204 clip-region blocks and 4 span tables; (3) per view i, calls CockpitClipRegions_Load on ed<i>/hd<i> and ClipRegions_BuildScanlineSpans on the result, and (unless CockpitArt_LoadOnDemand) CockpitCanopy_LoadViewBitmap for db<i>/hb<i>; (4) builds the CockpitView widget object (CockpitView_Ctor -> ColorSchemePanels_LoadAll, which sets CockpitViewInstance) and Gau_BuildCockpitWidgets; (5) THE PER-HERC COCKPIT COLOUR SCHEME: Palette_InstallRange(0x2a, 0x18, COCKPIT.DPL.entries + (schemeIdx*0x18 + 0x20)*4), i.e. live palette slots 42..65 are overwritten with COCKPIT.DPL entries [32 + 24*schemeIdx .. +24), where schemeIdx = mechTypeRecord+0x52 = offset 80 of simvol0/dat/<MECH>.DAT. Retail values are a 0-8 permutation: APOCA 0, COLOSSUS 1, SAMSON 2, MAVERICK 3, OGRE 4, OUTLAW 5, RAPTOR2 6, RAZOR 7, TOMAHAWK 8, so the nine 24-entry schemes fill COCKPIT.DPL entries 32..247. This matches the independently measured retail screenshots exactly (APOCA renders canopy index i as COCKPIT.DPL[i-10] => base 32; COLOSSUS as COCKPIT.DPL[i+14] => base 56) and explains why every WORLD<n>.DPL parks exactly slots 42-65 at filler green. (6) Repeats the same install with IMPACTCP.DPL into the secondary palette object ImpactPaletteObject for the damage flash.

entries.name: CockpitCanopy_LoadViewBitmap
entries.description: MECHVIEW.CPP:0x12e. The .HB0/.HB1/.HB2 (.DB0/.DB1/.DB2) load site. No literal 'hb0' string exists because the folder name is built at runtime: it copies the global folder literal 'dba' (or 'hba' when VideoMode_PanelMode==3) into a stack buffer and overwrites index 2 with an ASCII digit via _itoa, giving db0/db1/db2 or hb0/hb1/hb2, then ResourcePath_BuildFolderName(hercName, buf) + ClassItem_LoadResource. View->file map: fileIdx = viewIdx>2 ? viewIdx-1 : viewIdx, so views 0,1,2,3 -> files 0,1,2,2 and view 4 loads nothing; after loading file 2 the same handle is also stored in slot 3, i.e. views 2 and 3 share one bitmap (view 3 is drawn horizontally mirrored, see CockpitView_SetView). Result handles land in CockpitViewManager+8[viewIdx]. The CockpitLayoutMode==1 branch increments byte 2 of the SHARED global 'dba' literal (MOV ECX,[0x4a0a28]; INC byte ptr [ECX+2]) rather than the local buffer -- verified in raw disassembly at 00429d3e; the follow-on load still uses the unmodified local buffer, so that branch loads db0 twice and corrupts the global folder name. Treat CockpitLayoutMode==1 as an unused/buggy path.

entries.name: CockpitCanopy_FreeViewBitmap
entries.description: Releases the canopy bitmap handle for one view and nulls its slot; when freeing view 2 it also nulls slot 3, which shares the same handle. Only called when CockpitArt_LoadOnDemand (CockpitArt_LoadOnDemand) is set, i.e. the low-memory mode that loads and frees canopy art per view switch instead of keeping all four resident.

entries.name: CockpitView_ApplyViewState
entries.description: Installs one view's state into the global render context (DAT_006c5ff4): copies that view's 0x204-byte clip-region block (CockpitViewManager+0xc + viewIdx*0x204, filled by CockpitClipRegions_Load) into ctx+4..ctx+0x208, points ActiveScanlineClipSpans at the view's prebuilt per-scanline span table (CockpitViewManager+0x10[viewIdx]), and copies the view's six .VUE ints into ctx[0x84..0x89]. The .VUE record's last two ints are the view's origin inside the cockpit canvas and go to DAT_004cfa24/28 (or VideoMode_X/YCoordShift-space DAT_004d25da/de in CockpitLayoutMode 2). View 4 instead installs the default full-screen clip block at DAT_004cfb1c and hides the cockpit widgets -- it is the external/no-cockpit view.

entries.name: CockpitView_SetView
entries.description: Switches the cockpit to view 0-4. Calls CockpitView_ApplyViewState, then blits the view's full-screen canopy bitmap once via Bitmap_Blit(bitmap, {0,0}, flags) with flags = 2 (horizontal mirror) for view 3 and 0 otherwise -- this is where the side view's single authored bitmap is flipped for the opposite side. Finally repaints every cockpit widget (CockpitView_InvalidateWidgets). The canopy is NOT redrawn per frame: it is blitted once per view change and the 3D scene is then rasterized over it, clipped to ActiveScanlineClipSpans. In CockpitLayoutMode 1 view 0 additionally blits slot 1 at y+0xc5.

entries.name: CockpitView_QueueViewCommand
entries.description: Latches a pending view-change command (field +0x18) from an input action, guarded by the current view (field +0x14). Consumed by CockpitView_ProcessViewCommand.

entries.name: CockpitView_ProcessViewCommand
entries.description: Executes the pending view command. Command 4 selects glance view 2, command 5 glance view 3, command 6 returns to view 0, command 2 selects view 4 (external). The -/+0x3600 yaw adds on 4/5/6 are gated on VideoMode_PanelMode == 1, which no retail mode stores, so a glance never turns the camera: it is the forward view's image plane continued sideways (docs/retail/formats/cockpit-views.md). On the scroll-window path it first moves the image into the other half of the back buffer when a glance target would fall outside it (tests on Display_OriginX); on the -b paged path it instead holds glance commands until the draw page (+0x88) is 0 or 2 (1 under panel mode 1), and every pass past that gate and the cooldown calls Vga_WaitVerticalRetrace.

entries.name: CockpitView_StepViewTransition
entries.description: Runs a queued view change's animated slide, once per frame from Sim_EndFrame just before CockpitView_ProcessViewCommand, gated on pending != -1 and the armed flag at +0x1c. For commands 0/1 (heads-down pan) it steps the display origin y by 10 canvas rows per loop iteration over vue[dest].canvasOriginY - vue[src].canvasOriginY (237, or 474 after the coord shift), then a remainder step; commands 4/5/6 step x by 0x14. The loop has no timer, retrace poll or frame boundary, so its real-time speed is CPU-bound. On completion: +0x14 += 1 (or -1), +0x18 = -1, +0x1d = 2 (two-frame cooldown). See docs/retail/formats/cockpit-views.md.

entries.name: CmdLine_SetCockpitOverride
entries.description: (name): the -C switch. _stricmp against the 13 names at 0049ac64 (ROADRUNNER ... TEST3); on a match stores the index in CockpitOverride_Index and the name pointer in CockpitOverride_Name. Sim_ParseCommandLine calls it with the text after -C.

entries.name: CockpitView_SetShakeBand
entries.description: Seeds the shake's vertical band: copies the resting view offset into 004cfae4/004cfae8 and sets the two limits at 004cfaec/004cfaf0 to that offset and that offset plus or minus the amplitude argument, the sign chosen by the view mode enum at CockpitViewManager_Published's +0x14. Sets CockpitViewShakeArmed. Also reached from CockpitView_StepViewTransition.

entries.name: CockpitView_StepShake
entries.description: One frame of the shake: moves the view's y offset (004cfae8) by up to the step argument toward whichever of CockpitView_SetShakeBand's two limits is farther away, so the view ping-pongs across the band rather than settling, then reinstalls the projection. Does nothing unless CockpitViewShakeArmed is set, and nothing in view mode 4.

entries.name: CockpitView_ClearShake
entries.description: Undoes CockpitView_SetShakeBand: restores the view offset from the resting copy at 004cfadc/004cfae0, reinstalls the projection and clears CockpitViewShakeArmed. No-op when that byte is clear or the view mode is 4. Called when the cockpit damage shake ends or restarts, from CockpitView_ApplyViewState, and from the two mech-death screen flashes.

entries.name: CockpitView_ForgetKickOffset
entries.description: Zeroes CockpitView_KickOffset without touching the render context.

entries.name: CockpitView_SetKickOffset
entries.description: (value): on the current render context (006c5ff4), +0x224 -= CockpitView_KickOffset, then += value & 0xffff, which it stores in CockpitView_KickOffset.

entries.name: CockpitView_ClearKickOffset
entries.description: Takes CockpitView_KickOffset back out of the current render context's +0x224 and zeroes it.

entries.name: CockpitView_GetShakeOffset
entries.description: Returns a pointer to the static pair {0, (int)(short)DAT_004cfaf4}: the hit shake's vertical offset, which CockpitView_SetShakeBand, CockpitView_StepShake and CockpitView_ClearShake write. Sim_RenderFrame adds the pair into the projection centre for the frame and takes it out after.

entries.name: ExternalView_SetRect
entries.description: (rect, offset): stores the four-int rect (left, top, right, bottom) in ExternalView_Rect and at 004cfd28, and the two-int offset -- the projection centre negated, as ExternalView_DefaultRect's (-0xa0, -0x5a) shifted is -- at 004cfad4/004cfad8; when CockpitViewManager_Published is in view 4, also writes them into the render context's (006c5ff4) +0x210..+0x224. PreferencesPanel_Raise calls it (read).

entries.name: ExternalView_ResetRect
entries.description: ExternalView_SetRect's body with ExternalView_DefaultRect as the source. PreferencesPanel_Raise calls it.

entries.name: CockpitViewManager_FlushBorderFill
entries.description: (manager): View_FillOutside3dRect when the current view (+0x14) is 4, the external view; then clears +0x36. CockpitView_ProcessViewCommand calls it first when +0x36 is set.

entries.name: View_FillOutside3dRect
entries.description: Floods the four bands around the 3D rect (ExternalView_Rect/+4/+8/+0xc: left, top, right, bottom) with COLORS.DAT id 19 (DAT_004d3c26): a full-width band above it, one below it, and the left and right strips between. It installs a {0, colour} fill brush at the render context's +0x22c, zeroes the context's +0x208/+0x20c offsets for the fills and restores them, and issues one Raster_FillRect per non-empty band. Called by CockpitView_ApplyViewState for view 4, by CockpitViewManager_FlushBorderFill and twice by PreferencesPanel_Raise. See docs/retail/simulation/external-views.md.

entries.name: ExternalView_GetRect
entries.description: Returns &ExternalView_Rect. ViewChain_DrawCaption centres the caption in it.

entries.name: CockpitView_ShowsWorld
entries.description: Returns 1 when the current view's .VUE rect bottom (record +0xc of the 0x20-byte record CockpitViewManagerPublished+0x14 indexes under +4) is at least 1, or a view transition (+0x1c) is running; 0 otherwise -- so 0 in the heads-down view, whose rect is empty on every HERC but RAZOR. Sim_RenderFrame draws the terrain only when it returns 1.

entries.name: CockpitViewManager_StaticInit
entries.description: Static initialiser of the cockpit view-manager module (Borland _INIT_ entry 004a7b04, priority 0x20): Rtl_VectorNew(CockpitVueRecords (004cfa2c), 0x20, 4, 1, CockpitVueRecord_ElementCtor) for the four .VUE view records; constructs two global GLRectangleRegions at 004cfafe and 004cfd20 (ClassItem, GLBase, GLRegion, GLRectangleRegion vtables in turn, +4 zeroed), counting six live destructors; then stores the rect {0, 0xd2, 0x140, 0xf0} at 0049ac54/58/5c/60, ordered min/max per axis.

entries.name: CockpitViewManager_StaticDtor
entries.description: CockpitViewManager_StaticInit's _EXIT_ routine (Borland _EXIT_ entry 004a7c24): six decrements of *Rtl_DtorCountPtr, matching the init's six increments; those decrements are its whole body.

entries.name: CockpitVueRecord_ElementCtor
entries.description: (record): returns its argument -- the per-element constructor CockpitViewManager_StaticInit hands Rtl_VectorNew for the four 32-byte view records at CockpitVueRecords (004cfa2c), which CockpitViewManager_LoadViews points the manager's +4 at and reads vue\<herc> into.

entries.name: CockpitClipRegions_Load
entries.description: Parser for the per-view .ED0-.ED3 / .HD0-.HD3 files (folder name built by overwriting index 2 of the 'edg'/'hdg' literals with a digit). Layout after the 9-byte VOL prefix: int16 rectCount, rectCount x {int16 y0, y1, x0, x1}; then int16 spanBlockCount, and per block {int16 firstRow, int16 rowCount, rowCount x {int16 xStart, int16 xEnd}}. Rects become type-0 region objects, span blocks type-2. Coordinates are shifted by the caller's (xShift,yShift) pair, which is (0,0) for the .HD* hi-res set and VideoMode_X/YCoordShift for the .DB*-era .ED* set. Output is a 0x204-byte block (int count + up to 128 region pointers). APOCA.HD0 reads cleanly: one full-width rect for rows 0-76 then a 235-row span block from row 77 whose spans narrow inward (the canopy frame). APOCA.HD1 is empty (rectCount=0, blockCount=0), which is why view 1 shows no 3D at all.

entries.name: World_LoadTheater
entries.description: World/theater setup, called by DBSim_LoadScriptDat with script.dat's 20-byte header as its argument (it copies the first 5 dwords to DAT_004cfd48). Builds the base name 'world<N>' via _itoa where N = DAT_004cfd48*2 + DAT_004cfd5a, i.e. header[0]*2 + header[18] -- five theaters, two variants each. Loads dpl\world<N>.dpl (the per-theater palette, which is what the retail WORLD0.DPL..WORLD9.DPL family is), then reads wld\world<N>.wld field-by-field (descriptor layout decoded and verified byte-exact against all ten retail .WLD files), then 'shades' via World_LoadShades, then world<N>.rmp -- the 8-bit software renderer's colour-ramp/lighting LUT. .RMP layout, byte-verified against all 10 retail files (WORLD0-9.RMP, all exactly 98312 bytes): int32 width, int32 height, then width*height*256 raw bytes (every file: width=32, height=12, 8+32*12*256=98312). width/height are read via the same generic field-reader callback used for .wld fields; the body is read in one call into ShadeRampTable (VolRStream_Read(fileHandle, width*height*256, ShadeRampTable)). Installs _DAT_004a5b18=rampTableBase and DAT_004a5b1c=DAT_004a5b20=width -- height is used locally for the allocation size and not retained in any global. TSTexture4Poly_Render (its only reader) uses the ramp-offset formula ((DAT_004a5b1c-1)*shade & 0xffffff00, i.e. (width-1)*shade rounded down to a multiple of 256), which makes width=32 the light-level-row count with 256 bytes per row (one byte per dither-table output 0-255). The 12 height slices are the depth-fog slices Raster_SetDepthFadeFromDistance selects. Finishes with Terrain_BindTextureBank(the 4th of the descriptor's 5 trailing strings) and FlatObj_LoadResources.

entries.name: Scene_DrawTerrainPass
entries.description: (view): sets +0x71 of the theater's horizon object g_TheaterHzline and has Terrain_ProjectFarEdgeAhead write into its +0x72; when that object exists, Hzline_Draw(it, view, &DAT_004cfa24, the view's canvas origin) paints the sky backdrop; then slot +0x34 of DAT_0049aee4 when that is non-null, Scene_DrawTerrain(view) and Palette_NoOp. Sim_RenderFrame's conditional arm.

entries.name: World_LoadShades
entries.description: (name): reads dat\<name> -- World_LoadTheater passes 'shades' -- as a count byte N, then N zeroed 5-byte records {byte count, pointer} at WorldShades_TypeTable (004cfd64) (N at 004cfd68), then a byte K and K entries {record index byte, count byte, count two-byte pairs}, each pair list going into a new array on that record. WorldShades_ApplyForObject (0042e8e8) indexes the table by an object's type tag (+4).

entries.name: WorldShades_DistanceBand
entries.description: (obj, distance): the distance band index for an object's type tag (obj+4). Tag 0 uses the .WLD's second distance table (WorldShades_BandsTag0 (004cfd88), count 004cfd5e); any other tag the first (WorldShades_BandsTagged (004cfd84), count 004cfd5c), and tag 5 first adds WorldShades_DistanceOffsets (004cfd6c)[obj vtable +0x10 (SimObject_GetShapeRadius) >= 5000] to distance, clamped at 0. Returns in AX how many leading thresholds are <= distance (unsigned), at most count - 1.

entries.name: WorldShades_ApplyForObject
entries.description: (obj, distance, blend): re-points shade ramps by distance before a draw. When 0049aef2 is set it runs WorldShades_ResetRamps instead. Otherwise it takes the SHADES.DAT record for the type tag obj+4 (5 bytes at WorldShades_TypeTable (004cfd64) + tag*5: count byte, pointer to {ramp, column} byte pairs) and, when the count is non-zero, the band b = WorldShades_DistanceBand(obj, max(distance, 0)); for each pair, the index range WorldShades_LevelRanges (004cfd7c)[(column * 004cfd62 + b)] ({int16 start, int16 count}) is installed into that shade ramp through Palette_SetRampsToRange (00430518). With blend set it calls Palette_SetRampsToRangeList (00430590) with a two-segment descriptor instead: the band range shortened by count/4 + 1, and WorldShades_BlendRanges (004cfd80)[b] ending count/4 entries early and lengthened to count/4 + 1; Palette_SetRampsToRangeList (00430590) reads ramp 0's segments contiguously from the first pointer, so its second segment is the four bytes of the pointer array at [EBP-0x10]. ObjList_DrawEntryRender passes the entry's object, distance (+0x12) and byte 004cfa08 (copied from 004d2549 by ObjList_DrawCellObjects); Terrain_FillCellUntextured passes a stack object with tag 7, distance 0, blend 0.

entries.name: WorldShades_ResetRamps
entries.description: Installs the index range {16, 16} into shade ramps 0, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12 and 0x18, one Palette_SetRampsToRange (00430518) call each. WorldShades_ApplyForObject calls it when 0049aef2 is set; an absolute-address search of the disassembly finds one reference to 0049aef2, that read, and the byte is 0 in the image.

entries.name: Palette_ActivateImpact
entries.description: Swaps the active palette to ImpactPaletteObject through Palette_SetActive, saving the previous one at 004cfd8c/004cfd90 and latching 0049aef3. The flash half of the cockpit damage shake.

entries.name: Palette_ToggleImpact
entries.description: Swaps the saved and active palettes and flips 0049aef3, so repeated calls alternate between the theater palette and its impact palette -- unless Palette_RestoreFromImpact ran while the impact palette was active, which leaves the saved slot 004cfd8c on the theater palette, so later toggles swap it with itself. Called once per HitShakeNextToggleTick expiry while the shake runs.

entries.name: Palette_RestoreFromImpact
entries.description: Puts the palette Palette_ActivateImpact saved back. Called when the shake ends and when a new shake restarts over a running one.

entries.name: WorldShades_IsBeyondLastBand
entries.description: (obj, distance): WorldShades_DistanceBand's table choice -- tag 0 the second .WLD table, any other tag the first, tag 5 adding WorldShades_DistanceOffsets (004cfd6c)[shape radius >= 5000] and tag 8 adding WorldShades_DistanceOffsets (004cfd6c), clamped at 0 -- then returns whether the table's last threshold is below distance (unsigned). No caller found by es2_xref.

entries.name: Palette_NoOp
entries.description: Returns immediately. LiftStart_DarkenPalette and Sim_InitMissionSession call it.

entries.name: Hzline_Ctor
entries.description: hzline constructor (vtable 0049afb0, RTTI name 'hzline', 0x7a bytes over TSGroup): TSGroup_Ctor, then the defaults +0x6c = 1, +0x54 = 3, +0x58 = 16, +0x5c = 1, +0x60 = 8, +0x64 = +0x68 = 1, +0x50 = 0, +0x70 = 0, +0x71 = 1. World_LoadTheater overwrites +0x54..+0x60 and +0x6c from the .WLD.
entries.source: DBSIM decompile at 0042eb5c; RTTI via es2_classes.py; docs/retail/formats/distance-fog-and-sky.md#the-sky--hzline

entries.name: Hzline_SetColors
entries.description: (self, zenithColor, groundColor, yOffset): +0x28 = (zenithColor + band count +0x58 - 1) & 0xffffff, the horizon colour; +0x2c = groundColor & 0xffffff; +0x30 = yOffset. World_LoadTheater passes .WLD shorts 1, 4 and 7.
entries.signature: void __cdecl Hzline_SetColors(hzline *self, int zenithColor, int groundColor, int yOffset)

entries.name: Hzline_Draw
entries.description: (self, view, canvasOrigin): Hzline_DrawWithOffset(self, view, self+0x30, canvasOrigin). Called only by Scene_DrawTerrainPass, with &DAT_004cfa24.

entries.name: Hzline_DrawWithOffset
entries.description: (self, view, yOffset, canvasOrigin): +0x34 = -view pitch (+0x10), +0x36 = view roll (+0x12); Hzline_BuildHorizon; adds yOffset >> 1 to both line ends' y; Hzline_FillSky; moves both ends down one row; Hzline_FillGround.
entries.signature: void __cdecl Hzline_DrawWithOffset(hzline *self, void *view, int yOffset, int *canvasOrigin)

entries.name: Hzline_BuildHorizon
entries.description: (self, canvasOrigin): writes the horizon line's screen ends to +0x38/+0x3c and +0x40/+0x44: (256 << coord shift) either side of a midpoint f*tan(pitch) from the projection centre (006c60b8/bc) along the rolled screen vertical, f = 2^006c60ac, plus +0x30 in y. A non-zero canvas origin lengthens it by its own length: both ends for a non-zero y, else the end on the x's side. +0x48/+0x4c = (sin roll, -cos roll), Q14, the band step direction; the test that would negate it compares the unsigned pitch with -0x4000 and is never true.

entries.name: Hzline_FillSky
entries.description: Paints the sky above the horizon line with the solid brush {0, colour} at the render context's +0x22c: +0x58 - 1 bands of +0x54 rows, the first in the horizon colour +0x28 and each next one entry lower, then the zenith colour beyond the last. Raster_FillRect rects when roll (+0x36) is 0, Raster_DrawPolygonReversed quads otherwise; the rolled bands' y offset uses one band fewer than the level fill's.

entries.name: Hzline_FillGround
entries.description: Fills from the horizon line to the bottom of the view (render context +0x21c). With +0x71 set, which Scene_DrawTerrainPass does before its only call, one fill in the horizon colour +0x28: Raster_FillRect when level, else a polygon of the line and the view-rect corners below it through Raster_DrawPolygonDispatch. The rolled branch moves the line by its midpoint's offset from Terrain_ProjectFarEdgeAhead's point (+0x72/+0x76) into polygon slots 2-3, which every path overwrites or leaves past the vertex count. With +0x71 clear it would paint +0x60 bands of +0x5c rows down from colour +0x2c + +0x60 - 1.

entries.name: Hzline_BlitHorizonStrip
entries.description: (self, bitmapSet, view, yOffset, offset): blits the frames of a bitmap set (count +4, frame list +8) one after another along the hzline's horizon line, starting from a position scrolled by the view's heading (+0x14) and wrapping the frame index; VideoMode_BlitBitmapFlags when level, VideoMode_BlitRotated by the negated roll otherwise. es2_xref.py finds no reference to it.

entries.name: Hzline_LoadBitmapBank
entries.description: (self, name): loads the named resource from the folder PTR_DAT_004a0a28 names (the 'dba' folder Terrain_BindTextureBank uses) and stores it at +0x50, which Hzline_Ctor zeroes. es2_xref.py finds no reference to it.

entries.name: Hzline_Dtor
entries.description: hzline vtable +0x18 (0049afb0, the sky backdrop Hzline_Ctor builds), the destructor its class record names: (hzline, flags). One RTL destructor-count decrement, TSGroup_Dtor(hzline, 0), then Mem_Delete on flags bit 0.
entries.source: DBSIM disassembly at 0042f6d2; class record at 0042f682

entries.name: TexPoly_Ctor
entries.description: (poly, bankName, pointCount): TexPoly's constructor and the installer of its vtable 0049afe6: stamps ClassItem, TSBase, TSGroupItem, TSPoly, TSSolidPoly, TSTexture4Poly and TexPoly vtables in turn (five live destructors counted, a sixth at the end); vector-news five Point3I at +0x25; allocates pointCount*4 Point3I to +0xe, pointCount Point3S to +0x12 and pointCount zeroed bytes to +0x16, storing pointCount at +0x23 and +0xfd; loads bankName from the 004a0a28 folder with Resource_Load to +0x1a and BitmapArray_PackToAtlas of it to +0x1e; zeroes +0x61..+0x6c, the five points and +0x71..+0x7c, and clears +0x22 (TexPoly_SetupRings' done flag). No caller found by es2_xref.

entries.name: TexPoly_RandomPointOnCircle
entries.description: TexPoly vtable +0x24 (0049afe6), (poly, outPoint, outAngles, _, centre, radius, shift): draws a BAM angle a with Math_RandomNext, writes the Euler triple (0, 0, a) to outAngles, and outPoint = (centre.x + (Q14(radius, cos a) << shift), centre.y + (Q14(radius, cos(a - 0x4000)) << shift), poly+0x79).

entries.name: TexPoly_SetQuadAndRadius
entries.description: (poly, width, height, z, radius): stores width at +0x71 (the ring step TexPoly_SetupRings divides by), height at +0x75, z at +0x79 and radius at +0x6d, and writes the face's first four points (Point3I at +0x25 stride 12) as the rectangle (0,0)-(width,height) at height z: x of points 1 and 2 = width, y of points 2 and 3 = height, z of points 0-3 = z. No caller found by es2_xref.

entries.name: TexPoly_SetFifthVertex
entries.description: (poly, point): copies the Point3I point into +0x55, the fifth of the five face points at +0x25 that TexPoly_DrawAtPoints installs as DAT_006c6970. No caller found by es2_xref.

entries.name: TexPoly_SetupRings
entries.description: TexPoly vtable +0x20 (0049afe6), (poly, rect): ring count +0xf9 = +0x6d / +0x71 (the step); for ring i the radius step * (i + 1) + step / 2 at +0x9f[i], the int16 0xffff / ((step * (i + 1) * 4) / +0x75) at +0x81[i], and a Math_RandomNext angle at +0xdb[i]; then copies the rect's +4/+8/+0xc into +0xff/+0x103/+0x107 and sets +0x22.

entries.name: TexPoly_DrawAtPoints
entries.description: TexPoly's vtable (0049afe6, RTTI 'TexPoly' at 004302aa, base TSTexture4Poly) slot +0x34, a slot TSTexture4Poly does not have; es2_xref finds the vtable entry and no call. Runs slot +0x20 (0042f970) first while +0x22 is clear; installs g_CurrentShapeDbaContext = this+0x1a, the surface base 006c697a = this+0x61 and 006c6976 = 006c60ec; Raster_SetDepthFadeFromDistance(0). Then for each of the +0x23 12-byte points at +0xe: when the viewer (arg+4) has moved since the last call (+0xff/+0x103), a point not flagged in the byte array at +0x16 and farther than +0x6d + +0x7d is reflected through the midpoint of the old and new viewer positions and flagged, and a flagged point nearer than +0x6d - +0x7d is unflagged; each point below index +0xfd gets slot +0x28 with its distance, Raster_SetModelTransform at its position and slot +0x2c (TexPoly_Render). Stores the viewer position at +0xff..+0x107.

entries.name: TexPoly_Render
entries.description: TexPoly's vtable (0049afe6) slot +0x2c, which TexPoly_DrawAtPoints calls once per point. Normally builds the poly's quad from the frame descriptor g_CurrentShapeDbaContext[1] + surface*0x14 (surface base 006c697a, index this+0xc) and hands it to Raster_SetupTexturedSpan, as TSTexture4Poly_Render does; while g_TexturedPolyUseBitmapBrush is set it takes the bitmap of the surface's +0 field when Raster_FrontFacing on the points this+4/+6 is positive and of its +8 field otherwise, and draws through Poly_ProjectIndexedVertices and PolyFill_FillThenOutline, calling slot +0x30 when the projection reports a vertex behind the near plane.

entries.name: TexPoly_ClipPolygon
entries.description: TexPoly vtable +0x30 (0049afe6), (poly, pairsIn, pairsOut): walks the current polygon's DAT_006c6968 vertices (indices at DAT_006c6976 + DAT_006c696a*2) edge by edge against the per-vertex code at DAT_006c697e, keeping a vertex coded 2 and, on an edge with one end coded 2, inserting the crossing at depth DAT_006c60b0 -- position interpolated with Math_Mul32To64/Math_DivMod64 and offset by DAT_006c60b8/DAT_006c60bc into 006cbb86/006cbb8a, and the vertex's 8-byte pair from pairsIn interpolated the same way into pairsOut. Returns the output count, also left in DAT_006cbc86.

entries.name: TexPoly_Dtor
entries.description: TexPoly vtable +0x18 (0049afe6, RTTI 'TexPoly', 0x10b bytes, derived from TSTexture4Poly), the destructor its class record names: (poly, flags). Five RTL destructor-count decrements, TSBase_Dtor(poly, 0), then Mem_Delete on flags bit 0.
entries.source: DBSIM disassembly at 004302fa; class record at 004302aa

entries.name: TexPoly_Slot28NoOp
entries.description: TexPoly vtable +0x28 (0049afe6): an empty body.

entries.name: Palette_LoadResources
entries.description: The palette module's subsystem phase-2 loader, registered by the _INIT_ routine at Palette_RegisterSubsystem (00430e90) (Borland _INIT_ entry 004a7b0a; PUSH 0x43034c at 00430e92): g_ShadeRamps (0049b034) = Mem_NewArray(0x408), 0x81 8-byte {int16 *indices, int16 count} entries, each given a 0x102-byte index buffer; then zeroes the five dwords at 004cfde8 (Palette_CycleAnimatedRanges' descriptors). It lies outside every Ghidra function.

entries.name: Palette_LoadAndActivate
entries.description: Loads a .DPL by path and makes it THE active palette object (ActivePaletteObject / ActivePaletteObject). World_LoadTheater calls it with dpl\\world<N>, so the live 256-slot palette IS the theater palette in its entirety -- it is not a merge of COCKPIT.DPL and WORLD<N>.DPL. The only cockpit-owned slots are 42..65, overwritten afterwards by the per-herc scheme install in CockpitViewManager_LoadViews.

entries.name: Palette_SetActive
entries.description: Swaps ActivePaletteObject and returns the previous one. Used to temporarily retarget Palette_InstallRange at the secondary impact palette (ImpactPaletteObject) without disturbing the live one.

entries.name: Palette_InstallRange
entries.description: Palette_InstallRange(baseIndex, count, srcRgbaArray): copies count RGBA/RGB entries from srcRgbaArray into the global active display palette (*(ActivePaletteObject+8) + baseIndex*4), then tracks the min/max dirty index range (DAT_0049b028/DAT_0049b02c) for a batched hardware palette update -- classic indexed-display-mode palette management. Used by the cockpit-view constructor to install the small IMPACTCP.DPL flash palette into a 24-entry sub-range (base 0x2a) of the shared 256-slot palette, distinct from CockpitPaletteSingleton's own local RGB array.

entries.name: Palette_ReadRange
entries.description: (start, count, out): copies count dword entries from the active palette (ActivePaletteObject+8) from index start into out. The read-back of Palette_InstallRange.

entries.name: Palette_GetEntry
entries.description: (index): returns the active palette's dword entry at index (ActivePaletteObject+8).

entries.name: Palette_FlushDirtyRange
entries.description: Pushes the accumulated dirty index range to the display and clears it; if the active palette object changed since the last flush it uploads the whole palette instead.

entries.name: Palette_ReadShadeRampRanges
entries.description: (first, count, out): for count shade ramps from index first in g_ShadeRamps, writes {first palette index (*ramp.indices), ramp.count} as an int16 pair into out -- the read-back of Palette_SetRampsToRange (00430518)'s contiguous install. No caller found by es2_xref.

entries.name: Palette_SetRampsToRange
entries.description: (first, count, range{int16 start, int16 length}): for each of count records of g_ShadeRamps from index first, writes the consecutive indices start .. start+length-1 into the record's array (+0) and length into +4. The range pointer is read for every record without advancing, so all count records get the same range. Then Raster_SetColourRamps (00486d04)(first, count, records) copies the records into the raster's ramp table at g_RasterColourRamps (004a4fbd). Callers found by es2_xref: WorldShades_ApplyForObject (0042e8e8) and WorldShades_ResetRamps (0042ea0c) (twice; WorldShades_ResetRamps (0042ea0c) passes count 1 and range {0x10, 0x10} for ramps 0, 2, .. 12 and 0x18).

entries.name: Palette_SetRampsToRangeList
entries.description: (first, count, specs): for each of count records of g_ShadeRamps from index first, reads a 6-byte spec {int16 rangeCount; ranges**} (spec i, and the i-th pointer of that spec's pointer array), concatenates rangeCount contiguous {int16 start, int16 length} runs into the record's index array as consecutive indices, and stores the summed length at +4; then Raster_SetColourRamps (00486d04)(first, count, records) copies the records into the raster's ramp table at g_RasterColourRamps (004a4fbd). Caller found by es2_xref: WorldShades_ApplyForObject (0042e8e8), which passes count 1 and rangeCount 2.

entries.name: PaletteCycle_Register
entries.description: (record): stores record in the first empty slot of the five at 004cfde8, its due time (Time_GetCoarseTicks + record's int16 +4) at 004cfdfc and 0 at 004cfe10, returning 1; 0 when all five are taken. Palette_CycleAnimatedRanges walks the slots. World_LoadTheater registers each record of the theater's cyc file, reading three int16s per record but stepping 12 bytes through a count*6-byte buffer; no .CYC entry is in any retail VOL (name scan of the eleven, which finds the .WLD/.RMP entries).

entries.name: PaletteCycle_Unregister
entries.description: (record): clears the first of PaletteCycle_Register's five slots (004cfde8) holding record.

entries.name: Palette_CycleAnimatedRanges
entries.description: Per-frame animated palette cycling. Walks 5 fixed slots (DAT_004cfde8 descriptors, DAT_004cfdfc next-due times, DAT_004cfe10 rotation offsets); when a slot's due time passes it rotates that slot's palette sub-range by one entry and reinstalls it via Palette_InstallRange. Keyed off Time_GetCoarseTicks. Blinking cockpit/console lights.

entries.name: Palette_InterpolateColours
entries.description: Colour-space sibling of Palette_InterpolateIndexRanges: interpolates rampCount colour pairs across `levels` steps, emitting 0x01RRGGBB-style entries. Distinct from the index-range remapper used for terrain shading.

entries.name: Palette_BeginCrossFade
entries.description: Palette_BeginCrossFade(fromPalette, toPalette, durationCoarseTicks): precomputes per-channel 8.8 deltas (to - from) / duration into DAT_004cfe28/004d0028/004d0228 over the from object's entry count, and disarms the step timer (0049b03c). Either endpoint may be null, meaning fade to/from black. Callers: Sim_DeathFlash and LiftStart_DarkenPalette.

entries.name: Palette_StepCrossFade
entries.description: Steps the Palette_BeginCrossFade fade by wall clock, not by call: the first call arms an end time of now + duration in Time_GetCoarseTicks units, and each call writes from + delta * elapsed >> 8 into the live palette from entry DAT_004cfe20 (never written, so 0) and extends the dirty range. Returns the coarse ticks remaining; once past the end it returns 0 without writing, so the last value written is the one from the last call before the end, not the destination.

entries.name: Palette_InterpolateIndexRanges
entries.description: Palette_InterpolateIndexRanges(from, to, rampCount, levels, out): linearly interpolates palette index RANGES, not colours. Each of from/to/out is an array of (int16 start, int16 count) pairs; for each of rampCount ramps it emits `levels` interpolated ranges in 8.8 fixed point, with the final step forced exactly to the `to` endpoint. Called twice by maybe_World_LoadTheater with endpoint tables read from WORLD<n>.WLD. WORLD0 expands to 11 ramps x 16 levels, all ranges within indices 96-239 (terrain shading only; no cockpit equivalent found).

entries.name: Palette_ShadeRampMidIndex
entries.description: (value): returns 0 when ActivePaletteObject+0x0c (the ramp count) is 0; otherwise ramp = ActivePaletteObject+0x10 + (value & 0xff) * 8 and returns the int16 palette index at ramp.indices[ramp.length (int16 at +4) >> 1], the middle entry of that shade ramp. Unlike Palette_ShadeRampLookup it does not clamp the ramp number against the count. No caller found by es2_xref.

entries.name: Palette_ShadeRampLookup
entries.description: Palette_ShadeRampLookup(value, shade): idx = value & 0xff, clamped to 0 when >= ActivePaletteObject+0x0c (the ramp count); reads ActivePaletteObject+0x10 as an array of 8-byte {int16* indices, int32 length} shade ramps and returns ramp[idx].indices[ Math_Q8Multiply(shade, length) ], stepping back one when that lands on the end. So a value here is a RAMP NUMBER, not a colour: the ramps are per-material brightness sequences of palette indices. They live in the tail of each .DPL, after the 256 colour entries. Sole consumer found: TSShadedPoly_Render.

entries.name: Palette_RegisterSubsystem
entries.description: Static initialiser of the palette module (Borland _INIT_ entry 004a7b0a, priority 0x20): RegisterSubsystemLoader(Palette_LoadResources, 2). Palette_LoadResources (0043034c) allocates g_ShadeRamps (0x81 records of 8 bytes, each with a 0x102-byte index array) and clears the five PaletteCycle_Register slots at 004cfde8.

entries.name: Cockpit_CreateCanvasContext
entries.description: Allocates the cockpit widget layer's own 0x239-byte render context, sets clip mode 1 (single rect) at +0x208, turns on the blit translation at +0x20c (so Bitmap_BlitClipDispatch moves every blit by the rect's top-left less the origin at +0x220/+0x224), puts the caller's rect at +0x210..+0x21c, and stores it in DAT_004d042c. Gau_BuildCockpitWidgets passes the whole cockpit canvas and keeps the result at CockpitViewInstance+4.

entries.name: Panel_LoadWrapper
entries.description: Trivial wrapper funneling .DFN/.HFN panel loads into ClassItem_LoadResource with the panel's filename.

entries.name: Cursor_LoadWrapper
entries.description: Trivial wrapper funneling .DCI cursor loads into ClassItem_LoadResource with the cursor's filename.

entries.name: CockpitView_Ctor
entries.description: (view, mech): the 0x288-byte cockpit widget tree. Clears the int16 +0x218 and sets +0x214 to maybe_GlobalLiveObjectList (the target-selection cursor), stores mech at +0x203 and its HERCS.DAT record's int16 +0x6c at +0x201, ColorSchemePanels_LoadAll(view) (which sets CockpitViewInstance), then 004d0490 = a 16-byte array and 004d0494 = four 12-byte {0, 16-byte array, 16-byte array}. Returns view. CockpitViewManager_LoadViews builds it into manager+0x1f.

entries.name: ColorSchemePanels_LoadAll
entries.description: PANEL.CPP-adjacent. Lazy-loads the 18 color-scheme .DFN/.HFN panels (cpblue first, extension chosen by VideoMode_PanelMode==3) into the ColorSchemePanels array, then the 7 .DCI cursors into a separate array. Loop counts (0x12=18, 7) match the real retail file counts exactly.

entries.name: Cockpit_PushCanvasContext
entries.description: Pushes the current render context onto the stack at DAT_004d0470 and installs CockpitViewInstance+4, the full-canvas mode-1 context. Every cockpit widget paint runs inside a Cockpit_PushCanvasContext/Cockpit_PopRenderContext pair, which is why console instruments outside the canopy cutout can draw at all.

entries.name: Cockpit_PopRenderContext
entries.description: Restores the render context Cockpit_PushCanvasContext saved. Gunsight_TargetIndicatorPaint calls it deliberately mid-paint to drop back into the view's canopy-clipped context for the target box's blits.

entries.name: Widget_DrawToCockpit
entries.description: Stage 1 of the two-stage deferred paint that vtable slot +0xc drives. Acts only on the -b paged path (Display_UseScrollWindow == 0) and returns 0 otherwise: pushes the canvas render context, sets the source page (+0x38) and draw page (+0x3c) to the render target's +0x8c/+0x88 for a first argument of 1 (the reverse for 0) and copies the widget's rect between them with Region_CopyBetweenPages at the offset in the third argument, Cockpit_ZeroOffset ({0,0}) when that is null. Skips argument 1 while DAT_004d25ae is set. All 34 callers pass a null offset, and driver 3's rect copy returns at once on a zero offset, so in this image the copy moves nothing.

entries.name: CockpitView_RectCornerVisible
entries.description: (rect{x0, y0, x1, y1}): 0 when the cockpit's widgets are off (CockpitViewInstance+0x20f). Otherwise 1 when either corner (x0, y0) or (x1, y1), less the video-mode block's 004d25da/004d25de, lies inside the window whose origin is the render context's (view+4) +0x210 + +0x220 across and +0x214 + +0x224 down and whose size is the 3D viewport 004d25c2 x 004d25c6, bounds inclusive; 0 when neither does. The widget paint and update routines test their rect with it before drawing.

entries.name: CockpitView_DisableWidgets
entries.description: (view): sets the widgets-off byte view+0x20f to 1, the counterpart of CockpitView_EnableWidgets (00431518). CockpitView_ApplyViewState calls it on the manager's +0x1f view when it sets the manager's +0x14 to view 4.

entries.name: CockpitView_EnableWidgets
entries.description: (view): clears the widgets-off byte at +0x20f. CockpitView_ApplyViewState and CockpitView_ProcessViewCommand call it.

entries.name: Cockpit_LoadSquadmatePilots
entries.description: (cockpit): finds the player's machine (+0xa3) walking GlobalMechList with Pool_Prev, keeps its mission group (+0x45) at 0049b0f8, and takes up to three of the group's members (group +0xc, count +0x10, stopping at a null) other than the cockpit's own machine (+0x203) into 004d044c. Loads each one's pilot (+0x29c) into slot i of the HDD gauge (+0x1f9) with HddGauge_LoadPilotFrames, then calls MfdDisplay_SetStatusRoster(+0x1ed, count). Sim_InitMissionSession calls it.
entries.source: DBSIM decompile at 00431530; mech +0xa3 and +0x45 from known_structs.json

entries.name: Squad_SendOrderToSlot
entries.description: The [F7] command display's XMIT: addresses one squadmate by comm-box slot out of g_SquadmateMachines, stamps the record's issuer field at +0x02 with the player's machine (view+0x203), and calls that machine's vtable +0x28. Skips an empty slot, the player's own machine and a destroyed pilot; withdraws message 0x22 from the pilot-and-squad port (view+0x207) either way. Args derived from disassembly: [EBP+8], [EBP+0xc], [EBP+0x10].
entries.signature: void __cdecl Squad_SendOrderToSlot(int cockpitView, SquadOrderRecord *order, short slot)

entries.name: Squad_BroadcastOrderFromCockpit
entries.description: Stamps the order record's issuer field at +0x02 with the player's machine (view+0x203) and hands it to Squad_BroadcastOrder against the player's group (DAT_0049b0f8). Args derived from disassembly: [EBP+8], [EBP+0xc].

entries.name: Squad_CallsignOf
entries.description: (machine): walks the three g_SquadmateMachines slots and returns the matching slot's entry of SquadCallsignStrings (004d1424, STRINGS0.STR group 7: RED 1, RED 2, RED 3); otherwise 0. No caller found by es2_xref.

entries.name: CockpitView_InvalidateWidgets
entries.description: (cockpit): unless the widgets are off (+0x20f), calls vtable slot +4 (a widget's Invalidate) on each non-null widget pointer: the ten at +0x70 and those at +0x1e1, +0x1e5, +0x1e9, +0x1f1, +0x1ed and +0x1f9 inside Cockpit_PushCanvasContext / Cockpit_PopRenderContext, then +0x1f5 after the pop. CockpitView_SetView runs it after blitting the canopy.
entries.source: DBSIM decompile at 004316c0; slot +4 from known_vtables.json CockpitWidgetVtable

entries.name: Gau_Load
entries.description: PANEL.CPP's confirmed .GAU loader. Allocates a 1700-byte (0x6a4) struct -- matching .GAU's confirmed content size exactly -- then vector-constructs six arrays of 16-byte rects, counts 10, 3, 4, 13, 15 and 3: the first, the 10 weapon-row rects at +0x14 (.GAU offset 20, stride 16), with GauWeaponRect_ElementCtor, the other five with RectI_Ctor.

entries.name: Gau_BuildCockpitWidgets
entries.description: Caller of Gau_Load. Builds the cockpit's widget tree, and the order it does so in IS the flat clickable list's order, which first-hit-wins makes into precedence: SystemButtons_Ctor's two system gadgets, then the seven top-level gauges from fixed literal .GAU offsets (468 console buttons, 548 energy meter, 616 shields, 728 MFD, 1000 throttle, 1088 roving gunsight, 1212 heads-down display) stored at cockpit+0x1e1..+0x1f9, then WeaponMounts_BuildGauges for the weapon rows. Also builds the pilot message port at +0x207 from .GAU 1668 and the computer's message port at +0x20b from 1684. Ends with the flyer branch: when the piloted machine's type record has a non-zero +0x50 (InputFlagFlyer, the RAZOR alone) it marks the power-up already finished at cockpit+0x245 and both arms and immediately latches (+0x8d = 1) the ten gauges and the three widgets at +0x1e9/+0x1f5/+0x1ed, so none of them plays its power-up animation and Cockpit_PowerUpSound never stamps a start tick.

entries.name: CockpitView_RegisterWeaponGauge
entries.description: Stores a weapon-row gauge at cockpit+0x70 + row*4 (row -1 takes the first free slot), appends it to the view's widget list at +8 and counts it. The weapon-row array it fills is what Cockpit_PowerUpTick arms and the number-key handler indexes.

entries.name: CockpitView_CreateEnergyWeaponGauge
entries.description: (view, row, mount): copies the 16 bytes at CockpitGauRecord+0x14+row*0x10 to CockpitGauRecord+0x104, allocates 0xdf bytes, runs EnergyWeaponGauge_Ctor(gauge, record+0x104, view, row, mount) and CockpitView_RegisterWeaponGauge(view, gauge, row), and returns the gauge. 0040e0e0 stores the result at mount+0x77.

entries.name: CockpitView_CreateAmmoWeaponGauge
entries.description: (view, row, mount): copies the 16 bytes at CockpitGauRecord+0x14+row*0x10 to CockpitGauRecord+0xb4, allocates 0xef bytes, runs AmmoWeaponGauge_Ctor(gauge, record+0xb4, view, row, mount) and CockpitView_RegisterWeaponGauge(view, gauge, row), and returns the gauge. CockpitView_CreateEnergyWeaponGauge's ammunition twin; WeaponMount_CreateAmmoGauge stores the result at mount+0x77.

entries.name: CockpitView_CreatePodGauge
entries.description: Builds the cockpit weapon-row gauge for one equipment pod, switching on the pod's catalog id at pod+0x77: 0x12 (ECM) gets TogglePodGauge_Ctor, 0x1f (TURB) gets TurboPodGauge_Ctor, and 0x1d, 0x1e and 0x20 (TARG, SHLD, ENRG) get the plain PodGauge_Ctor. The split matches the tick table exactly -- the two classes with a tick of their own are the two with a gauge class of their own.
entries.signature: int __cdecl CockpitView_CreatePodGauge(int cockpitView, short hardpoint, void *pod)

entries.name: Gau_WeaponButtonsWidget
entries.description: .GAU offset 468 widget wrapper -> ConsoleButtons_Ctor: container for the Weapon Chain-select/Link/Auto-track button gadgets (4 children from offsets 484/500/516/532).

entries.name: Gau_EnergyMeterWidget
entries.description: .GAU offset 548 widget wrapper -> EnergyPoolGauge_Ctor: container for the Energy Meter widget (1 child from offset 564).

entries.name: Gau_ShieldDisplayWidget
entries.description: .GAU offset 616 widget wrapper -> ShieldsGauge_Ctor: Shield Display's front/rear numeric value label widgets (children at 632/648/664/680), nested inside the Shield Display's .GAU byte range.

entries.name: Gau_MfdPanelWidget
entries.description: .GAU offset 728 widget wrapper -> MfdDisplay_Ctor: the MFD's actual interactive behavior -- mode-switching state machine, radar-sweep table, damage-readout digits. Behaviour behind the MFD panel's bounding box at .GAU offset 952.

entries.name: Gau_ThrottleWidget
entries.description: .GAU offset 1000 widget wrapper -> ThrottleGauge_Ctor: the Throttle widget (already fully confirmed/ported in the C# port).

entries.name: Gau_RovingGunsightWrapper
entries.description: .GAU offset 1088 widget wrapper, constructs the roving-gunsight complex via Gau_RovingGunsightWidget.

entries.name: Gau_PilotRosterWidget
entries.description: .GAU offset 1212 widget wrapper -> HddDisplay_Ctor: pilot-roster/crew-status HDD readout ('hddclip'/'pilots'/'static' strings), constructs 15 sub-widgets, accounts for the rest of the .GAU, roughly bytes 1212-1588.

entries.name: Gau_PanelAmbienceWidget
entries.description: (cockpitView, gauRecord): .GAU offset 1604 (0x644) widget wrapper, the same shape as Gau_PilotRosterWidget: shifts the block at gauRecord+0x644 with Gau_ShiftRects2Point (00452274) (VideoMode_ShiftRect on its rect, then three x/y pairs at +0x10..+0x24 by VideoMode_X/YCoordShift), builds a 0xc1-byte PanelAmbience over it with PanelAmbience_Ctor(gauge, block, cockpitView), and appends the gauge to the view's widget array (+8, count +0x6c). No caller found by es2_xref; the rect and pairs at .GAU 1604 are zero in all nine retail .GAU files.

entries.name: CockpitWidgets_TranslateForView
entries.description: (cockpitView, delta) -- re-places the cockpit's widgets for a view change. FIRST calls Widget_TranslateRootForView on the root (*cockpitView), which is what converts screen coordinates to canvas coordinates for every later hit test; then subtracts the delta from the pair at +0x220/+0x224, then walks the list at +0x246 (count at +0x25a) offsetting each widget's rect by -delta through Widget_OffsetRect. The three screen-edge strips are NOT in that list and are handled separately: when the one-shot build flag at +0x23e is set, it hands the same delta to CockpitView_FlipScrollTriggers. Called from CockpitView_ApplyViewState (00429e60), which has two call sites for it -- one when leaving a glance, passing that view's own origin, and a general one passing the outgoing view's origin minus the incoming view's.

entries.name: CockpitView_PerFrameUpdate
entries.description: The cockpit's per-frame widget pass, called with CockpitViewInstance from Sim_RenderFrame just before Player_PerFrameCockpitUpdate. The whole body is skipped while DAT_0049b104 is nonzero. It builds the scroll triggers once (CockpitView_BuildScrollTriggers, flag +0x23e), runs Cockpit_PowerUpTick until the power-up flag +0x245 is set, then Cockpit_HitShakeTick and Cockpit_StepKickTick. With the widgets enabled (+0x20f clear) it calls the object at +0x207 (vtable +0x14), pushes the canvas context, paints (vtable +8) the ten weapon-row gauges at +0x70 and the widgets at +0x1e1, +0x1e5, +0x1e9, +0x1f1, +0x1ed and +0x1f9, pops the context, runs Cockpit_UpdateEdgeCursor, re-runs TargetSelect_CanTarget on the selection at +0x210 and clears it when that fails, then WidgetRoot_ServicePressFlashes and NavMarker_Tick. With the widgets off (+0x20f set, view 4) it paints only the widget at +0x1f9. See docs/retail/formats/cockpit-hud-widgets.md and docs/retail/simulation/target-selection.md, 'Losing the selection'.

entries.name: Cockpit_PowerUpSound
entries.description: The cockpit's power-up audio. Plays Sound_Play(0x13) -- start3, the start-up sequence -- once per session, gated on cockpit+0x245 and stamping cockpit+0x241 with Time_GetCoarseTicks. Then, ONLY when the piloted machine's type record (mech+0x1f2) has a nonzero +0x50 -- file offset 78, InputFlagFlyer, the RAZOR alone -- starts the looping engine hum Sound_Play(0x2d) and immediately drops it with Sound_SetPitch(0x2d, 42000), about 0.64 of its recorded rate. Despite the sample being called herceng1, a walking HERC never plays it; its running noise is its footsteps.

entries.name: Cockpit_PowerUpTick
entries.description: The cockpit power-up sequence, gated on the start tick Cockpit_PowerUpSound stamps at cockpit+0x241. Each pass arms any widget not yet armed with Widget_BeginPowerUpAnimation: the ten weapon-row gauges at cockpit+0x70 each after their own delay from PowerUp_RowArmDelays, and cockpit+0x1e9, +0x1f5 (the roving gunsight) and +0x1ed as soon as elapsed is non-zero. Separately, once 200 < coarse ticks have passed, sets cockpit+0x245, reads internals 0-9 with Mech_ReadEntryDamage (kind 0) and posts message 0x22 POWERUP INITIATED. INTERNAL DAMAGE DETECTED. at the first nonzero reading, else 0x21 ... ALL SYSTEMS NOMINAL. A nonzero reading also goes through Damage_ToConditionState and is compared against 0x5a, but that returns a condition index of 0-4, so the comparison always passes. At 16 ms a coarse tick that lands 3.2 s in, inside start3's five seconds rather than after them.

entries.name: CockpitView_ArmWeaponByGauge
entries.description: Thin wrapper: WeaponMounts_SelectByGauge on the player mech's weapon manager, returning whether anything was armed. Both the row gadget's click handlers and CockpitWidgets_HandleCommand's number-key case go through it.

entries.name: CockpitView_SetConsoleButtonsLatch
entries.description: (cockpitView): sets the byte +0x1e0 to 1 and the dword +0x1d4 to 0 -- the two stores Gau_WeaponButtonsWidget makes after building the console buttons -- then runs the console panel's (+0x1e1) vtable +0x08, ConsoleButtons_Update. No caller found by es2_xref.

entries.name: CockpitView_UnlightConsoleButtons
entries.description: (cockpitView): clears the byte +0x1e0; for the console panel's (+0x1e1) children at +0x18, +0x1c and +0x20 (chain, LINK, TRACK) clears the child's lamp byte +0x40 (the lit state ConsoleButton_Paint reads for the TRACK kind) and invalidates it through its vtable +0x04 (Widget_InvalidateDeferred); then runs ConsoleButtons_Update. No caller found by es2_xref.

entries.name: CockpitView_PollViewDevice
entries.description: Polls a device-state block for the four view axes -- bytes +0x1e/+0x1f/+0x20/+0x21 queue view commands 1/0/5/4 respectively -- i.e. the joystick hat's up/down/left/right, one of the two device paths into a view command alongside the screen-edge strips CockpitView_HandleEdgeTrigger answers. Also handles the +0xb button edge.

entries.name: CockpitWidgets_HandleCommand
entries.description: (view, code): the cockpit widget tree's command handler. Returns 0 at once while the widgets are off (+0x20f). The view is CockpitViewManager_Published()+0x14. 0x27 (;) clears the selection (TargetSelect_SetObject(view, 0)). 0x0f (Tab) goes to the HDD's (+0x1f9) key slot (+0xc) in view 1, and otherwise steps the cockpit machine's (+0x203) Targeting Pod (+0x30b) with TargetingPod_CycleComponent. 0x01 (Esc) queues view command 0, 1 or 6 from views 0, 1 and 2-3. 0x02-0x0b, outside view 1, take the weapon gauge at +0x70 + (code-2)*4 and, when there is one, CockpitView_ArmWeaponByGauge then Widget_PressChild(gauge, 0, 1). 0x13 (R) runs Mech_ToggleRadarMode. 0x1c (Enter) returns 0 in view 4 and, outside view 1, presses MFD (+0x1ed) child 9 on mode 3, child 7 on mode 4, and runs TargetSelect_Cycle on any other mode. 0x3b-0x40 (F1-F6) press MFD child code-0x3b, then queue view command 1 from view 1 or 6 from views 2-3. 0x41-0x42 (F7, F8) press HDD child code-0x41 and, unless maybe_CockpitLayoutMode is 1, queue view command 0. 0x43 (F9) queues 5 from view 0 or 6 from view 2; 0x44 (F10) 4 from view 0 or 6 from view 3. 0x57 (F11) builds and runs an ObjectivesPanel. 0x220 (Alt+D) runs NavMarker_DropAtPlayer. Any other code goes to MfdFlashComm_HandleAltKey, then in view 1 to the HDD's key slot, and otherwise to the key slots of +0x1d8 (when set), +0x1e1, +0x1e5, +0x1e9, +0x1f1, +0x1f5 and +0x1ed, and of +0x1f9 when maybe_CockpitLayoutMode is 1, stopping at the first that returns nonzero. Returns 1 for a code it handled, 0 otherwise.

entries.name: Squad_IndexOf
entries.description: Returns an object's index in the three-entry squadmate array g_SquadmateMachines, or -1. MfdStatusScreen_Paint uses it to decide between ID: with a pilot name and TARGET: with a type name.

entries.name: CockpitView_GetSquadMessagePort
entries.description: Returns the pilot and squad message port at CockpitViewInstance+0x207, or 0 when there is no cockpit view.

entries.name: TargetSelect_CanTarget
entries.description: Whether an object may be selected: alive (+0x99 and +0xa4 clear), on the other side (group+0x12), and known by either sensor route -- radar-visible (+0x95) within DAT_004d1cfc (200000, the last of the scanner's three ranges, read directly rather than the current setting), or a contact the viewer holds (viewer+0xc2+obj[0x4b]) within Detection_ContactScanRange (30000 short / 60000 long).

entries.name: TargetSelect_InForwardCone
entries.description: Bearing to the candidate less the machine's heading PLUS its turret twist (vtable +0x3c), accepted within +/-8999 -- just under 50 degrees each side. Wider cousin of the +/-0x3000 gate the missile-lock block uses. The twist sign is the original's; Mech_PerTickSystemsUpdate and the sensor sweep fold it the same way.

entries.name: TargetSelect_SetObject
entries.description: Cockpit target selection, on the widget tree (its +0x210 is the selection): selects one named object, or clears when passed 0. Reached by the ; key (scancode 0x27), the F4 scanner's TARGET button and a gunsight click. Walks +0x210 through the live-object list from the cursor at +0x214/+0x218 until it lands on the object asked for and it passes TargetSelect_CanTarget and TargetSelect_InForwardCone, so a request for something unselectable wraps back to where it started.

entries.name: TargetSelect_Nearest
entries.description: The manual's Nearest Target, the apostrophe key (scancode 0x28) via Sim_DispatchCommand. Nearest selectable object by 3D range, considering only target classes 0 (HERC) and 2 (flyer) -- structures are excluded -- and applying no cone test at all, so it reaches something behind the machine.

entries.name: TargetSelect_Cycle
entries.description: The manual's Select Target, [Enter] (scancode 0x1c) via CockpitWidgets_HandleCommand. Files every selectable object inside the forward cone into one of four buckets by bearing error (abs(err) >> 10, clamped to 3), sorted by range within a bucket keeping four, flattens them into the 4-entry shortlist at DAT_004d0490 and takes its head; a repeat press whose head is unchanged steps to the entry after the current selection. The angular-size correction it computes is multiplied by a literal PUSH 0x0 at 004335d0 and is therefore always zero.

entries.name: CockpitView_BuildScrollTriggers
entries.description: Builds the three ScrollTrigger widgets, allocating 0x24 bytes each and running Widget_CtorRect before overwriting +0x17 with ScrollTriggerVtable, storing the cockpit view at the widget's +0x20 and calling Widget_RegisterClickable. The rects are screen-relative, in the display's own width and height, with the band thicknesses scaled by VideoMode_XCoordShift/YCoordShift: {0, H-1-(3<<Y), W-1, H-1} the bottom strip at +0x21a, {0, 0, 5<<X, H-1} the left at +0x21e, and {W-1-(5<<X), 0, W-1, H-1} the right at +0x222. Called once, lazily, from the cockpit tick (004327ac) on the first frame that finds the one-shot flag at +0x23e clear -- not from any constructor, which is why the three sit apart from the rest of the widget build.

entries.name: CockpitView_FlipScrollTriggers
entries.description: (cockpitView, delta) -- re-places the three ScrollTrigger strips at +0x21a/+0x21e/+0x222 on a view change, and the only code that touches their rects after CockpitView_BuildScrollTriggers makes them. Per axis, a delta of at least a band's worth (>= 6, or < -5) sets a sign and a compensating shift of one full display width or height, and a smaller delta leaves that axis alone. Where the sign is set the band is reflected across its own edge -- y0 = y1, y1 = y0 + height for a downward delta, mirrored for an upward one -- and the rect is then translated by the delta net of the full-screen shift. Reflecting a band and shifting it by a screen is what carries an edge strip to the far side of the display, which is what retail shows: the bottom edge pans down to the heads-down view and the top edge comes back. Simulating it over all four views reproduces retail exactly, including that a click at the top of the heads-down view pans back up and a click at its bottom does nothing. For the bottom strip on a vertical pan the reflection and the translation cancel, leaving the rect alone and letting the root origin do the work; the reflection earns its keep on the side strips, where it carries the left strip's band to the right edge of the left window so the way back is the opposite edge. See docs/retail/formats/cockpit-input.md.

entries.name: CockpitView_HandleEdgeTrigger
entries.description: (cockpitView, trigger) -- maps a click on one of the three screen-edge ScrollTrigger strips to a view command, by current view. Not a keyboard handler and not reachable from one: its only caller in the image is ScrollTrigger_OnClick (00434df0), which passes the clicked widget. The manual's 'change views with the mouse by clicking on the screen edge leading to the view you want'. Compares the widget pointer against the three built by CockpitView_BuildScrollTriggers: +0x21a (bottom strip) queues command 0 from view 0 and 1 from view 1; +0x21e (left strip) queues 5 from view 0 and 6 from view 3; +0x222 (right strip) queues 4 from view 0 and 6 from view 2. Each strip therefore serves exactly two views and does nothing from any other. In screen terms each pair is the manual's rule in both directions, because widget rects are in canvas space and the root widget's origin moves with the view: the bottom edge pans down to the heads-down view and the TOP edge pans back up, the same widget both times, and from a side window it is the OPPOSITE edge that returns. Simulated over all four views, every strip lands on the edge facing the view it leads to; see docs/retail/formats/cockpit-input.md.

entries.name: Cockpit_PickEdgeCursor
entries.description: (view, point): hit-tests the pointer -- the position 0045b734 returns under TapePlayback -- rebased through the view's context origin, against the three screen-edge strips at view+0x21a and stores the arrow it should show at +0x22e, by strip and current view: the bottom strip 4 (scursor) in view 0 and 3 (ncursor) in view 1; the left strip 6 (wcursor) in view 0 and 5 (ecursor) in view 3; the right strip 5 in view 0 and 6 in view 2; 0 for no strip or no move. CockpitView_PollViewDevice calls it when +0x23e is set.

entries.name: Cockpit_UpdateEdgeCursor
entries.description: (view): with an arrow picked at +0x22e, puts Cockpit_CursorImages[arrow] in the edge slot +0x232 and makes it the active slot (+0x226), saving the previous active slot at +0x22a; with none, puts the saved slot back if the edge slot is active. Each change goes to maybe_Driver3_SetCursorImage (scroll-window path) or maybe_Cursor_SetImage, both empty in driver 3. CockpitView_PerFrameUpdate runs it.

entries.name: Cockpit_SetForwardCursor
entries.description: (index): puts Cockpit_CursorImages[index] in the forward-view slot view+0x236, skipping a repeat of the last index (0049b62c), and passes it on to maybe_Driver3_SetCursorImage/maybe_Cursor_SetImage unless the edge slot is active. Gunsight_ClickSurface_Paint passes 1 (pcursor) while the pointer is on the click surface and 0 otherwise.
