entries.name: Cockpit_SetOffForwardCursor
entries.description: (index): puts Cockpit_CursorImages[index] in the slot view+0x23a that Cockpit_UseOffForwardCursor activates for the heads-down view and the glances, skipping a repeat of the last index (0049b630), and passes the image (bitmap +4, hotspot +8) on to maybe_Driver3_SetCursorImage/maybe_Cursor_SetImage unless the edge slot is active. The HDD command display passes 2 (mcursor) while an order that wants a map pick is armed and 0 otherwise.

entries.name: Cockpit_UseOffForwardCursor
entries.description: Makes view+0x23a the active cursor slot (+0x226), or only the saved slot (+0x22a) while the edge slot is showing, and passes the image on to maybe_Driver3_SetCursorImage/maybe_Cursor_SetImage. CockpitView_StepViewTransition runs it on panning down to the heads-down view and on entering a glance.

entries.name: Cockpit_UseForwardCursor
entries.description: Makes view+0x236 the active cursor slot (+0x226), or only the saved slot (+0x22a) while the edge slot is showing, and passes the image on to maybe_Driver3_SetCursorImage/maybe_Cursor_SetImage. Sim_InitMissionSession runs it as the cockpit comes up and CockpitView_StepViewTransition on panning back up to the forward view.
entries.source: DBSIM decompile at 00433f7c and its two callers

entries.name: Cockpit_StartHitShake
entries.description: Starts (or restarts) the cockpit's damage shake: swaps the active palette to the theater's impact palette (ImpactPaletteObject, 0049aef8), seeds the view-offset band through CockpitView_SetShakeBand(5 << VideoMode_YCoordShift) and arms the two timers -- HitShakeEndTick at now + 0x3c coarse ticks and HitShakeNextToggleTick at now + rand%10. Returns immediately in view mode 4. Its two callers are Mech_ApplyDirectFireDamage (a hit on either of the player's own two cockpit components, while that component still reads under 0x64 damaged) and Mech_CollisionTest (the landing at the bottom of a long slide). Restarting over a running shake restores the palette and clears the view band, then skips the arm block because HitShakeNextToggleTick is still set -- so it extends the window without re-seeding the band; the flash continues only if the restart landed on a theater-palette phase (see Palette_ToggleImpact).

entries.name: Cockpit_HitShakeTick
entries.description: Per-frame half of the damage shake, called from the cockpit frame pass (CockpitView_PerFrameUpdate) immediately before the footfall kick's own tick. While HitShakeEndTick is in the future it flips the impact palette each time HitShakeNextToggleTick expires (rearming it at now + rand%10) and calls CockpitView_StepShake(rand%5) every frame; on expiry it restores the palette and the view. Returns whether the shake is running, which its caller ignores.

entries.name: Cockpit_StartStepKick
entries.description: Restarts the view's step kick unless the view manager's mode (+0x14) is 4: CockpitView_ClearKickOffset, then StepKickStartTick = now and StepKickEndTick = now + 0x3c coarse ticks, and CockpitView_ForgetKickOffset. Mech_PlaceLegsOnGround calls it on a footfall of the locally piloted machine.

entries.name: Cockpit_StepKickTick
entries.description: Per frame from CockpitView_PerFrameUpdate, after Cockpit_HitShakeTick. Clears StepKickEndTick in view mode 4 or once now passes it; while it is ahead, CockpitView_SetKickOffset(StepKickCurve[(now - start) * 10 / 0x3c]), halved when VideoMode_YCoordShift is 0 and shifted left by YCoordShift - 1 otherwise, and returns 1. On the frame it expires, CockpitView_ClearKickOffset.

entries.name: Hud_WorldUnitsToMetres
entries.description: THE GAME'S UNIT SCALE, stated by the original itself: 'return (worldUnits / 1000) * 6', i.e. 1000 world units = 6 metres, one world unit = 6 mm, 166.667 units per metre. Three call sites, two unrelated HUD gadgets, both feeding it a raw difference of two world positions: Hud_UpdateWaypointIndicator (0043c3e4, the 'WAYPOINT n: d M.' string) and the scanner MFD contact-range readout (0043ebe0/0043eecc). The integer divide quantises the displayed figure to multiples of 6 m.

entries.name: Pilot_PortraitOf
entries.description: (pilot): pilot / 3, the portrait bank dba\PILOT<n>.DBA a roster index talks with. HddGauge_LoadPilotFrames uses it.

entries.name: Pilot_VoiceBankOf
entries.description: (portrait): (portrait / 4) + 1 with 3 remapped to 4 -- the recorded voice bank a portrait speaks with. CommBox_BeginMessage and HddGauge_LoadPilotFrames use it.

entries.name: HudColorTable_Get
entries.description: Returns HudColorTable[DAT_0049b040[i]] -- resolves a logical colour id held in an initialised id array to a palette index. The array at 0049b040 holds three ids, 12, 15, 26 -- the squad comm-box slot colours (palette 14, 13, 5).

entries.name: Squad_PilotName
entries.description: The name in comm-box slot `slot`, by way of HddGauge_Name on the heads-down display at CockpitViewInstance+0x1f9.

entries.name: PilotMessagePort_GetHqName
entries.description: Returns 004d1430, STRINGS0.STR group 8's one entry, HQ. PilotMessagePort_ComposeLine signs a line whose record names no speaker with it.

entries.name: Squad_SlotOfPilotName
entries.description: (name): HddGauge_FindByName (0044b928)(CockpitViewInstance+0x1f9, name), returning its result: the comm-box slot 0-2 whose pilot name (+0x137 of the slot's gauge) is a case-insensitive prefix of name (strnicmp over the slot name's length), or -1. The name-to-slot counterpart of Squad_PilotName. No caller found by es2_xref.

entries.name: Player_DependentCondition
entries.description: Condition 0-4 of the player machine's dependent (internal) component n: Mech_ReadEntryDamage -> Component_ReadEntryDamage kind 0 gives damage << 8 / max, bucketed by Damage_ToConditionState. The sensor dropout's callers pass 2, SENSOR ARRAY.

entries.name: CockpitView_FindArmedMountGauge
entries.description: (cockpitView): the weapon gauge among the view's ten at +0x70 (count +0x98) whose mount (+0xbd) is the viewing machine's armed mount -- view+0x203 is the machine, its +0x202 the mount manager, whose +0x1d index into +4 is the armed mount, or 0 with the index negative -- or 0 when no gauge has it. MfdDisplay_SyncMissileCamMode's condition asks it first.

entries.name: SystemButtons_Ctor
entries.description: Registers the first two entries of the cockpit's clickable list, ahead of every gauge. Lazily loads the `sysbuttn` sprite bank into DAT_0049b63c (folder by VideoMode_PanelMode == 3), then builds two SystemGadgets from hardcoded coordinates rather than from the .GAU: x 305-317 and x 291-303, y 2-13 inclusive, in 320-wide units shifted by VideoMode_X/YCoordShift -- the screen's top-right corner, where CockpitWidgets_TranslateForView keeps them in every view. Frame 0 (a question mark) on the right-hand one, frame 1 (a window) on the left. Stored at cockpit+0x246 and +0x24a with the count 2 at +0x25a. Child 0 raises the on-line manual, child 1 toggles fullscreen -- see SystemButtons_OnChildClick.

entries.name: SystemButtons_PaintForPointer
entries.description: (cockpit, point): inside a Cockpit_PushCanvasContext pair, gives each system button (list cockpit+0x246, count +0x25a) state 0 when point.y plus the cockpit viewport's (004d042c) +0x224 lies within the button's y span (+4..+0xc) and state 3 otherwise, and paints it through its vtable slot 0. Sim_RenderFrame's last call, with the pointer position at 004d234c.

entries.name: SystemButtons_OnChildClick
entries.description: Owner slot 0 for both SystemGadgets. Matches the clicked widget against the pair at cockpit+0x246 by index and, unless a .TAP is replaying (TapePlayback), runs child 0 as OnlineManual_Raise followed by Help_Show and child 1 as Video_ToggleFullscreen followed by a repaint of the shield gauge at cockpit+0x1e9.

entries.name: SystemButtons_HideAll
entries.description: (cockpit): SystemGadget_SaveAndHide on each system button (list +0x246, count +0x25a). CockpitView_ProcessViewCommand runs it when its +0x1c is set.

entries.name: SystemButtons_RestoreAll
entries.description: (cockpit): SystemGadget_RestoreState on each system button (list +0x246, count +0x25a). CockpitView_StepViewTransition runs it.

entries.name: SystemGadget_Ctor
entries.description: Constructor for SystemGadget (object size 0x60), the on-line manual and fullscreen-toggle buttons at the screen's top-right corner; SystemButtons_Ctor builds both. Leaves the state byte at +0x1b holding 3 rather than 0, which Widget_HitTestChildren treats as clickable and SystemGadget_Paint draws as the art beneath. Class name from the descriptor record at 00434ced.

entries.name: SystemGadget_Paint
entries.description: SystemGadget's vtable +0. Blits the button's frame in state 0 after rebasing the rect through the widget render context, and in state 3 -- the state its constructor leaves it in -- restores the art underneath instead. Draws nothing in state 2.

entries.name: SystemGadget_OnClick
entries.description: SystemGadget's vtable +8. Forwards itself to SystemButtons_OnChildClick with the cockpit singleton; ignores the button flags the slot is called with.

entries.name: SystemGadget_SaveAndHide
entries.description: (gadget): saves the state +0x1b at +0x5c, sets state 3 and paints through vtable slot 0.

entries.name: SystemGadget_RestoreState
entries.description: (gadget): puts the state saved at +0x5c back in +0x1b and paints through vtable slot 0.

entries.name: NavMarker_Position
entries.description: Accessor for the cockpit nav marker's position: view+0x25e while the flag at view+0x26a is set, otherwise null. Called by Hud_UpdateWaypointIndicator (gunsight child 7's paint) and HddCommandScreen_DrawMap.

entries.name: NavMarker_DropAtPlayer
entries.description: Drops the cockpit's nav marker on the player machine's own position: copies mech+0x26 to view+0x25e, sets the marker flag at view+0x26a and clears the armed flag at +0x26b, so a marker dropped where the player stands cannot clear on the frame it appeared. Reached from CockpitWidgets_HandleCommand on command 0x220, which is [Alt+D].

entries.name: NavMarker_Tick
entries.description: The nav marker's whole lifecycle, run once a frame from the cockpit's own paint (CockpitView_PerFrameUpdate). With a marker down, takes the ground range to it: unarmed, leaving 10000 units arms it; armed, returning inside 10000 clears the marker and posts WAYPOINT REACHED (0x1d) to the computer's ticker.

entries.name: CockpitView_SetTargetBlock
entries.description: Writes the frame's target block into CockpitViewInstance+0x26c..+0x27e: the selected object, its world aim point (3 ints), and the two shorts Player_ResolveTargetAimPoint produced -- a component-present flag and the component id. Gunsight_UpdateAndPaint and MfdStatusScreen_Paint both read it.

entries.name: CockpitView_StaticInit
entries.description: Static initialiser of the cockpit view module (Borland _INIT_ entry 004a7b10, priority 0x20): stores 0, 4 and 0 at 004d0430, 004d0438 and 004d0440, and the six dwords 0, 1000, 0, -1000, 0, 0 at 0049b06e..0049b082 -- the last two are Cockpit_ZeroOffset (0049b07e), the {0, 0} offset Widget_DrawToCockpit uses when its third argument is null.

entries.name: GauWeaponRect_ElementCtor
entries.description: (rect): returns its argument -- the per-element constructor Gau_Load hands Rtl_VectorNew for the ten 16-byte weapon-row rects at .GAU +0x14 (PUSH 0x434ab9 at 004317ea; element size 0x10, count 10). Gau_Load's other five rect vectors use RectI_Ctor.

entries.name: SystemGadget_FlushDeferredPaintNoOp
entries.description: SystemGadget vtable +0x0c (0049b774): push ebp / mov ebp,esp / pop ebp / ret.

entries.name: SystemGadget_OnClickThunk
entries.description: The this-adjusting thunk at primary vtable +0x30 of SystemGadget's vtable block, in the table for its PanelGadget subobject at +0x20: subtracts 0x20 from this and jumps to SystemGadget_OnClick.

entries.name: SystemGadget_FlushDeferredPaintNoOpThunk
entries.description: The this-adjusting thunk at primary vtable +0x28 of SystemGadget's vtable block, in the table for its PanelGadget subobject at +0x20: subtracts 0x20 from this and jumps to SystemGadget_FlushDeferredPaintNoOp.

entries.name: SystemGadget_PaintThunk
entries.description: The this-adjusting thunk at primary vtable +0x24 of SystemGadget's vtable block, in the table for its PanelGadget subobject at +0x20: subtracts 0x20 from this and jumps to SystemGadget_Paint.

entries.name: ScrollTrigger_OnClick
entries.description: ScrollTrigger's vtable +0x08, and the whole of the class's behaviour: calls CockpitView_HandleEdgeTrigger(this->[0x20], this). ScrollTrigger carries no PanelGadget mixin, so +0x20 is a plain owner pointer rather than a second vtable, and the strip makes no console click.

entries.name: SystemGadget_Dtor
entries.description: SystemGadget's destructor (class record 00434ced): (gadget, flags). Four RTL destructor-count decrements, PanelSelectGadget_Dtor(gadget, 0), then Mem_Delete on flags bit 0.
entries.source: DBSIM decompile at 00434e05; class record at 00434ced

entries.name: MessagePort_QueueInit
entries.description: Builds the message port's queue: a vector of ten 0x31-byte records. The port is instantiated twice per cockpit view -- the computer's scrolling ticker at view+0x20b and the pilot/squad channel at view+0x207.

entries.name: MessagePort_Enqueue
entries.description: Fills one queued record from a SYSTEM.STR entry's eight attribute bytes: id at +0x00, filename digit at +0x16, priority at +0x17, and the four timings at +0x1c/+0x20/+0x24/+0x28, each multiplied by 0x3c coarse ticks. Bytes 7-11 go to +0x2c..+0x30: byte 7 is the clip number, and bytes 8-11 lie past the eight the file supplies. minTime/maxTime stay durations until the message is shown; minWait/maxWait get the post tick added at once. The insert stops at the first queued entry of strictly higher priority, so low sorts first.

entries.name: MessagePort_QueueFront
entries.description: (queue): 0 when the count +0x21c is 0, otherwise the record queue + slot0(+0x1ea) * 0x31. MessagePort_Tick takes it as the current message (+0x49a).

entries.name: MessagePort_QueueAt
entries.description: (queue, index): the queued record at slot index -- queue + slot(+0x1ea + index*4) * 0x31 -- or 0 when index is at least the count (+0x21c). MessagePort_QueueFront is the index-0 case. A 56-byte block inside it (004350e1-00435118) is jumped over: an inlined sprintf to 004d12c3 of a record's +0x18 string. Caller found by es2_xref: MessagePort_StampedQueueTimeAt.

entries.name: MessagePort_RemoveAt
entries.description: (port, index): when the queue is not empty (count +0x21c), clears the flag byte at +0x212 + the id held in slot index of the queue at +0x1ea, shifts the later slots down one and decrements the count. MessagePort_Tick calls it.

entries.name: MessagePort_QueueDropLast
entries.description: (queue): clears the flag byte at +0x212 + the id held in the tenth slot (+0x20e) and decrements the count +0x21c. MessagePort_Enqueue calls it when the queue is full (count 10).

entries.name: MessagePort_QueueNoOp
entries.description: Empty body (push ebp / mov ebp,esp / pop ebp / ret), between MessagePort_QueueDropLast and MessagePort_QueueExpire. No caller found by es2_xref.

entries.name: MessagePort_QueueExpire
entries.description: (queue): from the last slot down to slot 1, MessagePort_RemoveAt each whose record's maxWait (+0x28) is earlier than Time_GetCoarseTicks. Slot 0 is never dropped. MessagePort_Tick calls it.

entries.name: MessagePort_QueueRemoveMatch
entries.description: (queue, subject, id): removes the first queued record whose int16 id (+0) and subject pointer (+2) both match with MessagePort_RemoveAt and returns 1; returns 0 when none does. MessagePort_Withdraw calls it.

entries.name: MessagePort_QueueShiftDeadlines
entries.description: (queue, delta): adds delta to each queued record's +0x24 and +0x28 deadlines that are still later than Time_GetCoarseTicks. MessagePort_Resume calls it with the pause length.

entries.name: MessagePort_StampedQueueAppend
entries.description: (queue, record, msg): a five-slot variant of the message queue with a 9-byte string per slot at +0x21e. When the count (+0x21c) is 5 it drops slot 0 (MessagePort_StampedQueueRemoveAt). Takes the first free slot by its flag byte (+0x212 + id): copies record's five dwords at +2..+0x15 to the slot's record (queue + id*0x31), stores msg's attribute byte 0 (msg+5 points at the attributes) as the int16 at +0, attribute byte 1 at +0x16 and msg's text pointer (msg+0) at +0x18 -- msg is a SystemMessages_Index slot {text, count, attributes} -- copies PanelAmbience_FormatClock (00452218)'s HH:MM clock string (the PanelAmbience clock at PanelAmbience_ClockDigits (004d1e38)) into the slot's 9-byte string, and appends the id to the order list +0x1ea. No caller found by es2_xref.

entries.name: MessagePort_StampedQueueRemoveAt
entries.description: (queue, index): the same body as MessagePort_RemoveAt -- clears the flag byte of the id in slot index, shifts the later slots of +0x1ea down one and decrements the count +0x21c when it is non-zero. Caller found by es2_xref: MessagePort_StampedQueueAppend, with index 0.

entries.name: MessagePort_StampedQueueTimeAt
entries.description: (queue, index): the 9-byte clock string MessagePort_StampedQueueAppend stored for slot index (queue + 0x21e + id*9), or the empty string at 0049b928 when MessagePort_QueueAt returns 0 for that index. No caller found by es2_xref.

entries.name: MessagePort_CtorBase
entries.description: MsgPort constructor (vtable 0049bb00, RTTI name 'MsgPort', 0x4d3 bytes): builds the two queues at +4 and +0x222 with MessagePort_QueueInit, constructs the box at +0x49f as a GLRectangleRegion (vtable 004a327c) of type 0 holding the given rect at +0x4a7..+0x4b3, and clears the current message +0x49a, the latches +0x49e, +0x4c9..+0x4cb, +0x4d2 and the fields +0x4b7, +0x4b8, +0x4cc, +0x4d0. MessagePort_Ctor and DialogPort_Ctor run it first.
entries.source: DBSIM decompile at 00435490; RTTI at 0049bb00 and 004a327c

entries.name: MessagePort_PostNoOp
entries.description: MsgPort vtable +0x00 (0049bb00, the base of the cockpit message ports): an empty post. EventPort installs MessagePort_PickVariant, DialogPort PilotMessagePort_Post, CommandPort TrainingMessagePort_Post.

entries.name: MessagePort_ShiftRect
entries.description: (port, delta{dx, dy}): subtracts dx from port+0x4a7 and +0x4af and dy from +0x4ab and +0x4b3, moving the rect {x0, y0, x1, y1} at +0x4a7. CockpitView_ApplyViewState calls it on CockpitView_GetSquadMessagePort's port.

entries.name: MessagePort_AddBeginCallback
entries.description: Registers one of up to two begin callbacks at port+0x4b9, fired when a message comes due. Only the pilot/squad port registers any -- the comm box's CommBox_OnMessageBegin/CommBox_OnMessageEnd pair. The computer's port has none.

entries.name: MessagePort_AddEndCallback
entries.description: (port, callback): stores callback in the next of two slots at port+0x4c1 (count byte +0x4b8) and returns 1; returns 0 when both are taken. The end twin of MessagePort_AddBeginCallback. HddDisplay_Ctor registers CommBox_OnMessageEnd.

entries.name: MessagePort_Tick
entries.description: The message port's whole lifecycle, on four latches: +0x4c9 due, +0x4ca ready (set by the paint, which is what puts one frame between due and shown), +0x4cb cancelled, +0x49e a line is up. Drops queued messages past index 0 whose maxWait has passed, takes the queue front as current, then shows / holds / takes down. A line comes down when cancelled, when maxTime has passed, when minTime has passed and the queue holds more than one message, or when LocalPlayerMech+0x99 says the player's machine is dead. That middle clause is the whole of the port's preemption.

entries.name: MessagePort_LineOverlapsRect
entries.description: (port, rect{x0, y0, x1, y1}): 1 when a line is up (+0x49e set), the display is not suppressed (+0x4d2 clear) and rect overlaps the port's box at +0x4a7..+0x4b3 (edges inclusive); 0 otherwise. No caller found by es2_xref.

entries.name: SystemMessages_Index
entries.description: Indexes SYSTEM.STR into a 63-slot table at base + attr[0] * 9, each slot a {char *text; byte count; byte *attributes} triple, counting how many strings landed in each. Two entries sharing an id would become variants of one message and the post would roll between them; all 63 retail ids are distinct, so every count is one.

entries.name: MessagePort_StepToVariant
entries.description: (port, table, record, n): for n > 0, steps StrTable_NextString n times from the record's string and returns a record built in the static at 004d0d6a -- the string at +0, 0 at +4, 00453a08(table, string) at +5; for n = 0 returns record unchanged. MessagePort_PickVariant and PilotMessagePort_Post call it with the rolled variant.

entries.name: MessagePort_Withdraw
entries.description: Withdraws a posted message, matching on the message id AND the record's +0x02 subject pointer, so the same message about two machines is two entries. Sets the cancel latch on a matching current message unless it is due (+0x4c9: past its delay, waiting to go up), which is left alone and returns 0; the show clears +0x4c9, so a line already on screen is cancelled. Otherwise removes the match from the queue. Mech_ToggleRadarMode withdraws both radar lines before posting the one the mode became; Squad_SendOrderToSlot withdraws 0x22 STANDING BY... about the addressed squadmate from the pilot-and-squad port.

entries.name: MessagePort_MarkReady
entries.description: (port, record): sets the ready latch +0x4ca when record is the current message and it is due. Called by the comm box as a squadmate's portrait starts talking (HddDisplay_ServiceCommBoxes), and by CommBox_OnMessageBegin when the box cannot open.

entries.name: MessagePort_Cancel
entries.description: (port, record): sets the cancel latch +0x4cb when record is null or the current message. The comm box calls it when a squadmate's portrait script runs out.

entries.name: MessagePort_Pause
entries.description: Marks the port paused, recording the coarse tick it stopped at. Paired with MessagePort_Resume.

entries.name: MessagePort_Resume
entries.description: Shifts every deadline in the queue, the current message's two display deadlines and the scroll's publish time forward by however long the pause lasted, so a paused line keeps the rest of its display time.

entries.name: DialogPort_Ctor
entries.description: DialogPort constructor (vtable 0049bad4, RTTI name 'DialogPort', 0x4df bytes -- the pilot and squad message port): runs MessagePort_CtorBase, installs its vtable, and allocates two buffers of Region_PixelCount(+0x4a3) bytes at +0x4d3 and +0x4d7 for the box's save-unders. Gau_BuildCockpitWidgets and TrainingMessagePort_Ctor call it.

entries.name: PilotMessagePort_Post
entries.description: Vtable slot 0 of the ordinary pilot/squad port (0049bad4). A record whose +0x02 subject is null takes its id from the COMMAND0.STR table at 004d0971 (variants against 004d04c8); otherwise Squad_IndexOf picks the slot's PILOT<bank>.STR table at 004d04e8 + slot * 0x183, and a subject in no slot drops the post. Rolls among variants, then MessagePort_Enqueue.

entries.name: PilotMessagePort_ComposeLine
entries.description: Builds the pilot/squad channel's display line into the buffer at DAT_004d0d73 and returns it: the speaker's name, ": ", then the message text strncat'd at 0x4a characters. The name comes from the speaker's comm box through Squad_PilotName, or from PilotMessagePort_GetHqName when the record names no object. Reached through the port's vtable; the port argument is not read.

entries.name: PilotMessagePort_Speak
entries.description: Paints the pilot/squad channel's box: one line, sized to its own measured width plus a 10-unit margin each side and centred on the screen, filled with the speaking squadmate's COLORS.DAT colour and framed in the palette entry one below it, in ColorSchemePanels[2] CPRED. A message with no squadmate behind it takes ids 19 and 9 instead. Named for the BC_00000 voice arm it opens with, gated on record +0x2c (attribute byte 7): 0 for every PILOT<n>.STR line and 1 for every COMMAND0.STR one, so it is HQ's voice, and no BC_ clip ships. See docs/retail/formats/cockpit-messages.md, Its speakerless set.

entries.name: PilotMessagePort_Erase
entries.description: DialogPort and CommandPort vtable +0x0c, EventPort's MessagePort_Erase slot. Returns 1 at once when no line is up (+0x49e) or the display is suppressed (+0x4d2). Otherwise, unless the cockpit view manager's +0x1c byte is set (then it returns 0): calls each of the +0x4b8 end callbacks at +0x4c1 with the current message (+0x49a), restores the box's background from the save-under at +0x4d3 (Region_Restore inside Cockpit_PushCanvasContext/Cockpit_PopRenderContext), MessagePort_CopyBoxBetweenPages(port, 1), clears +0x49e and +0x4d2 and returns 1.

entries.name: PilotMessagePort_Update
entries.description: Ordinary pilot/squad port (vtable 0049bad4) slot +0x10. Sets the ready latch +0x4ca for a due message only when the record's +0x2c (attribute byte 7) is set -- a squadmate's line is made ready by the comm box instead (00435b14) -- repaints a line that is up, then MessagePort_Tick.

entries.name: TrainingMessagePort_Ctor
entries.description: Builds the training mission's pilot/squad port on top of the ordinary one (00435bf0): installs vtable 0049baa8, stores ColorSchemePanels[10] WHITE (0049b0d4) as its font at +0x4df, and extends the rect by eleven text lines to size the two save-under buffers.

entries.name: TrainingMessagePort_Post
entries.description: Training port (vtable 0049baa8) slot 0. Ignores the record's subject: enqueues the id's first COMMAND<n>.STR entry from the table at 004d0971, with no variant roll.

entries.name: PilotMessagePort_WrapText
entries.description: Training port (vtable 0049baa8) slot +8. Joins an instruction -- the id's first COMMAND<n>.STR entry and the count-1 entries after it in file order (StrTable_NextString) -- into 0x78-byte lines at DAT_004d0e13, at most 80 characters in the 640-wide mode and 60 in the 320-wide one. A sentence that fits is appended after a space; one that does not is split at its last fitting space, the head appended after a space (even to an empty line) and the rest copied unwrapped onto the next line. Sets +0x4eb to the line count, +0x4e7 to (lines + 1) * (8 << YCoordShift) and +0x4e3 to the measured width of the line with the most characters.

entries.name: TrainingMessagePort_Update
entries.description: Training port (vtable 0049baa8) slot +0x10. Repaints a line that is up, sets the ready latch for any due message, then MessagePort_Tick.

entries.name: PilotMessagePort_Paint
entries.description: The training mission's pilot/squad port class (vtable 0049baa8) show: the lines PilotMessagePort_WrapText built, left-aligned in ColorSchemePanels[10] WHITE on the computer's black with a red frame, the box as wide as the widest line plus 10 units each side, centred on the screen, (lines + 1) text lines tall from the .GAU rect's top (raised on this path by the offset-1664 lift). Then, unless PILOT MESSAGE is TEXT ONLY, plays <drive.cfg dir>\simvoice\TM<n>_<id+1>.wav through Voice_PlayNamed.

entries.name: MessagePort_Ctor
entries.description: Constructs a message port from the box rect Gau_BuildCockpitWidgets read out of the .GAU and coordinate-shifted into device pixels.

entries.name: MessagePort_SetText
entries.description: Latches the line the ticker will draw: strncpy of 0x50 characters, so a longer message is truncated there.

entries.name: MessagePort_PickVariant
entries.description: Rolls between the variants SystemMessages_Index counted for an id -- the same roll SOUNDS.STR attribute byte 6 drives. No retail id has more than one, so it always picks that one.

entries.name: MessagePort_Show
entries.description: Puts the current message up. Swallows a repeat of the same id inside 300 coarse ticks (about 4.8 s), and a swallowed repeat refreshes that window rather than leaving it. Otherwise latches the line, restores the box rect, publishes the scroll origin, repaints, plays an alert tone picked by a switch on the id (0x00/0x13 -> 0x19 strcfail; 0x0c/0x0f/0x10/0x14/0x15 -> 0x18 wrnwoop2; everything else 0x1a gnract -- the switch names fourteen further ids (0x17, 0x19, 0x1d-0x1f, 0x2a-0x2f, 0x34, 0x37, 0x38) that all reach the default arm's tone, and 0x36, whose arm also sets the blink latch +0x4d3), then speaks the line. Message 0x36 TRANSFERRING DATA is armed to blink here.

entries.name: MessageTicker_Paint
entries.description: Paints the computer's ticker: the box flooded with COLORS.DAT id 19 (black), a one-pixel frame in id 9 (red) through the fill brush's style 4, and the line in ColorSchemePanels[2] CPRED. Narrows the live clip rect by 3 << VideoMode_XCoordShift on each side before the glyphs go down, so the text slides under the frame rather than past it. Anchors the glyph row at ((height - cellHeight) >> 1) + inkHeight + 1, which HudFont_DrawGlyph subtracts inkHeight back off -- the cell centred in the box, not Label_SetRect's ink-centred rule. Message 0x36 is centred instead of scrolled.

entries.name: MessageTicker_ScrollText
entries.description: Recomputes the scrolling line's x every frame as port+0x4af - (0x23 << VideoMode_XCoordShift) * elapsed / 0x3c: it starts at the box's right edge and travels left at 35 authored units a second, 70 device pixels in the 640-wide mode. There is no wrap -- a line that outlives its own width simply leaves.

entries.name: MessagePort_Erase
entries.description: Takes the line down and erases its box, filling the same rect with the same COLORS.DAT id 19 the paint floods it with and nothing else -- which is what identifies that colour as the background rather than as part of the frame.

entries.name: PilotMessagePort_RestoreBackground
entries.description: DialogPort and CommandPort vtable +0x14: while a line is up, the display is not suppressed and the view manager's +0x1c byte is clear, puts the box's background back from the save-under at +0x4d3 (Region_Restore(port+0x4a3, port+0x4a7, +0x4d3) between Cockpit_PushCanvasContext and Cockpit_PopRenderContext). EventPort and MsgPort leave the slot empty (MessagePort_UnpaintNoOp).

entries.name: PilotMessagePort_RedrawFromSaveUnder
entries.description: DialogPort and CommandPort vtable +0x18, the slot EventPort fills with MessageTicker_Paint. Under the same three gates as PilotMessagePort_RestoreBackground: offsets the box rect (+0x4a7..+0x4b3) by the canvas origin (context +0x220/+0x224), saves the screen under it into +0x4d3 (Region_Save), takes the offset back off, and puts the box's own pixels back from +0x4d7 (Region_Restore).

entries.name: MessagePort_CopyBoxBetweenPages
entries.description: (port, direction): while a line is up (+0x49e) and +0x4d2 is clear, copies the box region at +0x4a3 between the display's pages with Region_CopyBetweenPages at offset {0, 0}: page +0x88 to +0x8c for direction 0, +0x8c to +0x88 for 1. Hides the cursor around the copy and shows it again unless the view manager's +0x14 is 4 and 0049dd8c is 0; restores the draw page after. MessagePort_Show, MessagePort_Erase, PilotMessagePort_Paint, PilotMessagePort_Speak and 00436130 pass 1; CockpitView_StepViewTransition passes 0.

entries.name: MessagePort_StaticInit
entries.description: Static initialiser of the cockpit message module (Borland _INIT_ entry 004a7b16, priority 0x20): Rtl_VectorNew of three StringTables at PilotStringTables (004d0498, 16 bytes each, StringTable_Ctor), then StringTable_Ctor on CommandStringTable (004d04c8) and SystemStringTable (004d04d8). MessagePort_StaticDtor undoes it.

entries.name: MessagePort_StaticDtor
entries.description: MessagePort_StaticInit's _EXIT_ routine (Borland _EXIT_ entry 004a7c2a): OwnedArray_Dtor(SystemStringTable, 2), OwnedArray_Dtor(CommandStringTable, 2), then Rtl_VectorDelete of the three PilotStringTables with OwnedArray_Dtor.

entries.name: TrainingMessagePort_Dtor
entries.description: CommandPort's destructor (class record 004373a3; table 0049baa8): (port, flags). Six RTL destructor-count decrements, then Mem_Delete on flags bit 0. Frees neither save-under buffer DialogPort_Ctor allocated.
entries.source: DBSIM disassembly at 004373f7; class record at 004373a3

entries.name: DialogPort_Dtor
entries.description: DialogPort's destructor (class record 0043734f; table 0049bad4): (port, flags). Five RTL destructor-count decrements, then Mem_Delete on flags bit 0. Frees neither save-under buffer (+0x4d3, +0x4d7) DialogPort_Ctor allocated.
entries.source: DBSIM decompile at 00437439; class record at 0043734f

entries.name: MessagePort_Dtor
entries.description: EventPort's destructor (class record 004372fb; table 0049ba7c, the computer's ticker MessagePort_Ctor builds): (port, flags). Five RTL destructor-count decrements, then Mem_Delete on flags bit 0.
entries.source: DBSIM disassembly at 004374ce; class record at 004372fb

entries.name: MessagePort_DtorBase
entries.description: MsgPort's destructor (class record 00437482; table 0049bb00): (port, flags). Four RTL destructor-count decrements, then Mem_Delete on flags bit 0.
entries.source: DBSIM decompile at 00437517; class record at 00437482

entries.name: QueuedMessage_ElementCtor
entries.description: (record): returns its argument; the LEA of +6 is an inlined empty member constructor. The per-element constructor MessagePort_QueueInit hands Rtl_VectorNew for a queue's ten 0x31-byte records (PUSH 0x437558 at 00434e57; element size 0x31, count 10).

entries.name: MessagePort_UnpaintNoOp
entries.description: MsgPort and EventPort vtable +0x14: push ebp / mov ebp,esp / pop ebp / ret. DialogPort and CommandPort install PilotMessagePort_RestoreBackground.

entries.name: MessagePort_GetRect
entries.description: Vtable +0x1c of all four message-port classes: returns port+0x4a7, the box rect inside the GLRectangleRegion at +0x49f.

entries.name: MessagePort_PaintNoOp
entries.description: MsgPort vtable +0x18: an empty body.

entries.name: SimStrings_LoadAll
entries.description: Opens one str\*.STR file and registers its string groups into .bss pointer arrays, in strict file order -- 41 registrations for STRINGS0.STR, so a group's index is its position in this sequence. The sixth (13 entries into MfdCaptionTable) is the MFD's caption/title table. A registration passes a second destination array only for groups whose entries carry attribute bytes, which matches the file's own self-describing per-entry attribute count. See docs/retail/formats/str-strings.md.

entries.name: SimStrings_StaticInit
entries.description: Static initialiser of the STRINGS0.STR module (Borland _INIT_ entry 004a7b1c, priority 0x20): StringTable_Ctor on SimStringTable (004d131c).

entries.name: SimStrings_StaticDtor
entries.description: SimStrings_StaticInit's _EXIT_ routine (Borland _EXIT_ entry 004a7c30): OwnedArray_Dtor(SimStringTable, 2).

entries.name: PaperDoll_InitTables
entries.description: Allocates the per-type 0x5c-byte .PDG table PaperDoll_Load fills, loads the weapon-icon bank weapons.hba/.dba into DAT_004d1754, and reads pdg\WEAPONS.PDG's {width, height} pairs into WeaponIconSizes, shifted by VideoMode_X/YCoordShift.

entries.name: PaperDoll_Load
entries.description: pdamage.cpp .PDG loader. Reads 3 views, each an origin/size pair plus a vector of 0x1c-byte regions {int index, int left, int top, int right, int bottom, int colorId, int spacer}; resolves each region's colorId through HudColorTable in place and shifts its coordinates by VideoMode_X/YCoordShift, with bottomRight additionally +1 in the 640-wide mode. Then reads the weapon-icon hardpoint list into +0x54 (count) / +0x58 (0x14-byte entries {int x, int y, int frameOffset, int alignment, int blitFlags}), shifting x and y.

entries.name: PaperDoll_GetView
entries.description: (machine, view): returns the machine's .PDG record (machine+0x1f2 type record, +0xda) + view * 0x1c -- one of the three 0x1c-byte views at the head of the 0x5c-byte record PaperDoll_Load fills. No caller found by es2_xref.

entries.name: PaperDoll_BuildWeaponIcons
entries.description: Builds one machine's weapon-icon list (count + 0x22-byte entries: bitmap, x, y, rect, blit flags, short gun index at +0x20), stored at mech+0x1fe by Sim_InitMissionSession. Entry n is .PDG hardpoint n; it finds the .GL record whose slot byte +0x17 is n, takes that mount's template +0x50 plus the entry's frame offset as the WEAPONS frame, and anchors it by the entry's alignment bits against the WEAPONS.PDG size.

entries.name: PaperDoll_RecolorRect
entries.description: Repaints one .PDG region in place, reading each pixel back out of the raster. Modes 0, 1 and 3 rewrite only the pixels holding keyIndex; mode 2 adds tintIndex to every pixel that is not the id-19 background. Modes 0 and 1 skip the walk entirely when the two colours agree. Mode 0 steps whole device pixels at a time when a 320-wide bank is being drawn doubled; the other three step one. The MFD status screen's route -- the HDD damage screen uses PaperDoll_RecolorRectFromArt instead. See docs/retail/formats/cockpit-hud-widgets.md.
entries.signature: void __cdecl PaperDoll_RecolorRect(int *rect, int keyIndex, int tintIndex, int mode)

entries.name: PaperDoll_RecolorRectFromArt
entries.description: PaperDoll_RecolorRect's four modes over a source bitmap rather than the raster: mode 0 walks art's own rows (width at +6, pixels at +0xe) offset by artOrigin, so a region can be recoloured from the art without the screen underneath being repainted first. Modes 1-3 still read the raster back and do not expand pixels. The HDD damage screen's route. See docs/retail/formats/cockpit-hud-widgets.md.
entries.signature: void __cdecl PaperDoll_RecolorRectFromArt(int *rect, void *art, int *artOrigin, int keyIndex, int tintIndex, int mode)

entries.name: Damage_PickRegionTint
entries.description: Picks the colour one .PDG damage region is repainted in. Writes {condition state, palette index} to the caller's two-int block. Bands are Damage_ToConditionState's -- intact >=90/74/51/1 -- and for the region mode at region+0x18 of 0, 2 or 3 the colours are HudColorTable ids 12, 15, 20, 9, 18 (green, yellow, orange, red, grey). Mode 1 instead keeps the region's own colour id (region+0x14) for the top three bands, so an undamaged region is left alone, and takes ids 6 and 17 for the last two; no retail region states a mode other than 0. Mode >= 4 falls through writing the caller's own scratch. See docs/retail/formats/cockpit-hud-widgets.md.

entries.name: Damage_ToConditionState
entries.description: Maps a Q8 damage fraction to a STRINGS0.STR group 28 condition index: intact = (0x100-damage)*100>>8, then >=0x5a OK, >=0x4a SHIELDS DN, >=0x33 INT DAMAGE, >=1 CRITICAL, else DESTROYED. Used for subjects with no per-component readings -- flyers and structures.

entries.name: PaperDoll_StaticInit
entries.description: Static initialiser of the paper-doll module (Borland _INIT_ entry 004a7b22, priority 0x20): Rtl_VectorNew(WeaponIconSizes 004d1758, 8, 0x1c, 1, Rtl_ReturnArg) -- 28 8-byte pairs.

entries.name: PaperDollType_ElementCtor
entries.description: (record): Rtl_VectorNew(record, 0x1c, 3, 1, PaperDollView_ElementCtor) and returns record -- the per-element constructor PaperDoll_InitTables hands Rtl_VectorNew for the per-type 0x5c-byte .PDG records (PUSH 0x438765 at 004378ea; element size 0x5c, count = its argument; the vector is stored at 0049bbe8).

entries.name: PaperDollRegion_ElementCtor
entries.description: (region): returns its argument; the LEA of +4 is an inlined empty constructor of the region's rect. The per-element constructor PaperDoll_Load hands Rtl_VectorNew for a view's 0x1c-byte regions (PUSH 0x438785 at 00437b15; element size 0x1c).

entries.name: PaperDollHardpoint_ElementCtor
entries.description: (entry): returns its argument. The per-element constructor PaperDoll_Load hands Rtl_VectorNew for the 0x14-byte weapon-icon hardpoint entries it stores at record+0x58 (PUSH 0x438790 at 00437bdd; element size 0x14).

entries.name: PaperDollWeaponIcon_ElementCtor
entries.description: (icon): returns its argument; the LEA of +0xc is an inlined empty constructor of the icon's rect. The per-element constructor PaperDoll_BuildWeaponIcons hands Rtl_VectorNew for its 0x22-byte weapon-icon entries (PUSH 0x438798 at 00437cb5; element size 0x22, count = the .PDG hardpoint count at +0x54).

entries.name: PaperDollView_ElementCtor
entries.description: (view): returns its argument. The per-element constructor PaperDollType_ElementCtor hands Rtl_VectorNew for a .PDG record's three 0x1c-byte views (PUSH 0x4387a3 at 0043876c).

entries.name: Label_Ctor
entries.description: A 0x21-byte HUD text label: zeroes it, stores the font at +0x00 and the panel-relative flag at +0x18 that makes Label_SetText subtract the global blit offset. Paired with Label_SetRect and Label_SetText.

entries.name: Label_SetRectAroundPoint
entries.description: (label, point{x, y}, text, flags): sizes the label's rect (+4..+0x10) to text's HudFont_MeasureString width w around point: flags 2 centres (x0 = x - w/2, x1 = x0 + w, anchor x +0x14 = their midpoint), 4 right-aligns (x1 = x, x0 = x - w + 1, anchor x = x), otherwise left (x0 = x, x1 = x + w, anchor x = x); y0 = y - HudFont_CellHeight2/2 and y1 = y. Stores anchor y +0x16 = font+0x16 + y1 + y, so y is counted twice, and flags at +0x19; returns label+4. No caller found by es2_xref.

entries.name: Label_SetRect
entries.description: Anchors a HUD text label: stores the caller's rect at label+1..4 and computes the text anchor. Horizontal depends on the flags argument -- 2 = centre ((x1-x0)/2 + x0 + margin[0]), 4 = right (x1 - margin[0]), otherwise left (x0 + margin[0]). Vertical has no flag at all: anchorY = ((y1-y0)>>1) + y0 + (inkHeight>>1) + margin[2] + 1, where inkHeight is font+0x16 (file offset 0x1a, 11 for .HFN) and NOT the cell height at font+0xa. All of it is integer arithmetic. margin is the caller's short[4]. Paired with Label_SetText. See docs/retail/formats/mfd.md.

entries.name: Label_SetText
entries.description: Sets a HUD label's text and places it against the anchor Label_SetRect computed. Measures the run and subtracts 1<<XCoordShift (dropping the trailing advance), then places left/centre/right per the same flags. Vertical position is the stored anchor; HudFont_DrawGlyph then draws each glyph with its top row at anchor - inkHeight, so the inked band is what gets centred in the rect and the remaining cell rows hang below. Fills the label's background first when its +0x1d colour id is non-zero. See docs/retail/formats/mfd.md.

entries.name: Label_SetNumber
entries.description: (label, n): _itoa(n, buffer, 10) into a stack buffer and Label_SetText(label, buffer). No caller found by es2_xref.

entries.name: Label_CtorWithAltFont
entries.description: (label, font, panelRelative): Label_Ctor, then stores the same font as the alternate at +0x21 that Label_SetTextWithHotkey draws its one character in. HddCommandScreen_Ctor and MfdFlashCommScreen_Ctor build labels with it.

entries.name: Label_SetText_Thunk
entries.description: Forwards (label, text) to Label_SetText.

entries.name: Label_SetTextWithHotkey
entries.description: (label, text, index): sets the label's text through Label_SetText_Thunk, then, when index is at most the string's length, advances the pen x at 004d1838 by the width of text[0..index) and draws text[index] again in the alternate font at label+0x21. The HDD command display's order rows and 0043f7a4/0043f878 draw their red hotkey letter this way.

entries.name: Label_StaticInitNoOp
entries.description: Borland _INIT_ entry 004a7b28 (priority 0x20): a lone RET. Placed after Label_SetTextWithHotkey, at the end of the Label block, where this binary puts each module's static initialiser.

entries.name: PanelGauge_Ctor
entries.description: PanelGauge base constructor (vtable 0049bc6c). Clears the sensor-dropout state (+0x74 condition, +0x76/+0x77 dark flag, +0x78 deadline, +0x6c sequencer) and defaults both spell ranges to 180-360 coarse ticks, sequences +0x70 = 0 and +0x72 = 1.

entries.name: PanelGauge_TickDropout
entries.description: The sensor dropout's two-state toggle over PanelGauge +0x6c..+0x88: +0x76 = 1 dark, 0 shown. Draws each state's length with PanelGauge_RollDuration from +0x7c/+0x80 (dark) or +0x84/+0x88 (shown) and flips when it passes; with a sequencer at +0x6c the expiry plays sequence +0x70 or +0x72 and flips when it ends. Condition +0x74 == 0 forces dark; every caller skips the call then.

entries.name: PanelGauge_RollDuration
entries.description: (Math_RandomNext(presentation generator 0x4d268f) & 0xffff) % (hi - lo) + lo; returns lo without drawing when hi == lo.

entries.name: Widget_PressChild
entries.description: (gauge, index, flags): unless the child at gauge+0x18[index] is in state 2, calls its press slot (+0x17 vtable, +8) with flags as if it had been clicked, then queues it on the cockpit root's press flash (WidgetRoot_FlashPress) so it shows pressed for 10 coarse ticks. This is how a bound key reaches a button: CockpitWidgets_HandleCommand, ConsoleButtons_HandleCommand, MfdDisplay_KeyDispatch and HddDisplay_KeyDispatch press their buttons through it rather than duplicating each button's own action, and es2_naming.py callers finds more.

entries.name: Widget_BeginPowerUpAnimation
entries.description: Starts one cockpit widget's power-up animation: sets the armed byte at widget+0x8c and stamps widget+0x90 with Time_GetCoarseTicks. Both live on the shared widget base, cleared by its constructor (00438b20) along with the done byte at +0x8d, and each class reads them in its own paint -- for the roving gunsight that is the compass wind-up in Gunsight_UpdateAndPaint. Cdecl with one stack argument and no used return: all eight call sites, in Cockpit_PowerUpTick and the flyer tail of Gau_BuildCockpitWidgets, discard EAX and pop their own argument.

entries.name: VideoMode_ShiftRect
entries.description: (rect{x0, y0, x1, y1}): shifts the x fields left by VideoMode_XCoordShift and the y fields by VideoMode_YCoordShift, scaling authored 320-wide coordinates to the current mode. HddGau_ApplyCoordShift and MfdGau_ApplyCoordShift use it.

entries.name: Widget_ClickSound
entries.description: push 0x11; call Sound_Play. Slot +8 of the secondary (CTLControl subobject) vtable in every button-family gadget class. It is called with the subobject pointer and ignores it, which is why one function serves them all; the slider family replaces it with the empty stub 00439014 and is therefore silent.

entries.name: Widget_ForwardClickToOwner
entries.description: The base OnClick at leaf-widget vtable slot +8, installed by the intermediate class at vtable 0049dee4 and inherited unchanged by the shield facings, the MFD's momentary button class and the HDD buttons. Gated on the left-button bit; calls owner->vtable[0](owner, self, buttonFlags) through the owner pointer the constructor stored at +0x24, then repaints itself and sounds Widget_ClickSound through slot +8 of its second vtable at +0x20.

entries.name: PanelSelectGadget_Dtor
entries.description: PanelSelectGadget's destructor (class record 004594a0), which every button leaf's destructor ends in: (gadget, flags). Reinstalls PanelSelectGadgetVtable at +0x17 and its PanelGadget mixin table at +0x20, Mem_Deletes +0x2c, deletes each of the three objects at +0x30/+0x34/+0x38 through its own vtable +0x18 with flags 3, then Mem_Delete on flags bit 0.
entries.source: DBSIM decompile at 00438e70; class record at 004594a0

entries.name: PanelStateGadget_OnClick
entries.description: PanelStateGadgetVtable +0x08 (gadget, flags): when flags bit 0 is set, flips the state byte +0x40, calls the owner's (+0x24) vtable slot 0 with (owner, gadget, flags), then slot 1 of the vtable at +0x17 and slot 2 of the sub-object at +0x20.

entries.name: PanelSliderGadget_Dtor
entries.description: PanelSliderGadget's destructor (class record 00455599), which every slider leaf's destructor runs on its mixin subobject at +0x3e: (mixin, flags). Reinstalls PanelSliderGadgetVtable at +0, Mem_Deletes +8, deletes the object at +0x10 through its own vtable +0x18 with flags 3, Mem_DeleteArrays +0x14 when set, GLBitmapArray_Dtor(+0x38, 3), then Mem_Delete on flags bit 0.
entries.source: DBSIM decompile at 00438f4c; class record at 00455599

entries.name: Widget_NoClickSound
entries.description: An empty function standing in for Widget_ClickSound at slot +8 of the slider family's secondary vtable. Dragging the throttle, or any other PanelHSliderGadget/PanelVSliderGadget leaf, makes no sound.

entries.name: HSliderGadget_OnClick
entries.description: OnClick (+0x08) of WeaponSliderGadgetVtable, ThrottleHSliderGadgetVtable and PanelHSliderGadgetVtable: the same body as VSliderGadget_OnClick (0043904c) -- owner's slot 0 with (owner, slider, value), then slot 1 at +0x17 and slot 2 of the +0x3e sub-object.

entries.name: VSliderGadget_OnClick
entries.description: PanelVSliderGadgetVtable +0x08 (slider, value): calls the owner's (+0x42) vtable slot 0 with (owner, slider, value), then slot 1 of the vtable at slider+0x17 with the slider, then slot 2 of the sub-object at slider+0x3e. ThrottleSlider_OnValue calls it as its base; for the throttle the owner's slot 0 is ThrottleGauge_OnChildValue. HSliderGadget_OnClick (0043901c) has the same body.

entries.name: BarGraph_Ctor
entries.description: BarGraph constructor (vtable 0049bd78, RTTI name 'BarGraph', 0x2c bytes): copies the rect {x0, y0, x1, y1} to +4..+0x10. LedBarGraph_CtorBase and LedBarGraph_CtorV run it first.

entries.name: BarGraph_NoOp
entries.description: Empty body (push ebp / mov ebp,esp / pop ebp / ret) between BarGraph_Ctor and BarGraph_GetRect. No caller found by es2_xref.

entries.name: BarGraph_GetRect
entries.description: Returns obj+4, the rect {x0, y0, x1, y1} BarGraph_Ctor copies there. ThrottleSlider_PaintV and ThrottleSlider_FlushPaintH call it on the slider's LED bar (+0x7e), 00444f20 and 00444fe0 on the gauge's bar (+0xb5) before CockpitView_RectCornerVisible.

entries.name: LedBarGraph_CtorBase
entries.description: LedBarGraph_CtorBase(obj, rect, range): precomputes span = (end - start) * 0x10000 / range at field 0x14, start at 0x18, end at 0x1c, and seeds the current fill position at 0x20 from the sign of span -- a negative span fills from the far end back, which is how the H and V variants share one implementation.

entries.name: BarGraphH_PaintToValue
entries.description: BarGraphH vtable +0x00 (0049bd60), (bar, value): pos = start (+0x18) + value * span (+0x14) >> 16, or end (+0x1c) minus that for a non-positive span; fills the lit run in colour +0x28 and the rest of the track in +0x24 with Raster_FillRect through the rect at +4, and stores pos at +0x20.

entries.name: BarGraphH_RepaintSpan
entries.description: BarGraphH vtable +0x04, (bar, a, b): orders a and b, clamps them to the track (+0x18..+0x1c), and refills just that span against the stored fill position +0x20 -- the lit part in the current brush, the unlit part in +0x24.

entries.name: LedBarGraph_CtorV
entries.description: Vertical LED bar graph ctor (obj, rect, range) -- the V twin of LedBarGraph_CtorBase (004390c4), taking start/end from the rect's y0/y1 instead of x0/x1. The throttle gauge builds two: .GAU ints [8..11] with range +0x400 (forward fill, above centre) and [12..15] with -0x400 (reverse fill, below). They are not four throttle detent points. NEITHER THROTTLE BAR IS EVER DRAWN: the slider holds them privately, ThrottleSlider_PaintV reads them only for their rects (via BarGraph_GetRect) to widen the region it invalidates, and the bar draw routines 00439398/00439460 have no callers in the image. A cut feature, along with the gauge+0xb1 speed fraction that would have filled them.

entries.name: BarGraphV_PaintToValue
entries.description: BarGraphV vtable +0x00 (0049bd48): BarGraphH_PaintToValue on the y axis, with the sign test on the span reversed.

entries.name: BarGraphV_RepaintSpan
entries.description: BarGraphV vtable +0x04, (bar, a, b): BarGraphH_RepaintSpan on the y axis (+8/+0x10 of the rect).

entries.name: LedBarGraph_Ctor
entries.description: LEDBarGraph constructor: calls LedBarGraph_CtorBase then installs vtable PTR_FUN_0049bd30.

entries.name: LedBarGraph_PaintToValue
entries.description: Paints the bar for a 16.16 fixed-point value: fills to start + (value * span >> 16) via LedBarGraph_FillPinstripe, then installs field 0x24 as the draw colour and covers the remainder.

entries.name: LedBarGraph_RepaintToValue
entries.description: LEDBarGraphH vtable +0x04 (0049bd30), (bar, value): LedBarGraph_PaintToValue's fill without its store -- the pinstriped lit run to the value's position, then the remainder through a temporary {0, +0x24} brush installed at the render context's +0x22c -- leaving the stored position +0x20 untouched.

entries.name: LedBarGraph_FillPinstripe
entries.description: Fills the lit span of an LED bar. Walks the x range twice -- once over even columns, once over odd -- drawing a full-height line each step, with field 0x2c as the even-column colour and 0x30 as the odd. Two near-identical shades interleaved at one pixel read as a single shaded fill rather than two colours.

entries.name: LEDBarGraphV_Ctor
entries.description: LEDBarGraphV constructor (vtable 0049bd18, RTTI name 'LEDBarGraphV', 0x3c bytes): (obj, rect, range) runs LedBarGraph_CtorV, which builds the BarGraphV (0049bd48) part, then installs its own vtable. Its call at 00444edc, range 0x400, is in the case-1 arm of EnergyPoolGauge_Ctor's switch on +0x20, which that constructor sets to 0 just before the switch (00444e41-00444e49), so the gauge takes the case-0 arm and builds the horizontal LEDBarGraph.

entries.name: LedBarGraphV_PaintToValue
entries.description: LEDBarGraphV vtable +0x00 (0049bd18): BarGraphV_PaintToValue with the lit run drawn by the vertical pinstripe fill at 00439a0c instead of a flat colour.

entries.name: LedBarGraphV_Repaint
entries.description: LEDBarGraphV vtable +0x04: redraws the whole bar at the stored fill position +0x20 -- one side through a temporary {0, +0x24} brush at the render context's +0x22c, the other with the vertical pinstripe fill at 00439a0c, which side by the span's sign. Its argument is loaded and not used.

entries.name: LedBarGraphV_FillPinstripe
entries.description: (bar, rect{x0, y0, x1, y1}): LedBarGraph_FillPinstripe turned on its side. Installs a temporary {0, colour} brush at the render context's +0x228 and draws Raster_DrawLine from (x0, y) to (x1, y) on every second row of y0..y1: first the even rows in colour +0x2c, then the odd rows in +0x30; restores the brush. LedBarGraphV_PaintToValue (twice) and LedBarGraphV_Repaint (twice) call it, per es2_xref.

entries.name: LedBmBarGraphH_Ctor
entries.description: LEDBMBarGraphH constructor (table 0049bd00, RTTI 'LEDBMBarGraphH', 0x68 bytes), (bar, rect, range, bitmapA, bitmapB): LedBarGraph_CtorBase, its own table, two GLRectangleRegion members at +0x2c and +0x44 (each with the dword after its vptr zeroed), the two bitmaps at +0x60 and +0x64, and a 5000-byte Mem_NewArray block at +0x5c.

entries.name: LedBmBarGraphH_PaintToValue
entries.description: LEDBMBarGraphH vtable +0x00 (0049bd00): BarGraphH_PaintToValue's layout. For a positive span the lit run and the remainder are drawn by 00439c48 with the bitmaps at +0x64 and +0x60; for a non-positive span both are Raster_FillRect. Stores the position at +0x20.

entries.name: LedBmBarGraphH_RepaintNoOp
entries.description: LEDBMBarGraphH vtable +0x04: push ebp / mov ebp,esp / pop ebp / ret.

entries.name: LedBmBarGraphH_DrawBitmapSpan
entries.description: (bar, bitmap): draws the columns of bitmap that line up with the bar's current rect (+4..+0x10). Sets region +0x2c's rect (+0x34..+0x40) to the bitmap's size (+6 columns, +4 rows, shifted by VideoMode_X/YCoordShift) at the canvas origin (render context 006c5ff4 +0x220/+0x224), and region +0x44's rect (+0x4c..+0x58) to the bar's rect moved left by the track start (+0x18) onto that origin. Points the raster's source page (+0x38) at its draw page (+0x3c), saves the screen under region +0x2c into the 5000-byte block +0x5c (Region_Save), draws bitmap there with Bitmap_Blit and again with VideoMode_BlitBitmap, copies region +0x44 back to the bar's own position with Region_CopyBetweenPages, and restores region +0x2c from the save (Region_Restore). LedBmBarGraphH_PaintToValue calls it with the lit (+0x64) and unlit (+0x60) bitmaps, per es2_xref.

entries.name: LedBmBarGraphV_Ctor
entries.description: LEDBMBarGraphV constructor (table 0049bce8, RTTI 'LEDBMBarGraphV', 0x68 bytes): LedBmBarGraphH_Ctor's body over LedBarGraph_CtorV.

entries.name: LedBmBarGraphV_PaintToValue
entries.description: LEDBMBarGraphV vtable +0x00 (0049bce8): LedBarGraphV_PaintToValue's layout with both runs drawn from the bitmaps at +0x64 (lit) and +0x60 (unlit).

entries.name: LedBmBarGraphV_RepaintNoOp
entries.description: LEDBMBarGraphV vtable +0x04: push ebp / mov ebp,esp / pop ebp / ret.

entries.name: LedBmBarGraphV_DrawBitmapSpan
entries.description: (bar, bitmap): LedBmBarGraphH_DrawBitmapSpan on the y axis -- the bar's rect is moved up by the track start (+0x18) onto the bitmap -- and with a single blit (VideoMode_BlitBitmap) where the H routine blits twice. LedBmBarGraphV_PaintToValue calls it four times, per es2_xref.

entries.name: BarGraphV_ResetToEmpty
entries.description: Vtable +0x08 of BarGraphV, LEDBarGraphV and LEDBMBarGraphV: stores the empty position in +0x20 -- the track end (+0x1c) for a positive span, the start (+0x18) otherwise.

entries.name: BarGraphH_ResetToEmpty
entries.description: Vtable +0x08 of BarGraphH, LEDBarGraphH and LEDBMBarGraphH: stores the empty position in +0x20 -- the track start (+0x18) for a positive span, the end (+0x1c) otherwise.

entries.name: LedBmBarGraphH_Dtor
entries.description: LEDBMBarGraphH's destructor (class record 0043a1a9): (bar, flags). Eight RTL destructor-count decrements -- the bar's levels and its two GLRectangleRegion members' -- then Mem_Delete on flags bit 0. It frees neither the 5000-byte block at +0x5c nor anything else the constructor allocated.
entries.source: DBSIM disassembly at 0043a22a; class record at 0043a1a9

entries.name: LedBmBarGraphV_Dtor
entries.description: LEDBMBarGraphV's destructor (class record 0043a128): LedBmBarGraphH_Dtor's body.
entries.source: DBSIM disassembly at 0043a284; class record at 0043a128

entries.name: MfdStatusScreen_Ctor
entries.description: Constructor for the MFD's status screen, shared by mode 0 (STATUS, F1) and mode 4 (TARGET, F5) -- MfdDisplay_Ctor builds one of each. Lazily loads the `bases`, `vehicles` and `flyers` sprite banks (folder "hba"/"dba" off VideoMode_UseHiResBanks) for target silhouettes, sets the wireframe viewport to inset+(0x2d,0xd)-(0x5f,0x3a), and builds five text labels from tables at 0049bd84 (x0), 0049bd8e (y0) and 0049bd98 (font selector into {ColorSchemePanels[10] WHITE, [14] RED}). The obvious reading of the sprite-bank load is that this is the BASES.DAT type-table loader, and it has been named Bases_LoadTypeTable on that basis; it is not. What this loads is the BASES *sprite* bank for target silhouettes. The BASES *data* file is read by Base_LoadResources (00405fac), which has no relationship to this function. See docs/retail/formats/mfd.md.

entries.name: MfdStatusScreen_Paint
entries.description: Paint for the MFD status screen shared by F1 and F5. Latches the subject from the display's shared block (+0xb9), then branches on its target class: a HERC gets its .PDG paper doll and a twelve-dependent condition scan, a flyer gets flyers-bank frame 0, a structure gets bases/vehicles frame BASES.DAT+0x28. ID: versus TARGET: follows whether the subject is the viewing object or a squadmate; the integrity-versus-range choice for label 4 follows the subject's mission-group side byte, as does the name label's font in the HERC branch; the flyer and structure branches set no font, so that label keeps the last one written (the ctor's [14] RED at first).

entries.name: MfdStatusScreen_Update
entries.description: The status screen's vtable +4: ticks a 30-tick blink latch at +0x34/+0x35, runs the paint, then invalidates the screen rect.

entries.name: MfdStatusScreen_SetCondition
entries.description: Writes the MFD status screen's fourth and fifth labels. Label 4 (screen+0x1c) takes MfdStatusConditionStrings[state] = STRINGS0.STR group 28; state is the caller's, or Damage_ToConditionState(damage) when the caller passes -1. Label 5 (screen+0x20) is composed from literals: "[ " (0049be2c), itoa((0x100 - damage) * 100 >> 8), then "% ]" (0049be2f) -- undamaged reads "[ 100% ]". When the subject is unreadable (screen+0x34 set) it writes "XXXXXX" and "XXX" instead. NOTE: STRINGS0.STR group 10 holds a near-identical five-string set and is dead data -- SimStrings_LoadAll is the only reference to its array. See docs/retail/formats/mfd.md.

entries.name: MfdStatusScreen_StaticInitNoOp
entries.description: Borland _INIT_ entry 004a7b2e (priority 0x20): a lone RET. Placed after MfdStatusScreen_SetCondition, at the end of the block that runs from PanelGauge_Ctor to the MFD status screen.

entries.name: Gunsight_ClickGadget_OnClickNoOp
entries.description: HUDRovingGunsightGadget vtable +0x08 (0049c188), the click surface's OnClick: tests bit 0 of its value argument and returns without acting on it.

entries.name: GunsightChild_CtorBase
entries.description: Base of all nine roving-gunsight children: stores the caller's {x0,y0,x1,y1} rect at +4..+0x10 and sets a stub vtable each subclass overwrites. Children 4, 5 and 6 additionally receive the 38-byte target state block at +0x14.

entries.name: HudSlideBar_CtorBase
entries.description: Base of the front-window HUD's sliding-bar widgets. Stores the rect, defaults the limits to +/-0x4800 at +0x24/+0x26, precomputes the range at +0x2c and seeds the current value at +0x3a to the midpoint. HudSlideBar_SetLimits (0043b3c0) is the vtable +0x10 slot that overrides those limits.

entries.name: HudSlideBar_SetLimits
entries.description: Slide-bar vtable slot +0x10: sets min/max at +0x24/+0x26, recomputes the range and the midpoint value, then runs the recompute slot (+8). The gunsight gives the heading tape and child 7 +/-0xe38 (~20 deg) and the rotation indicator +/-0x38e3 (~80 deg).

entries.name: HudSlideBar_AddDelta
entries.description: Slide-bar vtable slot +0xc: value (+0x3a) -= delta, clamped to [+0x24, +0x26]. The only caller is Gunsight_SetValues, which chooses the delta's sign per child so that a bar either tracks its angle or scrolls against it.

entries.name: HudRotationIndicator_Ctor
entries.description: The manual's Rotation Indicator -- child 2 of the roving-gunsight complex, driven by the turret twist angle. Has no .GAU rect of its own: Gau_RovingGunsightWidget derives it from the heading tape's rect at offset 1104 with literals (+15, -10, 90 wide, 4 tall) and then gives it limits +/-0x38e3.

entries.name: HudRotationIndicator_Recompute
entries.description: Slide-bar slot +8 for the rotation indicator: caches the rect's width at +0x28 as the bar's travel, and the track sprite's blit position at +0x2e/+0x32 -- the rect's top-left lifted by (2 << VideoMode_YCoordShift).

entries.name: HudRotationIndicator_Paint
entries.description: Blits HUD bank frame 11 (182x10) as the track, then the sliding bar: frame 13 (green) while |value| <= 299, frame 12 (yellow) otherwise, at rect.x0 + (value - min) * width / range, minus (15 << VideoMode_XCoordShift) to centre the 62px bar on that point. This is the manual's 'turns yellow and moves left or right if your Turret moves from center'.

entries.name: HudSlideBar_CtorHidden
entries.description: Child 3 of the roving-gunsight complex, driven by the turret pitch angle. Its vtable (0049c20c) has no-op stubs in both the paint (0043b574) and recompute (0043b56c) slots, so the pitch axis has a slide bar that is never drawn -- there is no on-screen pitch indicator.

entries.name: HudSlideBarHidden_RecomputeNoOp
entries.description: VFixRotationGauge vtable +0x08 (0049c20c), the recompute slot of HudSlideBar_CtorHidden's pitch bar: an empty body.

entries.name: HudSlideBarHidden_PaintNoOp
entries.description: VFixRotationGauge vtable +0x00 (0049c20c), the paint slot of HudSlideBar_CtorHidden's pitch bar: an empty body.

entries.name: HudHeadingTape_Ctor
entries.description: Constructor for the HUD heading tick tape. Lazily loads the `hudhtick` sprite bank into DAT_0049be70, selecting folder "hba" or "dba" off VideoMode_UseHiResBanks (the 640-wide vs 320-wide video mode flag).

entries.name: HudHeadingTape_Recompute
entries.description: Slide-bar slot +8 for the heading tick tape: caches the rect width at +0x28, the bank's frame span in Q16 at +0x40, the scroll x at +0x44 and the two frames to blit at +0x48/+0x4c, seeded to the bank's last and first.

entries.name: HudHeadingTape_SetHeading
entries.description: Slot +0xc for the heading tick tape: maps a heading onto the hudhtick bank with Math_Q16Multiply against +0x40, splitting the product into a frame index and a sub-frame pixel offset, both wrapped at the bank's frame count. Writes the scroll x at +0x44 = rect.x0 - offset and the consecutive frame pair at +0x48/+0x4c. The compass degrees are art, so the heading only picks which slice of the strip shows.

entries.name: HudHeadingTape_Paint
entries.description: Narrows the canvas clip to the tape's own rect, then blits the two frames HudHeadingTape_SetHeading chose at +0x44 and +0x44 + rectWidth, so the tape reads as a strip sliding through a window. Restores the four clip fields it borrowed before returning.

entries.name: HudHeadingTape_Repaint
entries.description: HRevRotationGauge vtable +0x04 (0049c1ec): calls the gauge's own slot +0x00, HudHeadingTape_Paint.

entries.name: HudHeadingTape_SetLimits
entries.description: HRevRotationGauge vtable +0x10 (0049c1ec), (tape, lo, hi): +0x40 = (hi - lo) / +0x28, then HudSlideBar_SetLimits(tape, lo, hi).

entries.name: Gunsight_ReticlePaint
entries.description: Gunsight child 4's paint: blits one HUD-bank reticle frame centred on the .GAU reticle point (offset 1136). Frame 0 with no target, with the selection behind the near plane, or with its aim point projecting further than 5 << (the video-mode coordinate shift) from the reticle on either axis; frame 2 inside that tolerance; frame 1 when the armed missile mount also has lock (state block +0x39 = mech+0x9b).

entries.name: Gunsight_TargetIndicator_Ctor
entries.description: Constructor for gunsight child 5, the target box and its off-screen arrow: GunsightChild_CtorBase plus vtable 0049c1c4, whose slot 0 is Gunsight_TargetIndicatorPaint.

entries.name: Gunsight_TargetIndicatorPaint
entries.description: Gunsight child 5's paint: the HUD target box (pip, four mirrored corner brackets, four edge ticks -- HUD frames 3-6 unlocked, 7-10 locked) and, when the target does not project inside the .GAU's offset-1148 rect, a flat-filled arrow at that rect's border pointing at it. Box side is clamp(2*(shapeRadius>>1)*focal/distance, 25, 75) device pixels, the clamp NOT coordinate-shifted. It is the only widget that calls Cockpit_PopRenderContext before drawing and Cockpit_PushCanvasContext after, so the box alone is clipped to the canopy cutout and goes behind the cockpit frame.

entries.name: Gunsight_ClickSurface_Ctor
entries.description: Gunsight child 0: the clickable gunsight surface over the 3D view, on the .GAU's offset-1148 rect. Allocates a gadget and registers it with the cockpit's clickable list, which is the 'gunsight click' path into TargetSelect_SetObject.

entries.name: Gunsight_ClickSurface_Paint
entries.description: Child 0's paint: draws nothing, only tests the cursor point at +0x42/+0x46 against its own rect and reports the result.

entries.name: Gunsight_UnusedChild_Ctor
entries.description: Gunsight child 6. Built on Gunsight_TargetIndicator_Ctor and fed the same target state block at construction, then overwritten with vtable 0049c174 whose paint slot is a bare RET. Never drawn, and never updated per frame either -- Gunsight_SetValues pushes live state to children 4 and 5 only.

entries.name: Gunsight_UnusedChild_Paint
entries.description: Child 6's paint slot: RET. See Gunsight_UnusedChild_Ctor.

entries.name: HudWaypointIndicator_Ctor
entries.description: Gunsight children 7 and 8, the manual's Waypoint Indicator. HudRotationIndicator_Ctor's object given vtable 0049c154 (paint Hud_UpdateWaypointIndicator, AddDelta HudWaypointIndicator_ShiftLimits) plus a label child at +0x4e on the rect it was handed dropped 3 << YCoordShift. Both children are handed the HEADING TAPE's rect and its +/-0xe38 limits; child 7 additionally sets its +0x45 flag, which is what makes it the nav marker's rather than the route's. The eight file-scope globals it writes are the diamond and arrow extents.

entries.name: HudWaypointIndicator_ShiftLimits
entries.description: Slide-bar slot +0xc as the waypoint indicator overrides it: adds the delta to BOTH limits at +0x24/+0x26 rather than to a value the way HudSlideBar_AddDelta does. Gunsight_SetValues sends child 7 the heading delta here, and it has no visible effect -- Hud_UpdateWaypointIndicator reads neither limit, only the range at +0x2c, which an equal shift of both leaves alone.

entries.name: Hud_UpdateWaypointIndicator
entries.description: Paint shared by gunsight children 7 and 8. The +0x45 flag picks the subject: set, NavMarker_Position and colour id 15; clear, the waypoint after the player group's route cursor with colour table entry 0, or -- on a branch gated by DAT_004d2af0, with no writer found by es2_xref.py -- the player's selected target. Takes the ground range with Vec2_DistanceBetween and the bearing as Math_Atan2Guarded(dx, dy) - 0x4000, then draws the error (mech.heading - bearing) as a filled diamond on the tape within +/-0xe38 and as a filled arrow past the rect's right or left end beyond it. Child 8 also composes 'WAYPOINT ' + cursor+1 + ': ' + Hud_WorldUnitsToMetres(range) + ' M.' into its label.

entries.name: Gau_RovingGunsightWidget
entries.description: Large composite 'roving gunsight' HUD-overlay container (matches HUDRovingGunsightGadget/HUDLockingGunsight/HUDPipper class names). Contains the confirmed HTorsoTwist (child rect at 1104, loads bitmap 'hudhtick') and a target-speed text-readout anchor (offsets 1120/1124/1132, format string '000 K/H'). NAVBAR is confirmed NOT here.

entries.name: Gunsight_AddChild
entries.description: Appends a child pointer to the roving-gunsight complex's array at widget+0xd7 (count at +0xff), so construction order is child index. Gunsight_Paint (0043d5c8) walks that array calling each child's slot 0.

entries.name: Gunsight_Paint
entries.description: Paints the front-window HUD: every child of the array at widget+0xd7 in order, then the mission-name label and the speed readout.

entries.name: Gunsight_UpdateAndPaint
entries.description: The roving gunsight's vtable +8, called once a frame from Sim_RenderFrame. Copies CockpitView+0x26c..+0x27e (target, world aim point, pod present flag) into the widget's state block at +0xb7..+0xc9, adds the target's heading (+0xc7), its shape radius from vtable +0x10 (+0xcd) and a literal 2000 (+0xd1), drives child 1, the heading tape, with the NEGATED viewing object's heading -- the sign that makes the compass strip run the same way the simulation's own bearings do -- then runs every child's slot +4 and repaints the whole complex. While the armed byte +0x8c is set and the done byte +0x8d clear, child 1 is given the power-up wind-up ramp (coarseTicks - +0x90) * 0x32 as a ushort instead: climbing from zero for a heading <= 0x8000, counting down from zero above it, latching +0x8d the frame it reaches the heading.

entries.name: Gunsight_SetValues
entries.description: Called once a frame by Player_PerFrameCockpitUpdate with the machine's heading (mech+0x10), turret twist (+0x298) and turret pitch (+0x29a). Caches them at widget+0xb1/+0xb3/+0xb5 and forwards each one's delta to a child's AddDelta slot (+0xc): heading -> child 7 as (new - old), twist -> child 2 (the rotation indicator) as (old - new), pitch -> child 3 as (old - new).

entries.name: Gunsight_GetStateBlock
entries.description: Returns the roving gunsight's 38-byte target/angle state block, widget+0xb1. Callers are Player_PerFrameCockpitUpdate and the three TargetSelect_* entry points, which set byte 36 to 1 to arm the target indicator.

entries.name: Gunsight_ShiftChildRects
entries.description: (gunsight, delta{dx, dy}): subtracts dx from x0/x1 and dy from y0/y1 of the rect (+4..+0x10) of five of the roving gunsight's children: +0xdb (HudHeadingTape), +0xdf (HudRotationIndicator), +0xe3 (the hidden HudSlideBar), +0xe7 (the GunsightChild_CtorBase reticle) and +0xf3 (the first HudWaypointIndicator) -- children 1-4 and 7 in Gau_RovingGunsightWidget's Gunsight_AddChild order. No caller found by es2_xref.

entries.name: Hud_UpdateSpeedReadout
entries.description: Formats the HUD speed text: itoa(Mech_GetDisplaySpeedKph(LocalPlayerMech)) followed by the literal ' K/H' (0049c112). The gadget it writes into is DAT_004d185c, built in Gau_RovingGunsightWidget against the width template '000 K/H'.

entries.name: HudClock_Tick
entries.description: The front window's TIME: clock: when Time_GetCoarseTicks passes the deadline at 004d1888, pushes it to now + 0x3c and carries the ASCII digits MM at 004d1860 and SS at 004d1863 by one second, wrapping 99:59 to 00:00, then rebuilds 'MM:SS' at 004d1868. Gunsight_Paint and Gunsight_UpdateAndPaint call it.

entries.name: Gunsight_PaintAltitudeScale
entries.description: (gunsight): only for a flyer (type record +0x50): from the point at +0x113 draws a scale 0x24 << YCoordShift tall out of Hud_BitmapBank frames 15-18 -- frame 15 at the point and 16 at the foot, a narrow column at frame 15's right edge filled in palette 0x4b up to the terrain height under the machine and edged in 0x49 above it, frame 17 at the machine's height (mech+0x2e), and frame 18 twice as a tape scrolled by height / 50. Heights map from grid+0x110 at the foot to grid+0x114 + 5000 at the top, clamped. For the tape it narrows the installed canvas context to the strip (rect +0x210..+0x21c, mode +0x208 = 1) and zeroes its origin +0x220/+0x224 but leaves the context's translation flag +0x20c at 1, so both tape blits are moved by the strip's own top-left and land right of the strip: the tape is never drawn. Gunsight_Paint and Gunsight_UpdateAndPaint call it inside Cockpit_PushCanvasContext.

entries.name: Gunsight_PaintHudScanner
entries.description: One line: HudScanner_Paint(scannerScreen, gunsight+0x10b). The gunsight complex's only reference to the MFD's scanner screen.

entries.name: GauRovingGunsight_ApplyCoordShift
entries.description: (block): VideoMode_ShiftRect on the first rect, then shifts the twelve x/y pairs at +0x10..+0x34 and +0x3c..+0x70 by VideoMode_XCoordShift / VideoMode_YCoordShift; the int at +0x38 is left alone. Gau_RovingGunsightWrapper runs it on the .GAU block at +1088 (0x440), as Gau_ThrottleWidget does GauThrottle_ApplyCoordShift.

entries.name: Gunsight_StaticInitNoOp
entries.description: Borland _INIT_ entry 004a7b34 (priority 0x20): a lone RET. Placed after GauRovingGunsight_ApplyCoordShift, at the end of the gunsight block, before its class-name strings.

entries.name: Gunsight_ReticleRepaint
entries.description: HUDCrosshairGunsight vtable +0x04 (0049c124): calls the gauge's own slot +0x00, Gunsight_ReticlePaint.

entries.name: HudWaypointIndicator_Repaint
entries.description: HNavGauge vtable +0x04 (0049c154): calls the gauge's own slot +0x00, Hud_UpdateWaypointIndicator.

entries.name: Gunsight_UnusedChild_Repaint
entries.description: HUDPipper vtable +0x04 (0049c174): calls the gauge's own slot +0x00, Gunsight_UnusedChild_Paint.

entries.name: Gunsight_ClickGadget_PaintNoOp
entries.description: HUDRovingGunsightGadget vtable +0x00 (0049c188): an empty body.

entries.name: Gunsight_ClickGadget_InvalidateNoOp
entries.description: HUDRovingGunsightGadget vtable +0x04 (0049c188): an empty body.

entries.name: Gunsight_ClickSurface_Repaint
entries.description: HUDRovingGunsight vtable +0x04 (0049c1b0): calls the gauge's own slot +0x00, Gunsight_ClickSurface_Paint.

entries.name: Gunsight_TargetIndicatorRepaint
entries.description: HUDLockingGunsight vtable +0x04 (0049c1c4): calls the gauge's own slot +0x00, Gunsight_TargetIndicatorPaint.

entries.name: HudSlideBarHidden_Repaint
entries.description: VFixRotationGauge vtable +0x04 (0049c20c): calls the gauge's own slot +0x00, which for this class is HudSlideBarHidden_PaintNoOp.

entries.name: HudRotationIndicator_Repaint
entries.description: HFixRotationGauge vtable +0x04 (0049c22c): calls the gauge's own slot +0x00, HudRotationIndicator_Paint.

entries.name: MfdRadarScreen_Ctor
entries.description: Constructor for the MFD's SCANNER screen (mode 3), the largest of the six at 0x524 bytes. Builds the plot geometry (dish at inset+(0x26,1), centre at inset+(0x41,0x1c), plot radius 0x19 GAU), the 100-entry contact vector at +0x68 and the four corner readouts. Binds MFD bank frames 14 (dish) and 15 (turret wedge). Range comes from MfdScannerRanges 004d1cf4 = 50000/100000/200000 world units (300/600/1200 m at 1000 units = 6 m) indexed by the zoom field at MfdDisplay+0xc5, default 2. The `radar` bank's 10-frame sweep is NOT this screen's -- MfdDisplay_Update plays it over the same dish on a switch to mode 3. See docs/retail/formats/mfd-scanner.md.

entries.name: MfdRadarScreen_Update
entries.description: Rebuilds the SCANNER screen's contact list from the live object list: skips the viewing machine, anything dead (+0x99/+0xa4), a group still awaiting deployment (group+0x14), an invulnerable structure type (class 1 with BASES.DAT +0x1e), a Cybrid not currently radar-visible (+0x95), and anything past the current display range on the ground plane. Survivors are rotated by Math_BuildRotation2D(-heading) and stored as (x, -y) with a colour id per class and side, so the plot is hull-relative nose-up. Also mirrors mech+0x96 into +0x34 and re-presses PASS or ACTIVE when it changed. Its hostile branch's blinking obj+0x1aa last-known-position marker is DEAD CODE: every constructor sets obj+0xa7 = 1 and nothing clears it. See docs/retail/formats/mfd-scanner.md.

entries.name: MfdRadarScreen_UpdateAndPaint
entries.description: MFDRadar vtable +0x04 (0049c328), the MFD screen's per-frame slot: MfdRadarScreen_Update, then the screen's own slot +0x00, MfdRadarScreen_Paint.

entries.name: MfdRadarScreen_Paint
entries.description: Paints the SCANNER screen: floods the dish rect with raw palette index 0x11, blits MFD frame 15 rotated about its own corner at the plot centre by turretTwist - 0x6000, covers it with frame 14, draws the passive-range ring (ellipse outline, colour id 11) only when passive and 140000 < range, then frame 17 (reference line), frame 18 (player marker), each contact as a 2x2 fill, frame 16 over the selected target, and the four RNG:/TRG: readouts as right-aligned zero-padded four-character fields. See docs/retail/formats/mfd-scanner.md.

entries.name: HudScanner_Paint
entries.description: The front window's floating scanner repeater. Belongs to the GUNSIGHT complex, not the MFD: Gunsight_Paint and Gunsight_UpdateAndPaint reach it through the one-line Gunsight_PaintHudScanner after the child loop.
