entries.description: HDDSelectGadget vtable +0x0c (0049d60c): while the button is on screen, at stage 2 (+0x1f) repaints it through its own slot +0x00; at stage 1 repaints buttons 10-12 (index +0x28) the same way and copies any other to the cockpit with Widget_DrawToCockpit(0, button); decrements the stage either way.

entries.name: HddButton_OnClick
entries.description: HDDSelectGadget vtable +0x08 (0049d60c), (button, value): unless the button is lit (+0x40) and is button 0 or 1 (+0x28), toggles the lit byte, calls the owning display's (+0x24) slot +0x00 with (display, button, value), invalidates itself (slot +0x04) and runs its PanelGadget mixin's (+0x20) slot +0x08, the click sound. So buttons 0 and 1 latch on.

entries.name: HDDisplayGadget_Ctor
entries.description: Constructor for HDDisplayGadget (object size 0x24), the Heads-Down Display's clickable-surface base; HddMarker_Ctor derives HDDMapGadget from it. Class name from the descriptor record at 004505ab.

entries.name: HddGau_ApplyCoordShift
entries.description: Pre-pass over the .GAU HDD block: adds 0x28 to the origin's y, then shifts every rect in the block by VideoMode_X/YCoordShift. The bias is what turns each retail file's authored origin (0,197) into (0,237), i.e. the same canvas origin the herc's own .VUE gives view 1 -- the row .HB1 is blitted at.

entries.name: HddDisplay_StaticInit
entries.description: Static initialiser (Borland _INIT_ entry 004a7b46, priority 0x20): zeroes the two dwords of HddStaticFramePos (0049d240, 0049d244).

entries.name: PanelStateGadget_OnClickThunk
entries.description: The this-adjusting thunk at primary vtable +0x30 of PanelStateGadget's vtable block, in the table for its PanelGadget subobject at +0x20: subtracts 0x20 from this and jumps to PanelStateGadget_OnClick.

entries.name: PanelStateGadget_Dtor
entries.description: PanelStateGadget's destructor (class record 0044c054): (gadget, flags). One RTL destructor-count decrement, PanelSelectGadget_Dtor(gadget, 0), then Mem_Delete on flags bit 0.
entries.source: DBSIM disassembly at 0044c0ba; class record at 0044c054

entries.name: CommBox_ElementCtor
entries.description: (box): Rtl_VectorNew's per-element constructor for HddDisplay_Ctor's three 0x14e-byte comm-box gauge records at hdd+0x12d (PUSH 0x44c0e7 at 00448d1c, count 3, mode 1): runs Rtl_VectorNew over the box's 30 x 8-byte array at +0x3d with Rtl_ReturnArg as the element constructor and returns its argument. The LEAs of +0x1d (the video rect CommBox_PushVideoClip reads) and +0x2d are inlined empty member constructors.

entries.name: HDDSelectGadget_OnClickThunk
entries.description: The this-adjusting thunk at primary vtable +0x30 of HDDSelectGadget's vtable block, in the table for its PanelGadget subobject at +0x20: subtracts 0x20 from this and jumps to HddButton_OnClick.

entries.name: HDDSelectGadget_FlushDeferredPaintThunk
entries.description: The this-adjusting thunk at primary vtable +0x28 of HDDSelectGadget's vtable block, in the table for its PanelGadget subobject at +0x20: subtracts 0x20 from this and jumps to HddButton_FlushDeferredPaint.

entries.name: HDDSelectGadget_PaintThunk
entries.description: The this-adjusting thunk at primary vtable +0x24 of HDDSelectGadget's vtable block, in the table for its PanelGadget subobject at +0x20: subtracts 0x20 from this and jumps to HddButton_Paint.

entries.name: HDDisplay_ShowNoOp
entries.description: HDDisplay vtable +0x0c (0049d668), the screen base's Show slot (HddCommandScreen_Show is the map screen's): an empty body.

entries.name: HddButton_Dtor
entries.description: HDDSelectGadget's destructor (class record 0044c175), HddButton_Ctor's object: (button, flags). Two RTL destructor-count decrements, PanelSelectGadget_Dtor(button, 0), then Mem_Delete on flags bit 0.
entries.source: DBSIM disassembly at 0044c1f0; class record at 0044c175

entries.name: HddMap_WorldToScreen
entries.description: Projects a world point to screen: view transform (Raster_ModelToView), Raster_PerspectiveDivide, Raster_ProjectToScreen.

entries.name: HddCommandScreen_Ctor
entries.description: The [F7] command display. Builds the map viewport as the screen rect inset (4<<XCoordShift, 2<<YCoordShift) with its right edge at the order column's left minus the same, a 0x239-byte offscreen map render target centred on the zone, 140 map marker gadgets (not registered as clickable), and nine label rows down the order column at (y1-y0)/9 pitch: row 0 the incoming-message label in ColorSchemePanels[2], rows 1-8 the orders in [1] with [2] as the hotkey alternate. Registers exactly two clickables, in this order: an HDDListGadget over the whole order column at screen+0x35, then a second over the map viewport at screen+0x39. Both run before HddDisplay_Ctor builds its own fifteen buttons, so they precede those in the flat list.

entries.name: HddCommandScreen_Repaint
entries.description: Floods the screen rect with colour id 19, refreshes the order rows, draws the selected order's 2px marker bar in id 15, repaints the two magnifier buttons, builds the map markers while the screen's +0x109 latch is 0 (HddCommandScreen_BuildMapMarkers sets it), rasterizes the map, and sets the +0x13a label's text from +0x140 while +0x13e is nonzero and +0x144 is 0.

entries.name: HddCommandScreen_Update
entries.description: Vtable slot 1: services a queued map click, advances the half-second blink, re-fonts the order rows whose selection changed, and redraws the map when anything moved it.

entries.name: HddCommandScreen_KeyDispatch
entries.description: Vtable slot 4 of the [F7] command display: switches on a DOS scancode, not a widget index. D/A/F/T/G/O/C/E feed their row to the order column's click (HddCommandScreen_SynthesizeListClick), so each acts as a click on that row, ,< and .> step through them, Tab cycles the eligible unit for ATTACK ENEMY or DEFEND POSITION, Enter feeds the map's click -- arm 1 with a held unit for ATTACK ENEMY or DEFEND POSITION, arm 0 for DEFEND POSITION without one and for PATROL GRIDPOINT and GOTO GRIDPOINT, nothing for ATTACK ENEMY without one -- keypad 5 recentres the map, and X and Backspace press the XMIT and CANCEL widgets. Tab is the case with sounds of its own: Sound_Play(0x1a) when the unit slot +0x15c holds a unit after the cycle and it becomes the pick, 0x1b when the slot is empty. X only presses XMIT, through Widget_PressChild.

entries.name: HddCommandScreen_Show
entries.description: Command display vtable +0xc, run by HddDisplay_SetPage on the incoming page. Clears the state byte on three widgets: the order-column list gadget at screen+0x35, and the display's XMIT and CANCEL buttons. It does NOT touch the map viewport gadget at screen+0x39 -- no writer of state 2 into that widget is found (the cockpit's press code writes only 1 and 0 through the shared clickable list), so the map region is registered at state 0 and stays hit-testable on the damage detail page too.

entries.name: HddCommandScreen_Hide
entries.description: Command display vtable +8, run by HddDisplay_SetPage on the outgoing page. Sets state 2 on the order-column list gadget at screen+0x35 and on XMIT and CANCEL. See HddCommandScreen_Show for the map viewport gadget it leaves alone.

entries.name: HddMap_ZoomOut
entries.description: One magnifier step out, up to the scale that fits the whole mission box.

entries.name: HddMap_ZoomIn
entries.description: One magnifier step in, down to a floor of 60000 (8.8 fixed world units per pixel).

entries.name: HddMap_PanLeft
entries.description: Scrolls the map one pan step toward the mission box's minimum x, or by whatever room is left.

entries.name: HddMap_PanRight
entries.description: The same toward maximum x.

entries.name: HddMap_PanUp
entries.description: The same toward maximum y.

entries.name: HddMap_PanDown
entries.description: The same toward minimum y.

entries.name: HddMap_ClampAndInstallView
entries.description: Clamps the map centre so the viewport stays inside the mission box grown by 60000 on every edge, then writes the centre and the scale into the map view projection.

entries.name: HddMap_ToViewport
entries.description: Adds the map viewport origin and half-extent to a projected point.

entries.name: HddMap_FromViewport
entries.description: The inverse of HddMap_ToViewport.

entries.name: HddCommandScreen_InstallMapContext
entries.description: (screen): sets the rect of the screen's own render context (screen+0x10, +0x210..+0x21c) to the map viewport rect at +0x71..+0x7d, less the current context's origin (+0x220/+0x224) and the view offsets 004d25da/004d25de, installs it with Raster_InstallRenderContext and returns it. HddCommandScreen_DrawMap and HddMarker_Paint draw through it.

entries.name: HddCommandScreen_BlinkTick
entries.description: Sets 0049d6ac and 0049d6ae to 1 and flips the blink phase 0049d6ad; marks the widget at *(0049d6b0 + 8) for repaint (+0x10f = 1, paint count +0xb0 = 2); and counts 0049d6b0+0x13e down when non-zero, setting +0x144 when it reaches 0. HddCommandScreen_Update calls it every 0x1e coarse ticks.

entries.name: HddCommandScreen_QueueListClick
entries.description: Records a pending list click on the command display: sets the flag at screen+0x14d, stores which gadget at +0x14e and the point at +0x152 (biased by the view-offset globals 004d25da/de), copies CockpitMouse_DoubleClick to +0x15b, and marks the display dirty. HddCommandScreen_HandleListClick drains it.

entries.name: HddCommandScreen_HandleListClick
entries.description: Drains the pending list click and branches on which gadget it was. Order column (screen+0x35): walks the eight row rects and stops at the first hit, using STRICT inequalities on all four edges -- unlike Widget_HitTest's inclusive test -- so a row's own boundary lines are dead. With no pilot selected it prints the SELECT PILOT message instead; a hit on the row already armed presses XMIT through Widget_PressChild when both the pick flag +0x104 and +0x15b are set, and otherwise does nothing; any other row calls HddCommandScreen_SelectOrder. After either, with +0x15a set, it moves the cursor to the row's centre (Cursor_SyncPosition), then clears +0x15a. Map viewport (screen+0x39): stores the point as the map cursor at +0x11d sets the armed flag at +0x11c and flags the display for a full repaint.

entries.name: HddCommandScreen_SynthesizeListClick
entries.description: (screen, gadget, pick): the keyboard's entry into the queued-click path, so key and mouse converge before anything is decided. Sets +0x15a to 1. For the order column (+0x35) it feeds the corner of row rect pick-10 (the rect at +0x3d + (pick-10)*4, its +4/+8 fields plus 1). For the map viewport (+0x39), pick 0 feeds Cursor_GetPosition rebased through the canvas context's +0x210/+0x214 and +0x220/+0x224, and pick 1 projects the unit at +0x15c (its +0x26 position) through the map's view (+0x14, eye +0x18/+0x1c/+0x20) with HddMap_ToViewport. Each feeds HddCommandScreen_QueueListClick.
entries.signature: void __cdecl HddCommandScreen_SynthesizeListClick(int screen, void *gadget, int pick)

entries.name: HddCommandScreen_PickTarget
entries.description: Resolves a map click for an armed order. For ATTACK ENEMY and DEFEND POSITION it hit-tests the point (HddCommandScreen_HitTestMarker) and takes a unit whose group side byte (type+0x12) is 1 for ATTACK ENEMY or 0 for DEFEND POSITION as the pick, into +0x15c and the selected pilot's pick slot. Otherwise DEFEND POSITION, PATROL GRIDPOINT and GOTO GRIDPOINT take the map cursor (+0x374) as a gridpoint pick; ATTACK ENEMY without an eligible unit takes nothing. A pick sets the pick flag +0x104, plays Sound_Play(0x14) bptslct and clears the message row. Always clears the cursor's armed flag +0x11c and sets DAT_0049d6ae.

entries.name: HddCommandScreen_PickPilot
entries.description: (screen): hit-tests the map cursor (+0x11d) against the markers with HddCommandScreen_HitTestMarker; when that finds an object whose +0x99 is clear and Squad_IndexOf places it in a squad slot, calls HddDisplay_SelectPilot on the heads-down display for that slot, with no test of the slot already selected. Then clears the armed flag +0x11c and sets DAT_0049d6ae. The manual's 'select the pilot's marker on the map'.

entries.name: HddCommandScreen_HitTestMarker
entries.description: Turns a map viewport point into world units and returns the first live object within the marker click radius of it.

entries.name: HddCommandScreen_SelectOrder
entries.description: (screen, order): arms one of the eight orders (10-17), or clears with -1. Orders 0xb-0xe (ATTACK ENEMY to GOTO GRIDPOINT) call Cockpit_SetOffForwardCursor(2), put prompt 3 (0xb) or 2 (the rest) from the DAT_004d16bc table in the message row, and set +0x103 (wants a pick) to 1, +0x380 to 1 and the ready flag +0x104 to 0; any other order, -1 included, calls Cockpit_SetOffForwardCursor(0), sets +0x103 to 0, +0x104 to 1 and +0x380 to 0, and clears the message row. When the order changes it keeps the old one at +0x81, stores the new at +0x5d, and marks the display (DAT_0049d6b0+8) for repaint (+0x10f = 1, +0xb0 = 2).

entries.name: HddCommandScreen_SelectPilot
entries.description: (screen, slot): moves the comm-box selection to slot, or none with -1. When a pilot is selected (+0x105) it toggles that pilot's button and, when an order is armed (+0x5d not -1), runs HddCommandScreen_SelectOrder(screen, -1) and clears that pilot's record flag (+0xa6 in its 0x2a-byte record), +0x104, +0x381, +0x15c and +0x103 and sets +0x144 -- whether or not the new slot is the same pilot. Stores the slot; -1 runs HddCommandScreen_DisableOrders, any other toggles the new pilot's button, runs HddCommandScreen_EnableOrders and sets +0x381. Marks the display for repaint.

entries.name: HddCommandScreen_FillOrderRecord
entries.description: Copies the armed order's committed pick into the transmit record: a gridpoint pick into the record's x/y/z at +0x06/+0x0a/+0x0e, a unit pick into its subject pointer at +0x12. Which of the two is decided by the pick kind latched in the selected pilot's pick slot (three 0x2a-byte slots at +0x85, indexed by +0x105). With no pilot selected (+0x105 = -1) it writes nothing. HddCommandScreen_CommitPick latches a kind when the armed order wants a pick (+0x103) and leaves the slot's kind as it was otherwise, so a pickless order writes that pilot's last pick again. This is what settles the record's layout. Args derived from disassembly: [EBP+8], [EBP+0xc].

entries.name: HddCommandScreen_CommitPick
entries.description: Promotes the selected pilot's pending map pick (slot +0x85 + pilot*0x2a) to its committed one -- the point triple or the subject pointer, per the order's pick kind -- and latches that kind alongside it, so the following HddCommandScreen_FillOrderRecord knows which to copy. XMIT calls the pair in that order. Args derived from disassembly: [EBP+8] only.

entries.name: HddCommandScreen_CancelTransmission
entries.description: CANCEL: drops the armed order, the map pick and the pilot selection together.

entries.name: HddCommandScreen_SetMessageRow
entries.description: (screen, text, flag): fills the message row above the order list. Given no text it picks from STRINGS0 group 32 (DAT_004d16bc): with no order armed that wants a pick (+0x103), SELECT PILOT with no pilot selected (+0x105 = -1) and SELECT COMMAND with one; DESIGNATE TARGET for ATTACK ENEMY; DESIGNATE LOCATION for DEFEND POSITION, PATROL GRIDPOINT and GOTO GRIDPOINT. Given text it shows that. A flag of 1 also sets +0x13e to 6.

entries.name: HddCommandScreen_ClearMessageRow
entries.description: (screen): floods the message-row label's rect (*(screen+0x13a)+4) in the colour at 004d3c26, copies it to the other page with Widget_DrawToCockpit(1, rect) and clears +0x144. HddCommandScreen_SetMessageRow runs it before writing a prompt, HddCommandScreen_Update when +0x144 is set, and the select, pick and transmit paths.

entries.name: HddCommandScreen_DrawOrderHighlight
entries.description: Blits HDD bank frame 2 + state (or 4) -- the 116x18 selected-order bar -- at an order label's own text position.

entries.name: HddCommandScreen_RedrawOrderHighlight
entries.description: (screen, pressed): when the selection +0x5d is not -1, HddCommandScreen_DrawOrderHighlight(screen, +0x5d - 10, pressed, 0). HddButton_Paint, read alongside it, passes its own press byte (+0x1b).

entries.name: HddCommandScreen_RefreshOrders
entries.description: Re-fonts and re-texts the eight order rows from STRINGS0 group 0 entries 10-17, passing each entry's single attribute byte as the index of its hotkey character within its own text. An available order draws in ColorSchemePanels[1] CPGREEN with the hotkey in [2] CPRED, an unavailable one wholly in [0] CPBLUE, and the selected one in [3] CPYLW.

entries.name: HddCommandScreen_BuildMapMarkers
entries.description: Fills the map's marker gadgets, appending from the screen's +0x10a count, and sets the +0x109 latch HddCommandScreen_Repaint tests before calling it: up to 9 waypoint markers from the player's own route (icons 0x4e+), then one per object in the three global object lists, then a gadget for the player's dropped nav marker (icon 0x57), built unconditionally; HddCommandScreen_DrawMap positions and paints it only while NavMarker_Position returns one. Gadgets past the last used one, out of the 140 allocated, are released.

entries.name: HddCommandScreen_AddObjectMarker
entries.description: One object's map marker: icon from its target class and its group's side byte, size from HddMarker_SetSize, and for the two structure classes the colour and reference size its range falloff draws a box with.

entries.name: HddCommandScreen_DrawMap
entries.description: Everything inside the command display's map viewport, in order: flood, re-centre on the player plus the pan offset, clamp, terrain raster, the 1200 m grid, the mission border rect, then every marker with the selected pilot's link line and the chosen unit's box.

entries.name: HddCommandScreen_DrawMarker
entries.description: (screen, marker, isSelectedPilot): paints one marker of the command display's map. Its point is the marker's object's (+0x38) position (+0x26/+0x2a), or its own +0x3c/+0x40/+0x44 with no object. An object flagged +0xa4 or +0x99 on a group whose side (+0x12) is non-zero is not drawn; one with +0x95 clear on a group with a side or awaiting deployment (+0x14) blinks with coarse-tick bit 0x20 and is drawn at its +0x1aa point instead (not at all when +0xa7 is set). Projects the point into the map viewport (HddMap_ToViewport) and moves the marker there (0045242c). With isSelectedPilot and an object it draws the link line to the armed order's pick in the pilot's HudColorTable colour, then returns before painting while a pilot is selected (screen +0x381) and the blink flag 0049d6ad is set. A marker with +0x4c set records its distance from screen +0x18 at +0x53. Paints through slot 0 of the vtable whose pointer is at marker +0x17. HddCommandScreen_DrawMap calls it for every marker. See docs/retail/formats/heads-down-display.md.

entries.name: HddCommandScreen_TogglePilotButton
entries.description: (screen, index): flips bit 0 of byte +0x36 of the button at (screen+0x31)[index] and calls slot 1 of the vtable at the button's +0x17 on it. HddCommandScreen_SelectPilot calls it on the previous selection (+0x105) and on the new one.

entries.name: HddCommandScreen_EnableOrders
entries.description: Sets all eight order-availability bytes, which is the whole of what makes the order list live.

entries.name: HddCommandScreen_DisableOrders
entries.description: Clears all eight, greying the list back to CPBLUE.

entries.name: HddCommandScreen_NextOrder
entries.description: Steps the armed order forward one place, wrapping; returns at once with none armed.

entries.name: HddCommandScreen_PreviousOrder
entries.description: The same backwards.

entries.name: HddMap_RecomputePanStep
entries.description: Recomputes the arrow pan step from the current zoom: 5000 world units at the closest view rising to 50000 at the widest.

entries.name: HddCommandScreen_CycleHostileUnit
entries.description: (screen): HddCommandScreen_CycleUnit(screen, 1). HddCommandScreen_KeyDispatch's Tab stores the result at +0x15c while ATTACK ENEMY (0xb) is armed.

entries.name: HddCommandScreen_CycleFriendlyUnit
entries.description: (screen): HddCommandScreen_CycleUnit(screen, 0). HddCommandScreen_KeyDispatch's Tab stores the result at +0x15c while DEFEND POSITION (0xc) is armed.

entries.name: HddCommandScreen_CycleUnit
entries.description: (screen, side): the next unit for Tab. When the pick at +0x15c is null or of another group side (+0x45 -> +0x12), returns maybe_GlobalLiveObjectList's first object if HddCommandScreen_IsEligibleUnit(screen, obj, side) passes it, else walks on from the second. When the pick is of that side, walks the list to it first -- a loop with no exit when the pick is not on the list -- and goes on from the object after it. The walk wraps to the list's head and ends where it began, the pick or the first object tested last; it returns the first eligible object, or 0 when none is.

entries.name: HddCommandScreen_IsEligibleUnit
entries.description: (screen, obj, side): 1 when obj's group side (+0x45 -> +0x12) is side, obj is not destroyed (+0x99), HddCommandScreen_IsOnMap(screen, obj+0x26), obj+0x98 is set, and side is 0 or Ai_KnowsObject(the cockpit's machine, obj).

entries.name: HddCommandScreen_IsOnMap
entries.description: (screen, pos): copies the screen's eye +0x18/+0x1c/+0x20 into its map view (+0x14), installs that projection, projects pos (y negated after the divide) and maps it with HddMap_ToViewport; returns whether it lands inside the map rect +0x71..+0x7d.

entries.name: HddMarker_Ctor
entries.description: One of the command display map's 140 marker gadgets. Lazily loads the `icons` sprite bank into DAT_0049d6b4, folder selected by VideoMode_PanelMode == 3.

entries.name: HddMarker_Paint
entries.description: Paints one map marker: eight-octant heading frame plus its nudge for a HERC or flyer, a range-scaled box for a structure far from the map centre, and the scanner circle for a radar structure.

entries.name: HddMarker_Invalidate
entries.description: HDDMapGadget vtable +0x04 (0049d9b0): this->[0x1f] = 2, and marks the command map screen (*(DAT_0049d6b0+8)) for a repaint: its +0x10f = 1 and +0xb0 = 2.

entries.name: HddMarker_FlushDeferredPaint
entries.description: HDDMapGadget vtable +0x0c (0049d9b0): when the marker is on screen and at stage 2 (+0x1f), paints it through slot +0x00 (HddMarker_Paint) with +0x37 raised for the call, copies it to the cockpit with Widget_DrawToCockpit(1, marker), and sets the stage to 0.

entries.name: HddMarker_OnClick
entries.description: HDDMapGadget vtable +0x08 (0049d9b0), (marker, value): clears +0x37 when bit 0 of value is set.

entries.name: Widget_PaintUnlessByte37
entries.description: (widget): calls slot 0 (Paint) of the vtable at widget+0x17 on it unless the byte at +0x37 is set. HddCommandScreen_Update runs it on the selected pilot button ((screen+0x31)[+0x105]) and then clears that button's +0x1f.
entries.source: DBSIM decompile at 0044f61c; slot meaning from known_vtables.json CockpitWidgetVtable

entries.name: HddMarker_SetSize
entries.description: Sets a marker gadget's square extent and the half-extent its icon is drawn back by, so the icon lands centred on the object.

entries.name: HDDListGadget_Ctor
entries.description: Constructor for HDDListGadget (object size 0x2c), one of the two order lists HddCommandScreen_Ctor builds. Derives from PanelListGadget. Class name from the descriptor record at 00450737.

entries.name: HDDListGadget_OnClick
entries.description: Vtable +8 for both of the command display's list gadgets. Left button only; queues the click through HddCommandScreen_QueueListClick with the owner at the gadget's +0x28 and the cockpit click point at DAT_004d1e67. Nothing is decided here. It makes no other call, its PanelGadget mixin's click slot included, so the click makes no sound of its own.
entries.signature: void __cdecl HDDListGadget_OnClick(int gadget, unsigned char buttonFlags)

entries.name: HddMap_BuildTerrainRaster
entries.description: Builds the map raster HddMapTerrainRaster once per mission. Cell index = min(height,0x7f)/8 + 16, 0 off the grid. Grown mission box shifted to cells x0..x1, y0..y1 (unclamped); upscale s = min(400/(y1-y0+1), 640/(x1-x0+1)); bitmap (x1-x0+1)*s by (y1-y0+1)*s, zeroed. Rows y1 down to y0+1, columns x0 to x1-1, each an s-pixel square split bottom-left to top-right into two triangles filled by Raster_FillContourTriangle.

entries.name: HddMap_DrawTerrain
entries.description: Blits the map raster HddMapTerrainRaster through the installed map projection: projects the grown mission box's own corners (world units, not cell edges), turns the top-left corner about the map centre by the angle with Math_Rotate2DPoint in screen space, and hands the bitmap to Bitmap_BlitRotatedUnpacked with the same angle. The command display passes 0; MfdMapScreen_Paint passes the machine's heading.

entries.name: HddCommandScreen_StaticInit
entries.description: Static initialiser (Borland _INIT_ entry 004a7b4c, priority 0x20): stores the int16 triple (0xc000, 0, 0) at HddMapView_Angles (0049d6c0) and runs GLBitmap_Ctor on HddMapTerrainRaster (004d1d7a). HddCommandScreen_StaticDtor is its _EXIT_ counterpart.

entries.name: HddCommandScreen_StaticDtor
entries.description: HddCommandScreen_StaticInit's _EXIT_ routine (Borland _EXIT_ entry 004a7c42): GLBitmap_Dtor(HddMapTerrainRaster, 2).

entries.name: PanelListGadget_PaintNoOp
entries.description: Empty body. The Paint slot +0 of PanelListGadget (vtable 0049d904, RTTI name 'PanelListGadget', 0x28 bytes), MFDListGadget (0049cee0) and HDDListGadget (0049d944), and the target of the panel-gadget thunks 00450565 and 0045078f.
entries.source: DBSIM disassembly at 004504fc; RTTI at vtable-0xc

entries.name: PanelListGadget_InvalidateNoOp
entries.description: Empty body. The Invalidate slot +4 of PanelListGadget (0049d904), MFDListGadget and HDDListGadget.

entries.name: PanelListGadget_FlushDeferredPaintNoOp
entries.description: Empty body. The FlushDeferredPaint slot +0xc of PanelListGadget (0049d904), MFDListGadget and HDDListGadget, and the target of the panel-gadget thunks 0045055b and 00450785.

entries.name: PanelListGadget_FlushDeferredPaintNoOpThunk
entries.description: The this-adjusting thunk at primary vtable +0x28 of PanelListGadget's vtable block, in the table for its PanelGadget subobject at +0x20: subtracts 0x20 from this and jumps to PanelListGadget_FlushDeferredPaintNoOp.

entries.name: PanelListGadget_PaintNoOpThunk
entries.description: The this-adjusting thunk at primary vtable +0x24 of PanelListGadget's vtable block, in the table for its PanelGadget subobject at +0x20: subtracts 0x20 from this and jumps to PanelListGadget_PaintNoOp.

entries.name: HddPilotPick_ElementCtor
entries.description: (slot): returns its argument -- Rtl_VectorNew's per-element constructor for HddCommandScreen_Ctor's three 0x2a-byte pilot pick slots at screen+0x85 (PUSH 0x4505ef at 0044c2a6, count 3, mode 1), the slots HddCommandScreen_CommitPick and HddCommandScreen_FillOrderRecord index by +0x105. The LEA of +0xc is the inlined empty constructor of the pending pick point.

entries.name: GLRect_Dtor
entries.description: GLRect vtable +0x18 (0049d984, RTTI 'GLRect', 0x14 bytes; bases GLPrimitive and Box32_2d at +4), the destructor its class record names: (rect, flags). Three RTL destructor-count decrements, then Mem_Delete on flags bit 0.
entries.source: DBSIM disassembly at 0045068d; class record at 00450631

entries.name: HDDListGadget_OnClickThunk
entries.description: The this-adjusting thunk at primary vtable +0x30 of HDDListGadget's vtable block, in the table for its PanelGadget subobject at +0x20: subtracts 0x20 from this and jumps to HDDListGadget_OnClick.

entries.name: HDDListGadget_FlushDeferredPaintNoOpThunk
entries.description: The this-adjusting thunk at primary vtable +0x28 of HDDListGadget's vtable block, in the table for its PanelGadget subobject at +0x20: subtracts 0x20 from this and jumps to PanelListGadget_FlushDeferredPaintNoOp.

entries.name: HDDListGadget_PaintNoOpThunk
entries.description: The this-adjusting thunk at primary vtable +0x24 of HDDListGadget's vtable block, in the table for its PanelGadget subobject at +0x20: subtracts 0x20 from this and jumps to PanelListGadget_PaintNoOp.

entries.name: HddDamageScreen_Ctor
entries.description: The [F8] damage detail. Resolves the four colour ids at HddDamageColorIds through HudColorTable in place -- nothing ever reads them -- then builds 13 rows of two labels each down the damage column: a name from the column's left edge + 0x1e<<XCoordShift, and a value column whose width is the measured width of the literal '100'. Rows are 4<<YCoordShift tall at 7<<YCoordShift pitch, all in ColorSchemePanels[1] on colour id 19. Also builds the subject caption at the screen's bottom-left and a centred no-data label, then calls HddDamageScreen_SetView(obj, 0).

entries.name: HddDamageScreen_Repaint
entries.description: HDDDamage vtable +0x00 (0049dab0): sets +0x80 to -1, then HddDamageScreen_Update(screen, 0).

entries.name: HddDamageScreen_Tick
entries.description: HDDDamage vtable +0x04 (0049dab0), the per-frame slot: HddDamageScreen_Update(screen, 1).

entries.name: HddDamageScreen_SetView
entries.description: Selects the damage category and its row count: 0 structural = 0x13 rows, 1 internal = 0xc, 2 weapons = the subject's own fitted weapon count. The manual binds these to [S], [I] and [W], and to the display's up/down arrow buttons.

entries.name: HddDamageScreen_NextView
entries.description: Steps the damage category forward, 2 wrapping to 0, through HddDamageScreen_SetView. Reached from HddDisplay_HandleWidgetPress's arrow-up (2) and widget-9 cases on page 1.

entries.name: HddDamageScreen_PrevView
entries.description: Steps the damage category back, 0 wrapping to 2, through HddDamageScreen_SetView. Reached from HddDisplay_HandleWidgetPress's arrow-down (3) case on page 1.

entries.name: HddDamageScreen_PageDown
entries.description: Adds 13 to the damage row offset +0x84 while offset + 13 is below the row count +0x90. es2_xref finds no branch, stored pointer or vtable slot reaching it.

entries.name: HddDamageScreen_PageUp
entries.description: Takes 13 off the damage row offset +0x84 unless that would go below 0. es2_xref finds no branch, stored pointer or vtable slot reaching it.

entries.name: HddDamageScreen_Update
entries.description: Per-frame update and repaint. Picks the name table by category and subject type -- STRINGS0 groups 13/14 for structural (walker/flyer), 15/16 for internal, the mech's own weapon names for weapons -- floods the screen with colour id 3, sets the subject caption, blits the .PDG view for the category (0 structural, 1 internal) at the screen rect's top-left plus the view's own origin, tints its regions through PaperDoll_RecolorRectFromArt, and refills the rows. A row is a .PDG region in file order, not a table entry: the region's index selects both the name and the reading (armour entry 1+id for structural, dependent entry 20+id for internal, combined entry 32+slot for a weapon mount). Both of a row's labels are re-fonted from Damage_PickRegionTint's state through ColorSchemePanels 1, 3, 9, 2, 7. Structural regions 0 and 1 share a rect, so row 0 tints on the mean of both cockpit halves and row 1 tints nothing. See docs/retail/formats/heads-down-display.md.

entries.name: HddDamageScreen_Show
entries.description: HDDDamage vtable +0x0c (0049dab0): HddDamageScreen_SetView(screen, +0x7c), the category it last showed, then +0x80 = -1.

entries.name: HddDamageScreen_BlitWeaponIcons
entries.description: Blits every non-null bitmap of a weapon-icon list at its position plus the doll origin, with the entry's blit flags. HddDamageScreen_Update calls it in both of its category branches.

entries.name: HDDisplay_HideNoOp
entries.description: HDDisplay vtable +0x08 (0049d668), kept by HDDDamage: push ebp / mov ebp,esp / pop ebp / ret. HddCommandScreen_Hide is the map screen's.

entries.name: HddDamageScreen_KeyDispatch
entries.description: Vtable slot 4 of the damage screen (0049dab0), the slot HddDisplay's key dispatch forwards unhandled scancodes to. Returns 0: the screen handles no key of its own.

entries.name: PanelAmbience_Ctor
entries.description: PanelAmbience constructor (table 0049db5c, RTTI 'PanelAmbience', 0xc1 bytes), (gauge, record, arg): PanelGauge_Ctor over the record's rect (+0x10), its own table, then three 0x21-byte Labels in ColorSchemePanels at +0xb1, +0xb5 and +0xb9 placed in that rect (alignments 1, 4 and 2), and the refresh deadline +0xbd = now + 0x1e coarse ticks. It also builds a local name from the cockpit's (CockpitOverride_Name, or the type's entry in DAT_004a9de4) and overwrites it with 'cpwincrk'.

entries.name: PanelAmbience_Paint
entries.description: PanelAmbience vtable +0x04 (0049db5c): calls 00452144(gauge).

entries.name: PanelAmbience_Update
entries.description: PanelAmbience vtable +0x08 (0049db5c): forces the dirty byte +0xb0 to 2 while the cockpit view manager's +0x1c byte is set; when dirty, copies the rect from (+0xb1)+4/+8 to (+0xb5)+0xc/+0x10 to the cockpit with Widget_DrawToCockpit and clears it. Every 0x1e coarse ticks (deadline +0xbd) reruns 00452144 and sets the dirty byte to 1.

entries.name: PanelAmbience_TickClock
entries.description: (gauge): toggles PanelAmbience_ColonOn (0049dac4); on each call that sets it to 1, advances the ASCII clock in PanelAmbience_ClockDigits by one second -- seconds ones 004d1e3c (rolls past '9'), seconds tens 004d1e3b (past '5'), minutes ones 004d1e39 and tens PanelAmbience_ClockDigits (004d1e38), wrapping 99:59 to 00:00 -- the carry HudClock_Tick uses. Then, when CockpitView_RectCornerVisible passes for the +0xb1 label's rect, pushes the canvas context (Cockpit_PushCanvasContext), Label_SetTexts the +0xb1 label with the minutes (PanelAmbience_ClockDigits (004d1e38)), the +0xb5 label with the seconds (004d1e3b) and, while the colon byte is set, the +0xb9 label with ':' (004d1e3e), and pops it. It is the whole body of PanelAmbience_Paint; PanelAmbience_Update reruns it every 0x1e coarse ticks.

entries.name: PanelAmbience_FormatClock
entries.description: Builds 'MM:SS' in PanelAmbience_ClockText (004d1e40) -- a copy of the minutes string at PanelAmbience_ClockDigits (004d1e38), then _strcat of ':' (0049db4e) and of the seconds string at 004d1e3b -- and returns PanelAmbience_ClockText (004d1e40). Caller found by es2_xref: MessagePort_StampedQueueAppend, which copies the result into a 9-byte slot at +0x21e of a five-entry log; es2_xref finds no caller of MessagePort_StampedQueueAppend (004352ec).

entries.name: Gau_ShiftRects2Point
entries.description: (rects): VideoMode_ShiftRect on the rect at +0, then shifts the rect at +0x10 and the x/y pair at +0x20 by VideoMode_XCoordShift / VideoMode_YCoordShift. Caller found by es2_xref: Gau_PanelAmbienceWidget, which runs it on the .GAU block at +0x644 (1604) before PanelAmbience_Ctor reads that block; es2_xref finds no caller of Gau_PanelAmbienceWidget (004326a8), and the block is zero in all nine retail .GAU files.

entries.name: PanelGauge_OnChildClickNoOp
entries.description: PanelGauge vtable +0x00 (0049bc6c), kept by HUD, WeaponGauge, ChainedWeaponGauge and PanelAmbience: push ebp / mov ebp,esp / pop ebp / ret -- an owning display that ignores its children's forwarded clicks.

entries.name: PanelGauge_KeyDispatchNone
entries.description: PanelGauge vtable +0x0c (0049bc6c), and the same slot in twelve classes below it: returns 0, handling no key. The Heads-Down Display installs HddDisplay_KeyDispatch in the slot.

entries.name: Widget_SetHitShape
entries.description: (widget, shape): stores shape in the hit-shape byte +0x10; for shape 1 also sets the int16 radius +0x15 = (x1 - x0) >> 1 and the int16 centre +0x11/+0x13 = (x0 + radius, y0 + radius) -- the circular form Widget_HitTest tests. No caller, stored pointer or vtable slot found by es2_xref.

entries.name: Widget_HitTest
entries.description: Point-in-widget test against a single widget, param_1. A per-widget flag at param_1+0x10 selects the shape: 0 = axis-aligned rect, inclusive bounds at param_1[0..3] (x0,y0,x1,y1); nonzero = circular/diamond region, Manhattan distance from a centre point (param_1+0x11/+0x13, int16 cx,cy) at most a radius (param_1+0x15, int16). Widget_CtorRect clears the flag for every leaf widget and CTLWindow_Ctor clears it too; Widget_SetHitShape (0045234c) sets the second form, and es2_xref finds no caller of it.

entries.name: Widget_OffsetRect
entries.description: (widget, delta) -- adds delta.x to the widget rect's +0x00 and +0x08 and delta.y to its +0x04 and +0x0c. A pure translate; the only rect mutator the view-change path uses.

entries.name: Widget_MoveTo
entries.description: (widget, pos): moves the widget rect so its top-left is pos and keeps its size: +0x00/+0x04 = pos, +0x08/+0x0c = pos plus the old x1 - x0 / y1 - y0. Caller found by es2_xref: HddCommandScreen_DrawMarker, which places a map marker at its projected point.

entries.name: Widget_CtorRect
entries.description: Base widget constructor. Installs the base vtable (0049dbb6) at +0x17, copies the four rect ints from param_2, clears the hit-shape byte at +0x10 and the deferred-paint counter at +0x1f. Every leaf widget in the cockpit's clickable list runs through it.

entries.name: SliderWidget_CtorBase
entries.description: Shared slider base ctor (obj, trackRect, min, max, initial, knobSize). Sets the widget's +0x1d drag flag to 1 unconditionally -- the only ctor that does, and every slider is built on it: the throttle (ThrottleSlider_CtorV, ThrottleSlider_CtorFixed), the energy rows' charge bars (WeaponSliderGadget_Ctor) and AlertSliderGadget_Ctor's alert-panel slider. Of the cockpit's, only the throttle can be pressed: each charge bar lies under its row's select gadget. Widget_OnMouseDown (004527a0) tests that flag before latching Widget_DragCapture.

entries.name: SliderWidget_DragToPointH
entries.description: Horizontal slider drag handler, twin of SliderWidget_DragToPointV (004525d8). Saves the previous knob position to +0x2a, clamps the pointer x into [trackLeft (+0), trackRight (+8) - knobWidth (+0x2c)], and stores it as the knob's LEFT edge at +0x28.

entries.name: SliderWidget_GetValueH
entries.description: Horizontal slider get-value, twin of SliderWidget_GetValueV (00452628): (knobLeft (+0x2e) - trackLeft (+0)) * 0x10000 / scale (+0x20) + min (+0x24).

entries.name: SliderWidget_SetValueH
entries.description: Horizontal slider set-value, twin of SliderWidget_SetValueV (00452644): clamps the value into [min (+0x24), max (+0x26)], sets knobLeft (+0x28) = trackLeft (+0) + ((value - min) * scale (+0x20) >> 16), then dispatches the commit slot (+8 of the table at +0x17) with the clamped value.

entries.name: SliderWidget_RecomputeScaleH
entries.description: Horizontal slider scale, twin of SliderWidget_RecomputeScaleV (00452694): +0x20 = ((trackRight (+8) - knobWidth (+0x36 - +0x2e)) - trackLeft (+0)) * 0x10000 / (max - min).

entries.name: SliderWidget_DragToPointV
entries.description: Vertical slider drag handler (vtable +0x18). Saves the previous knob position to +0x2a, clamps the pointer y into [trackTop + knobHeight, trackBottom], and stores it as the knob's BOTTOM edge at +0x28 -- so grabbing the knob jumps its lower edge under the cursor. Horizontal twin is 004524f8.

entries.name: SliderWidget_GetValueV
entries.description: Vertical slider get-value (vtable +0x10): (knobTop(+0x32) - trackTop(+4)) * 0x10000 / scale(+0x20) + min(+0x24). Reads the knob's TOP against the track's top while SetValueV places its BOTTOM, so it returns the NEGATION of what SetValueV was given (for the symmetric +/-0x400 range). Not a bug: ThrottleGauge_OnChildValue negates again, and the two cancel. Horizontal twin is 00452544, which is self-consistent.

entries.name: SliderWidget_SetValueV
entries.description: Vertical slider set-value (vtable +0x14): knobBottom(+0x28) = trackBottom(+0xc) - ((value - min) * scale >> 16), then dispatches the commit slot (+8). Max puts the knob at the track top. Horizontal twin is 0045255c.

entries.name: SliderWidget_RecomputeScaleV
entries.description: Vertical slider scale (vtable +0x1c): +0x20 = ((trackBottom - knobHeight) - trackTop) * 0x10000 / (max - min), i.e. Q16 device pixels per value unit over the knob's travel. Horizontal twin is 004525a8.

entries.name: CTLWindow_Ctor
entries.description: CTLWindow constructor (vtable 0049db7a at +0x17, RTTI name 'CTLWindow', 0x398 bytes): clears +0x10, constructs a GLViewport at +0x1b, copies the rect argument to +0 and +0x22b, sets +0x223 = 1 and clears +0x254. Gau_BuildCockpitWidgets builds the cockpit's from the .GAU record and stores it at cockpit+0; AlertPanel_CtorBase builds one per panel at +0x285.

entries.name: Widget_TranslateRootForView
entries.description: (root, delta) -- moves the cockpit widget root for a view change: adds the delta to the origin pairs at +0x233/+0x237 and +0x22b/+0x22f and to the root's own rect through Widget_OffsetRect. THIS IS THE SCREEN-TO-CANVAS MAPPING the whole input path depends on: Widget_OnMouseDown and Widget_OnMouseUp hit-test point - root->rect.x0/y0, so moving the root's rect by the view-origin delta is what makes one canvas-space widget rect answer a different part of the screen in each view. Its two calls to GLDisplay_GetAttribute discard their results. Reached only through the argument-forwarding thunk Widget_TranslateRootForView_Thunk, itself called only by CockpitWidgets_TranslateForView.

entries.name: Widget_OnMouseDown
entries.description: Hit-tests the press position via Widget_HitTestChildren; if a widget is hit, marks its state (+0x1b) pressed (1) and, if that widget opts in via its own +0x1d==1 flag, begins mouse capture (Widget_DragCapture=1) and forwards the position to the widget's drag-move vtable slot. Widgets built with +0x1d left 0 (every button/gauge traced so far) never enter capture and are handled entirely by press/release instead.

entries.name: Widget_OnMouseUp
entries.description: (root, point): rebases the release point by the root's origin (plus 004d25da/de while 0049dbec is set), hit-tests it with Widget_HitTestChildren and stores the result in Widget_PressedIndex. On a hit, when it is the widget the press stored there or the button word 0049db6c has the right-button bit, it calls that widget's GetValue (+0x10) then OnClick (+8) with the value; on any hit it then sets the hit widget's state +0x1b to 0, repaints it and sets Widget_PressedIndex to -1. The state cleared is the hit widget's, which is not the pressed one when the release lands elsewhere. Its own code has no timing test: a release fires however long the button was held.

entries.name: Widget_TrackPressedWidget
entries.description: On a position change while a button is held, keeps the pressed widget's appearance in sync with the pointer: hit-tests, and if the hit is still the widget in Widget_PressedIndex sets its state (+0x1b) to 1, otherwise clears it to 0, repainting via Widget_Repaint on each change. This is the button that pops back up when you drag off it and depresses again when you return. Guarded entirely on Widget_PressedIndex != -1, and that global is set only by Widget_OnMouseDown and cleared to -1 by Widget_OnMouseUp, so this cannot run unless a button is down. It is not a hover handler: DBSIM has no hover state, and CockpitMouse_Init's event mask (0x1e) excludes plain movement.

entries.name: Widget_HitTestChildren
entries.description: Linear-scans the flat clickable-widget list at param_1+0x256 (count at +0x254) with Widget_HitTest, returning the index of the FIRST widget under the point whose state (+0x1b) is not 2 (hidden), or -1. First-hit-wins is what makes registration order the tie-break wherever two visible rects overlap, and retail has four such overlaps. Not a tree walk: every clickable widget anywhere in the cockpit is registered into one shared list by Widget_RegisterClickable, so an off-screen panel's buttons are excluded purely by their hidden state, not by not being reachable.

entries.name: Widget_NotifySelfAndChildren
entries.description: Clears a guard flag (+0x227), calls vtable slot 0 on the owner, then calls slot 0 on every widget in its +0x256 clickable-child array. Unreachable in the retail image: its only caller, 00452bac, has no rel32 branch, no stored pointer and no vtable slot anywhere in the PE. The cascades the cockpit actually runs are per class (00442058/0044207c for the console panel).

entries.name: Widget_Repaint
entries.description: Calls a widget's own Paint vtable slot after a state change. The slot's numeric offset is not uniform across classes (confirmed +4 for MfdDisplay and HddButton via unambiguous ctor evidence; do not assume the same offset for every class without checking).

entries.name: CTLWindow_Slot00NoOp
entries.description: CTLWindow vtable +0x00 (0049db7a, RTTI 'CTLWindow', 0x398 bytes, derived from CTLBox), the table's one slot: an empty body.

entries.name: CTLControl_PaintNoOp
entries.description: Empty body. CTLControl's (vtable 0049dbb6, RTTI name 'CTLControl', 0x20 bytes) Paint slot +0; no other vtable uses it.

entries.name: CTLControl_InvalidateNoOp
entries.description: Empty body. CTLControl's (vtable 0049dbb6) Invalidate slot +4; no other vtable uses it.

entries.name: CockpitMouse_Init
entries.description: Called once at cockpit setup. Registers CockpitMouse_OnEvent with MouseListener_Register under event mask 0x1e (button down/up on both buttons -- bits 1-4; bit 0, plain movement, is deliberately excluded), allocates the double-buffered per-frame event queue (two Rtl_VectorNew'd 0xe-byte-record vectors, swapped by CockpitMouse_ProcessQueue), and sets the click-vs-drag timing gate CockpitMouse_DoubleClickTicks = 0x1e (30 coarse ticks, ~480ms at the ~62.5Hz UI timebase -- the same literal 0x1e as the event mask above but an unrelated field, easy to conflate).

entries.name: Widget_ClearPressed
entries.description: Swaps in a clickable list as the active one and clears Widget_PressedIndex to -1, so nothing that was held under the previous list stays armed.

entries.name: Widget_NotifySelfAndChildren_Thunk
entries.description: (window): calls Widget_NotifySelfAndChildren(window). No caller, stored pointer or vtable slot found by es2_xref.

entries.name: Widget_NoOp
entries.description: Empty body (PUSH EBP; MOV EBP,ESP; POP EBP; RET) between Widget_NotifySelfAndChildren_Thunk and Widget_TranslateRootForView_Thunk. No caller, stored pointer or vtable slot found by es2_xref.

entries.name: Widget_TranslateRootForView_Thunk
entries.description: (root, dx, dy) -- forwards to Widget_TranslateRootForView(root, &dx), taking the delta as two inline stack ints rather than a pointer. Decompiles as a one-argument call passing &stack0x00000008, which loses the delta; the raw call site at 0043272e-0043273f pushes both ints before the root pointer.

entries.name: WidgetRoot_Delete
entries.description: (root): Mem_Delete(root) when non-null; its three member destructors are trivial (the exception-count bookkeeping only). AlertPanel_Leave runs it on the panel's widget root +0x285.

entries.name: Widget_RegisterClickable
entries.description: Appends one widget pointer to the caller's flat +0x256 array (count at +0x254) that Widget_HitTestChildren scans. Called once per child during every cockpit widget tree's construction (MfdDisplay_Ctor's 13 MFD buttons, ShieldsGauge_Ctor's 2 facings, etc.) with the *dereferenced* CockpitViewInstance pointer as the shared root -- every clickable widget in the whole cockpit lands in one list, not a per-panel one.

entries.name: Widget_Show
entries.description: Sets a child's state byte (+0x1b) to 0. UNREFERENCED: no rel32 branch, no vtable slot and no stored pointer anywhere in the image. Every show and hide the cockpit actually performs is a direct store to that byte at the site that wants it -- HddDisplay_SetPage's visibility-table loop, HddCommandScreen_Show/_Hide, and the gauge constructors' own flyer branches.

entries.name: Widget_Hide
entries.description: Sets a child's state byte (+0x1b) to 2. UNREFERENCED: no rel32 branch, no vtable slot and no stored pointer anywhere in the image. Every show and hide the cockpit actually performs is a direct store to that byte at the site that wants it -- HddDisplay_SetPage's visibility-table loop, HddCommandScreen_Show/_Hide, and the gauge constructors' own flyer branches.

entries.name: CockpitMouse_OnEvent
entries.description: The cockpit's one mouse-listener callback. Does not act on the event synchronously: pushes a {x,y,buttonMask,timestamp} record into the back-buffer queue via CockpitMouseQueue_Push (debounced to once per coarse tick) and, when a software/hardware cursor sprite is active (DAT_0049dbdf), calls Cursor_SyncPosition to keep the drawn pointer following the raw event position immediately rather than waiting for the once-per-frame queue drain.

entries.name: CockpitMouse_ProcessQueue
entries.description: Swaps the double-buffered event queue and drains it once per frame: the cockpit's click, press and drag logic. Per 14-byte record it first sets the button word 0049db6c to the record's buttons. On a position change it stores the position, calls Cursor_SyncPosition only while TapePlayback is set and the cursor flag 0049dbdf is, and sets the click point DAT_004d1e67/6b relative to the root; outside a capture it hit-tests the root with Widget_HitTest and, on a hit, calls Widget_TrackPressedWidget; under a capture it calls the captured widget's drag slot (+0x18) and repaints it. It then clears CockpitMouse_DoubleClick. A left-button down edge calls Widget_OnMouseDown; a right one only latches. On a release edge of either button it sets CockpitMouse_DoubleClick when the record's time is less than CockpitMouse_DoubleClickTicks after that button's previous release, stores the time as the new previous release, and ORs that button's bit into 0049db6c; then, outside a capture, Widget_OnMouseUp, and under one it clears the captured widget's state, repaints it, ends the capture, calls its GetValue (+0x10) then OnClick (+8) with that value, and sets Widget_PressedIndex to -1. 0049db6c returns to 0 at the end of each record.

entries.name: CockpitMouseQueue_Push
entries.description: Appends one 0xe=14-byte record {int32 x, int32 y, uint16 buttonMask, int32 timestamp} to the back-buffer vector at DAT_004d1e88, capped at 99 entries (silently drops further events past that).

entries.name: WidgetRoot_FlashPress
entries.description: (root, widget): appends {widget, Time_GetCoarseTicks() + 10} to the root's press-flash list, eight 8-byte entries from +0x356, incrementing the count at +0x396 first and with no bound check, so a ninth entry lands on the count. WidgetRoot_ServicePressFlashes shows the widget pressed until that time. Callers found by es2_naming.py callers: Widget_PressChild, AlertPanel_PressWidget and ControlsPanel_HandleEvent.

entries.name: WidgetRoot_ServicePressFlashes
entries.description: (root): walks the press-flash list at +0x356 (count +0x396). An entry whose deadline is still ahead of Time_GetCoarseTicks puts its widget's state +0x1b to 1, if it is not 1 already, and invalidates it (vtable at +0x17, slot +4); one whose deadline has come puts the state to 0, invalidates it, and is removed by shifting the later entries down. Callers found by es2_naming.py callers: CockpitView_PerFrameUpdate, AlertPanel_Present and PreferencesPanel_Present.

entries.name: WidgetRoot_PressFlashCount
entries.description: Returns the number of entries in a widget root's press-flash list, the short at +0x396. AlertPanel_Present reads it to hold the close flag back while a flash is queued (read).

entries.name: Widget_StaticInit
entries.description: Static initialiser of the widget and cockpit-mouse block (Borland _INIT_ entry 004a7b52, priority 0x20): a bare RET.

entries.name: CockpitMouseEvent_ElementCtor
entries.description: (record): returns its argument -- Rtl_VectorNew's per-element constructor for the two 100 x 0xe-byte cockpit mouse event queues CockpitMouse_Init allocates (PUSH 0x453171 at 00452ae8 and 00452b1a; the vectors go to 004d1e7c and 004d1e84).

entries.name: CornerFrame_LoadStyles
entries.description: (path): opens path as a VolRStream, reads an int16 count into CornerFrame_StyleCount (004d1e94) and, when it is non-zero, Rtl_VectorNews that many 0x40-byte style records with CornerFrameStyle_ElementCtor into CornerFrame_Styles (0049dc24) and reads each record raw with VolRStream_Read; then destroys the stream. The record layout is CornerFrame_Draw's. No caller, stored pointer or vtable slot found by es2_xref.

entries.name: CornerFrame_Draw
entries.description: (style, x0, y0, x1, y1): draws a bevelled frame from a 0x40-byte style record. Fills (x0+3, y0+3)-(x1-3, y1-3), normalised, through Raster_FillRect with a {0, style+0x00} brush installed at the render context's +0x22c (the context DAT_006c5f54+0x44 points at, less 4 when non-zero), then restores the brush; then CornerFrame_DrawEdgeRing three times -- inset 0, grow 0, colours +0x04..+0x10; inset 1, grow -2, +0x14..+0x20; inset 2, grow -4, +0x24..+0x30 -- and CornerFrame_DrawCorners, which reads the corner frames +0x34..+0x3a and the corner size +0x3c/+0x3e. No caller, stored pointer or vtable slot found by es2_xref.

entries.name: CornerFrame_DrawEdgeRing
entries.description: (style, x0, y0, x1, y1, inset, grow, first): draws one ring of four one-pixel edges with Raster_DrawLine, each under its own {0, colour} pen at the render context's +0x228 (restored after) and skipped when that colour dword is 0. With left = x0 + inset, top = y0 + inset, w = x1 - x0 + grow and h = y1 - y0 + grow: dword style[first] colours the left edge (left, top+1)-(left, top+h-1), style[first+1] the top edge (left+1, top)-(left+w-1, top), style[first+2] the right edge at x = left+w, style[first+3] the bottom edge at y = top+h. Callers found by es2_xref: CornerFrame_Draw (three calls).

entries.name: CornerFrame_DrawCorners
entries.description: (style, x0, y0, x1, y1): Bitmap_Blits four frames of the corners bank (004d1e98, loaded by CockpitFontsAndCorners_Init) with flags 0 -- frame int16 +0x34 at (x0, y0), +0x36 at (x1 - w, y0), +0x38 at (x0, y1 - h), +0x3a at (x1 - w, y1 - h) -- where w and h are the style's int16 +0x3c and +0x3e. Caller found by es2_xref: CornerFrame_Draw.

entries.name: CornerFrameStyle_ElementCtor
entries.description: (record): returns its argument -- the per-element constructor CornerFrame_LoadStyles hands Rtl_VectorNew for its 0x40-byte style records (PUSH 0x4535e2 at 004531c3).

entries.name: CockpitFont_Load
entries.description: (slot, path): opens path as a VolRStream, stores ClassItem_LoadResource's result in *slot and destroys the stream. CockpitFontsAndCorners_Init's seven font loads; byte-identical to CockpitCorners_Load.

entries.name: CockpitCorners_Load
entries.description: (slot, path): the same code as CockpitFont_Load. Its one call loads CockpitFontsAndCorners_Init's `corners` bank.

entries.name: CockpitResource_Load
entries.description: (slot, path): opens path as a VolRStream, stores ClassItem_LoadResource(stream, 0) in *slot, then VolRStream_Close and VolRStream_Dtor(stream, 2). CockpitFont_Load's body with the explicit VolRStream_Close added (es2_naming diff). No caller, stored pointer or vtable slot found by es2_xref.

entries.name: Raster_FrameRectColour
entries.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1, colour), all on the stack by value (colour an int16): installs a {4, colour} brush at the current render context's (006c5ff4) +0x22c -- brush mode 4 makes Raster_FillRect draw the rect's four edges with Raster_DrawLine -- calls Raster_FillRect on the rect and restores the previous brush. No caller, stored pointer or vtable slot found by es2_xref.

entries.name: Raster_FillFrameRectColours
entries.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1, fill, frame), all on the stack by value (the colours int16): Raster_FillRect on the rect with a {0, fill} brush, then again with a {4, frame} brush (the outline), both at the current render context's (006c5ff4) +0x22c, then restores the previous brush. No caller, stored pointer or vtable slot found by es2_xref.

entries.name: Raster_DrawLineColour
entries.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1, colour), all on the stack by value (colour an int16): installs a {0, colour} pen at the current render context's (006c5ff4) +0x228, draws (x0, y0)-(x1, y1) with Raster_DrawLine and restores the previous pen. No caller, stored pointer or vtable slot found by es2_xref.

entries.name: StringTable_Ctor
entries.description: Clears a string table: buffer +0, cursor +4, length +8 and the group counters +0xc and +0xe. Callers found by es2_xref: World_StaticInit, MessagePort_StaticInit (two tables), SimStrings_StaticInit, Sound_StaticInit, HddDisplay_Ctor, AlertPanel_CtorBase, ObjectivesPanel_Ctor and DemoTape_PickRandom.

entries.name: OwnedArray_Dtor
entries.description: (holder, flags): decrements the counter at *006cbf74, Mem_DeleteArray of the array pointer at holder+0 when non-null, then Mem_Delete(holder) when flags bit 0 is set. Alert_Dtor runs it on its +0x34 member and 00457a80 on its +0x332, both with flags 2.

entries.name: StringTable_Load
entries.description: (table, path): opens path with VolRStream_CtorFromPath, reads it with StringTable_LoadFromStream, destroys the stream and returns that result. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's StringTable_Load without its open assert.

entries.name: StringTable_LoadFromStream
entries.description: (table, stream): reads the int32 content length into +8, allocates that many bytes (Mem_NewArray) at +0, reads the content into it and sets the cursor +4 to the start. Returns 1. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's StringTable_LoadFromStream without its allocation assert.

entries.name: StringTable_ReadNext
entries.description: (table, &text, &attributes): reads the next string of a string table, taking the group's int16 count first at the start of a group. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's StringTable_ReadNext.

entries.name: StringTable_LoadGroup
entries.description: Pops the next .STR group into a destination pointer array, one entry per string, advancing the table's own cursor. The capacity argument is the destination array's size and is not read; the group's own count decides how many are written.
entries.signature: short __cdecl StringTable_LoadGroup(int *table, void **destination, int capacity, void **attributeDestination)

entries.name: StrTable_FirstString
entries.description: (table): the loaded .STR buffer (*table) + 4, the first entry's text, or 0 when nothing is loaded. HddGauge_LoadPilotFrames walks DAT_0049d238 from it.

entries.name: StrTable_NextString
entries.description: (table, string): the string after the given one in a loaded .STR buffer -- steps over the NUL-terminated text by its length prefix, the attribute count byte and its attributes, and the next entry's length -- or null past the buffer's end. Ignores ids and groups.

entries.name: StrTable_GetAttributes
entries.description: (table, string): the entry's attribute bytes -- string + its int16 length prefix (string-2) is the attribute count byte, and the result is the byte after it -- or 0 when the count is 0 or string lies past the buffer (*table + size table[2]). MessagePort_StepToVariant stores it at its record's +5.

entries.name: Screenshot_BuildPath
entries.description: (base, ext): builds the screenshot file name in ScreenshotPath (004d1ed6): base's characters up to its NUL or first '.', at most 8 - len of them, where len is the length of ScreenshotCounter (0049dcdc) in decimal (_itoa); then the counter's digits; then ext. Returns the address ext was written at. Callers found by es2_xref: Screenshot_Save (twice, with '.SCR' and '.PAL').

entries.name: Screenshot_WriteScr
entries.description: (path): writes the captured screen in ScreenshotBitmap (width 004d1ec2, height 004d1ec0, one byte per pixel at 004d1eca) to path through a FileRWStream as nibble-split chunks; each tag and size is written as a little-endian dword. With n = width * height: 0x5343523a ('SCR:' read big-endian) with size (n/2)*2 + 0x1e | 0x80000000; 0x44494d3a ('DIM:'), size 4, int16 width, int16 height; 0x42494e3a ('BIN:'), size n/2 + 5, byte 0, dword 0, then for each pixel pair (p0 << 4 | p1 & 0xf), the low nibbles; 0x5647413a ('VGA:'), size n/2 + 5, byte 0, dword 0, then (p0 & 0xf0 | p1 >> 4), the high nibbles; then a closing dword 0. Caller found by es2_xref: Screenshot_Save.

entries.name: Screenshot_WritePal
entries.description: (path): reads 256 palette entries through g_RasterRoutines_GetPalette (004a57fc) with (0, 0x100, buffer) into a local GLPalette's 4-byte entries and writes them to path through a FileRWStream: dword 0x50414c3a ('PAL:' read big-endian), bytes 08 03 00 80, dword 0x5647413a ('VGA:'), bytes 00 03 00 00, then the low three bytes of each entry in order. Ends with GLPalette_Dtor(palette, 2). Caller found by es2_xref: Screenshot_Save.

entries.name: Screenshot_Save
entries.description: (base): captures the screen and writes <base><n>.SCR and <base><n>.PAL. Sets ScreenshotBitmap's header at 004d1ec0 to the display's (DAT_006c5f54) size from GLDisplay_GetAttribute 0 and 1 (width 004d1ec2, height 004d1ec0), format byte 8, size width * height (004d1ec6) and a Mem_NewArray pixel buffer (004d1eca); points the display's source page (+0x38) at its visible page (+0x34) through maybe_g_RasterRoutines_SetSourcePage; installs a local GLViewport spanning the screen and reads it with Bitmap_GrabClipDispatch(004d1ec0, {0, 0}, 0); restores the render context and the source page. Then Screenshot_BuildPath(base, '.SCR'), Screenshot_WriteScr, Mem_DeleteArray of the pixels, Screenshot_BuildPath(base, '.PAL'), Screenshot_WritePal, and increments ScreenshotCounter (0049dcdc). No caller, stored pointer or vtable slot found by es2_xref.

entries.name: Screenshot_StaticInit
entries.description: Static initialiser (Borland _INIT_ entry 004a7b58, priority 0x20): GLBitmap_Ctor on ScreenshotBitmap (004d1ebc). Screenshot_StaticDtor is its _EXIT_ counterpart.

entries.name: Screenshot_StaticDtor
entries.description: Screenshot_StaticInit's _EXIT_ routine (Borland _EXIT_ entry 004a7c48): GLBitmap_Dtor(ScreenshotBitmap, 2).

entries.name: AlertPanel_CtorBase
entries.description: The alert panels' shared base constructor. Stores the screen rect at +0x04..+0x10 and the same rect panel-local (origin 0,0) at +0x1c..+0x28, allocates the offscreen backing store the panel restores the screen from, builds the widget list at +0x285, and sets the cancel widget +0x2fb to -1.

entries.name: Alert_Dtor
entries.description: Alert destructor (vtable 0049e05c, RTTI name 'Alert', 0x332 bytes): Mem_Delete on each pointer in the array at +0x291 (count +0x2cd), frees the array at +0x2c, deletes the object at +0x30 through its virtual destructor, frees +0x44, clears +0x2e6, runs GLCursor_Dtor on +0x2e2 and 00453804 on +0x34, and frees the alert when flag & 1.

entries.name: CockpitFontsAndCorners_Init
entries.description: Loads the cockpit fonts title, cpylw, active, pushed, inactive, green6x8 and red6x8 with CockpitFont_Load from "hfn" when VideoMode_PanelMode is 3 and "dfn" otherwise, into 004d1e9c..004d1eb4; the `corners` bank from the folder PTR_DAT_004a0a28 names with CockpitCorners_Load into 004d1e98 (no hba\CORNERS.HBA exists); zeroes 004d1eec/004d1ef0, stores GLDisplay_GetAttribute 0 and 1 (screen width and height) at 004d1ef4/004d1ef8 and 4 << the X/Y coord shifts at 004d1f04/004d1f08; and loads the `alert` bank into DAT_0049dd88 once, from the hi-res folder when VideoMode_UseHiResBanks.

entries.name: AlertPanel_Enter
entries.description: Puts a modal alert panel up: cancels and pauses the squad message port and pauses the cockpit view's port at +0x20b; when no panel is up yet (0049dd8c is 0) zeroes 0049eacc and 0049dbec; saves the current input state block, the pointer position included, at +0x300..+0x32f; latches joystick buttons 1-4 with Input_LatchButton so one held at open does not act; focuses with AlertPanel_SetFocus(-1), adopting the widget under the pointer; clears Widget_PressedIndex and swaps in the panel's own clickable list; installs the panel's render context and draw page; saves and sets the cursor-visibility flag 0049dbdf and calls the 0049dd94 hook when set; loads the alert cursor once; copies the screen under the panel into the backing store and calls the panel's own paint; then counts the panel in 0049dd8c and resets the present timer.

entries.name: AlertPanel_Leave
entries.description: The inverse of AlertPanel_Enter. Restores the saved screen (Region_Restore) when the panel saved one and presents it on the scroll-window path; restores the cursor image and the visibility flag 0049dbdf, calling the 0049dd98 hook when set; reinstates the previous render context and draw page; deletes the panel's widget root and reinstates the clickable list at +0x289 with Widget_ClearPressed; puts the input state block back, the pointer position at +0x302 included, and warps the cursor there with Mouse_WarpCursorToPoint when there is a mouse device, storing it with Cursor_SyncPosition (Driver3_SyncCursorPosition on the scroll-window path). Then decrements the open-panel count 0049dd8c, setting 0049eacc and 0049dbec back to 1 when it reaches 0, and resumes both message ports.

entries.name: AlertPanel_ResetPresentTimer
entries.description: Sets the alert panels' next present time 004d1ee8 to Time_GetCoarseTicks(), so the next AlertPanel_Present flips the frame at once.

entries.name: AlertPanel_Present
entries.description: The tail of one pass of a modal loop. Sets the close flag +0x2d1 when the quit flag 004d2582 is set, runs Sfx_Service while SfxManager is up, and services the press flashes on the panel's widget root (+0x285). Then, while the close flag is set and WidgetRoot_PressFlashCount is nonzero, it moves the flag to +0x331 and clears it; on a pass that finds +0x331 set otherwise, it moves it back. So a press that closes the panel and flashes a widget keeps the loop running one more pass. Last, on the scroll-window path (Display_UseScrollWindow), it calls Display_Present once the repaint interval (004d1ee4) has passed since the last one. StatusAlertPanel_RunModal, ObjectivesPanel_RunModal and ControlsPanel_Run call it at the end of every pass (callers found by es2_xref, each read).

entries.name: AlertPanel_SetTitleText
entries.description: The alert panels' shared vtable slot +4: sets the title label at +0x44 to the given text.

entries.name: AlertPanel_LoadCursor
entries.description: (panel, cursor): fills the panel's cursor record -- +0x2e6 = 004a3630 - 4, +0x2ea = 004a3640, +0x2ee = 004a3644, +0x2f2 = cursor -- then sets the cursor image through maybe_Driver3_SetCursorImage on the scroll-window path (Display_UseScrollWindow) or maybe_Cursor_SetImage otherwise. AlertPanel_Enter passes DAT_0049dd90.

entries.name: AlertPanel_RestoreCursorImage
entries.description: (panel): when +0x330 is set, hands the saved cursor (bitmap +0x2e6, plus 4 when non-null; hotspot +0x2ea) to maybe_Driver3_SetCursorImage on the scroll-window path (Display_UseScrollWindow) or maybe_Cursor_SetImage otherwise -- both empty in retail. AlertPanel_Leave calls it.

entries.name: AlertPanel_SetFocus
entries.description: Moves the panel's focus to widget index, storing it at +0x2f7. Focus is the pointer: it warps the cursor to the widget's centre (Mouse_WarpCursorToPoint when there is a mouse device) and stores that position with Cursor_SyncPosition. Index -1 instead adopts the first widget whose rect contains the pointer position the input build reports, and stays -1 when none does or there is no mouse device.

entries.name: AlertPanel_FocusChild
entries.description: (panel, widget): finds the widget pointer in the panel's +0x291 list (count +0x2cd) and focuses its index with AlertPanel_SetFocus; does nothing when the widget is not in the list.

entries.name: AlertPanel_FocusNext
entries.description: Focuses the next widget with AlertPanel_SetFocus, wrapping to 0 at the count in +0x2cd; from no focus (-1) that is widget 0.

entries.name: AlertPanel_FocusPrevious
entries.description: Focuses the previous widget with AlertPanel_SetFocus, wrapping from widget 0, or from no focus (-1), to the last one (count +0x2cd minus 1).

entries.name: AlertPanel_PressWidget
entries.description: Presses one of the panel's widgets for the player: unless the widget at index in the +0x291 list is in state 2, calls its click slot (+8 of the vtable at +0x17) with flags, then WidgetRoot_FlashPress on the panel's own widget root at +0x285, so the widget shows pressed for 10 coarse ticks.
entries.signature: void __cdecl AlertPanel_PressWidget(int panel, int index, undefined4 flags)

entries.name: AlertPanel_HandleEvent
entries.description: The alert panels' shared vtable slot +0x10. Joystick button 1 (+0x0d) presses the focused widget (+0x2f7) through AlertPanel_PressWidget, or focuses widget 0 when the focus is -1, and latches the button. Otherwise joystick button 2 (+0x17) focuses the next widget and latches it. Otherwise the key code: [Return] (0x1c) does what button 1 does; [Esc] (0x01) presses the cancel widget at +0x2fb when it is set; [Tab] (0x0f) and scancode 0x52 focus the next widget and 0x80f, Shift+Tab, the previous -- a code the loops' input build has already masked to 0x0f with SimCommandMask. Returns 1 when it acted and 0 for any other code.

entries.name: AlertPanel_SetRect
entries.description: Writes a panel rect to the shared four-int scratch at DAT_004d1f0c as (x, y, x + width, y + height) and returns it, which is what a panel constructor hands its base.
entries.signature: void * __cdecl AlertPanel_SetRect(int x, int y, int width, int height)

entries.name: AlertPanel_CenterRect
entries.description: Centres a panel rect of the given size on the screen: ((screenW - w) >> 1, (screenH - h) >> 1) against DAT_004d1ef4/DAT_004d1ef8.

entries.name: PanelButton_Ctor
entries.description: An alert panel's button widget. Stores the owner and the index it reports back to it, and takes its four caption fonts from the cockpit set: ACTIVE at rest (+0x40), PUSHED held (+0x44), INACTIVE disabled (+0x48), ACTIVE again (+0x4c). Its two plate frames are filled in by the panel that builds it.
entries.signature: void * __cdecl PanelButton_Ctor(void *button, int *rect, void *owner, int index)

entries.name: PanelButton_Paint
entries.description: Blits the plate frame for the button's current state (+0x1b) from the table at +0x30, asks its owner (slot +0x14) for its caption, overwrites the caption label's font with the state's entry from +0x40 and sets the text, all with the cursor hidden when the scroll window is off. It has no state test of its own: a state-2 button draws its third frame. The font overwrite is why a button caption is never drawn in the font its label was constructed with.

entries.name: PanelButton_Tick
entries.description: The per-pass slot the modal loop calls on each child: repaints while the auto-release counter at +0x1f is running down.

entries.name: PanelButton_OnClick
entries.description: Forwards the click to the owner's slot +0xc with the button's own index, repaints, then sounds the shared widget click.

entries.name: AlertSliderGadget_Ctor
entries.description: Constructor for AlertSliderGadget (object size 0x7e), an alert panel's slider row; derives from PanelHSliderGadget, so its click-sound slot is the empty stub 00439014 and it makes no sound. Class name from the descriptor record at 00455810.

entries.name: AlertSliderGadget_Paint
entries.description: AlertSliderGadget vtable +0x00 (0049dfd8): puts back the background under the knob's last position (Region_Restore from +0x52) when the knob (+0x28) has moved; runs the bar (+0x46) slots +0x08 and +0x00 with the value +0x7a and records it at +0x4a; rebuilds the knob rect at +0x2e..+0x3a, saves the screen under it (Region_Save into +0x52) and blits the knob bitmap +0x4e with VideoMode_BlitBitmap, recording the position at +0x6e/+0x72.

entries.name: AlertSliderGadget_FlushDeferredPaintNoOp
entries.description: AlertSliderGadget vtable +0x0c (0049dfd8): an empty body.

entries.name: Alert_StaticInit
entries.description: Static initialiser of ALERT.CPP (Borland _INIT_ entry 004a7b5e, priority 0x20): zeroes the mode dword of Alert_FillBrush (004d1efc).

entries.name: Widget_InvalidateDeferred
entries.description: The base Invalidate at leaf-widget vtable slot +4, which Widget_Repaint calls. Its whole body is this->[0x1f] = 2: it schedules a repaint rather than performing one. Slot +0xc, walked once per frame, is what acts on the counter.

entries.name: Widget_GetButtonValue
entries.description: The default GetValue vtable slot (+0x10) for a widget class that does not override it: returns the global mouse-button word 0049db6c, which CockpitMouse_ProcessQueue sets to buttons|1 on a left release and buttons|2 on a right one. A click's 'value' is therefore which button clicked it, and the weapon rows branch on exactly that -- left arms, right toggles chain membership.

entries.name: CTLControl_SetValueNoOp
entries.description: Empty body. CTLControl's SetValue slot +0x14, inherited by 25 widget vtables.

entries.name: CTLControl_DragMoveNoOp
entries.description: Empty body. CTLControl's DragMove slot +0x18, inherited by 25 widget vtables.

entries.description: CTLWindow's destructor (class record 004554c8): (window, flags). Three RTL destructor-count decrements, then Mem_Delete on flags bit 0.

entries.description: The this-adjusting thunk at primary vtable +0x34 of AlertSliderGadget's vtable block, in the table for its PanelSliderGadget subobject at +0x3e: subtracts 0x3e from this and jumps to AlertSliderGadget_OnClick.

entries.name: StatusAlertPanel_CtorMinimal
entries.description: Chains AlertPanel_CtorBase and installs gnl_alrt's vtable, nothing else. Both the status alert and the pause panel start here and then build their own widgets; the pause panel goes on to overwrite the vtable pointer with its own duplicate of the same six entries.
entries.signature: void * __cdecl StatusAlertPanel_CtorMinimal(void *panel, int status, char ownsBackingStore, int *rect)

entries.name: StatusAlertPanel_Ctor
entries.description: Builds gnl_alrt, the modal alert a mission-status change raises: 444x218 device, one or two buttons chosen by the status code, title and four body lines out of its own string table. Status 5 takes its body from DAT_004d1f1c, the first unsatisfied objective's text.
entries.signature: void * __cdecl StatusAlertPanel_Ctor(void *panel, int status, char ownsBackingStore, int *rect)

entries.name: GeneralAlert_Dtor
entries.description: GeneralAlert destructor (vtable 0049e148, RTTI name 'GeneralAlert', 0x57e bytes): reinstalls the vtable, Mem_Delete on the four pointers at +0x33e, Alert_Dtor(panel, 0), then Mem_Delete when flags bit 0 is set. Sim_DeathFlash runs it with 3.
entries.source: DBSIM decompile at 00455f90; RTTI at vtable-0xc

entries.name: StatusAlertPanel_RunModal
entries.description: gnl_alrt's modal loop, vtable slot +8. Enters, focuses widget 0, then until the close flag +0x2d1 is set: builds the input block and, unless DemoAbort is set, hands it to the slot +0x10 handler, runs each widget's deferred paint (slot +0xc) and AlertPanel_Present; with DemoAbort set it sets the close flag instead. Then AlertPanel_Leave, and returns the close flag & 1, so button 0 reads 0 and button 1 reads 1.

entries.name: StatusAlertPanel_Paint
entries.description: gnl_alrt's vtable slot 0. Plate at the panel origin, title, then the body: counts the rows up to the first empty or null one (max 4) and draws them from row 0 -- except that a one-line body is drawn on row 1 instead, so a short message sits nearer the middle of the plate. Then each button's own paint.

entries.name: StatusAlertPanel_OnChildClick
entries.description: gnl_alrt's vtable slot +0xc. Writes close flag 2 for child 0 and 3 for child 1; the loop returns that & 1, which is what lets the caller tell the two buttons apart.

entries.name: StatusAlertPanel_GetButtonCaption
entries.description: gnl_alrt's vtable slot +0x14: indexes the two-entry caption pointer at +0x336 that the constructor pointed at this status's row of GNL_ALRT.STR group 1.

entries.name: PausePanel_Ctor
entries.description: The small 178x68 sibling of the status alert, built on GNL_ALRT.HBA frame 1 and the same three GNL_ALRT.STR groups. Only statuses 0 and 1 have a case -- PAUSE with one button and EXIT EARTHSIEGE? with two -- and both reach it as constants from Sim_DispatchCommand. Any other status leaves it with no buttons.
entries.signature: void * __cdecl PausePanel_Ctor(void *panel, int status, char ownsBackingStore, int *rect)

entries.name: PreferencesPanel_Ctor
entries.description: prf_alrt: the [F12] preferences panel, the fourth member of the alert-panel family and the only one that does not centre -- it calls AlertPanel_SetRect with an explicit origin, (0, 0x96) << the coord shifts, for a 0x13f x 0x59 strip along the bottom of the screen. Loads hba\PRF_ALRT.HBA (plate frame 0, button frames 1-4) and str\PRF_ALRT.STR (five groups: title, 11 captions, OFF/ON, the three message words, the five detail words), then builds eleven buttons from the rect tables at 0049e224 and nine GREEN6X8 readouts from those at 0049e292. The nine option buttons are left in widget state 3 and CONTROLS and DONE put back to 0.

entries.name: PrefsAlert_Dtor
entries.description: PrefsAlert destructor (vtable 0049e40c, RTTI name 'PrefsAlert', 0x3c7 bytes): (panel, flags) reinstalls the vtable, Mem_Delete on the nine pointers at +0x332, GLBitmapArray_Dtor(_, 3) on DAT_004d1f80 when set (clearing +0x30), Alert_Dtor(panel, 0), then Mem_Delete when flags bit 0 is set. PreferencesPanel_Raise runs it with 3.
entries.source: DBSIM decompile at 00456cd4; RTTI at vtable-0xc

entries.name: PreferencesPanel_Run
entries.description: The preferences panel's modal loop and its action switch. Greys widgets 0-3 to state 2 when SfxManager is null, clears the queued action (+0x356), enters, focuses widget 0, and copies the panel's region between display pages. Each pass hands the input build to the slot +0x10 handler, acts on a queued widget index, then calls PreferencesPanel_CallDrawHook and PreferencesPanel_Present. Cases 0, 1 and 5 toggle options 0, 1 and 8; cases 4 and 6 step options 7 and 9 forward on a left click and back on a right; cases 7 and 8 (options 10 and 11) call the FORWARD step down both arms of their right-button test, so STRUCTURE DETAIL and EFFECTS DETAIL cannot be stepped backwards; cases 2 and 3 step options 2 and 3 forward only, and only while VoiceArchivePresent is set. A case that steps an option sets that row's refresh count to 2. Case 9 constructs ctl_alrt and runs it inline, then repaints this panel and focuses its cancel widget (+0x2fb). Case 10 calls PreferencesPanel_Save and sets the close flag to 3. Returns the close flag & 1.

entries.name: PreferencesPanel_Paint
entries.description: PrefsAlert vtable +0x00 (0049e40c): blits the panel bitmap (+0x30) at its rect (+0x1c) offset by the screen origin (DAT_004d25da/DAT_004d25de), sets the title from +0x35e through its own slot +0x04 (AlertPanel_SetTitleText), paints its +0x2cd children (listed from +0x291) through each one's slot +0x00, and runs PreferencesPanel_RefreshRow for rows 0-8.

entries.name: PreferencesPanel_Present
entries.description: (panel): the preferences panel's copy of the modal loop's tail.
