Sets the close flag +0x2d1 when the quit flag 004d2582 is set; calls vtable slot 3 (+0xc, the deferred paint) of each widget in the +0x291 list (count +0x2cd); for the first of the nine rows whose refresh count (+0x3be + row) is non-zero, PreferencesPanel_RefreshRow and decrements it; then WidgetRoot_ServicePressFlashes(+0x285) and Display_Present. Unlike AlertPanel_Present it puts no hold on the close flag. PreferencesPanel_Run calls it every pass (read).

entries.name: PreferencesPanel_RefreshRow
entries.description: Sets one of the nine readout labels from its option byte. Rows 0-3 and 5 index their string group directly; the four detail rows index the five-word group through a five-entry short[] map of their own at 0049e2da, 0049e2e4, 0049e2ee and 0049e2f8. The three {0,2,4,0,0} maps are why a three-setting row reads LOW / MED HIGH / MAXIMUM.

entries.name: PreferencesPanel_OnClick
entries.description: The preferences panel's click slot (vtable +0xc). Records the right-button flag at panel+0x2ff from bit 1 of the click value, walks the widget list for the clicked child, queues its index at panel+0x356 for the loop to act on, moves the highlight for widgets 0-8 (the row that had it, +0x3b6, back to state 3, this one to 0), and moves the focus (+0x2f7) to it, so [Return] next presses the widget last clicked. Ends with AlertPanel_ResetPresentTimer.

entries.name: PreferencesPanel_GetButtonCaption
entries.description: PrefsAlert vtable +0x14 (0049e40c), (panel, index): returns *(panel + 0x362 + index*4), the caption a button's paint asks its owner for.

entries.name: PreferencesPanel_SetDrawHook
entries.description: (panel, hook): stores hook at panel+0x3ba. PreferencesPanel_Raise installs 0045cfac.

entries.name: PreferencesPanel_CallDrawHook
entries.description: (panel): when the hook +0x3ba is set, points the display's (006c5f54) draw page +0x3c at its +0x8c (through maybe_g_RasterRoutines_SetDrawPage, mirroring it to 004a36a2), installs the panel's +0x281 render context, calls the hook, and reinstalls the panel's own context at +0x48. Its one caller found by es2_xref is PreferencesPanel_Run (read), once a pass of its loop.

entries.name: PreferencesPanel_Save
entries.description: Prefs_SaveSelectedOptions(9, DAT_0049e304), that list being options 0, 1, 2, 3, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11 -- the preferences panel's nine rows. Its one caller is PreferencesPanel_Run at 0045707a, on the arm that closes the panel; the CONTROLS arm jumps past it, so raising the controls panel does not save.

entries.name: PreferencesPanel_Revert
entries.description: Tests the same nine options with Prefs_OptionChanged and, if any changed, calls Prefs_RevertSelectedOptions over them. UNREFERENCED: ES2FindAddressRefs on 004574e0 returns nothing, against a fired positive control on 004574cc which returns its one caller. So the preferences panel has no reachable cancel -- leaving it saves.

entries.name: ObjectivesPanel_Ctor
entries.description: Builds obj_alrt, the [F11] objectives panel: 630x278 device, centred on the screen when rect is null. Writes its layout block to DAT_004d1f84..004d1fa4 once, loads hba\OBJ_ALRT.HBA as the plate and str\OBJ_ALRT.STR as its two captions, copies block 13's mission.str pointers (count DAT_004a9ec8, refs DAT_004a9ecc) into +0x34a, then builds the title label, the RETURN button with its ALERT bank plates, and seven objective-line labels at y 34 on a 20px pitch.

entries.name: ObjectivesPanel_Dtor
entries.description: ObjectiveAlert's destructor (class record 00457c7a), ObjectivesPanel_Ctor's object: (panel, flags). Reinstalls its table (0049e4f8), Mem_Deletes the seven pointers at +0x39c, OwnedArray_Dtor(panel+0x332, 2), Alert_Dtor(panel, 0), then Mem_Delete on flags bit 0.
entries.source: DBSIM decompile at 00457a80; class record at 00457c7a

entries.name: ObjectivesPanel_RunModal
entries.description: obj_alrt's modal loop, vtable slot +8. Enters via AlertPanel_Enter, focuses widget 0, then polls input, hands the event to the panel's slot +0x10 handler, ticks each clickable child and presents, until the close flag at +0x2d1 is set. It never calls the sim tick, which is why the simulation is stopped while a panel is up. gnl_alrt has its own near-identical copy at StatusAlertPanel_RunModal.

entries.name: ObjectivesPanel_Paint
entries.description: obj_alrt's vtable slot 0. Blits the plate at the panel origin plus the global blit offset, sets the title label, then walks block 13's resolved pointers filling line labels - skipping an empty string rather than leaving its row blank, and stopping once seven are filled. Finally calls each clickable child's own paint.

entries.name: ObjectivesPanel_OnChildClick
entries.description: obj_alrt's vtable slot +0xc. Sets the close flag when the clicked child is child 0, which is the panel's only widget - the RETURN button.

entries.name: ObjectivesPanel_GetButtonCaption
entries.description: obj_alrt's vtable slot +0x14: returns +0x346, the RETURN caption a button's paint asks its owner for.

entries.name: ControlsPanel_ActionAt
entries.description: Reads the per-button action table: eight rows of thirteen bytes at 0049e619 walking and 0049e681 flying, selected by PilotingRazor. Code 0 TERMINATES a row rather than meaning OFF -- the constructor counts a row's length by walking until it reads one -- so although OFF is action name 0 it is never an offered choice. Row 0 (BUTTON 1) holds one entry, FIRE. Args derived from raw disassembly: two stack slots at EBP+8 and EBP+0xc, both MOVSX from 16-bit (AX, DX); the row stride is 13 (LEA r,[x+x*2] then LEA r,[x+r*4]); RET with no operand.

entries.name: ControlsPanel_Ctor
entries.description: ctl_alrt: the joystick-binding panel the preferences panel's CONTROLS button raises. 0xb9 x 0xba << the coord shifts, centred when its third argument is null, which every reachable call site passes. Loads hba\CTL_ALRT.HBA (plate frame 0, then three button sizes at frames 1-4, 5-8 and 9-12) and eight groups of str\CTL_ALRT.STR -- and, when PilotingRazor is set, five more that overwrite the title and all four axis word sets, which is how the same panel becomes RAZOR CONTROLS. Builds fourteen buttons from the rect tables at 0049e510, twelve readouts from those at 0049e5b8, the OPTIONS caption and twelve list labels, then counts each button row's action list via ControlsPanel_ActionAt into panel+0x46a.

entries.name: ControlsAlert_Dtor
entries.description: ControlsAlert destructor (vtable 0049e82c, RTTI name 'ControlsAlert', 0x47e bytes): PrefsAlert_Dtor's shape with the twelve pointers at +0x3f6 and the bank DAT_004d1fb8. PreferencesPanel_Run runs it on its local with 2.
entries.source: DBSIM decompile at 004585d8; RTTI at vtable-0xc

entries.name: ControlsPanel_Run
entries.description: The controls panel's modal loop and its 14-case action switch. First asks Input_GetDevice(3) for a joystick and, when that answers null or with bit 0 clear, stores no capability block (+0x47a) and greys all twelve rows to state 2; otherwise stores Input_QueryCapabilities' block and greys the THROTTLE, RUDDER and HAT rows and every button row past the reported count. Seeds the four axis bytes and each button row's slot (+0x462) from the option array, enters, focuses widget 0, and loops until the close flag +0x2d1 is set: input to the slot +0x10 handler, then the queued action (+0x45a), then each widget's deferred paint (slot +0xc) and AlertPanel_Present. The switch runs only with a capability block whose first word is non-zero, and only then clears +0x45a. Cases 1-4 step an axis option over three values, forward on a left click and back on a right, when that axis is present (for JOYSTICK, when the block is), and clear the list selection; 5-12 select that button row and step it, forward on a left click and back on a right, when it is under the button count; 13 writes Input_RecommendedBindings' twelve bytes; 14 calls ControlsPanel_Save and Prefs_CommitOptions. The close itself is ControlsPanel_OnClick's.

entries.name: ControlsPanel_Paint
entries.description: ControlsAlert vtable +0x00 (0049e82c): PreferencesPanel_Paint's sequence with the title at +0x332 and ControlsPanel_RefreshRow for rows 1-12, then Label_SetText(+0x456, +0x3f2).

entries.name: ControlsPanel_RefreshRow
entries.description: Sets one of the twelve readout labels, 1-based: 1-4 are the axis rows and index their own three-word group through a cached byte, 5-12 are the button rows and index the twenty-one action names with the option byte directly. Every case is gated on that row's capability and sets NO text when it fails, which is why a greyed row reads blank rather than showing a stale binding.

entries.name: ControlsPanel_OnClick
entries.description: The controls panel's click slot (vtable +0xc). Records the right-button flag at panel+0x2ff, walks the widget list for the clicked child, moves the highlight (+0x472) for widgets 0-11 (the old one to state 3, this one to 0), and then decides between selecting and acting: a button row (widgets 4-11) that is not the selected one (+0x476) is selected with ControlsPanel_ShowOptionList, and anything else queues its action at +0x45a as the widget index plus 1 -- so a button row takes two clicks to change, and every click on an axis row is an action. Widget 13, DONE, also sets the close flag +0x2d1 to 3. It leaves the focus alone. Ends with AlertPanel_ResetPresentTimer.

entries.name: ControlsPanel_HandleEvent
entries.description: The controls panel's own event handler, vtable slot +0x10, in place of the family's AlertPanel_HandleEvent. Copies the device block's trigger byte (+0x0d) back over button state 0 so BUTTON 1 is live on the panel although the input build zeroes it, then takes the first of the eight button states that is set: a press on the selected row (+0x476) runs ControlsPanel_StepButton and flashes the row's widget (row + 4) on the panel's root (+0x285); a press on another row, when there is a capability block (+0x47a) and the row is under its button count (+2), runs ControlsPanel_ShowOptionList for it, flashes its widget, and moves the highlight (+0x472) to it, the old one to state 3 and this one to 0; in every case Input_LatchButton(row + 1) holds the button. Then the keys: [Return] (0x1c) presses the focus +0x2f7 through AlertPanel_PressWidget, or focuses widget 0 when it is -1; [Esc] (0x01) presses the cancel widget +0x2fb when it is set; [Tab] (0x0f) and scancode 0x52 focus the next widget and 0x80f, Shift+Tab, the previous -- a code the loop's input build has already masked to 0x0f with SimCommandMask. Any other code returns 0.

entries.name: ControlsPanel_CaptionAt
entries.description: The controls panel's caption slot (vtable +0x14), which PanelButton_Paint calls through the button's owner pointer to get the text for the index the button was built with. Returns *(panel + 0x336 + index*4), one of the fourteen str\CTL_ALRT.STR group-1 captions. Args derived from raw disassembly: EBP+8 and EBP+0xc, a single scaled-index load, RET with no operand.

entries.name: ControlsPanel_Save
entries.description: Builds a 13-entry index list spanning ControlsOptionBase-1 through ControlsOptionBase+11 -- option 12 plus the twelve bindings for a walker -- then Prefs_SaveSelectedOptions over it. The list is built once and latched by DAT_0049e7fc, so it keeps whatever ControlsOptionBase was at the first save. Called by ControlsPanel_Run at 00458c07, immediately before Prefs_CommitOptions.

entries.name: ControlsPanel_RevertAxisOptions
entries.description: (panel): Prefs_RevertOption(ControlsOptionBase + i, 1) for i = 0..3, the four axis options; copies the restored SimOptions bytes into the panel's axis bytes +0x45e..+0x461 (the cache ControlsPanel_RefreshRow indexes the axis word groups by); then ControlsPanel_Save. No caller, stored pointer or vtable slot found by es2_xref.

entries.name: ControlsPanel_ShowOptionList
entries.description: (panel, list): refills the option list with ControlsPanel_FillOptionList when list differs from the one shown (+0x476), then stores it there.

entries.name: ControlsPanel_StepButton
entries.description: Steps one button row to the next action in its own list: increments the slot index at panel+0x462+row, wraps to 0 past the row's length at panel+0x46a, then writes out whatever code ControlsPanel_ActionAt holds at that slot -- so the cycling is over slots, not codes, and a row whose stored code is not in its list steps from the top. Args derived from raw disassembly: EBP+8 into ESI (the panel, used as a base for +0x462/+0x46a) and EBP+0xc into EBX (the row, used as a byte index and added to ControlsOptionBase); RET with no operand.

entries.name: ControlsPanel_StepButtonBack
entries.description: ControlsPanel_StepButton's twin, decrementing the slot and wrapping to the row's length when it reaches 0xff. Same argument derivation.

entries.name: ControlsPanel_FillOptionList
entries.description: Refills the twelve OPTIONS labels from the selected button row's action list. Writes an empty string into every one when the selection is -1, and past the end of that row's list otherwise, which is why a freshly raised panel's list box is blank.

entries.name: PanelButton_Dtor
entries.description: AlertSelectGadget's destructor (class record 0045960c), PanelButton_Ctor's object: (button, flags). One RTL destructor-count decrement, PanelSelectGadget_Dtor(button, 0), then Mem_Delete on flags bit 0.
entries.source: DBSIM disassembly at 00459668; class record at 0045960c

entries.name: Prefs_InitPathAndHandlers
entries.description: When Prefs_Path is empty, copies Path_PrefixBaseDir("data\\prefs.cfg") into it (0xff characters); zeroes the 0x36 dword option-handler slots at Prefs_OptionHandlers; then Prefs_Init. Input_BuildSourceTable calls it.

entries.name: Prefs_LoadOptions
entries.description: Loads data\prefs.cfg over the option array: memset(&SimOptions, 0, 0x36) then a 0x36-byte read straight into it, so THE FILE IS THE ARRAY -- unparsed, an option's index is its byte offset, and a retail prefs.cfg is 54 bytes. Then walks all 0x36 options calling each one's handler from Prefs_OptionHandlers and seeding the shadow copies at DAT_004d1ff2 (when param_1 is non-zero) and DAT_004d2028. Its argument was not derived from disassembly, so no signature is recorded.

entries.name: Prefs_SaveAllOptions
entries.description: Opens the prefs path at Prefs_Path for write and writes all 0x36 bytes of SimOptions straight over it, with no read-modify-write. UNREFERENCED: ES2FindAddressRefs on 0045981c returns nothing of any kind, against a fired positive control on 00459b78 which returns its four callers. Every save retail actually performs goes through Prefs_SaveSelectedOptions instead.

entries.name: Prefs_CommitOptions
entries.description: Walks all 0x36 options: where SimOptions differs from the load-time shadow at DAT_004d1ff2 it calls that option's handler (when apply is set) and re-baselines the shadow, and it refreshes the outgoing shadow at DAT_004d2028 unconditionally. ControlsPanel_Run calls it at 00458c0f immediately after saving, so the controls panel applies and re-baselines on the way out.

entries.name: Prefs_RevertAllOptions
entries.description: (apply): for each of the 0x36 options whose load-time shadow (004d1ff2) differs from SimOptions, copies the shadow byte over SimOptions and, when apply is non-zero and Prefs_OptionHandlers has a handler for it, calls the handler with the restored value. No caller, stored pointer or vtable slot found by es2_xref.

entries.name: Prefs_UndoSetOption
entries.description: (index): SimOptions[index] = 004d2028[index], the previous value Prefs_SetOption saved there. It leaves the option's handler uncalled. No caller, stored pointer or vtable slot found by es2_xref.

entries.name: Prefs_SetOption
entries.description: Writes one simulator option: saves the old byte to (&DAT_004d2028)[index], stores value at (&SimOptions)[index], and when apply is non-zero calls the option's handler at (&Prefs_OptionHandlers)[index] with the new value. The option array based at SimOptions is what makes DAT_004d1fc3 (terrain detail) option 7. Derived from raw disassembly: three stack args at EBP+8/+0xc/+0x10, RET with no operand.
entries.signature: void __cdecl Prefs_SetOption(short index, unsigned char value, char apply)

entries.name: Prefs_ToggleOption
entries.description: Flips one option between 0 and 1 -- literally value ^ 1 -- and hands it to Prefs_SetOption. Returns the new value. The preferences panel's MUSIC, SOUNDS and TERRAIN TEXTURE rows take this where the other six take the step pair. Args derived from raw disassembly: two stack slots at EBP+8 (MOVSX from AX, so short) and EBP+0xc (read as a byte), RET with no operand.

entries.name: Prefs_StepOption
entries.description: Steps one option forward, wrapping to 0 when the incremented value equals the caller's modulus, and hands it to Prefs_SetOption. Returns the new value. The caller supplying the modulus is why one pair drives a three-value row and a five-value one. Args derived from raw disassembly: EBP+8 (MOVSX from AX), EBP+0xc and EBP+0x10 (both read as bytes), RET with no operand.
entries.signature: uchar __cdecl Prefs_StepOption(short index, char modulus, char apply)

entries.name: Prefs_StepOptionBack
entries.description: Prefs_StepOption's twin, stepping back and wrapping to modulus-1 when the decrement reaches 0xff. Reached only on a right-click, and only from four of the eleven rows that offer stepping at all. Same argument derivation as Prefs_StepOption.
entries.signature: uchar __cdecl Prefs_StepOptionBack(short index, char modulus, char apply)

entries.name: Prefs_IncreaseOption
entries.description: (index, amount, apply): saves SimOptions[index] to 004d2028[index], computes 0 when the value is 0xff, 0xff when value + amount would pass 0xff, else value + amount; hands that to Prefs_SetOption(index, new, apply) and returns it. No caller, stored pointer or vtable slot found by es2_xref.

entries.name: Prefs_DecreaseOption
entries.description: (index, amount, apply): Prefs_IncreaseOption's mirror -- saves SimOptions[index] to 004d2028[index], computes 0xff when the value is 0, 0 when it is below amount, else value - amount; hands that to Prefs_SetOption(index, new, apply) and returns it. No caller, stored pointer or vtable slot found by es2_xref.

entries.name: Prefs_RevertOption
entries.description: (index, apply): Prefs_SetOption(index, 004d1ff2[index], apply) -- the load-time shadow value -- and returns that value. Callers found by es2_xref: ControlsPanel_RevertAxisOptions (four calls, apply 1).

entries.name: Prefs_RevertSelectedOptions
entries.description: Copies the named options back out of the load-time shadow at DAT_004d1ff2 over SimOptions -- the revert half of the preferences panel. Memory only; it does not touch the file.

entries.name: Prefs_ApplyOption
entries.description: (index, apply): when apply is non-zero and Prefs_OptionHandlers[index] is set, calls that handler with SimOptions[index]. No caller, stored pointer or vtable slot found by es2_xref.

entries.name: Prefs_SaveOption
entries.description: One-option wrapper over Prefs_SaveSelectedOptions, taking the index off the stack. Called once, from MAIN's startup at 0045f413, immediately after Prefs_SetOption(6, ...) -- so option 6 is written to disk at every launch.

entries.name: Prefs_SaveSelectedOptions
entries.description: The only save path retail reaches. Re-reads the current 0x36-byte prefs.cfg into a local buffer, copies just the count options named in indices[] out of SimOptions over it, then writes the merged buffer back. So an option this call does not name keeps whatever is on disk rather than whatever is in memory. Four callers: PreferencesPanel_Save (9 options), ControlsPanel_Save (13), Joystick_InitAndSeedBindings (25, first run only) and the single-option wrapper Prefs_SaveOption.

entries.name: Prefs_OptionChanged
entries.description: Whether SimOptions[index] differs from the load-time shadow at DAT_004d1ff2. Note it reads the load-time shadow, not the per-write outgoing shadow at DAT_004d2028.

entries.name: Prefs_RegisterOptionHandler
entries.description: Writes one entry of the option handler table at 004d2060. Called five times by Prefs_Init.

entries.name: Prefs_ApplySoundsOption
entries.description: Handler for prefs option 1 (SOUNDS). Stores the byte through Sound_SetEffectsEnabled (00462c58), then -- unless PrefsInitInProgress (004d2138) is up -- calls Sound_UnmuteEffects or Sound_MuteEffects. Ghidra leaves this undefined as Prefs_ApplySoundsOption; Prefs_Init registers it by address.

entries.name: Prefs_ApplyMusicOption
entries.description: Handler for prefs option 0 (MUSIC) in the table at 004d2060. Stores the byte through Sound_SetMusicEnabled (00462c3c), then -- unless PrefsInitInProgress (004d2138) is up -- calls Sound_UnmuteMusic or Sound_MuteMusic. Byte-for-byte the twin of Prefs_ApplySoundsOption.

entries.name: Prefs_ApplyPilotMessageOption
entries.description: Handler for prefs option 2 (PILOT MESSAGE). Sets Sound_SpeechEnabled (0049f97e) from the byte being non-zero, so text-only (0) silences the voice half and both other settings enable it.

entries.name: maybe_Input_SetMouseActive
entries.description: (on): when the byte on differs from the byte at 0049e9ce, stores it there and, when Input_GetMouseDevice_Thunk returns non-zero, calls MouseDriver_NoOp (00480710) (an empty body) for a non-zero on and MouseDriver_ReturnZero (00480708) (returns 0) otherwise. Grep of the disassembly finds no other access to 0049e9ce. No caller, stored pointer or vtable slot found by es2_xref.

(value): stores the byte value at 0049eace, beside 0049eacc (the command-queue gate SimCommandQueue_Push tests) and 0049eacd (the byte SimInput_SetEnabled toggles). Grep of the disassembly finds no other access to 0049eace. No caller, stored pointer or vtable slot found by es2_xref.

entries.name: Input_SetThrottleLeverMode
entries.description: Sets ThrottleLeverMode (0049a06e) to 1 only when the input config struct (Input_QueryCapabilities) reports a throttle control at +2 AND the caller's mode == 1 (the preferences page's THROTTLE rather than TURRET assignment); 0 otherwise. This is the function that proves 0049a06e is a joystick-lever mode and not a forward/reverse gear -- with no lever it is 0, which leaves Mech_ApplyThrottleInput's clamp spanning the full +/-0x400 so the keyboard can reach reverse.

entries.name: Prefs_NoOp
entries.description: Empty body (PUSH EBP; MOV EBP,ESP; POP EBP; RET) between Input_SetThrottleLeverMode and Prefs_ApplyTerrainTextureOption. No caller, stored pointer or vtable slot found by es2_xref.

entries.name: Prefs_ApplyTerrainTextureOption
entries.description: Handler for prefs option 8 (TERRAIN TEXTURE). Sets TerrainTexturingEnabled (004aab2c) to 0 or 1. Terrain_LoadZone writes the same global from the same option byte, so the setting still reaches the terrain on the next zone load without the handler.

entries.name: Voice_ArchiveExists
entries.description: Builds the localised simvoice archive name via Voice_ArchiveName, fopens it, closes it again and returns whether it opened. Its answer is VoiceArchivePresent (0049e9cd), which is the whole of what lets the preferences panel's two message rows be stepped.

entries.name: Joystick_InitAndSeedBindings
entries.description: Builds the joystick device with JoystickDevice_Ctor(obj, 3, 0x201, 0xf, 1) and branches on option 12, the joystick-configured flag (DAT_004d1fc8). At 0: when the device's bit 0 says it enumerated, sets option 12, seeds options 0x0d-0x18 and 0x19-0x24 from Input_RecommendedBindings(0) and (1), saves options 12-36 through Prefs_SaveSelectedOptions (DAT_0049e9d0) and enables the device; otherwise destroys it. At 1: when it enumerated, enables it; otherwise destroys it and sets options 0x0d-0x18, the walking block, to 0 with apply, without saving. Any other value of option 12 builds nothing.

entries.name: Prefs_Init
entries.description: Preferences subsystem init: registers the five per-option handlers into the 004d2060 table via Prefs_RegisterOptionHandler (indices 0, 1, 2, 8 and 0x0e -- the last being Input_SetThrottleLeverMode, which is the herc controls block's THROTTLE row and so corroborates that block starting at 13), calls Prefs_LoadOptions, then sets VoiceArchivePresent from Voice_ArchiveExists and forces options 2 and 3 to 0 when it is clear.

entries.name: Input_RecommendedBindings
entries.description: Fills and returns the twelve-byte recommended binding block at 004d2139: four axis modes then eight action codes. Walking {1,0,2,2, 01,02,04,06,12,13,09,0a}, flying {1,0,2,2, 01,02,0d,0e,12,13,09,0a}. It also carries an arm that memsets the block to zero when the first word of Input_QueryCapabilities' block is 0, and that word is written unconditionally as 1 or 2, so the arm cannot be reached through its own input. Args derived from raw disassembly: one stack slot at EBP+8, tested as 0 / 1 / anything else; returns EBX, the literal 0x4d2139; RET with no operand.

entries.name: Input_KeyjoyAxisKey
entries.description: The simulator's axis-key subscriber, registered by SimInput_SetEnabled against the 30-byte list at 0049eb33 (keypad, M, J, K, I and Space, then the same fifteen with the key-up bit). Strips the 0x80 up-bit, finds the code's index in that list, folds the two banks of fifteen together and updates the three 15-byte key-state blocks at 004d2418 that Input_BuildKeyboardAxes reads.

entries.name: maybe_Input_CtrlDigitKeySubscriber
entries.description: (code): for a key code with Ctrl (0x400) set and Alt (0x200) clear, stores an int16 at 0049eb8a from the code's signed low byte c (the scancode) -- (c - 6) * 0x80 when c < 7, else (c - 7) * 0x80, so Ctrl+1..Ctrl+5 (2-6) give -0x200..0, Ctrl+6 (7) gives 0 and Ctrl+7..Ctrl+0 (8-0x0b) give 0x80..0x200 -- and returns 1; returns 2 for every other code. 1 and 2 are the claim results a keyboard subscriber returns (SimCommandQueue_Push returns 2 when its queue is closed). Grep of the disassembly finds no reader of 0049eb8a. No caller, stored pointer or vtable slot found by es2_xref.

entries.name: SimCommandQueue_Push
entries.description: Appends one command code to the queue at DAT_004d2148 that Input_BuildPlayerDevice drains into Sim_DispatchCommand, or returns 2 when the queue is closed (DAT_0049eacc). Registered as a keyboard subscriber by SimInput_SetEnabled against the 7-byte wanted-code list at 0049eb5d -- 1c 0c 0d 1a 1b 4e 4a, i.e. Enter, -, =, [, ] and the keypad +/- -- which is why it has no call site and why only those seven scancodes take this route.

entries.name: Input_BuildKeyboardAxes
entries.description: Builds the keyboard's contribution to the input axes: TWO signed pairs, not four independent axes. Held keys 0-7 accumulate into the first pair at 004d2445/004d2449, except that the first held diagonal (flags at 0049eb65: keypad 7, 9, 1, 3) zeroes the pair, adds its own entry and ends the group. Of keys 8-13 only the first held key counts, into the second pair at 004d244d/004d2451. Each entry comes from the table at 0049eb6d, shifted left 7 (+/-0x80). That table is filled at startup by the static initialiser at 0045b888. The pairs are sources, not destinations: Input_BuildSourceTable registers them alongside the joystick axes in the source-pointer table at 004d2394, and the binding config chooses which source each game axis reads.

entries.name: Input_BuildSourceTable
entries.description: Input-system init. Populates the source-pointer table at 004d2394 with the address of every available input value -- the two keyboard axis pairs Input_BuildKeyboardAxes writes, the four joystick axes at DAT_004d2414+0x0d/0x11/0x15/0x19, and the buttons -- so that a key or axis binding is a choice of pointer rather than a hardcoded path. This indirection is why Sim_PollPlayerInput reads some axes through a pointer-to-pointer.

entries.name: Input_BuildPlayerDevice
entries.description: The per-frame input build: reads the twelve controls-block bytes at ControlsOptionBase and routes the joystick's four normalised axes, hat and eight buttons into the device struct at PlayerInputBlock that Sim_PollPlayerInput consumes. Each axis row's byte selects a DESTINATION pair (0 unassigned, 1 the movement pair, 2 the turret pair), not a source; a control whose destination is taken falls to a second rank that wins when both have moved, and the keyboard pairs are the last fallback. Also: pulls the first FIRE-bound button of the walker's block out to +0x0d and zeroes its byte (using a hardcoded 0x11 rather than ControlsOptionBase+4, so a RAZOR finds its trigger through the walker's block), applies the press-once button latch Input_LatchButton sets, writes the hat over the turret pair at 0xc0 under HAT=2, and applies keyjoy.cfg's Backturn and Rudder reversals. It also owns the command queue at DAT_004d2148: it drains each code through Sim_DispatchCommand after masking with SimCommandMask = 0x47ff (which discards the Shift bank, folding a shifted key onto the plain one) and then resets the count. It is the input-tape record and playback point too -- see docs/retail/formats/tap-input-tape.md.

entries.name: Input_ReadMaskedKeyboardCommand
entries.description: (out): calls Input_ReadKeyboardCommand(out, 1), repeating while it returns non-zero with *out non-zero and its low (scancode) byte zero; then ANDs *out with SimCommandMask and returns the result. No caller, stored pointer or vtable slot found by es2_xref.

entries.name: SimInput_SetEnabled
entries.description: Toggles the simulator's keyboard input on and off. Turning it on registers two subscribers with KeyListener_Register: Input_KeyjoyAxisKey against the 30-byte list at 0049eb33 and SimCommandQueue_Push against the 7-byte list at 0049eb5d. Turning it off clears the three 15-byte key-state blocks at DAT_004d2418.

entries.name: Input_LatchButton
entries.description: (button 1-8, state): marks a joystick button as acted on, setting the byte at 004d2379 + button to 1 and storing state at 004d2381 + button. Input_BuildPlayerDevice then masks that button to zero until the player releases it, which is the whole of the press-once rule (docs/retail/formats/joystick-input.md, The buttons). Read callers: AlertPanel_HandleEvent latches buttons 1 and 2 as it answers them, and ControlsPanel_HandleEvent the pressed row's button.

entries.name: Input_GetCursorPos
entries.description: Returns &Input_CursorPos (004d238a). Cockpit_PickEdgeCursor reads the cursor from it during TapePlayback.

entries.name: Mouse_FitBoundsToDisplay
entries.description: Reads the bounds of the driver 0045c23c returns, sets x1 and y1 to the current display's width and height (GLDisplay_GetAttribute 0 and 1) less one, and writes them back with MouseDriver_SetBounds. Does nothing when 0045c23c returns 0.

entries.name: Keyjoy_LoadConfig
entries.description: Reads data\keyjoy.cfg once at input init: four GetPrivateProfileStringA calls against section [Keyjoy] for Tilt, Backturn, Missile and Rudder, each a case-insensitive compare against the word Reverse setting DAT_0049eab8/eabc/eac0/eac4. Anything else, the shipped Default included, leaves the flag clear. DBSIM's only profile import is GetPrivateProfileStringA.

entries.name: Input_InitKeyboardAxisTable
entries.description: Static initialiser (Borland _INIT_ entry 004a7b64, priority 0x20) that writes the 28-byte (dx,dy) table KeyboardAxisDeltas (0049eb6d) read by Input_BuildKeyboardAxes.

entries.name: Input_PollDeviceBlock
entries.description: Zeroes the 0x29-byte device block at 004d247a and refills it from each device whose kind is recorded: the keyboard (004d2520) through Input_ReadKeyboardCommand into the head word, bits 12 and 13 then cleared; the joystick (004d2528) through JoystickDevice_Poll on Input_GetDevice(3) and Input_ReadJoystickState into +0x0d..+0x28; the mouse (004d2524) through Input_ReadMouseState into the two ints at +2 and +6 and the bytes +0xa/+0xb/+0xc from button bits 0/1/2. Returns the block. Input_BuildSourceTable stores the pointer at 004d2414.

entries.name: Input_ReadKeyboardCommand
entries.description: (out, kind): for kind 1 with the keyboard device enabled, stores Input_ReadDeviceEvent's next code at out; returns 0 only when the device is disabled. Any other kind writes nothing and returns 1. Input_PollDeviceBlock fills the device block's head word with it, and Input_BuildPlayerDevice calls it.

entries.name: Input_ReadJoystickState
entries.description: (out, kind): for kind 3 or 4, takes the device in Input_DeviceTable[kind] less 0x1f; when it is enabled and its vtable (+0x24) slot 1 returns a record, copies 0x1d bytes of it into out. Returns 0 when the device is disabled or gives no record, 1 otherwise (other kinds write nothing). Input_PollDeviceBlock reads the joystick (kind in 004d2528) through it. The shape of Input_ReadMouseState.

entries.name: Input_ReadMouseState
entries.description: (out, kind): for kind 2 with the mouse device enabled, copies the {int, int, int16 buttons} record 0045c22c returns into out and caches it at 004d24a3; when 0045c22c returns null it copies the cached record instead. Returns 0 only when the device is disabled; for any other kind it writes nothing and returns 1.

entries.name: Input_EnableDevice
entries.description: (device): finds device among the nine entries of Input_DeviceTable and runs InputDevice_Enable on it; 0 when it is not registered.

entries.name: Input_DisableDevice
entries.description: (device): finds device among the nine entries of Input_DeviceTable and runs InputDevice_Disable on it.

entries.name: Input_GetKeyboardDevice_Thunk
entries.description: Calls Input_GetKeyboardDevice and returns its result (the decompile drops it). SimInput_SetEnabled tests it for nonzero.

entries.name: Input_GetMouseDevice_Thunk
entries.description: Calls Input_GetMouseDevice and returns its result. CockpitMouse_Init registers its listener on the device it returns; Gau_RovingGunsightWidget, AlertPanel_SetFocus and 00459cd8 test it for nonzero.

entries.name: InputDevice_StaticInit
entries.description: Static initialiser of the input-device block (Borland _INIT_ entry 004a7b6a, priority 0x20): a bare RET.

entries.name: InputDevice_Register
entries.description: (device, kind, slot): the input-device base: stores kind at device+1, slot in Input_DeviceTable[kind] (004d24ec) and clears the kind's enabled byte (004d2510 + kind). Kind 0 and 1 store the kind at 004d251c and 004d2520. Kind 2 (mouse) and 3 (joystick) first disable whichever device of that kind is already registered, then store the kind at 004d2524 or 004d2528 -- the nonzero 'one is registered' tests Input_GetMouseDevice and the device poll make. Returns device.

entries.name: InputDevice_Enable
entries.description: (device): for kind 2 or 3, disables the registered device of that kind when there is one and re-records the kind at 004d2524/004d2528; then sets device+0 = 1 and the kind's enabled byte at 004d2510. Input_BuildSourceTable enables the keyboard and mouse devices through it, Joystick_InitAndSeedBindings the joystick.

entries.name: InputDevice_Disable
entries.description: (device): clears device+0 and the kind's enabled byte at 004d2510 + device+1.

entries.name: InputDevice_IsEnabled
entries.description: (device): returns the enabled byte at device+0.

entries.name: Input_DeviceSlot
entries.description: (index): returns the input device pointer at Input_DeviceTable + index * 4. Input_GetDevice reads the table through it.

entries.name: Input_GetKeyboardDevice
entries.description: Returns Input_DeviceTable[the keyboard's kind at 004d2520] less 4, or 0 when 004d2520 says none is registered. The keyboard twin of Input_GetMouseDevice.

entries.name: Input_GetMouseDevice
entries.description: Returns the registered mouse device -- the device-table slot the value at 004d2524 names (Input_DeviceSlot(DAT_004d2524)), less 0x3a, the offset of its InputDevice sub-object -- or 0 when 004d2524 says none is registered. InputDevice_Enable records the slot there for kind 2 or 3. AlertPanel_Leave calls it directly.

entries.name: Input_IsKindEnabled
entries.description: (kind): returns the enabled byte at 004d2510 + kind.

entries.name: Kind0InputDevice_Ctor
entries.description: (this, word): InputDriverKind0_Ctor(this, word), then registers the InputDevice sub-object at this+6 as kind 0 with InputDevice_Register(this+6, 0, this+6), counts one live destructor (*Rtl_DtorCountPtr += 1) and returns this -- the kind-0 sibling of KeyboardInputDevice_Ctor and MouseInputDevice_Ctor. No caller, stored pointer or vtable slot found by es2_xref.

entries.name: KeyboardInputDevice_Ctor
entries.description: (this, arg): runs KeyboardDriver_Ctor(this, arg), registers the InputDevice sub-object at this+4 as kind 1, stores arg at +9 and clears +0xd. Input_BuildSourceTable constructs it with 0x10000.

entries.name: IMKeyboard_Dtor
entries.description: IMKeyboard's destructor, the dtor its class record (0xe bytes, at 0045b988) names: (keyboard, flags): decrements *Rtl_DtorCountPtr; when keyboard is not null, clears the byte at 004d2511, clears the dword at 004d2520 when it equals the keyboard's dword at +5, DVKeyboard_Dtor(keyboard, 0) for its DVKeyboard base, then Mem_Delete when flags bit 0 is set.

entries.name: Input_ReadDeviceEvent
entries.description: Pops one code from the unclaimed-key ring at 006bb734 for a keyboard device, draining the rest when the device asks for it. This is the route a code takes when no Key_WndProcHook subscriber claimed it.

entries.name: KeyboardInputDevice_SetReadMode
entries.description: (device, mode): calls DVKeyboard_ReturnZero (00477978) (a body that returns 0) with (device, mode), stores mode at device+9 and returns 1. device+9 is the read mode Input_ReadDeviceEvent switches on (0x10000 and 0x20000 pop a code with Keyboard_PopKey, 0x40000 returns 0), and the dword KeyboardInputDevice_Ctor stores its argument in. No reference found by es2_xref.

entries.name: KeyboardInputDevice_GetReadMode
entries.description: (device): returns the dword at device+9, the read mode KeyboardInputDevice_SetReadMode stores and Input_ReadDeviceEvent switches on. No reference found by es2_xref.

entries.name: Input_GetKeyboardDeviceUnchecked
entries.description: Frameless: Input_DeviceSlot(1) less 4 (the offset of the keyboard's InputDevice sub-object), or 0 when the slot is empty. The keyboard twin of Input_GetMouseDeviceUnchecked. No reference found by es2_xref.

entries.name: Input_GetKeyboardDevice2
entries.description: Frameless copy of Input_GetKeyboardDevice (0045bf24): 0 when the dword 004d2520 is 0, else Input_DeviceSlot(*004d2520) less 4, or 0 when that slot is empty. No reference found by es2_xref.

entries.name: MouseInputDevice_Ctor
entries.description: (this): runs MouseDriver_Ctor, then registers the InputDevice sub-object at this+0x3a as kind 2 with InputDevice_Register. Input_BuildSourceTable constructs it.

entries.name: MouseInputDevice_Dtor
entries.description: (this, flags): clears the enabled byte of the kind at this+0x3b, clears 004d2524 when that kind is the registered mouse, runs MouseDriver_Dtor and frees the object when flags bit 0 is set.

entries.name: MouseInputDevice_GetState
entries.description: (device): MouseDriver_GetState(); device is passed on and not read. Input_ReadMouseState copies the record it returns.

entries.name: Input_GetMouseDeviceUnchecked
entries.description: Input_DeviceTable[2] less 0x3a, or 0 when the slot is empty -- Input_GetMouseDevice without its 004d2524 registration test. Mouse_FitBoundsToDisplay calls it.

entries.name: Input_GetMouseDevice2
entries.description: Frameless copy of Input_GetMouseDevice (0045bf4c): 0 when the dword 004d2524 is 0, else Input_DeviceSlot(*004d2524) less 0x3a, or 0 when that slot is empty. No reference found by es2_xref.

entries.name: JoystickDevice_Ctor
entries.description: Constructs the joystick input device: base ctor JoystickDevice_CtorBase (which enumerates and sets the resolution field +0x16 to 7), registers it in the device table as kind 3, installs vtable PTR_FUN_0049ec9c at +0x24 and stores the response-curve selector at +0x28. Its one caller Joystick_InitAndSeedBindings passes (3, 0x201, 0xf, 1).

entries.name: JoystickDevice_Dtor
entries.description: IMJoystick vtable +0x00 (0049ec9c, the table at +0x24 of the joystick device JoystickDevice_Ctor builds), the destructor its class record names: (device, flags). Reinstalls that table, clears the kind's enabled byte (004d2510 + the kind at +0x20) and DAT_004d2528 when that holds the same kind, runs DVJoystick_Dtor (00477524) with flags 0, and Mem_Deletes on flags bit 0. It leaves the kind's Input_DeviceTable slot holding the device, so Input_GetDevice(3) goes on returning it after it is destroyed.
entries.source: DBSIM decompile at 0045c2c4; class record at 0045c537

entries.name: Joystick_ReadWithResponse
entries.description: The joystick device object's vtable +4: normalises, applies the deadzone and the response curve selected by the object's +0x28, then expands the button mask and hat bits into the 0x1d-byte block at DAT_004d24b0. A joystick is always built with mode 1 (Joystick_InitAndSeedBindings passes it to JoystickDevice_Ctor), the SQUARED curve: deadzone 0x19 SUBTRACTED to give +/-103, then |x|^2 scaled by 1/((103*103)>>8), so full deflection is 103*103/41 = 258, just over the 0x100 the control laws clamp at. Mode 0 is linear; mode 2 reads through Joystick_ReadAxisSigns, whose -1/0/+1 axes the deadzone then zeroes. Neither is used by the joystick; reading the deadzone as mode 0's linear rescale puts full deflection on 0x80 and halves every downstream response.

entries.name: Input_GetDevice
entries.description: (kind): Input_DeviceSlot(kind) less 0x1f, the joystick device's offset to its object base, or 0 when the slot is null. Kind 3 is the joystick. It reads the slot alone, and JoystickDevice_Dtor leaves the slot set, so after a stick fails to enumerate Input_GetDevice(3) returns the destroyed device rather than 0 (docs/retail/formats/joystick-input.md, A stick that does not enumerate).

entries.name: JoystickDevice_Poll
entries.description: (device): Joystick_Poll(device). Input_PollDeviceBlock calls it on Input_GetDevice(3).

entries.name: Vga_WaitVerticalRetrace
entries.description: MOV DX,0x3da / IN AL,DX / TEST AL,8 / JZ: spins until the VGA input-status register reports vertical retrace. One caller, CockpitView_ProcessViewCommand (0042a726), on the -b paged path only. A user-mode IN faults on NT-family Windows.

entries.name: Vga_WaitRetraceEnd
entries.description: Frameless: MOV DX,0x3da / IN AL,DX / TEST AL,8 / JNZ: spins while the VGA input-status register reports vertical retrace, the complement of Vga_WaitVerticalRetrace (0045c61c) just before it. A user-mode IN faults on NT-family Windows. No reference found by es2_xref.

entries.name: MonoComponentPanel_Init
entries.description: (block): a developer panel on the monochrome monitor. Stores block at MonoComponentPanel_Block (004d2530) and block+2 at the cursor MonoComponentPanel_Cursor (004d2534), maybe_Mono_Clear, then for each of the 41 label pointers at MonoComponentPanel_Labels (0049eca4) (FRONT_COCKPIT, REAR_COCKPIT, the brackets, shoulders, legs and feet, LEFT/RIGHT LEG SERVO, SENSORS, TARGETING COMPUTER, SHIELD GENERATOR, ENGINE, HYDRAULICS, STABILIZER, LIFE_SUPPORT, PILOT, the rear leg servos, WEAPON 1-10) prints the label with Mono_Printf at (column MonoComponentPanel_LabelColumn (004d2538), row MonoComponentPanel_Row (004d253a)), zeroes the int16 at the cursor and prints it with '%d' at column MonoComponentPanel_ValueColumn (004d253c), advancing the cursor by 2. Rows run 1 to 0x16; a full column moves both columns 0x28 right. Then resets the cursor to block+2, row 1, columns 2 and 0x1e, and prints '>' at (1, 1). No reference found by es2_xref.

entries.name: MonoComponentPanel_CursorDown
entries.description: Frameless: prints ' ' at (MonoComponentPanel_LabelColumn (004d2538) - 1, MonoComponentPanel_Row (004d253a)); unless the cursor MonoComponentPanel_Cursor (004d2534) is at MonoComponentPanel_Block (004d2530) + 0x52 (the 41st value), advances it by 2 and the row MonoComponentPanel_Row (004d253a) by 1, moving to the next column pair (row 1, both columns +0x28) on reaching row 0x17; prints '>' at the new row. Mono_Printf throughout. No reference found by es2_xref.

entries.name: MonoComponentPanel_CursorUp
entries.description: Frameless: prints ' ' at (MonoComponentPanel_LabelColumn (004d2538) - 1, MonoComponentPanel_Row (004d253a)); unless the cursor MonoComponentPanel_Cursor (004d2534) is at MonoComponentPanel_Block (004d2530) + 2 (the first value), moves it back 2 and the row up 1, moving to the previous column pair (row 0x16, both columns -0x28) on reaching row 0; prints '>' at the new row. No reference found by es2_xref.

entries.name: MonoComponentPanel_IncreaseValue
entries.description: Frameless: adds 0x20 to the int16 at the cursor MonoComponentPanel_Cursor (004d2534), clamps it to 0xff, and prints it with '%d     ' at (MonoComponentPanel_ValueColumn (004d253c), MonoComponentPanel_Row (004d253a)). No reference found by es2_xref.

entries.name: MonoComponentPanel_DecreaseValue
entries.description: Frameless: subtracts 0x20 from the int16 at the cursor MonoComponentPanel_Cursor (004d2534), clamps it to 0, and prints it with '%d     ' at (MonoComponentPanel_ValueColumn (004d253c), MonoComponentPanel_Row (004d253a)). No reference found by es2_xref.

entries.name: VideoMode_BlitBitmap
entries.description: (block, bitmap, point): draws a bitmap at point less block+0x9a/+0x9e (004d25da/004d25de). Does nothing for a null bitmap. With the panel mode (+0x7b) 3 and the hi-res-banks flag (+0xb0) clear it calls 004816bc with a size of the bitmap's column count (+6) and row count (+4) shifted left by the X and Y coordinate shifts (+0x7e, +0x80), stored at 004d275c/004d2760; otherwise Bitmap_Blit(bitmap, point, 0). All 39 call sites pass the video-mode block 004d2540.

entries.name: VideoMode_BlitBitmapFlags
entries.description: (block, bitmap, point, flags): VideoMode_BlitBitmap with a flags argument passed through: Bitmap_BlitScaled at the bitmap's size doubled by the coordinate shifts in panel mode 3 without hi-res banks, else Bitmap_Blit(bitmap, point, flags).

entries.name: VideoMode_BlitBitmapSized
entries.description: (block, bitmap, point, flags, size): Bitmap_BlitScaled at an explicit size, with the size shifted left by the coordinate shifts (+0x7e, +0x80) first in panel mode 3 without hi-res banks. The point is offset by block+0x9a/+0x9e as in VideoMode_BlitBitmap.

entries.name: VideoMode_BlitRotated
entries.description: (block, bitmap, point, a, b, c): does nothing for a null bitmap; otherwise Bitmap_BlitRotatedUnpacked(bitmap, point less block+0x9a/+0x9e, a, b, c). All callers pass the video-mode block 004d2540.

entries.name: Main_StaticInit
entries.description: MAIN.CPP's C++ static initialiser: the priority-0x20 entry at 004a7b70 in Borland's _INIT_ table (00 20 d8 ca 45 00), with no direct caller. Loads the video-mode/sim-globals block base 004d2540 into EBX, constructs the member object at 004d2603 (GLBitmap_Ctor), memsets the 0xc3-byte block to zero and fills its defaults through EBX: among them VideoMode_PanelMode (+0x7b) and maybe_CockpitLayoutMode (+0x7c) = 0, the 320-wide mode-0 geometry, Display_UseScrollWindow (+0xaa, 004d25ea) = 1, PilotingRazor = 0 and ControlsOptionBase = 0xd. Ends by seeding the two Math_RandomNext state blocks at 004d261d and 004d268f. The only write of +0x7c anywhere, and the only writer of +0x7b besides VideoMode_Configure.

entries.name: Main_StaticDtor
entries.description: MAIN.CPP's _EXIT_ routine (the function pointer at 004a7c50), Main_StaticInit's counterpart: decrements *Rtl_DtorCountPtr and runs GLBitmap_Dtor(004d2603, 2) on the GLBitmap member at +0xc3 of the MGlobs block at 004d2540.

entries.name: MGlobs_Dtor
entries.description: MGlobs's destructor, the dtor its class record (0xdd bytes, at 0045cc07) names: (globs, flags): when globs is not null, decrements *Rtl_DtorCountPtr, GLBitmap_Dtor(globs+0xc3, 2), then Mem_Delete when flags bit 0 is set.

entries.name: Tape_PackFile
entries.description: Writes one bundle block into an open tape: a uint32 size then the named file's bytes in 500-byte chunks. A source file it cannot open writes size 0, which is why data\object.str is empty in every retail tape.

entries.name: Tape_UnpackFile
entries.description: Reads one bundle block out of an open tape and writes it to the named path, in 500-byte chunks. A null destination consumes the block and discards it.

entries.name: Resource_Load
entries.description: Resource_Load(path): wraps a folder\name string into a temporary object and calls ClassItem_LoadResource(obj, 0), returning the loaded resource handle. The single entry point every HUD sprite bank, panel and cursor load goes through after ResourcePath_BuildFolderName builds the path.

entries.name: Cursor_LoadCursorResource
entries.description: (): ResourcePath_BuildFolderName('cursor', the folder string at 004a0a2c, 'dci'), VolRStream_CtorFromPath on the result, ClassItem_LoadResource(stream, 0), VolRStream_Dtor; returns the loaded item. Resource_Load's body with this one path built in. No reference found by es2_xref.

entries.name: DemoTape_PickRandom
entries.description: Loads group 0x14 of tapes\demolist.str and returns entry time() % count, or entry 0 when the table holds one name. The retail table holds DEMO1, DEMO2 and DEMO3.

entries.name: PreferencesPanel_OrbitViewHook
entries.description: Frameless draw hook: Cam_Steer(ViewObjectPtr, -0x40, 0, 0), Cam_Update(ViewObjectPtr), Sim_RenderFrame(). PreferencesPanel_Raise installs it with PreferencesPanel_SetDrawHook (PUSH 0x45cfac at 0045d28b) after attaching the view camera to LocalPlayerMech (Cam_AttachTo, CAM+0x36 = 1 when CAM+0x4a is 0), and PreferencesPanel_CallDrawHook runs it once per pass of PreferencesPanel_Run's loop, so the camera turns about the player's machine behind the panel.

entries.name: PreferencesPanel_Raise
entries.description: What commands 0x58 ([F12]) and 0x219 ([Alt+P]) reach. Builds prf_alrt (PreferencesPanel_Ctor, 004566c4 -- NOT ctl_alrt, which is 00457d1c), saves DAT_004d2576 and sets it to stop the simulation, and copies the view camera's (ViewObjectPtr) +0x04..+0x4d into a local CAM. Sets the external view's 3D rect through ExternalView_SetRect: columns 0..DAT_004d25c2-1, rows 0..panel+0x08-1 (the panel's screen top), projection centre ((DAT_004d25c2-1) >> 1, 0x32 << VideoMode_YCoordShift), passed negated. With the cockpit view manager (CockpitViewManagerInstance) in view 4 it then Cam_AttachTo(LocalPlayerMech), sets CAM+0x36 = 1 when CAM+0x4a is 0, and runs Cam_Update and Sim_RenderFrame once. From any other view it runs Sim_EndFrame/Cam_Update/Sim_RenderFrame frames while the published manager's step flag +0x1c is set or its queued command +0x18 is not -1, saves the manager's view, queues view command 2 (CockpitView_QueueViewCommand), and runs frames until the step flag has been seen set and then clear, attaching the camera the same way on the frame it is first seen set. Then installs PreferencesPanel_OrbitViewHook (0045cfac) with PreferencesPanel_SetDrawHook, runs the panel through its vtable +0x08 (PreferencesPanel_Run, 00456d4c) and destroys it. On the way out writes the camera block back and calls ExternalView_ResetRect; then from view 4 repaints the band and caption (CockpitViewManager_Published, View_FillOutside3dRect, ViewChain_DrawCaption) around one Cam_Update/Sim_RenderFrame/Sim_EndFrame frame, and from any other view calls CockpitView_SetView with the saved view on both sides of one such frame, with DAT_0049b104 raised between them. Restores DAT_004d2576 last.

entries.name: ShapeDetail_ApplyHercDetailSetting
entries.description: Applies the HERC DETAIL preference (DAT_004d1fc5, 0-4) to three globals through three key/value table pairs: g_ShapeDetailSizeScaleQ10 (2000 in every slot), g_ShapeDetailBias {4,3,2,1,0} and g_TSDetailBiasFromHercDetail {2,2,1,1,0}. Called from Sim_RenderFrame when the byte changes and unconditionally at mission bring-up (00461ddc); both sites push the preference byte itself, with nothing in between.

entries.name: StructureDetail_ApplySetting
entries.description: The STRUCTURE DETAIL counterpart of ShapeDetail_ApplyHercDetailSetting, called with DAT_004d1fc6 from the same two sites. Walks g_StructureDetailKeys and writes the matching g_StructureDetailValues entry into both g_TSDetailBiasFromStructureDetail -- which Structure_DrawWithDetailBias pushes into the TSDetailPart bias -- and DAT_004a9e48, whose consumer is not traced.

entries.name: LiftStart_DarkenPalette
entries.description: The lift start's darkening, left over from Metaltech: Earthsiege's elevator-lift mission start: called from Sim_InitMissionSession at 00461cec when block +0x54 is set. Builds two GLPalette objects whose headers copy ActivePaletteObject's, each over its own copy of the live entries (004d27c8 over 004d27d0, 004d27cc over 004d27d4), sets 0049aef6 to 8 and calls Palette_NoOp, rewrites entries 32-47 and 64-79 of the first as (G>>1, R>>1, B>>1) -- red and green swapped as well as halved -- installs those two spans live, and starts a 0x78-coarse-tick Palette_BeginCrossFade from the darkened object to the copy. Clears 0049aef4. LiftStart_Rise steps the fade and frees all four allocations.

entries.name: LiftStart_Rise
entries.description: The lift start's ride, left over from Metaltech: Earthsiege: called from Sim_InitMissionSession at 00461e28 when block +0x54 is set. Loads dba\intro (absent from every retail VOL) and uses its frame 0 unchecked. Raises the player machine from placed z - 4000 to placed z, 35 units a frame, with sound 0x21 running; each frame projects view-space (0, 1000, -camera z) -- world height 0, 1000 units ahead -- to a screen row, renders the scene with the viewport bottom cut to that row, blits intro from the row down and fills colour id 19 (DAT_004d3c26) below it, and steps the cross-fade while the row is below -200 and LiftStart_FadeRemaining is nonzero, then Sim_EndFrame. Sim_MainTick does not run. At the top: stops 0x21, plays 0x29, CockpitView_SetShakeBand(5) and one CockpitView_StepShake((next & 0xffff) % 5) on 0x4d268f per Sim_RenderFrame for 0x1e coarse ticks, with no Sim_EndFrame, so none of those frames is presented. Then clears the shake, frees the palettes and sets 0049aef4.

entries.name: Sim_DeathFlash
entries.description: Loads the death1/death2/world0 palettes, mutes effects, plays 0x26, fades death1 -> death2 -> black over 0x78 ticks each while shaking the view (band 10, Math_RandomBelow(0x4d268f, 10)) for the first 0x1e ticks, then installs world0 and runs a StatusAlertPanel of kind 2. es2_xref finds nothing reaching it, and the death1 and death2 palettes it loads are in no shipped VOL or install file. The player's death plays ViewChain_PlayerDeathCamera instead.

entries.name: ViewChain_NoOp1
entries.description: Frameless lone RET between Sim_DeathFlash and ViewChain_Apply. No reference found by es2_xref.

entries.name: ViewChain_NoOp2
entries.description: Frameless lone RET after ViewChain_NoOp1, before ViewChain_Apply. No reference found by es2_xref.

entries.name: ViewChain_Apply
entries.description: Once a tick from Sim_MainTick. While the view manager's step flag (+0x1c) is up, moves ViewChain_View to the pending view 004d259e and sets the camera up for it (views 1-4: free, cockpit, outside, chase); otherwise, in the outside view on the player, copies the preference 004d259c into InputDrivesCamera. Draws the caption while 004d25a4 counts.

entries.name: ViewChain_ViewObject
entries.description: Moves ViewObjectPtr onto the squad camera (004d270c) already viewing the object, or a free one seeded from the current camera and attached afresh, or the spare at 004d27d8. Stores the object in 004d2708 and sets InputDrivesCamera to 1, or to 004d259c for the player.

entries.name: ViewChain_DrawCaption
entries.description: The external view's caption: 'VIEW: ' + YOU / the squad pilot's name at x 50 and 'CONTROL: ' + CAMERA / HERC at x 215, STRINGS0.STR groups 36 and 17, in the green 6x8 font, centred in the band below the view-4 3D rect.

entries.name: ViewChain_StaticDtor
entries.description: _EXIT_ routine (entry 004a7c54, pointer at 004a7c56) for two function-local statics: when the guard byte 0049f214 is set, two *Rtl_DtorCountPtr decrements and TSContext_Dtor(ViewChain_SpareCamera, 0), the CAM ViewChain_ViewObject constructs on first use; when the guard byte 0049f05a is set, OwnedArray_Dtor(DemoTape_NameTable (004d2764), 2), the StringTable DemoTape_PickRandom constructs on first use. The 'PrefsAlert' class record follows it.

entries.name: VideoMode_Configure
entries.description: Sets the whole video-mode global block from a mode byte read out of the prefs file. Mode 0: VideoMode_PanelMode=0, UseHiResBanks=0, viewport 320x240, canvas 320x480, back buffer 640x480, coord shifts 0. Mode 1: UseHiResPanels=3, UseHiResBanks=0, viewport 640x480, canvas 640x960, back buffer 1280x960, shifts 1. Mode 2: as mode 1 but UseHiResBanks=1. So UseHiResPanels==3 selects .HFN/.HBA/.HB<n> art while UseHiResBanks separately selects the hi-res HUD sprite banks -- which is why the two idioms documented in cockpit-views.md differ. All three branches also set Display_UseScrollWindow (004d25ea) to 1, the scroll-window display path; Sim_ParseCommandLine runs later and its -b case clears it, selecting the paged path. None of them writes maybe_CockpitLayoutMode (004d25bc), which no code in the image can write at all.

entries.name: WinMain_ParseSwitches
entries.description: (argc, argv): WinMain's first switch pass, after VideoMode_Configure(0) and before MainWindow_Create. For each of argv[1..] that starts with '-': 'X' stores _atol of the rest in 004d283c (WinMain's return value); 'Z' stores 1 in 004d25e2 when the next character is '1', else 0 (WinMain toggles full screen when it is set); 'c' stores the word 1 at 004d25b2 (+0x72 of the 004d2540 block); 'v' calls VideoMode_Configure(next character - '0'). Sim_ParseCommandLine parses the rest. docs/retail/command-line.md#dbsim.

entries.name: Sim_ParseCommandLine
entries.description: DBSIM's own argument parser. Owns the input-tape switches -r (record to <name>.tap), -p (play it back) and -D (play a tape DemoTape_PickRandom chooses, with the demo abort armed), plus -eggplant, the language and video switches and the -d dmp log.

entries.name: Cam_AttachTo
entries.description: Asks the object's vtable +0x30 for its eye and orbit-centre points, then Cam_AttachEye and Cam_AttachOrbit on ViewObjectPtr -- so an attach always ends in mode 1, directly behind at the least distance.

entries.name: View_GetActiveObject
entries.description: Returns ViewObjectPtr. HddMap_DrawTerrain reads the map projection's +4 triple through it: centre x, centre y, scale.

entries.name: Path_PrefixBaseDir
entries.description: Returns 004d28e0, a static buffer holding the directory string at 004d2840 followed by the given path with any drive letter ('X:') removed. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's Path_PrefixBaseDir; DBSim_LoadScriptDat, DBSim_SpawnMissionObjects, DemoTape_PickRandom and Keyjoy_LoadConfig build paths with it.

entries.name: DriveCfg_PrefixPath
entries.description: (path): copies the directory at 004d2890 -- DriveCfg_Directory, which Sim_Run fills from data\drive.cfg -- into 004d2930, appends path less a leading drive 'X:' when path[1] is ':', and returns 004d2930. OnlineManual_Raise resolves es2guide.hlp through it and PilotMessagePort_Paint the training voice clips.

entries.name: Config_BuildPath
entries.description: (name): 'data\' + name, or 'tapes\' + name while TapePlayback is set, built in the static buffer 004d2980, which it returns. prefs.cfg and keyjoy.cfg are opened through it.

entries.name: Language_StringFilePath
entries.description: (name, extension): builds 'st<letter>\<name>.<extension>' in the static buffer 004d29a0, the letter being the language letter 004d25ba patched into the 'str' literal at 0049f27d (so 'str' for the default r). The name and extension go through Path_WithExtension. ColorSchemePanels_LoadAll, the alert panel constructors and the sound catalog build their .STR paths with it.

entries.name: Voice_ArchiveName
entries.description: Returns the voice archive name, patching the last character of the literal 'simvoice' with the language byte at 004d25ba: SIMVOICE / SIMVOICF / SIMVOICG.

entries.name: Voice_FilePath
entries.description: (name, extension): builds '<Voice_ArchiveName()>\<name>.<extension>' in the static buffer 004d29be, the name and extension going through Path_WithExtension. The message ports and CommBox_BeginMessage find their speech files with it.

entries.name: Language_GetFolderName
entries.description: Reads the first byte of data\language.cfg and returns the matching resource folder name: 'F' -> FRENCH, 'G' -> GERMAN, 'S' -> SPANISH, anything else ENGLISH. The retail CD ships the first three.

entries.name: OnlineManual_Raise
entries.description: Command 0x35's handler: composes <Language_GetFolderName()>\es2guide.hlp into the buffer at 004d29dc, resolves it to a full path through DriveCfg_PrefixPath and returns that path -- the caller passes it to Help_Show. Two callers, Sim_DispatchCommand's `?` case and SystemButtons_OnChildClick's child 0, so the key and the right-hand system button are one path. This is the manual's 'On-Line Manual' MISC. entry -- a Windows help file, not a game screen.

entries.name: Sim_Suspend
entries.description: Sets DAT_004d25f6, which holds Sim_Run's loop in its sleep-and-pump branch, suspends every sound (Sound_SuspendAll) and, when CockpitViewInstance is set, pauses the cockpit's two message ports. MainWndProc calls it on WM_KILLFOCUS and on WM_POWERBROADCAST with PBT_APMSUSPEND (4). The pair to Sim_Resume.

entries.name: Sim_Resume
entries.description: Clears DAT_004d25f6, resumes every sound (Sound_ResumeAll) and, when CockpitViewInstance is set, resumes the cockpit's two message ports. MainWndProc calls it on WM_SETFOCUS and on WM_POWERBROADCAST with PBT_APMRESUMESUSPEND (7). The pair to Sim_Suspend.

entries.name: Cockpit_RepaintShieldGauge
entries.description: When CockpitViewInstance and its shield gauge (+0x1e9) are set, calls the gauge's vtable slot 1. Video_ToggleFullscreen calls it.

entries.name: Sim_Run
entries.description: WinMain's body: reads data\drive.cfg into DriveCfg_Directory, parses the command line, and shows a message box and returns when 004d25a8 is clear. Otherwise runs subsystem phases 0 and 1, asserts at under 8 MB physical memory and sets CockpitArt_LoadOnDemand under 12 MB, runs Sim_InitMissionSession and phase 3, then loops: phase 4, Time_BeginSimTick unless TapePlayback, then while 004d25f6 is set Sleep(100) and Win_PumpMessages (WM_QUIT ends it), else Sim_MainTick, Cam_Update(ViewObjectPtr), Sim_RenderFrame, Sim_EndFrame, phase 6 and Sim_FrameCount++, until DemoAbort, the quit flag 004d2582 or a non-zero Sim_MainTick. Then stops the music and sound, saves option 6 if the full-screen state changed, reopens tapes\prefs.cfg and tapes\keyjoy.cfg after a tape playback, and calls Sim_Shutdown.

entries.name: Sim_MainTick
entries.description: DBSIM's per-frame simulation tick. Updates SimTickDelta from a hardware/timer source, iterates every global object list, and calls Mech_PerTickSystemsUpdate once per live mech in GlobalMechList.

entries.name: ViewChain_PlayerDeathCamera
entries.description: Sim_MainTick calls it once a tick in place of Mission_PollStatus while the player's machine is destroyed (+0x99) and the simulation is not frozen (DAT_004d2576); a nonzero return makes Sim_MainTick raise the status alert for 2 and end the mission whatever the answer. First call, latched by DeathCamera_Started: arms DeathCamera_Countdown from its class table, makes the player ViewChain_Chosen, enters the outside view on the player (from the cockpit by view command 2 and pending view 3, otherwise ViewChain_ViewObject and ViewChain_CaptionFrames = 2), sets InputDrivesCamera, runs CockpitView_ProcessViewCommand and ViewChain_Apply itself, and unless the camera is locked writes the orbit pitch, roll 0, heading and distance. Every call: clears the camera lock +0x4a, Cam_Steer with the class's constant steer, throttle and trigger, sets the lock, and returns Timer_CountDown(DeathCamera_Countdown) == 0. Every table is indexed by the type record's +0x50, 0 walker and 1 RAZOR. Holds the 004d2540 block base in ESI throughout.

entries.name: Sim_StaticInitNoOp
entries.description: _INIT_ entry 004a7b76 (pointer at 004a7b78): a lone RET, after ViewChain_PlayerDeathCamera, closing the block that holds Sim_Run, whose assert strings name MAIN.CPP.

entries.name: Sim_EndFrame
entries.description: Per-frame tail. Scroll-window path (Display_UseScrollWindow != 0): CockpitView_StepViewTransition, Palette_CycleAnimatedRanges, Palette_FlushDirtyRange, Display_Present, CockpitView_ProcessViewCommand, with the +0xac render target selected around them under VideoMode_PanelMode 1. Paged path (-b): the same calls without Display_Present, plus a page flip -- the render target's +0x8c becomes the visible page (+0x34, g_RasterRoutines slot 18), +0x88 the draw page (+0x3c, slot 17), and the two swap. Driver 3 fills both slots with empty stubs, so under -b nothing here reaches the screen.

entries.name: Sim_RenderFrame
entries.description: The whole frame draw; Sim_Run calls it once a frame, between Cam_Update and Sim_EndFrame. Order: Subsystem_RunPhase(5); ShapeDetail_ApplyHercDetailSetting when option byte 004d1fc5 has changed and StructureDetail_ApplySetting when 004d1fc6 has; adds CockpitView_GetShakeOffset's pair into the ints at Sim_RenderContext +0x220/+0x224 for the frame; Raster_InstallViewProjection(ViewObjectPtr), Terrain_SetupVisibleRegion(ActiveHeightGrid, view, 0), CockpitView_PerFrameUpdate, Scene_SubmitFrameObjects; then, when CockpitView_ShowsWorld, Raster_InstallViewProjection(ViewObjectPtr) again, LightManager_SetCameraPosition(ViewObjectPtr + 4), Terrain_SetupVisibleRegion again, Raster_SetModelTransform(0), Scene_DrawTerrainPass and ObjList_DrawAfterTerrain; then Player_PerFrameCockpitUpdate, slot +8 of CockpitViewInstance+0x1f5, slot +0x10 of CockpitView_GetSquadMessagePort's port and of CockpitViewInstance+0x20b; takes the shake offset back out; and ends with SystemButtons_PaintForPointer(CockpitViewInstance, &DAT_004d234c).

entries.name: ViewChain_ToggleCameraControl
entries.description: [Enter]/[Tab] in view 4: flips 004d259c, and redraws the caption when the camera is on the player.

entries.name: Sim_HandleWindowKey
entries.description: (code): 0x21c ([Alt+Enter]) runs Video_ToggleFullscreen unless a tape is playing back with 004d25b0 set; 0x430 ([Ctrl+B]) calls __break (INT3) when 004d25b0 is set. Returns 1 for either code, 0 otherwise. Input_BuildPlayerDevice and Sim_DispatchCommand call it.

entries.name: Sim_DispatchCommand
entries.description: The simulator's command dispatcher: every queued command code passes through here, and Sim_PollPlayerInput also calls it directly (passing 0x14 for one of the MFD cases). Offers the code to the cockpit widget tree (CockpitWidgets_HandleCommand), then to Sim_HandleWindowKey, then its own switch, and finally to the player mech's vtable +0x2c. Codes are PC set-1 scancodes with 0x200 added for Alt -- 0x26 is L, 0x29 is backquote, 0x11/0x211 are W and Alt+W, 0x02-0x0b and 0x202-0x20b the two number-key banks. Case 0x0e/0x14 latch g_CenterTurretMode and clear g_CenterBodyMode; case 0x2b does the reverse and caches g_CenterBodyTargetHeading. Both also clear the auto-turret-tracking flag at mech+0x202 -> +0x14.

entries.name: Sim_PollPlayerInput
entries.description: Reads the input device struct (axes at +0x0e steer, +0x10 throttle, +0x12 torso twist, +0x14 torso pitch) and dispatches player control: Mech_ApplyThrottleInput, Mech_TorsoTwistTick, Mech_TorsoPitchTick. Also hosts the keyboard command switch.

entries.name: Cockpit_GetConsoleButtons
entries.description: Returns CockpitViewInstance+0x1e1, the weapon console panel: WeaponMounts_SetChain hands it to ConsoleButtons_SetChainNumber, Sim_DispatchCommand to ConsoleButtons_ToggleAutoTrack and reads its auto-track latch +0xb3.

entries.name: PausePanel_Dtor
entries.description: GeneralSmallAlert's destructor (class record 0046107d), PausePanel_Ctor's object: (panel, flags). One RTL destructor-count decrement, GeneralAlert_Dtor(panel, 0), then Mem_Delete on flags bit 0.
entries.source: DBSIM disassembly at 004610d9; class record at 0046107d

entries.name: Sim_CreateRenderContext
entries.description: Allocates 0x239 bytes, runs GLViewport_Ctor on them, stores the result in Sim_RenderContext (004d2552), sets its int at +0x208 to 1 and installs it with Raster_InstallRenderContext. Sim_InitMissionSession calls it.

entries.name: Sim_AssertCleanupHook
entries.description: Assert hook Sim_InitMissionSession registers with Assert_AddHook (PUSH 0x4611f8 at 0046151a): Sound_Shutdown; when TapeFile is open, fcloses it and, when open, the checkpoint file at 004d2562, clearing both; ShadeRamp_Free; clears the exit code 004d283c.

entries.name: Light_CreateMissionSun
entries.description: Called exactly once per mission, unconditionally, from Sim_InitMissionSession (Sim_InitMissionSession) right after the light-system reset (Light_ResetSystem) and before DBSim_LoadScriptDat -- creates the ONE directional 'sun' light every mission gets. Direction is NOT read from any mission/theater file: it's built from two HARDCODED constant vectors, local_38=(0,0x1000,0) and local_40=(-6000,0,21000), combined via BuildEulerRotationMatrixQ14 (looks like a normalize/transform) then RotateVectorByMatrixQ14 (looks like it derives a direction from a target-point + up-vector pair, output stored as the light's direction field). Intensity is set via vtable+4 call with literal 0x100 (256). The created light is registered via Light_Register (Light_Register) AND pushed onto a persistent list (Light_PersistentList) via Light_AddPersistent, so it survives a later Light_ReregisterPersistent (Light_ReregisterPersistent) call. No separate ambient (type=0) light creation was found anywhere in the binary -- Light_ComputeShadeForFace's type-0 branch may be genuinely unused by real missions, meaning faces angled away from the sun likely render fully unlit (shade=0), not floor-lit. BuildEulerRotationMatrixQ14/RotateVectorByMatrixQ14/DotProductVec3Short_Thunk (the actual per-face dot-product math) are not decoded; the lighting is a single fixed sun direction and intensity with no mission-specific lighting data.

entries.name: Sim_ShowLoadingScreen
entries.description: (name): builds the bitmap's path with ResourcePath_BuildFolderName under the folder at PTR_DAT_004a0a28 (PTR_DAT_004a0a40 when VideoMode_PanelMode is 3), loads it with Resource_Load, blits frame 0 at (0, 0), Display_Present, and frees the array with GLBitmapArray_Dtor. Sim_InitMissionSession shows the mission loading screen with it.

entries.name: Sim_ReadLoadingScreenChoice
entries.description: (theaterOut, isRazorOut): reads the 0x14-byte header of data\script (with the dat extension) and stores its first int16 -- the theater World_LoadTheater doubles -- in theaterOut; then reads the first five int16s of data\player.mec and sets isRazorOut when the fifth, the player entry's mech type, is 8 (RAZOR in MECHS.NAM). Asserts (INIT.CPP lines 0xde, 0xe4, severity 5) that each file opens. Sim_InitMissionSession builds the loading screen's name from them: 'flyrX' for the Razor, else 'hercX', X = theater + 1.
entries.source: DBSIM decompile and disassembly at 004613b4; strings at 0049f879 and 0049f88e; MECHS.NAM

entries.name: Sim_InitMissionSession
entries.description: Per-mission session setup: resets the light system (Light_ResetSystem), creates the mission's one hardcoded sun light (Light_CreateMissionSun), then calls DBSim_LoadScriptDat and DBSim_SpawnMissionObjects. Confirms lighting setup happens once per mission load, independent of which script.dat/theater is loaded. Also picks the FOCAL SHIFT -- 9 when DAT_004d30c4 >= 0x4b1 and 8 otherwise -- and passes it as the third argument of the view constructor View_Ctor, which stores it at view+0x1a. That is the whole of the field of view; see docs/retail/formats/cockpit-views.md.
entries.source: flat-shaded lighting RE; docs/retail/formats/cockpit-views.md for the focal shift

entries.name: Sim_ReleaseSessionObjects
entries.description: (): InputDriverKind0_Dtor(*004d258e, 3), the 6-byte input driver Sim_InitMissionSession builds, then, when Sim_RenderContext is set, adds Rtl_GetPolymorphicDtorCount(context, 0) to *Rtl_DtorCountPtr and calls its vtable +0x18 destructor with flags 3. Sits before Sim_Shutdown. No reference found by es2_xref.

entries.name: Sim_Shutdown
entries.description: The simulator's exit path, run by Sim_Run however the main loop ends: closes the tape files, Mission_WriteResults(LocalPlayerMech), then the exit code at 004d283c -- 6 under DemoMode, 0 with the quit flag 004d2582, else 4 when the player's +0x99 is set and MissionModeFlag (004a9ed6) is, else 3 -- then Sim_ShutdownNoOp1 and Sim_ShutdownNoOp2.

entries.name: TSSunLight_Dtor
entries.description: The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's TSSunLight_Dtor (00427e3d).
entries.source: ES2DecompileContainingBatch DBSIM 00462003 / VSHELL 00427e3d: identical after normalisation; RTTI TSSunLight vtable 0049f8d8 slot +0x00

entries.name: TSLight_Dtor
entries.description: The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's TSLight_Dtor (00427e02).
entries.source: ES2DecompileContainingBatch DBSIM 0046209e / VSHELL 00427e02: identical after normalisation; RTTI TSLight vtable 0049f8ec slot +0x00

entries.name: Cam_Dtor
entries.description: CAM vtable +0x00 (0049f900, RTTI 'CAM', 0x4e bytes, derived from TSCamera), the destructor its class record names: (cam, flags). Two RTL destructor-count decrements, TSContext_Dtor(cam, 0), then Mem_Delete on flags bit 0.
entries.source: DBSIM disassembly at 00462150; class record at 00462104

entries.name: Sound_ResolveSamplePath
entries.description: Prefixes a catalog filename with 'HMI\\', or 'HMX\\' when CockpitArt_LoadOnDemand is set. SIMSOUND.VOL carries both banks, hmx being the same content at half the sample rate; EXPLO5.WAV is in hmi only.

entries.name: sfxWndProc
entries.description: MainWndProc filter registered by Sound_Init (see WndProcHook_Register). Two messages only: WM_TIMER (0x113) pumps the SOS/MME service routine, and MM_MCINOTIFY (0x3b9) with MCI_NOTIFY_SUCCESSFUL re-issues Music_PlayTrack, which is what loops the CD track.

entries.name: Sound_Init
entries.description: (enable). Registers sfxWndProc as a MainWndProc hook, allocates the five-slot speech channel pool (5 x 0x42-byte records plus a 5 x 100-byte script buffer at 004d2df4), then allocates and initialises the SFX manager with a cache cap of 2,000,000 bytes -- 1,000,000 when CockpitArt_LoadOnDemand is set -- 60 resource slots and 90 voice slots, and loads the sound catalog.

entries.name: SoundCatalog_Load
entries.description: Loads str\SOUNDS.STR -- one .STR group of 57 entries, each a filename plus a 7-byte attribute blob -- into three parallel arrays: names (004d2b0c), attribute pointers (004d2bfc) and voice handles (004d2cfc), count in 004d2dec. Per entry: _strlwr the name, pick the Sfx_Open type from two strstr tests (.hmp gives 0, else .wav gives 1, else EDI is left as it was), resolve the path through Sound_ResolveSamplePath and Sfx_Open it; on success priority 5, Sfx_SetLooping to attribute byte 0, Sfx_SetVolume to Math_Q16Multiply(byte 1, 65000), Sfx_Cache if byte 2 is set, then default byte 4 to 5 and byte 5 to 100 where they are 0xff and set byte 8 to 100. Both strstr calls search the 20-byte stack buffer the function reserves at entry and never writes, not the name, so the type is the same for every row and, when the stale bytes hold neither extension, is EDI's value on entry. A row == 0 gives type 2 arm at 004624eb follows an unconditional jump past it. Finally it sets each speech slot's +0x3c to the row count and +0x3e to -1. The code reads a TEN-byte blob: bytes 7-9 are runtime scratch (resume flag, category volume, request counter) that the file does not supply.

entries.name: Sound_Preload
entries.description: Caches one catalog id's sample without playing it.

entries.name: Sound_Shutdown
entries.description: Stops the CD, unregisters sfxWndProc, tears the SFX manager down and clears SfxManager.

entries.name: Sound_IsCategoryEnabled
entries.description: Splits the catalog at id 10: below 10 answers to the music enable flag (0049f90c), 10 and up to the effects flag (0049f910). This is why every data-driven table plays its sound id + 10.

entries.name: Sound_ConsumeRequest
entries.description: (catalogId) -> may play. interval = (2 - detailSetting 004d1fc7) * attribute byte 3; interval 0 always plays, otherwise attribute byte 9 counts up (wrapping at 0x0f) and only every interval-th call passes. Keeps a sound fired by many objects at once from playing once per object. Dead code in the shipped binary: no CALL to it exists anywhere in the code section and its address is stored nowhere, so the authored divisors in attribute byte 3 never take effect.

entries.name: Sound_Play
entries.description: (catalogId). Non-positional. Rolls the variation count (attribute byte 6) to displace the id, sets volume to Math_Q16Multiply(byte 1, 65000) * byte 8 / 100 -- or 0 when the category is muted -- and plays.

entries.name: Sound_PlayAt
entries.description: (catalogId, worldPoint). Positional. Does nothing while SfxManager is null. Rolls the variation count (attribute byte 6, Math_RandomBelow on the state at 004d268f) onto the id, then Sound_Place computes volume and pan from the point unchanged, and Sfx_Play starts the id's voice only if that reports it audible.

entries.name: Voice_PlayNamed
entries.description: (wavName, volume). Acquires a speech slot for the name with no .SNC script, sets its volume and starts it.

entries.name: Sound_UpdatePosition
entries.description: Re-runs Sound_Place for a sound already playing, without starting it.

entries.name: Sound_Place
entries.description: (catalogId, worldPoint) -> audible; false while SfxManager is null. Resets the model transform and pushes the point through the current camera transform (Raster_ModelToView), so the listener is the camera. With d = Math_FastMagnitude3D(view): volume is 0 when the id's category is disabled or d is beyond attribute byte 5 * 1024; otherwise Math_Q16Multiply(byte 1, 65000), and at or past byte 4 * 1024 it is (max - d) * vol / max -- the divisor is max, not max - min, so a sound at exactly min is already attenuated. Sfx_SetVolume gets volume * attribute byte 8 / 100. Only when audible: pan is (-2a) & 0xffff for a = Math_Atan2Bam(viewX, viewY) below 0x8000, and 2a & 0xffff otherwise, so a = 0 (dead abeam right, and a point with no horizontal offset, for which Math_Atan2Bam answers 0) pans to 0, hard left.

entries.name: Sound_Stop
entries.description: Stops one catalog id's voice.

entries.name: Sound_NoOp
entries.description: Empty body (PUSH EBP / MOV EBP,ESP / POP EBP / RET) between Sound_Stop and Sound_IsPlaying. No reference found by es2_xref.

entries.name: Sound_IsPlaying
entries.description: Returns whether one catalog id's voice is still playing.

entries.name: Voice_EvictLru
entries.description: Picks the speech slot with the oldest last-use tick (+0x37), closes whatever voice it held and returns it.

entries.name: Voice_Acquire
entries.description: (wavName, sncPath) -> slot.
