Looks the name up across the five speech slots; a miss evicts the least recently used (Voice_EvictLru), copies the name in, opens an SFX voice at priority 0xff so catalog voices can never evict it, caches it, and loads the .SNC script. Gated on Sound_SpeechEnabled.

entries.name: Sound_SetMusicEnabled
entries.description: Stores the music enable flag when it differs from the current value. No side effect of its own; the caller mutes or unmutes.

entries.name: Sound_SetEffectsEnabled
entries.description: Stores the effects enable flag when it differs from the current value. No side effect of its own; the caller mutes or unmutes.

entries.name: Sound_MuteMusic
entries.description: Zeroes the volume of catalog ids 0-9 and clears the music enable flag; when a CD track is set, saves the position and stops the CD instead.

entries.name: Sound_MuteEffects
entries.description: Zeroes the volume of catalog ids 10 and up and clears the effects enable flag.

entries.name: Sound_MuteOne
entries.description: (id): zeroes one catalog id's volume and clears both the music and effects flags. No reference found by es2_xref.

entries.name: Sound_UnmuteMusic
entries.description: Restores ids 0-9 to Math_Q16Multiply(byte 1, 65000) * byte 8 / 100, or resumes the CD from the saved position, and sets the music enable flag.

entries.name: Sound_UnmuteEffects
entries.description: Restores ids 10 and up to their own volumes and sets the effects enable flag.

entries.name: Sound_UnmuteOne
entries.description: (id): the counterpart of Sound_MuteOne -- restores the id's attribute volume and raises both the music and effects flags. No reference found by es2_xref.

entries.name: SoundCatalog_EffectiveVolume
entries.description: (id): 0 when there is no SfxManager, else SoundCatalog_Attributes[id] byte 1 (volume) times byte 8 (category volume percent) / 100. CockpitView_StepViewTransition stores sound 0x2d's into 004cfd38.

entries.name: Sound_SetBaseVolume
entries.description: Overwrites attribute byte 1 (the authored 0-100 volume) and re-applies it.

entries.name: Sound_SetCategoryVolume
entries.description: Writes attribute byte 8, the per-sound category scale every volume computation multiplies through, and re-applies the resulting volume.

entries.name: Sound_ShiftMusicSet
entries.description: (delta, charIndex). Offsets one character of each of the ten music filenames by delta and re-opens them -- how a different music set would have been selected. All ten name battle1.wav, which ships in no archive.

entries.name: Sound_SetPitch
entries.description: Sets one catalog id's playback rate through Sfx_SetPitch, as the original's 16.16 ratio (0x10000 = 1.0). Cockpit_PowerUpSound is the only caller found, dropping the engine hum to 42000.

entries.name: Sound_StartMissionMusic
entries.description: Plays Music_CdTrack when the SFX manager is up, a track is set and Sound_MusicEnabled is up. Sim_InitMissionSession's own music start, called immediately after it writes the track and the enable byte.

entries.name: Sound_StopMusic
entries.description: Frameless: Sfx_StopMusic(SfxManager) when SfxManager is set. Follows Sound_StartMissionMusic. No reference found by es2_xref.

entries.name: Sound_SuspendAll
entries.description: Sets attribute byte 7 for each catalog voice that loops forever (record +0x18 == 0) and is playing (flag 0x100), clearing it for the rest; saves the CD position into 0049f91c when music is on; stops the CD, every voice (Sfx_StopAll) and releases the driver (Sfx_ReleaseDriver). Paired with Sound_ResumeAll.

entries.name: Sound_ResumeAll
entries.description: Replays exactly the catalog voices whose attribute byte 7 was set by Sound_SuspendAll, and resumes the CD from the saved TMSF position.

entries.name: Snc_ServiceQueue
entries.description: Drains the global .SNC event queue (004d2efa, 8-byte {time, slot} entries, count 0049f97c) of everything now due, calling each slot's Snc_Advance.

entries.name: Snc_ClearSlot
entries.description: (slot): clears slot+0x2f (the pointer to the .SNC script buffer Snc_Load reads into) and slot+0 (the voice handle). VoiceSlot_ElementCtor calls it; es2_xref finds that one call.

entries.name: maybe_Snc_Ctor
entries.description: (slot, sncPath, voiceHandle): Snc_Load(slot, sncPath, voiceHandle), returning slot -- a constructor's shape. No reference found by es2_xref.

entries.name: Sim_InitMissionSessionNoOp
entries.description: Empty body. Sim_InitMissionSession calls it after Sound_Init, before Light_ResetSystem.

entries.name: Snc_Load
entries.description: (slot, sncPath, voiceHandle). Reads the .SNC file into the slot's 100-byte buffer: an int32 length followed by that many bytes of {int8 frame, int8 deltaTicks} pairs, then appends the 0xff terminator itself -- the terminator is NOT in the file. With no path the buffer is just 0xff and the voice plays with the portrait held.

entries.name: Snc_Start
entries.description: Points the slot's cursor at the start of its script; an immediately-0xff script sets the frame to 1 and plays without animation, otherwise stamps the start time and runs Snc_Advance. Then plays the voice.

entries.name: SfxHandle_IsPlaying
entries.description: (handle*): 1 when SfxManager is set, *handle is neither 0 nor -1, and Sfx_IsDone(SfxManager, *handle) returns 0; else 0. The by-pointer sibling of SfxHandle_SetVolume. No reference found by es2_xref.

entries.name: Snc_Advance_Thunk
entries.description: One-line forwarder to Snc_Advance with the same argument. Snc_ServiceQueue calls it.

entries.name: Snc_Advance
entries.description: Reads {frame, delta} pairs, accumulating delta into the slot's next-event time until it passes now, publishes the frame at slot+0x08, and re-inserts the slot into the global event queue. Reaching 0xff sets the frame to -1, which is what tells HddGauge_PaintPilotFrame the message is over.

entries.name: Snc_GetFrame
entries.description: Returns the slot's current portrait frame (slot+0x08); -1 once the script has ended.

entries.name: SfxHandle_SetVolume
entries.description: (handle*, volume): Sfx_SetVolume(SfxManager, *handle, volume) when the manager exists and *handle is not -1. Voice_PlayNamed calls it.

entries.name: Sound_StaticInit
entries.description: _INIT_ entry 004a7b7c (pointer at 004a7b7e): StringTable_Ctor(SoundCatalog_StringTable, SoundCatalog_StringTable (004d2cec)).

entries.name: Sound_StaticDtor
entries.description: _EXIT_ entry 004a7c5a (pointer at 004a7c5c): OwnedArray_Dtor(SoundCatalog_StringTable, 2). The 'Strings' class record follows it.

entries.name: VoiceSlot_ElementCtor
entries.description: (slot): Snc_ClearSlot(slot), clears the in-use byte +0x3b and the last-use tick +0x37, returns slot. Sound_Init's Rtl_VectorNew(0, 0x42, 5, 1, this) (PUSH 0x463520 at 0046234f) builds the five speech channel records with it and stores the array pointer at VoiceSlots (004d2df0).

entries.name: Sfx_Init
entries.description: (manager, memoryCap, resourceSlots, voiceSlots). Called as (cap, 60, 90). Allocates the resource table at +0x34 (stride 0x21c) and the voice table at +0x38 (stride 0x28), fills every slot's handle with -1, then brings the backend up with the config block at +0x24.

entries.name: Sfx_ReadConfig
entries.description: (sfx): initialises the SFX manager and reads [Sound] from data\sound.cfg with GetPrivateProfileString into its config block at +0x24. Clears the resource and voice tables (+0x34, +0x38), the playing counts (+0x3c, +0x40), the bytes cached (+0x1c), +0x44, +0x2c and +0x2e; sets the handle generation +0x20 to 1, +0x26 to 1 and +0x32 to 0x200. Driver: 'DirectSound', compared case-insensitively, gives +0x2a = 2, anything else 1. Buffers: atol, 1-64 into +0x30, else 5. Rate: atol of 11 gives +0x24 = 0x10, anything else 0x20. Width: 'Mono', compared case-insensitively, gives +0x28 = 4, anything else 8. Increments the count at *006cbf74 and returns sfx.

entries.name: SfxManager_Dtor
entries.description: (manager, flags): Sos_Shutdown, Mem_Delete on the arrays at +0x34 and +0x38 (clearing both), then Mem_Delete(manager) when flags bit 0 is set. Sound_Shutdown runs it on SfxManager with 3.

entries.name: Sfx_ReleaseDriver
entries.description: Sos_ReleaseDigiDriver. Sound_SuspendAll's last step after Sfx_StopAll.

entries.name: Sfx_AcquireDriver
entries.description: Returns Sos_AcquireDigiDriver's answer. Sound_ResumeAll's first step.

entries.name: maybe_Sfx_FillDefaultsThunk
entries.description: (sfx, out): maybe_Sfx_FillDefaults(out); the first argument is not read. es2_xref finds no reference to it. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's maybe_Sfx_FillDefaultsThunk (0042c102).

entries.name: Sfx_SetMemoryCap
entries.description: (manager, cap): with a non-zero cap below the current cap +0x18, Sfx_EvictUntilFree(manager, +0x18 - cap); when +0x18 is 0 and a non-zero cap is below the cached total +0x1c, Sfx_EvictUntilFree(manager, +0x1c - cap); then stores cap at +0x18, the cap Sfx_Cache tests. No reference found by es2_xref.

entries.name: Sfx_ServiceTimer
entries.description: (manager, hwnd, msg, wParam, lParam): Sos_Service(hwnd, msg, wParam, lParam). sfxWndProc's WM_TIMER arm.

entries.name: Sfx_Open
entries.description: (manager, name, type, userValue, loadState) -> voice handle, or -1. Handles are generation<<16|slotIndex, the generation coming from the manager's counter at +0x20; every accessor re-reads the slot's own copy and rejects a mismatch. Takes a free voice slot and defaults it (priority 5, volume 100, loop 1, pan 0x8000, pitch 0x10000), then binds a resource: an existing resource with the same name is shared and its refcount bumped, otherwise a free resource slot takes the name. type 0 = .hmp MIDI song (flag 0x1), 1 = digital sample, 2 = the streamed path (flag 0x1000).

entries.name: Sfx_Close
entries.description: Releases one voice slot and drops its resource's refcount.

entries.name: Sfx_Cache
entries.description: (manager, voiceHandle, in). Loads or unloads the voice's resource. Loading stats the file for its byte size into record+0x210, and if cached+size would exceed the manager's cap at +0x18 runs Sfx_EvictUntilFree first; on success sets record+0x20c and adds the size to the cached total at +0x1c. Unloading refuses while the resource refcount (+0x208) is 2 or more.

entries.name: Sfx_Play
entries.description: (manager, voiceHandle). Caches the resource on demand, starts it through Sos_StartVoice, sets the playing flag 0x100 and bumps the manager's playing-sample (+0x3c) or playing-song (+0x40) count. It does NOT test the 0x100 flag first: playing a voice that is already sounding starts a second concurrent copy on another SOS channel rather than restarting or being ignored, and the voice record keeps only the newest handle (+0x24), so Sfx_Stop can no longer reach the older copies.

entries.name: Sfx_Stop
entries.description: Stops one voice and clears its playing flag.

entries.name: Sfx_IsDone
entries.description: Returns nonzero when the voice is not playing; when the backend reports it finished, calls Sfx_Stop to clear the state.

entries.name: Sfx_Service
entries.description: Sos_Service(0, 0, 0, 0): the library service call with no window message. AlertPanel_Present calls it while SfxManager is set.

entries.name: Sfx_PickEvictionVictim
entries.description: Scores every live voice: (resource cached ? 100 : 0) + priority + (playing ? 1000 : 0) + (playing && looping ? 10000 : 0), and closes the lowest-scoring one with Sfx_Close and returns its handle; returns -1 when every score is 20000 or more. An idle, uncached, low-priority voice is taken first and a looping playing one last.

entries.name: Sfx_EvictUntilFree
entries.description: Frees cached resources by repeatedly taking Sfx_PickEvictionVictim's choice until the requested number of bytes fits under the manager's cap.

entries.name: Sfx_SetCallback
entries.description: Writes voice+0x10, handed to the backend sample object when the voice starts.

entries.name: Sfx_SetVolume
entries.description: Writes voice+0x14 (0-100) and re-applies it to the backend if the voice is live.

entries.name: Sfx_SetPitch
entries.description: Writes voice+0x20 as 16.16; 0x10000 is 1.0 and clears flag 0x400, anything else sets it.

entries.name: Sfx_SetPan
entries.description: Writes voice+0x1c; 0x8000 is centre and clears flag 0x800, anything else sets it.

entries.name: Sfx_SetLooping
entries.description: Writes voice+0x18 as a repeat COUNT, not a boolean: 0 = forever, 1 = once, n = n times. Sets flag 0x80 for any value other than 1.

entries.name: Sfx_SetPriority
entries.description: Writes voice+0x0c. The sound catalog uses 5; the speech channel uses 0xff so catalog voices can never evict it.

entries.name: Sfx_GetAttributes
entries.description: (manager, voiceHandle): for a handle other than -1 whose voice record (table +0x38, stride 0x28, index handle & 0xffff) still holds it at +0, returns the record's flags dword +8 (0x80 set by Sfx_SetLooping, 0x100 by Sfx_Play); else 0. No reference found by es2_xref.

entries.name: Sfx_SetAttributes
entries.description: (manager, voiceHandle, flags): the setter for Sfx_GetAttributes' dword: for a valid handle writes flags to the voice record's +8. No reference found by es2_xref.

entries.name: Sfx_PlayMusicTrack
entries.description: SFX-level thunk to Music_PlayTrack. Music does not go through SOS, so the manager reaches MCI through four thunks of this kind rather than through its own backend.

entries.name: Sfx_StopMusic
entries.description: SFX-level thunk to Music_Stop.

entries.name: Sfx_IsMusicIdle
entries.description: SFX-level thunk to Music_IsIdle.

entries.name: Sfx_GetSampleData
entries.description: Validates a voice handle and returns a pointer to its record+4, or 0.

entries.name: Sfx_StopAll
entries.description: (manager). Sfx_Stop's body over every voice with the 0x100 playing flag and a live resource: Sos_StopVoice (which returns 1 unconditionally), decrement the playing-song (+0x40) or playing-sample (+0x3c) count, clear 0x100. The loop is bounded by +0x10, the resource slot count (60), not the voice count +0x14 (90). Only caller: Sound_SuspendAll (0046311c).

entries.name: Sfx_GetMusicPosition
entries.description: SFX-level thunk to Music_GetPosition.

entries.name: Sfx_ResumeMusicAt
entries.description: SFX-level thunk to Music_ResumeAt.

entries.name: Str_FormatStatic
entries.description: (format, ...): _vsprintf into the static buffer 004d2f74 and returns it.

entries.name: Display_SetOrigin
entries.description: Driver 3's g_RasterRoutines slot 15 target, reached through the stub 00489802. Moves the viewport window over the back buffer to point param_2: sets the render target descriptor's pixel pointer and row-table base to base + y*width + x and stores the point in Display_OriginX/Y. Ignores param_1, the page.

entries.name: Display_Present
entries.description: Screen_PresentFrame(&Display_OriginX, &Display_ScreenRect): puts the viewport window at the display origin on screen. 29 call sites (es2_xref): 25 on the scroll-window path only, 21 in CockpitView_StepViewTransition and one each in AlertPanel_Present, AlertPanel_Leave, Sim_EndFrame and Sim_InitMissionSession; the mission loading screen Sim_ShowLoadingScreen, the preferences panel's per-pass PreferencesPanel_Present, and MainWndProc's WM_PAINT (windowed) and 0x812 handlers unconditionally.

entries.name: Display_PresentRect
entries.description: Presents one rect {x0,y0,x1,y1} of the view: offsets it by the render context's origin (+0x210/+0x214 minus +0x220/+0x224) when the context's +0x20c is set, then calls Screen_PresentFrame with that rect offset by Display_OriginX/Y as the source and by Display_ScreenRect as the destination. es2_xref finds no rel32 caller and no stored pointer.

entries.name: Display_StaticInitNoOp
entries.description: _INIT_ entry 004a7b82 (pointer at 004a7b84): a lone RET, after Display_PresentRect.

entries.name: Win_ConfirmMessageBox
entries.description: (hInstance, hwnd, stringId): LoadStringA(hInstance, 1000) into the caption buffer 004d3698 (0x20 bytes) and stringId into the text buffer 004d36b8 (0x80), then MessageBoxA(hwnd, text, caption, 0x31 = MB_OKCANCEL | MB_ICONEXCLAMATION); returns 1 for IDOK, else 0. WinMain's MainWindow_Create failure box uses the same buffers. No reference found by es2_xref.

entries.name: Window_Centre
entries.description: (hwnd, flags): with a parent and flags bit 0, centres hwnd on the parent's window rect, pulling it back so its right and bottom edges stay on screen; otherwise centres it on the screen (GetSystemMetrics 0 and 1). flags bit 1 skips the vertical centring. SetWindowPos with 0x14 (SWP_NOSIZE | SWP_NOZORDER). MainWndProc's message 0x812 case calls it with 0 after sizing the window to 0x294 x 0x212 when the screen size differs from the video mode's.

entries.name: Window_CentreRect
entries.description: (left, top, right, bottom, flags, out): SetRect(out, x, y, width, height) for a rect of the given size centred on the desktop -- y is kept as top when flags bit 1 is set. The last two fields are the size, not the far corner. MainWindow_Create passes its adjusted window rect and 004d3750.

entries.name: Win_SetPumpCursor
entries.description: (cursor): stores Win_PumpCursor (004d37a4). Sim_Run and 00465288 call it with a non-null HCURSOR.

entries.name: Win_PumpMessages
entries.description: Drains the thread's message queue with PeekMessageA(PM_REMOVE), translating and dispatching each message. Returns 1 at WM_QUIT (0x12); otherwise, once the queue is empty, restores the cursor 004d37a4 (SetCursor, when set) and returns 0.

entries.name: Screen_ResetBackBufferGlobals
entries.description: Clears the back-buffer globals (the bitmap header 004d30a4, the display 004d30a8, BackBuffer_Pixels, the memory DC 004d30b8 and its DIB 004d30bc, the palette flag 004d30b0, the timer id 004d368c), takes the size from VideoMode_BackBufferWidth/Height into 004d30c4/c8, and resets the BITMAPINFOHEADER at 004d30d0 to size 0x28, one plane, 8 bits. MainWindow_Create runs it before creating the window.

entries.name: Screen_CreateBackBuffer
entries.description: Builds the back buffer: a memory DC (004d30b8), the system palette read into 004d30f8 with red and blue swapped, an 8-bit top-down DIB section of 004d30c4 x 004d30c8 whose pixels are BackBuffer_Pixels, a 0xe-byte bitmap header over it at 004d30a4, and a 0xa0-byte display named 'BMP_8' at 004d30a8 (GLDisplay_Ctor, GLDisplay_Open) made current with Raster_SelectRenderTarget, draw page 1 and visible page 0, and its four page origins zeroed: they are set 0/200/400/600 rows apart only for a display named 'VGA_8' (004a085f). Ends with GLDisplay_SetAttribute(display, 9, 0). MainWindow_Create runs it once the window exists.

entries.name: Assert_Stub
entries.description: Returns immediately. Assert_Report calls it.

entries.name: MainWindow_KillTimer
entries.description: KillTimer(MainWindow_Handle, the timer id at 004d368c) when that id is nonzero. Sim_Run runs it before Sim_Shutdown; MainWndProc, Video_ToggleFullscreen and Assert_Report run it before PostQuitMessage, and MainWindow_Create when CreateWindowExA fails.

entries.name: WinMain_RegisterWindowClass
entries.description: (hInstance): loads BWCC32.DLL and registers the window class 'ES2': MainWndProc, icon 'es2icon', the arrow cursor, no background brush. Callers found by es2_naming.py callers: WinMain, when there is no previous instance. VSHELL's Shell_RegisterWindowClass (004062cb) is the same code with BWCC.DLL and the class 'shell'.

entries.name: MainWindow_Create
entries.description: (hInstance, nCmdShow): creates the 'EarthSiege II' window sized from the display size at 004d25c2/c6 and centred on the desktop -- or, with the fullscreen flag 004d25e2 set, sized to the whole desktop and made topmost with SetWindowPos -- and stores it in MainWindow_Handle. On failure runs MainWindow_KillTimer; on success Screen_CreateBackBuffer, ShowWindow and UpdateWindow. Returns whether the window exists.

entries.name: WinMain_SplitCommandLine
entries.description: (cmdLine, argv): splits cmdLine at spaces into argv with argv[0] = 'dbsim' (004a088e), each token copied into its own Mem_NewArray(length + 2) buffer; returns argc. WinMain hands the pair to WinMain_ParseSwitches and Sim_Run.

entries.name: WinMain
entries.description: (hInstance, hPrevInstance, cmdLine, nCmdShow), reached through the startup's stored pointer at 00497044: VideoMode_Configure(0), the window-switch pre-parse WinMain_ParseSwitches, MainWindow_Create (a message box and 0 on failure); then, with the full-screen flag 004d25e2 set by prefs option 6 or -Z1, clears it, calls Video_ToggleFullscreen and Screen_ClearToBlack; sets the pump cursor, runs Sim_Run, posts WM_QUIT, pumps to it, releases DirectDraw and returns the exit code 004d283c.

entries.name: Screen_ClearToBlack
entries.description: Clears the screen to palette index 0. Windowed (004d25e2 clear): zeroes BackBuffer_Pixels and StretchBlts a 10x10 corner of the zeroed DIB over the whole client rect inside BeginPaint/EndPaint, realizing the palette when 004d30b0 is set. Fullscreen: restores the DirectDraw surface 004d3798 when IsLost reports DDERR_SURFACELOST, locks it -- or 004d379c below 640 wide -- zeroes each row, unlocks, and below 640 wide flips 004d3798. Sim_InitMissionSession and Sim_Run call it.

entries.name: Screen_SetSoftwareCursor
entries.description: (bitmap): stores Screen_SoftwareCursor (004d37a8), the sprite Screen_PresentFrame draws at the pointer in fullscreen. Its one caller, Sim_InitMissionSession, passes the 'lo_curs' resource when the display is narrower than 640.

entries.name: Screen_PresentFrame
entries.description: Screen_PresentFrame(int *srcPoint, int *dstRect): copies the back buffer's rect at srcPoint (BackBuffer_Pixels, row stride VideoMode_BackBufferWidth) to dstRect on screen. Fullscreen (_DAT_004d25e2 != 0): restores a lost surface, locks the DirectDraw primary (004d3798), or below 640 wide the back surface (004d379c), copies row by row, blits the software cursor bitmap (Screen_SoftwareCursor) at GetCursorPos() colour-keyed on byte 1, unlocks, and below 640 wide flips. Windowed: StretchBlt from the DIB's DC (004d30b8) inside BeginPaint/EndPaint. Its only callers are Display_Present and Display_PresentRect.

entries.name: Win_DrainMessageQueue
entries.description: (): PeekMessageA(PM_REMOVE), TranslateMessage, DispatchMessageA until the queue is empty; WM_QUIT is dispatched like any other message. Win_DrainMessageQueue_Thunk calls it.

entries.name: Win_DrainMessageQueue_Thunk
entries.description: Loads its stack argument into EAX and calls Win_DrainMessageQueue, which does not read it. No reference found by es2_xref.

entries.name: Palette_CreateForDisplay
entries.description: (quads, count): builds the 256-entry LOGPALETTE at 004d37ac from RGBQUADs and returns CreatePalette's handle. With the system palette in SYSPAL_NOSTATIC use, it copies count entries flagged 1 (PC_RESERVED), clears the rest, and forces entry 0 to black and 255 to white, both flagged 0. Otherwise it keeps the NUMRESERVED/2 system colours at each end (flags 0) and copies the middle entries flagged 5 (PC_RESERVED | PC_NOCOLLAPSE), moving the blue of any that matches a static colour by 3 (down from 0xfc and up, up otherwise). Screen_SetPalette calls it.

entries.name: Palette_ClearSystemPalette
entries.description: Creates a palette from the LOGPALETTE header at 004a041c with all 256 entries black and flagged 5 (PC_RESERVED | PC_NOCOLLAPSE), selects and realizes it on the screen DC, then selects the old palette back and deletes it. Screen_SetPalette runs it before realizing a new palette.

entries.name: Palette_SetDisplayEntries
entries.description: (palette): builds 256 PALETTEENTRYs: the NUMRESERVED/2 system colours at each end flagged 0, the rest from the palette's 6-bit entries at +8 shifted left 2 and flagged 5. Windowed (004d25e2 clear) it sets them as the back buffer DIB's colour table (SetDIBColorTable on 004d30b8) and AnimatePalettes the screen palette 004d30b0; full screen it hands them to the DirectDraw palette 004d37a0 (slot +0x18, SetEntries(0, 0, 256, entries)). Palette_FlushDirtyRange calls it.

entries.name: Screen_SetPalette
entries.description: (palette): nothing for null. Stores palette at 004d3bb0 and converts its 256 four-byte entries (+8; R, G, B, flags) to RGBQUADs: flags bit 0 means 6-bit components, shifted left 2; otherwise an entry is copied only when flags bit 1 is set. Runs 00465b3c, makes 00465920(quads, 256)'s result the palette 004d30b0, selects and realizes it on the screen DC and SetDIBColorTable's the back-buffer memory DC 004d30b8. In full screen (004d25e2) it also copies the quads to a PALETTEENTRY array at 004d37b0 with peFlags 1 and calls 004d3794's vtable +0x14 (IDirectDraw::CreatePalette, flags 0x4c) into 004d37a0, and on success 004d3798's vtable +0x7c (IDirectDrawSurface::SetPalette) with it.

entries.name: ClassItem_LoadFromFile
entries.description: (path): opens path with VolRStream_CtorFromPath, loads one class item from it with ClassItem_LoadResource, destroys the stream and returns the item. Palette_LoadAndActivate and Sim_InitMissionSession call it.

entries.name: MainWindow_SetTitle
entries.description: (text): SetWindowTextA(MainWindow_Handle, text). No reference found by es2_xref.

entries.name: WndProcHook_Register
entries.description: Appends a raw (hwnd,msg,wParam,lParam)-shaped filter function to the first free slot (of 10) in the table at DAT_004d3bb4 that MainWndProc tries, in order, before its own message switch -- any hook returning nonzero short-circuits MainWndProc entirely. Mouse_WndProcHook is one of four registered hooks found; the others are sound/movie-playback related.

entries.name: WndProcHook_Unregister
entries.description: Removes a hook previously added by WndProcHook_Register from the DAT_004d3bb4 table.

entries.name: Video_CreateDirectDrawExclusive
entries.description: DirectDrawCreate into 004d3794, then IDirectDraw::SetCooperativeLevel (vtable +0x50) with MainWindow_Handle and flags 0x57 (FULLSCREEN | ALLOWREBOOT | NOWINDOWCHANGES | EXCLUSIVE | ALLOWMODEX). Returns 1 when both succeed, else 0. Video_ToggleFullscreen calls it. VSHELL's Display_CreateDirectDrawExclusive is the same without ALLOWMODEX.

entries.name: DDraw_SetModeAndCreateSurfaces
entries.description: (width, height, bpp): IDirectDraw::SetDisplayMode on 004d3794 (slot +0x54); on success releases the back surface 004d379c, the primary 004d3798 and the palette 004d37a0, and creates the primary (slot +0x18) into 004d3798: below a display width (004d25c2) of 640 a ModeX flip chain with one back buffer (caps 0x204218) whose back surface it fetches into 004d379c (GetAttachedSurface, slot +0x30), otherwise a single primary (caps 0x4200). A failed create is retried once without DDSCAPS_VIDEOMEMORY (0x4000). Returns 1 on success, 0 otherwise. Video_ToggleFullscreen calls it.

entries.name: DDraw_Release
entries.description: Clears the screen (Screen_ClearToBlack) when a DirectDraw object exists, releases the back surface 004d379c, the primary 004d3798, the palette 004d37a0 and the DirectDraw object 004d3794 (slot +8 each, nulling the globals), and ClipCursors the pointer to the whole screen. Video_ToggleFullscreen calls it on the way back to a window, and 00465288 once its message loop ends.

entries.name: Video_ToggleFullscreen
entries.description: Fullscreen/windowed switch on the flag at 004d25e2. Going fullscreen: saves the window rect to 004d3750, takes the window topmost at the game resolution via AdjustWindowRectEx + SetWindowPos, ClipCursors the pointer into it, centres it and hides the software cursor; failure posts WM_QUIT. Coming back: releases DirectDraw and restores the saved rect. Repaints the shield gauge either way. Reached from the left system button, from Help_Show (which runs it first, so raising the on-line manual leaves fullscreen), from Sim_HandleWindowKey on [Alt+Enter], from Video_LeaveFullscreen, and from WinMain at startup.

entries.name: Video_LeaveFullscreen
entries.description: Video_ToggleFullscreen when the full-screen flag 004d25e2 is set, otherwise nothing. Key_WndProcHook calls it for [Alt+Tab] (0x20f), [Ctrl+Esc] (0x401) and [Alt+Esc] (0x201) instead of passing those codes on.

entries.name: Help_Show
entries.description: WinHelpA(mainWindow, path, HELP_CONTENTS, 0), after Video_ToggleFullscreen drops the game back to a window when 004d25e2 says it is fullscreen.

entries.name: AnimDisplay_Dtor
entries.description: AnimDisplay's destructor, the dtor its class record (0xa0 bytes, at 00466901) names: (display, flags): when display is not null, decrements *Rtl_DtorCountPtr, GLDisplay_Dtor(display, 0) for its DVDisplay base, then Mem_Delete when flags bit 0 is set.

entries.name: Math_MeanVec3Short
entries.description: Component-wise (a + b) >> 1 of two 3-short vectors into the static at 004d3bdc, whose address it returns. Its one caller is FlightModel_Step, averaging this tick's angular rates with last tick's before integrating the attitude.

entries.name: Math_IntegrateVec3IntOverTick
entries.description: Math_IntegrateRateOverTick over a 3-int vector, in place, returning it. It reads each component as a SHORT and writes back an int, so a component past 0x7fff is truncated before integration.

entries.name: Math_IntegrateVec3ShortOverTick
entries.description: Math_IntegrateRateOverTick over a 3-short vector, in place, returning it. The short-stride twin of Math_IntegrateVec3IntOverTick.

entries.name: FlightModel_Step
entries.description: The flight model. Settles, in order: the throttle setting at state+0x1e, the airspeed it demands (throttle interpolated across the type's minimum..maximum airspeed, biased by pitch attitude at Q10 250 nose-down against 62 nose-up), sideslip drag, the three angular rates, the new attitude, and the velocity vector in that attitude. It moves nothing -- it produces the world velocity Razor_MovementTick integrates. Turning is bank-driven: the heading rate is -roll >> fm[30] and is applied on top of the integrated attitude. Attitude is integrated as a rotation MATRIX from the mean of this tick's rates and last tick's, with the eulers read back out, so a vertical climb does not gimbal. The fifth argument, a literal 1 at both call sites (Razor_ApplyFlightInput, Flyer_ApplyFlightCommand), is never read.
entries.signature: void __cdecl FlightModel_Step(int *input, int *state, short *flightModel, int *wingDestroyed, int unused)

entries.name: FlightModel_StaticInitNoOp
entries.description: _INIT_ entry 004a7b88 (pointer at 004a7b8a): a lone RET, after FlightModel_Step.

entries.name: Time_GetCoarseTicks
entries.description: (GetTickCount() - startTick) >> 4, i.e. elapsed time in 16 ms units (62.5 Hz). The mission clock gadget (HudClock_Tick) advances one displayed second per 0x3c=60 of these units, so the original's clock runs ~4% fast. This is the coarse UI/event timebase and is NOT the same thing as SimTickDelta, which Sim_MainTick reads from a separate per-frame timing struct.

entries.name: Time_AdvanceCoarseTick
entries.description: Subtracts 0x10 from Time_GetCoarseTicks' start tick (004d3bfc), moving the 16 ms clock on by one tick. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's Time_AdvanceCoarseTick (00465a2c).

entries.name: Time_InitSimClock
entries.description: SimTickDelta = 0x100 and 004d3bea = 0x100, 004d3bf4 = 1000, 004d3bec/004d3bee/004d3bf0/004d3bf6 = 0x7d, and 004d3bf8/004d3bfc = GetTickCount(). Sim_InitMissionSession calls it after Light_CreateMissionSun, before DBSim_LoadScriptDat.

entries.name: Time_ElapsedToQ8Clamped
entries.description: (unit, elapsed): (elapsed << 8) / unit clamped to [0x40, 0x1c2], returned in AX (the decompile drops the return). Time_BeginSimTick computes SimTickDelta with unit 004d3bec and 004d3bea with unit 004d3bee through it.

entries.name: Time_BeginSimTick
entries.description: Spins until 40 ms have elapsed (25 Hz frame cap), then sets SimTickDelta = clamp((elapsedMs << 8) / 125, 0x40, 0x1c2). SimTickDelta is Q8 with 1.0 = 125 ms, so rate units are per-125 ms.

entries.name: Math_IntegrateRateOverTick
entries.description: Q8mul(SimTickDelta, rate), clamped to signed 16-bit range. Core 'apply a per-unit-time rate as this tick's delta' primitive.

entries.name: Math_IntegrateRateOverTick2
entries.description: (rate): Math_Q8Multiply(004d3bea, rate) clamped to +/-0x7fff: Math_IntegrateRateOverTick with the second Q8 delta, the one Time_BeginSimTick computes with unit 004d3bee. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's Math_IntegrateRateOverTick2 (00465b50).
entries.source: DBSIM decompile at 00467858; compared with VSHELL 00465b50

entries.name: Math_RateFromTickDelta
entries.description: (delta): (delta << 8) / SimTickDelta, the inverse of Math_IntegrateRateOverTick: the per-unit rate that yields delta this tick. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's Math_RateFromTickDelta (00465b84).

entries.name: Math_IntegrateRateWithRemainder
entries.description: (value, remainder): value = clamp(value * SimTickDelta >> 8, +/-0x7fff) in place, and remainder = the low 8 bits of |value * SimTickDelta| shifted left 2, or 0x3ff when the product overflows, with value's sign. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's Math_IntegrateRateWithRemainder (00465ba4).
entries.source: DBSIM decompile at 004678a8; compared with VSHELL 00465ba4

entries.name: Math_MulTickDelta64
entries.description: (x): (int64)x * SimTickDelta. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's Math_MulTickDelta64 (00465c08).

entries.name: Math_CountupTimerTick
entries.description: (rec): the short at rec+1 += SimTickDelta; returns it. Math_CountdownTimerTick's mirror. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's Math_CountupTimerTick (00465c1c).
entries.source: DBSIM decompile at 0046792c; es2_naming.py match against VSHELL 00465c1c

entries.name: Math_CountdownTimerTick
entries.description: Countdown-timer tick over a 3-byte packed record. THE COUNTER IS THE SHORT AT +1 FROM THE PASSED POINTER, NOT AT +0: rec[+1] -= SimTickDelta, clamped at 0, returns the new value in AX. Verified across all 40 call sites -- each passes a base whose sibling code reads or writes the short one byte higher (mech+0x258 with the word at +0x259, mount+0x30 with the refire counter at +0x31, rocket+0x5c with the counter at +0x5d). Records sit in stride-3 runs: mech+0x258/0x25b/0x25e and +0x264/0x267/0x26a, globals 0x4a9ee6/0x4a9ee9. The leading byte is untouched by this function, and for all four global instances (0x4a9be8, 0x4a9bec, 0x4a9ee6, 0x4a9ee9) is never read or written anywhere in DBSIM -- only ever address-taken -- so its meaning is still OPEN, not settled as padding. Rocket_TickUpdate's use reloads the counter from ROCKETS.DAT +0x08, which is the exhaust-flame cell-anim and NOT a seeker target-reacquire.

entries.name: Timer_SetShort
entries.description: (rec, value): the short at rec+1 = value * 004d3bf6 * 0x100. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's Timer_SetShort (00465c5c).

entries.name: Timer_CountUp
entries.description: (rec): the int at rec+1 += SimTickDelta; returns it. Timer_CountDown's mirror. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's Timer_CountUp (00465c84).
entries.source: DBSIM decompile at 0046798c; es2_naming.py match against VSHELL 00465c84

entries.name: Timer_CountDown
entries.description: Generic countdown step in the simulation's timer unit (about 0.49 ms per count, not a millisecond): subtracts SimTickDelta from the int at p+1, clamps at 0, returns it. Taking p+1 rather than p is why the AI behaviour block's dwell countdown sits at an unaligned +0x05 with a spare byte at +0x04. Mech_AiTick passes &block+0x04, so descriptor+0x04 is a dwell time in timer units.

entries.name: ActionTimer_SetDelay
entries.description: (timer, value): stores value << 11 at timer+1, converting the file's delay into the simulation's timer counts. DBSim_BuildActionTimerRecord and ActionTimer_Tick call it.

entries.name: Math_RateLimitedMoveToward
entries.description: Generic per-tick turn/slew-rate limiter: moves current toward target by at most step, returns remaining error. Used by rocket guidance and the shield recharge tick.
entries.signature: short __cdecl Math_RateLimitedMoveToward(short *current, short target, short step)

entries.name: Math_RateLimitedMoveTowardInt
entries.description: 32-bit twin of Math_RateLimitedMoveToward (004679d8), the same operation on a short. Steps *current toward target by step without overshooting and returns the remaining gap, or 0 on arrival. The flight model uses it for airspeed, which is an int where every rate a walker slews is a short.
entries.signature: int __cdecl Math_RateLimitedMoveTowardInt(int *current, int target, int step)

entries.name: HudColor_LoadResources
entries.description: Frameless phase-2 loader HudColor_RegisterSubsystem registers: Ovl_ReadFile(HudColorTable, 0x36, 1, path) with the path ResourcePath_BuildFolderName builds from 'colors' (004a089c) and the folder maybe_DatFolderPrefixPtr names ('dat'): the first 54 bytes of dat\COLORS.DAT, 27 int16 entries, read into the table at HudColorTable (004d3c00) (PUSH 0x4d3c00 at 00467a78).

entries.name: HudColor_RegisterSubsystem
entries.description: _INIT_ entry 004a7b8e (pointer at 004a7b90): RegisterSubsystemLoader(HudColor_LoadResources (00467a60), 2).

entries.name: VolumeGroup_Ctor
entries.description: (group, a, b, c, d): clears the 0x1e volume pointers and the count byte +0x78, sets VolumeGroup_BufferSize to 0x400, then VolumeGroup_SetGroup(group, a, b, c, d) -- what VolRStream_SetGroup runs on an existing group. VolRStream_SetGroup builds g_VolumeGroup with it.

entries.name: VolumeGroup_Dtor
entries.description: VolumeGroup's destructor, the dtor its class record (0x79 bytes, at 004735b4) names: (group, flags): decrements *Rtl_DtorCountPtr; when group is not null, Volume_Dtor(volume, 3) on each of the volume pointers at +0 (count: the byte at +0x78), then Mem_Delete when flags bit 0 is set.

entries.name: VolumeGroup_SetBufferSize
entries.description: (size): stores max(size, 0x80) in VolumeGroup_BufferSize. Sim_Run calls it with 0x200 immediately before the only VolRStream_SetGroup call; when that call creates the group, VolumeGroup_Ctor stores 0x400 over it before any volume is loaded. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's VolumeGroup_SetBufferSize.

entries.name: Path_JoinSkipDrive
entries.description: (dir, name): copies dir, or the empty string at 004a08a8 when it is null, into the static buffer 004d3c38, appends name without a leading 'X:' drive prefix and returns the buffer. VolumeGroup_SetGroup builds each volume's path with it. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's Path_JoinSkipDrive.

entries.name: Path_SkipDrive
entries.description: (path): returns path + 2 when path[1] is ':', else path. VolumeGroup_SetGroup compares loaded volume names through it. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's Path_SkipDrive.

entries.name: VolumeGroup_SetGroup
entries.description: (group, mask, extension, dir, dirFirst): the DBSIM copy of VSHELL's VolumeGroup_SetGroup without its assert: removes the volumes whose flags +0x20 share no bit with mask, returns when the group holds 0x1e volumes, then scans 'vol\*<extension>' with findfirst/findnext twice, once under dir and once without it (dirFirst nonzero puts the dir pass first), adding each file whose 'vol\<name>' matches no loaded volume's name (+8, compared through Path_SkipDrive) with VolumeGroup_AddVolume(group, Path_JoinSkipDrive(dir, name), mask). Sim_Run's call passes extension '.vol'.
entries.source: DBSIM decompile at 00467bd4; strings at 004a08a9 and 0049f4b6

entries.name: VolumeGroup_RemoveVolume
entries.description: (group, index): Volume_Dtor(volume, 3) on the volume at index, shifts the later pointers down one, decrements the count byte +0x78 and clears the freed last slot. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's VolumeGroup_RemoveVolume without its asserts.

entries.name: VolumeGroup_AddVolume
entries.description: (group, path, mask): Volume_LoadVolume(path, mask, VolumeGroup_BufferSize) and, when it loads, inserts the volume so the list stays in descending order of the byte at volume +0x1c (read from the volume header), then increments the count byte +0x78. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's VolumeGroup_AddVolume.

entries.name: VolumeGroup_LoadVolume
entries.description: (group, path): returns 0 for a null path or a full group (0x1e volumes); otherwise, unless a loaded volume's name (+8) equals path, VolumeGroup_AddVolume(group, path, 0xffffffff); returns 1. VolRStream_LoadVolume calls it on g_VolumeGroup. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's VolumeGroup_LoadVolume without its assert.

entries.name: VolumeGroup_FindEntry
entries.description: Tries Volume_FindEntry (0047ccec) on each volume in a VolumeGroup (volume pointers from +0, count byte at +0x78) in order and returns 1 at the first hit. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's VolumeGroup_FindEntry.

entries.name: Raster_SetShadeRampDimensions
entries.description: Raster_SetShadeRampDimensions(shadeLevels, depthSlices) -> DAT_004d3d38 / DAT_004d3d3c, plus a 1/n reciprocal table. Sole caller is World_LoadTheater, which passes the world<N>.rmp header's own two int32s (32 and 12 in every retail file) straight through -- which is what fixes Raster_ShadeRampRow's row arithmetic.

entries.name: Raster_SetVisibilityRange
entries.description: Sets DAT_004a08c4, the far limit Raster_SetDepthFadeFromDistance measures against. Sole caller is Terrain_DrawCellQuad, per cell, with grid[+0x10c] << grid[+0x108] -- the HeightGrid's view radius in cells scaled to world units. Retail zones land on 40960, 81920 or 163840 world units (246 m, 492 m, 983 m).

entries.name: Raster_SetDepthFadeFromDistance
entries.description: Sets DAT_004a08c8, the depth-slice byte offset Raster_ShadeRampRow adds: zero for anything inside half the visibility range (DAT_004a08c4), otherwise Math_Q16Multiply(t, depthSlices - 1) * shadeLevels * 256. That is the original's distance fog, and it is what the world<N>.rmp's 12 height slices are for. Called per drawn object (ObjList_DrawEntryRender, with the object's own distance), per terrain cell (Terrain_DrawCellQuad), and with zero from TexPoly_DrawAtPoints.

entries.name: Raster_ShadeRampRow
entries.description: Raster_ShadeRampRow(shade) = ((shade * (DAT_004d3d38 - 1) + DAT_004a08c8) & 0xffffff00) + ShadeRampTable -- the base of one 256-byte row of the theater's world<N>.rmp, indexable directly by palette index. DAT_004d3d38 is the ramp's shade-level count (32 in every retail file) and DAT_004a08c8 a whole number of 8192-byte depth slices set from the drawn object's distance by Raster_SetDepthFadeFromDistance. Both flat poly renderers call it with a literal 0x80, which with 32 levels is row 15.

entries.name: Raster_SetupTexturedSpan
entries.description: Per-vertex setup for the textured/Gouraud span fills. In its param_6 == 2 (Gouraud) branch it computes each vertex's ramp row as shade * (DAT_004d3d38 - 1) + DAT_004a08c8 << 8 -- the same arithmetic as Raster_ShadeRampRow, depth bias included. Together with Raster_DrawPolygon's mode-1 branch this is why the Gouraud and textured paths fog by the same rule as the flat ones, even though neither renderer calls Raster_ShadeRampRow itself. Its param_1 (positions, stride 3 int32) and param_2 (UV corners, stride 2 int32) are both walked one entry per vertex for param_3 vertices, and param_3 is the poly's own vertex count (poly+8). That is why a 3-vertex TSTexture4Poly is textured from the first three of the four corners its caller always writes -- see docs/retail/formats/dts-texture-binding.md, 'Three-vertex texture polys'.

entries.name: Raster_DrawPolygon
entries.description: Polygon submit: (vertexCount, vertices, mode, atlasPage, shadeLevelPtr, transparencyFlag). Clips, builds edges, then walks scanlines calling the span routine the mode selects -- 0 Raster_SpanTextured (u,v only), 1 Raster_SpanTexturedShaded (u,v plus a shade level taken from param_5), 2 Raster_SpanTexturedGouraud (u,v plus a third interpolant, which Raster_DrawPolygon reads from slot +0x14 of its edge records; it sits at +0x18 in the vertex record Raster_SetupTexturedSpan fills). param_4 goes to DAT_004a09b4 as the atlas page; param_6 to DAT_004a09ac, which selects the span routine's transparent half. In mode 1 it turns *param_5 into a ramp row in place -- shade * (DAT_004d3d38 - 1) + DAT_004a08c8, the depth bias included -- so this path fogs by the same rule as Raster_ShadeRampRow without calling it. See Raster_SetupTexturedSpan for the mode-2 equivalent.

entries.name: Raster_DrawTexturedPolyNear
entries.description: (verts, uvs, vertexCount, bitmapHandle, shades, shadeMode, worldSpaceFlag, transparency): the perspective-correct textured polygon fill, DBSIM's counterpart of VSHELL's TSTexture4Poly_RasterizeB. Terrain_DrawCellQuad uses it for cells inside twice the near-distance threshold (DAT_0049aad0) and Raster_SetupTexturedSpan, which maps affinely, for the rest. Per vertex it stores 1/z (1 << DAT_006c60ac over the view depth) at +0x14 and u and v << 16 times 1/z; clips (Raster_ClipPolygonX/Y) and builds edges (Raster_BuildEdgeTables, flags 0xb, 0xf in shade mode 2). Each row is drawn in runs of 2^k pixels: k = 10 when the row's ends have equal 1/z, else 4, 5, 6 or 7 as |delta 1/z| >> 12 is over 3000, over 1000, over 300 or less; at each run's end u and v are recovered with Int64Pair_Q16Divide and the run is filled affinely by Raster_SpanTexturedShaded, or Raster_SpanTexturedShadedClipped through a run list. With g_PerspectiveUseQuadraticFit set, the row's start and its last partial run's end take Raster_BuildEdgeTables' quadratic fit instead of a divide. shadeMode is DAT_004aab30: mode 1 turns shades[0] into one ramp row for the polygon, DAT_004a09c4 = (shade * (shadeLevels-1) + depthBias) << 8, the Raster_ShadeRampRow formula; mode 2 builds that row per vertex and interpolates it along the edges, but no span reads it. Terrain only ever fills shades[0] (from the cell's baked byte), so retail terrain is flat-shaded per triangle, mode 1.

entries.name: maybe_Raster_DrawTexturedPolyW
entries.description: (verts, uvs, vertexCount, bitmapHandle, shades, shadeMode, viewSpaceFlag, transparency), the parameters of Raster_SetupTexturedSpan and Raster_DrawTexturedPolyNear. Fills the 0x28-byte records at Raster_VertexBuffer as they do (Raster_ModelToView unless viewSpaceFlag; Raster_PerspectiveDivide and Raster_ProjectToScreen for a vertex at or beyond the near plane DAT_006c60b0; mode 2's ramp row from shades) and also stores (1 << (DAT_006c60ac + 16)) / z at +0x14. The near-plane pass copies 7 dwords of each kept vertex to 004d4768 and multiplies its u and v by that +0x14 value; a crossing vertex gets +0x14 = 0x10000 and u, v interpolated and shifted left 16. Then Raster_ClipPolygonX/Y and Raster_BuildEdgeTables with flags 3 (|4 in mode 2, |8 with maybe_g_DepthBufferEnabled), mode 1's ramp row from *shades, and each row filled by the mode's affine span routine (Raster_SpanTextured, Raster_SpanTexturedShaded, Raster_SpanTexturedGouraud, or their Clipped variants while ActiveScanlineClipSpans is in use), its two interpolants stepped linearly across the row. transparency goes to DAT_004a09ac and bitmapHandle to DAT_004a09b4. No reference found by es2_xref.

entries.name: RasterVertexBuffer_StaticInit
entries.description: _INIT_ entry 004a7b94 (pointer at 004a7b96): Rtl_VectorNew(Raster_VertexBuffer, 0x28, 10, 1, RasterVertex_ElementCtor).

entries.name: RasterVertex_ElementCtor
entries.description: (vertex): returns vertex; the LEA EDX,[EAX+0x1c] is left over from an inlined empty member constructor at +0x1c, the view-space position. Raster_StaticInit's per-element constructor (the pointer at 0046976d).

entries.name: Raster_ClipEdgeCrossX
entries.description: (x, a, b, out, flags): writes the vertex where edge a-b crosses the vertical line x into out and returns 1; returns 0 and writes nothing when either endpoint lies exactly on the line. Interpolates from the endpoint with the smaller x by t = (x - lo.x) / (hi.x - lo.x) (Q16): y always, and by flags as in Raster_BuildEdgeTables -- 8 depth (+8), 1 u and v (+0xc, +0x10), 1 with 2 w (+0x14), 4 shade (+0x18). Raster_ClipPolygonX's crossing routine.

entries.name: Raster_ClipPolygonX
entries.description: (count, in, out, flags): one Sutherland-Hodgman pass of a ring of 7-dword vertices against x in [ctx+0x210, ctx+0x218 + 1] of the installed render context (006c5ff4). An inside vertex is copied; an edge that crosses a bound gets the crossing from 00469790 (passed the bound, both vertices, the output slot and flags), kept when that returns non-zero. Returns the output count. The first stage of Raster_DrawPolygon and Raster_DrawTexturedPolyNear.

entries.name: Raster_ClipEdgeCrossY
entries.description: Raster_ClipEdgeCrossX for a horizontal line y, interpolating x from the endpoint with the smaller y. Raster_ClipPolygonY's crossing routine.

entries.name: Raster_ClipPolygonY
entries.description: Raster_ClipPolygonX for y (vertex +4) against [ctx+0x214, ctx+0x21c + 1], crossings from 00469a28. Returns the output count.

entries.name: AtlasPage_SetRootIndex
entries.description: (index): stores index at +0x804 of the root atlas page AtlasPage_Root (004a08cc), the page-index field AtlasPage_Init sets. No reference found by es2_xref.

entries.name: AtlasPage_Init
entries.description: (page, index): fills the 256 two-int entries at page+0 with {0, 0x100}, zeroes page+0x800 and stores index at page+0x804. Bitmap_PlaceInAtlasPage calls it on a new chained page with the current page's +0x804 plus one; 0046a2bc on page 0.

entries.name: Bitmap_PlaceInAtlasPage
entries.description: Finds free space in a 256x256 atlas page and blits one bitmap into it at maybe_g_BitmapAtlasCache + page*0x10000 + y*0x100 + x, recursing into a chained page when the current one is full. Writes the caller's descriptor as {x0, y0, x0+w-1, y0+h-1, int16 pageIndex} plus a +0x12 short set when any texel was palette index 0.

entries.name: BitmapArray_PackToAtlas
entries.description: Packs every frame of a loaded .DBA into 256x256 atlas pages via Bitmap_PlaceInAtlasPage and returns a vector of 20-byte descriptors {x0, y0, x1, y1, int16 pageIndex}.

entries.name: AtlasFrame_DrawRotated
entries.description: (desc, position, flipFlags, size, angle): draws one atlas frame as a rotated textured quad. The four vertices take the UV rectangle of the 20-byte frame descriptor desc (+0 x0, +4 y0, +8 x1, +0xc y1); flipFlags bit 1 swaps the UVs of corners 0/1 and 3/2, bit 0 those of corners 0/3 and 1/2. The corners (0,0), (w,0), (w,h), (0,h) from size {w, h} are turned by Math_BuildRotation2D(angle) with Math_Rotate2DPoint, offset by position {x, y}, and drawn with Raster_DrawPolygon(4, verts, 0, the int16 page at desc+0x10, 0, 0). No reference found by es2_xref.

entries.name: AtlasPage_StaticInit
entries.description: _INIT_ entry 004a7b9a (pointer at 004a7b9c): Mem_New(0x808), AtlasPage_Init(page, 0) when the allocation succeeds, and stores the page (or 0) in AtlasPage_Root (004a08cc). 0x808 is the size of the 'Sheet' class record at 0046a32f.

entries.name: AtlasFrameDesc_ElementCtor
entries.description: (desc): returns desc. BitmapArray_PackToAtlas's per-element constructor for its 20-byte frame descriptors: Rtl_VectorNew(0, 0x14, the source's frame count at +4, 1, this) (PUSH 0x46a327 at 00469f44).

entries.name: ShadeRamp_Allocate
entries.description: (_, _, rows): when 004a0930 is clear, allocates (rows + 1) * 0x100 bytes into 006b4fa4 and points ShadeRampTable at the next 256-byte boundary above it (a full 0x100 above an aligned block). Returns the byte 004a0930. World_LoadTheater then reads the theater's rows of 256 into ShadeRampTable.

entries.name: ShadeRamp_Free
entries.description: (): when the word 004a0930 is non-zero, Mem_Delete(ShadeRamp_Allocation), clears the dword at 006b4f96 and the word 004a0930. es2_xref finds one caller, Sim_AssertCleanupHook.

entries.name: AtlasPage_LoadFromFile
entries.description: (path, page): when the word 004a0930 is non-zero and VolRStream_Open(path) succeeds, reads 0x10000 bytes into maybe_g_BitmapAtlasCache + page * 0x10000, closes the stream and returns 1; else returns 0. No reference found by es2_xref.

entries.name: ShadeRamp_StaticInit
entries.description: _INIT_ entry 004a7ba0 (pointer at 004a7ba2): GLBitmap_Ctor(maybe_ShadeRamp_Bitmap (006b4f88)). Closes the block that holds ShadeRamp_Allocate, ShadeRamp_Free and AtlasPage_LoadFromFile.

entries.name: ShadeRamp_StaticDtor
entries.description: _EXIT_ entry 004a7c60 (pointer at 004a7c62): GLBitmap_Dtor(maybe_ShadeRamp_Bitmap (006b4f88), 2).

entries.name: Group_FirstAbleMember
entries.description: Returns the first of up to four of a group's members that is neither immobilised (+0xa4) nor destroyed (+0x99), or null. The ground-vehicle layer's notion of the group leader.

entries.name: GroundVehicle_CollisionTest
entries.description: The two object sweeps of Mech_CollisionTest standing alone, for the ground vehicle class instead of the mech: same group +0x14 action gate, same asymmetric vtable +0x5c versus +0x7c radius pair, same Structure_GatherWalkCandidates volume sweep behind them. Declared void by the decompiler, but the return is real and is set in two places: AX = 1 on an object block, and otherwise whatever the GatherWalkCandidates tail reports. It drops the mech version's other two arms -- no terrain steepness test, so a ground vehicle drives up anything, and no collision damage. On an object block it still calls the blocker's vtable +0x68 (SimObject_SetRunInto), which makes it the SECOND of the two writers of obj+0xb1. Its only reference is GroundVehicle_ThinkTick.

entries.name: GroundVehicle_ThinkTick
entries.description: StructureGroundVehicleVtable's +0x18 tick slot (slot address 00497830), the only one of the five structure classes that moves. Gated on the group's first member answering targetClass 3, so a ground-vehicle type in a group led by anything else is an ordinary building. Fights with Base_ArmedThinkTick -- plus, with nothing on +0x1a4, a Base_TurretSeek with its own two turret angles fed back negated, which walks the turret to centre -- or for typeRec+0x2e == 0 just Base_ThinkTick. Then saves position/pitch/heading, runs GroundVehicle_Advance and SimObject_ConformToTerrain, and on a block from GroundVehicle_CollisionTest restores the save, zeroes speed and arms the back-off pair at +0x223/+0x227 the way Mech_MovementTick does. Its steering helpers are GroundVehicle_LocomotionTick (0046a798) and GroundVehicle_DriveToPoint (0046a854).

entries.name: GroundVehicle_Advance
entries.description: Steers a ground vehicle and steps it forward. Picks the group leader through 0046a4b8; if that is this object it drives the route (0046a8e4), otherwise it keeps formation on the leader (0046a95c). Then transforms (0, speed, 0) -- speed from +0x220, forward being model Y -- through the object's own frame at +0x12, rebuilding that frame first if +0x32 says it is stale, and writes the result as the new position. The frame includes the pitch and roll SimObject_ConformToTerrain gave it last tick, so the ground distance covered is foreshortened on a slope.

entries.name: GroundVehicle_LocomotionTick
entries.description: The ground vehicle's whole control law and the counterpart of Mech_LocomotionTick: (this, steer, speed). While the back-off countdown at +0x222 is still running it REPLACES the speed with +/-200 by the reverse flag at +0x227 and leaves the steer alone, so a blocked vehicle keeps navigating while it crawls clear. Then the steer is clamped to +/-0x100, the speed slews into +0x220 through Math_RateLimitedMoveToward at 0x1e a tick, and heading (+0x10) takes Math_Q8Multiply(200, steer) added straight on -- there is no turn rate and no inertia in the heading, only in the speed. Finally clears the rotation-valid flag at +0x32. Nothing here is scaled by the tick length. Called by both steering halves and by 0046a854.
entries.signature: void __cdecl GroundVehicle_LocomotionTick(void *vehicle, short steer, short speed)

entries.name: GroundVehicle_DriveToPoint
entries.description: (this, point, legBearing, speed) -> arrived. The ground vehicle's Ai_DriveToPoint, with the same 10000-unit ground-range arrival test (Math_GroundDistanceBetweenPoints) and two differences. It does NOT steer at the point it is given: it offsets a copy of it along legBearing by (9000 - range) with Math_OffsetPointByBearing and steers at that. The subtraction is 32-bit but the offset is taken in 16 bits, so the aim point is always within 32768 of the destination along the leg: from 9000 out to 41767 it sits short of the destination back down the incoming line, inside 9000 it swings past, and further out it cycles every 65536 units of range. And its gain is four times a HERC's: (Math_HeadingToward(aim, this) - heading) >> 4, not >> 6. The shift is encoded SAR EDX, 0x64, which x86 masks to 4. A speed argument of zero means none stated and takes 0xaa, the same default Ai_DriveToPoint uses. Pushes a fourth argument, 0, to the three-argument GroundVehicle_LocomotionTick.
entries.signature: int __cdecl GroundVehicle_DriveToPoint(void *vehicle, int *point, short legBearing, int speed)

entries.name: GroundVehicle_LeaderSteer
entries.description: The group leader's route follow for a ground vehicle. No waypoint after the cursor means GroundVehicle_LocomotionTick(this, 0, 0) -- steer and speed both zero; otherwise it drives at that waypoint with GroundVehicle_DriveToPoint on the bearing between it and the cursor's own, passing speed 0 so the drive takes its own 0xaa default, and advances the route cursor when the drive reports arrival.

entries.name: GroundVehicle_FollowerSteer
entries.description: A non-leader ground vehicle's formation keeping. Takes Group_FirstAbleMember's position, asks its own vtable +0x78 for the formation slot -- note that Formation_RotateAndAddOffset rotates the offset by the group's member array SLOT 0, not by the able leader it is anchored on -- and branches on heading agreement. Inside 0x4000 it matches speed (the leader's own +0x220 minus the along-track error in the leader's frame >> 5, clamped +0x100 / -0x96) and drives at a point 20000 ahead of the post along the leader's heading, with no lateral steering term at all. Outside 0x4000 it abandons the leader's heading and turns straight at the post at (distance >> 5) capped the same way.

entries.name: Raster_SpanTextured
entries.description: Mode 0 span routine: fetch atlasPage[v][u] via a packed page<<16|v<<8|u index into maybe_g_BitmapAtlasCache, store that palette byte to the framebuffer, step the fixed-point u/v, repeat. Two halves selected by DAT_004a09ac: zero is an opaque copy, non-zero skips texels of palette index 0. No shade level, no colour lookup, no blending -- which is why a beam ignores BEAM.DAT's colour index.

entries.name: Raster_SpanTexturedShaded
entries.description: Mode 1 span routine of Raster_DrawPolygon: as Raster_SpanTextured, but each texel goes through one ramp row, ShadeRampTable + (DAT_004a09c4 >> 16) * 0x100, fixed for the span. Two halves selected by DAT_004a09ac: zero stores every texel, non-zero skips a raw texel of palette index 0.

entries.name: Raster_SpanTexturedGouraud
entries.description: Mode 2 span routine of Raster_DrawPolygon: as Raster_SpanTexturedShaded, but the ramp row is per pixel, DAT_004a09c4 stepped by DAT_004a09c8, and there is only an opaque half (no DAT_004a09ac test).

entries.name: maybe_Raster_SpanTexturedShadedQuadratic
entries.description: Frameless span routine (PUSH EBP/ESI/EDI/EBX); Raster_SpanTexturedShadedQuadraticClipped calls it (0048b664). Fills DAT_004a0984 pixels from DAT_004a0980 with atlas texels (page DAT_004a09b4) through the ShadeRampTable row (DAT_004a09c4 >> 16), writing every pixel. u and v start from 004a098e/004a0992 and 004a0996/004a099a and step by 004a099e/004a09a2 and 004a09a6/004a09aa, and those steps change by 004a09bc and 004a09c0 each pixel: second-order stepping.

entries.name: maybe_Raster_SpanTexturedGouraudQuadratic
entries.description: Frameless span routine; Raster_SpanTexturedGouraudQuadraticClipped calls it (0048b72c). The second-order u/v stepping of maybe_Raster_SpanTexturedShadedQuadratic with the ramp row per pixel (DAT_004a09c4 stepped by DAT_004a09c8), and ESP as the destination pointer (ESP saved at 004a09e4, SS loaded from DS for the loop).

entries.name: FireEffect_PerFrameReset
entries.description: The burning-object pool's phase-5 subsystem hook, registered by FireEffect_RegisterSubsystem and driven once a frame from Sim_RenderFrame. Returns the pool's dead entries (ObjectPool_FlushDeleteQueue over DAT_006b4fb8/g_FirePool) and resets DAT_006b4fc0 to 0x7fffffff -- the running nearest-fire distance FireEffect_TickUpdate tests before it calls Sound_UpdatePosition(0x33), which is what keeps the one shared burning loop on the fire nearest the camera. No prologue; it is the tail of the 0046b0xx block, ending at 0046b0a3 where FireEffect_LoadResources begins.

entries.name: FireEffect_LoadResources
entries.description: Loader for the BURNING-OBJECT effect, not the muzzle flash. Reads dts/fire.dts (fire2.dts when CockpitArt_LoadOnDemand is set) into g_FireShapes, allocates the ten-entry g_FirePool and its free list, loads the two banks fire0/fire1 (fire0s/fire1s on demand), then reads dat/FIRE.DAT -- a 4-byte count header plus one byte per shape -- and points each shape's +0x26 at the bank that byte names. Retail: 4 shapes, banks [0, 0, 0, 1]. Carries the fire.cpp assert string.

entries.name: FireEffect_AcquireSlot
entries.description: Takes a free entry from g_FirePool, or when none is free walks the live ones and returns the one with the lowest +0x59 -- the loop count FireEffect_TickUpdate decrements each time the flipbook wraps. So a full pool never refuses a new fire; the one nearest going out pays for it.

entries.name: FireEffect_Ctor
entries.description: Builds one burning-object effect on a FIRE.DTS shape index: owner at +0x4a, attach cluster id at +0x4e (negative uses the raw local point, 0xffff is the structures' 'no cluster'), attach point at +0x50, frame timer +0x57 = 0x40, and the loop count at +0x59 (30, or 5 in theater 4, the Moon, the script.dat header's theater index). On the Moon only shapes 1 and 3 are built; the others go straight back on the free list. The first live instance starts sound 0x33 and FireEffect_Dtor stops it on the last, counted by DAT_006b4fbc. Two spawn sites: Component_DestroyAndCascade, whose .DMG destruction flags' bit 1 releases the machine's other fires and lights shape 0 in their place while bit 3 adds shape 2, and Base_DeathSequenceTick's last stage.

entries.name: FireEffect_Dtor
entries.description: Destroys one burning-object effect and decrements DAT_006b4fbc, stopping sound 0x33 when it reaches zero.

entries.name: FireEffect_ReleaseForOwner
entries.description: Walks the effect pool and returns every entry whose owner pointer at +0x4a matches the argument to the free list -- an object's fires going out when it is destroyed.

entries.name: FireEffect_TickUpdate
entries.description: Burning-object vtable +0x14. Counts the frame timer at +0x57 down, reloads it to 0x40 and steps the shape's cell animation, decrementing the loop count at +0x59 each time the frame wraps to zero -- so a fire LOOPS its flipbook where an impact effect plays it once, and ends when that count reaches zero. Then re-places itself from wherever the owner has carried it to, and keeps the shared burning sound on whichever live fire is nearest the camera: isqrt(Math_ISqrt) of the squared offset to ViewObjectPtr, tested against the running minimum DAT_006b4fc0 that FireEffect_PerFrameReset clears each frame, and Sound_UpdatePosition(0x33) on a win. That test sits above the loops-remaining test, so a fire counts on the tick it goes out. The three squares are 32-bit IMULs and the sum wraps past about 46341 units, which is what makes a distant fire able to read as the nearest one.

entries.name: Fire_GetOwnerDrawCell
entries.description: (fire): returns the address of the cached draw cell (+0x1e8) of the object at fire+0x4a. Scene_SubmitFrameObjects files every fire under it with Scene_SubmitObjectAtCell.

entries.name: FireEffect_RegisterSubsystem
entries.description: Registers FireEffect_LoadResources as a phase-2 subsystem loader and FireEffect_PerFrameReset as phase 5, and nulls the effect pool pointer.

entries.name: FireEffect_StaticDtor
entries.description: _EXIT_ entry 004a7c66 (pointer at 004a7c68): decrements *Rtl_DtorCountPtr and Mem_Delete(g_FirePool) when it is set. The module's _INIT_ is FireEffect_RegisterSubsystem (entry 004a7ba6).

entries.name: TSObj_Draw
entries.description: TS_OBJ vtable +0x00 (004a0b98), inherited unchanged by ANIM_OBJ, EXPLOSION, SMOKE_BALL and FIRE: SimObject_InstallModelTransform(this), then draws the shape instance at +0x34 through its own vtable +0x1c. DET_ANIM_OBJ replaces it with Shape_DrawAtDetailLevel.

entries.name: SimObject_GetPosition
entries.description: Returns obj+0x26, the object's position (the translation of the transform at obj+0x12). Vtable +0x04 of every simulation-object, projectile, effect and FlatObj table; Scene_SubmitObjectWithRadius and ObjList_DrawCellObjects call it for the position.

entries.name: SimObject_GetShapeRadius
entries.description: SimObject vtable +0x10: the current LOD shape's bounding radius, shape+8 via the shape instance at obj+0x34. Every hit test's coarse reject uses it, as does the LOD selector Shape_DrawAtDetailLevel. shape+8 is the third of the three int16 head fields TSPartBase_ReadFromStream reads -- a radius, not an id.

entries.name: TSObj_Dtor
entries.description: TS_OBJ vtable +0x08 (TSObjVtable, 004a0b98, RTTI 'TS_OBJ', 0x41 bytes): the deleting destructor, (this, flags). Reinstalls TSObjVtable at 0046b8b0, deletes the shape instance at +0x34 through its own vtable +0x18 with flags 3, and Mem_Deletes this on flags bit 0. TS_OBJ is the base of every shaped simulation object -- projectiles, effects, FlatObj and, through ANIM_OBJ, the ACTOR hierarchy -- and its destructor is the level all of their destructors reinstall last.

entries.name: MatObj_Dtor
entries.description: MAT_OBJ vtable +0x08 (00497289): the deleting destructor, (this, flags). Two RTL destructor-count decrements (MAT_OBJ, DRAWABLE), then Mem_Delete(this) on flags bit 0.

entries.name: maybe_TextureBankSlot_ElementCtor
entries.description: (slot): returns slot. Per-element constructor of three Rtl_VectorNew arrays of 8-byte records, each a set of bitmap-bank slots: 0xf in Explosion_LoadResources (00407c09, into DAT_004a96bc, whose entries name the banks it loads), 8 into g_MechTextureGroupSlots in Mech_RegisterLoader (00420663), and 2 in FireEffect_LoadResources (0046b249) for the fire0/fire1 banks.

entries.name: ObjPool_FIRE_Dtor
entries.description: ObjPool<FIRE>'s destructor, the dtor its class record (0x8 bytes, at 0046bac5) names: (pool, flags): decrements *Rtl_DtorCountPtr; when the pool is not null, Mem_Delete of its entry buffer at +0 when that is set, then Mem_Delete of the pool when flags bit 0 is set.

entries.name: Terrain_FillCellUntextured
entries.description: (points, count, shades): Terrain_DrawCellQuad's fill for a cell when terrain texturing is off. Installs the points as the current face (DAT_006c6970, count DAT_006c6968, index list 006c60ec, state bytes cleared), projects them (Poly_ProjectViewVertices) and clips them to the near plane (Poly_ClipRingToNearPlane) when that reports one behind it. With shade mode DAT_004aab30 == 2 it installs a mode-1 brush on ramp 2 with the per-vertex shades (carried through the clip by Poly_ClipRingToNearPlaneWithShade), which Raster_FillContourPolygon bands; otherwise a mode-0 brush of the one colour Raster_ShadeRampRow(0x4b)[Palette_ShadeRampLookup(2, shades[0])]. Then 0042e8e8 on a stack object (vtable 004a0cb8) and PolyFill_Fill.

entries.name: Terrain_BindTextureBank
entries.description: Binds the terrain texture bank. Takes a bare base name, joins it with the 'dba' folder pointer (PTR_DAT_004a0a28), loads that resource, and stores its 20-byte-stride frame descriptor table into _DAT_006b4fc4 for Terrain_ResolveCellTexture to index. Called from World_LoadTheater with the 4th of the five NUL-terminated strings at the end of the world<N>.wld descriptor -- so the terrain bank is named in DATA, not in code, which is exactly why neither DBSIM.EXE nor VSHELL.EXE contains the strings 'ice'/'bsnow'/'volcan'/'moon' despite those .DBA files shipping. Retail mapping: WORLD0/1 urban, 2/3 bsnow, 4/5 volcan, 6/7 ice, 8/9 moon.

entries.name: Terrain_ResolveCellTexture
entries.description: Terrain texture selection and tiling. Takes an 8-byte dat\mat0 record, the cell's X and Y, and a UV-rect output of four (u, v) pairs -- pair i belongs to vertex i of Terrain_DrawCellQuad's quad, in its corner order (cellX,cellY), (cellX,cellY+1), (cellX+1,cellY+1), (cellX+1,cellY), so u rises with cellX and the negated v FALLS with cellY. Indexes the active terrain bitmap descriptor table (_DAT_006b4fc4, 20-byte stride -- the SAME per-frame descriptor structure the mech texture path uses, see dts-texture-binding.md) by mat0 field 0, i.e. mat0's first field IS a DBA frame index. Then branches on mat0 field 1 (BlockShift): if 0, the frame's own F0..F3 UV corners are used verbatim (texture stretched across the quad); otherwise shift = cellShift + BlockShift - 13 and the rect becomes u0 = (cellX << shift) & 0xff, v0 = (cellY << shift) & 0xff, spanning 2^shift texels, with V negated. The & 0xff wrap is a 256-texel tiling space -- which is why the terrain banks are 256x256 and must be edge-tileable. Returns descriptor field 4 (bytes 16-19) as a short: the bitmap handle handed to the polygon draw. Retail: mat0 record 0 = {frame 0, BlockShift 6}, record 1 = {frame 1, BlockShift 6}; that is shift = cellShift - 7, so 128 texels per cell at cellShift 14 and 64 at 13 -- 128 world units per texel either way.
entries.signature: int __cdecl Terrain_ResolveCellTexture(int *materialRecord, int cellX, int cellY, int *uvOut)

entries.name: Terrain_FaceVisibilityTest
entries.description: Per-triangle backface test in Terrain_DrawCellQuad: dot(faceNormal, viewerPos - facePoint) > 0, with the viewer position read from g_TerrainViewerPos, DAT_006b4fcc, DAT_006b4fd0. Takes the cell's three-short normal (cell+0x1 for the near triangle, cell+0x7 for the far) and a world point on that triangle. Purely a visibility gate -- it computes no light term; the shade the triangle draws at was baked at zone load, see Terrain_BuildCellSurfaceAndShade.

entries.name: HeightGrid_Constructor
entries.description: Zero-initializes a freshly-allocated 0x129-byte HeightGrid (fields +0x3d/+0x3e/+0x3f=0, +0x42=10, +0x43=8 defaults), assigns its vtable. Called once per zone load, right after the Mem_New(0x129) allocation in Terrain_LoadZone.

entries.name: HeightGrid_Dtor
entries.description: The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's HeightGrid_Dtor (0042878b).
entries.source: es2_naming.py diff DBSIM 0046be78 VSHELL 0042878b: differs only in callee labels and decompiler typing; RTTI HeightGrid vtable slot

entries.name: Terrain_BuildCellSurface
entries.description: Writes one height-grid cell's diagonal selector (cell+0xf bits [0:1]) and both face normals (cell+0x1 and cell+0x7, three shorts each) from its four corner heights. Selector 1 = coplanar quad (h00+h11 == h01+h10, both normals identical), 2 = split along the (0,0)-(1,1) diagonal, 0 = along the anti-diagonal. Normals are in raw height units -- horizontal components are corner differences, vertical is the cell size over the height scale -- doubled, then rescaled to length 0x800 by Math_NormalizeVec3ShortToLength. This is the writer of the selector bits; neither zone loader touches them.

entries.name: Math_NormalizeVec3ShortToLength
entries.description: Rescales a three-short vector in place to a requested length (param_2). Halves all three components until Math_FastMagnitude3D fits under 0x7d01, then multiplies each by Math_Q16Divide(length, magnitude). Called by Terrain_BuildCellSurfaceAndShade with 0x800 for both of a cell's face normals -- which is the constant that makes Light_ComputeShadeForNormal's >> 22 come out as a saturating 512*cos.

entries.name: Terrain_BuildSurface
entries.description: Runs Terrain_BuildCellSurfaceAndShade (0046c2ec) over every cell of a height grid, row by row. The last row and column have no east/north neighbour to difference against and keep a flat (0,0,0x800) normal and selector 0. Two callers: TerrainZone_LoadHeightmap's zone load, and the tail of Terrain_FlattenStructureFootprints (00471190), which has just changed raw heights and so needs every normal, selector and baked shade rebuilt over them.

entries.name: Terrain_BuildCellSurfaceAndShade
entries.description: Terrain_BuildSurface's per-cell body, and THE ANSWER TO WHERE TERRAIN LIGHT COMES FROM. For an interior cell it runs Terrain_BuildCellSurface then normalises both face normals (cell+0x1 near, cell+0x7 far) to length 0x800 via Math_NormalizeVec3ShortToLength; edge cells get a flat (0,0,0x800) instead. Then, unconditionally, it BAKES A SHADE BYTE PER TRIANGLE: cell[+0xd] = Light_ComputeShadeForNormal(cell+0x1), cell[+0xe] = Light_ComputeShadeForNormal(cell+0x7). Terrain_DrawCellQuad reads those two bytes straight back out as the ramp row -- so terrain lighting is computed ONCE at zone load and never per frame, and cell bytes +0xd/+0xe are not dead as the engine's HeightGrid assumed.

entries.name: Terrain_CellSecondPassNoOp
entries.description: Empty body. Terrain_BuildSurface's second pass over every cell calls it once per cell.

entries.name: TerrainZone_PopulateFromBitmap
entries.description: Real retail terrain loader. Takes a loaded Dynamix bitmap (the SAME format used for ordinary .DBM/.DBA textures) and treats its 8-bit grayscale pixel grid directly as the heightmap: the width and height shifts are re-derived from the bitmap's own width/height fields (log2), each pixel byte (minus a bias param_3) becomes one HeightGrid cell's raw height byte (offset 0), and cell diagonal-select/material-type bits (offset 0xf) are assigned via a weighted random roll (~30.6% chance, first match wins) sparsely at an LOD-driven block stride. The roll's upper bound is the hard literal 2 (CMP EBX,0x2 at 0046c5ca), NOT the mat0 count, so this path only ever produces material 0 or 1 -- every shipped zone is a .dba and comes through here. Only the ASCII fallback in TerrainZone_LoadHeightmap bounds the roll by the mat0 count, and materials 2-12 reach shipped terrain solely through Terrain_PaintFormationPad (00471260) (finer cells inherit their block's already-rolled material). Verified byte-exact against real ES2/VOL/ZONES.VOL/DBA/ZONE*.DBA files: 128x128 zones are 16418 bytes (128*128+34-byte bitmap header), 256x256 zones are 65570 bytes (256*256+34) -- exact match.

entries.name: TerrainZone_LoadHeightmap
entries.description: terrain.cpp. Called by Terrain_LoadZone with the zone's built 'dba\zoneNNNN' path. Also separately loads the shared 'dat\mat0' material/detail-type table (count-prefixed array of 8-byte records, ZONES_MaterialTable) into HeightGrid+0x121. Branches on the path's extension: '.dba' (real retail data, ZONES.VOL\DBA\ZONE*.DBA) goes through ClassItem_LoadResource -> TerrainZone_PopulateFromBitmap; any other extension falls back to an ASCII fopen/fscanf format ('%d %d %d %d' header = width shift, height shift, max raw height, min raw height, then one '%d' per cell) -- almost certainly a level-design/debug-only path, no such loose files found in retail data.

entries.name: Terrain_SetupVisibleRegion
entries.description: Per-frame terrain visibility setup, called twice per frame from the frame function 0045fb9c with ActiveHeightGrid passed AS A PARAMETER (which is why a search for readers of the ActiveHeightGrid global missed the terrain render path entirely). WRITES the LOD field: grid[+0x10c] = (short)DAT_004a0bcc[DAT_004d1fc3], then >>= (cellShift - 14) when cellShift > 14. DAT_004a0bcc is three int16s -- 6, 10, 14 cells -- indexed by the terrain-detail option DAT_004d1fc3, so the draw radius is a player setting; the >> only ever fires on the two shift-15 zones and nothing compensates below shift 14. Passes grid[0x10c] << cellShift to 00428bc0 (which derives 5 distance bands), builds the visible cell-space region into grid+0x28 with count grid+0xc8 / pointer grid+0xcc / visible flag grid+0x11c, and installs the grid origin in view space at grid+0x1c and the view-space step of one cell along X at grid+4 and along Y at grid+0x10. The region: Terrain_BuildDrawRegionQuad's square clipped by ViewFrustum_ClipGroundPolygon against a ViewFrustum_Build frustum loosened by 1.5 cells, points shifted down by the cell shift; when nothing is left grid+0x11c goes 0 and the previous polygon stays. Also copies the view's position to g_TerrainViewerPos.

entries.name: Terrain_DrawVisibleCells
entries.description: (grid, view): the terrain draw. Nothing while grid+0x11c is clear. Installs the identity model transform, points the render context's +0x22c at a zero dword for the duration, puts the view's cell (position >> cellShift) in g_TerrainViewerCellX/fd8 and that cell's pending-object count in g_TerrainViewerCellPending, then walks the visible region (grid+0xc8) about that cell: by column (CellWalk_PolygonByColumn, Terrain_DrawCellColumnRun) when the view's heading (+0x14) has magnitude 0x2001..0x5fff (-0x8000 read as 0x7fff), by row (CellWalk_Polygon, Terrain_DrawCellRowRun) otherwise. Ends with Terrain_DrawCellObjects for the viewer's cell when g_TerrainViewerCellPending is still set.

entries.name: Terrain_BuildDrawRegionQuad
entries.description: Builds the terrain draw region as a square of radius (grid[+0x10c] << cellShift) world units centred on the viewer (g_TerrainViewerPos / DAT_006b4fcc), clamped to the grid's own extent ((1 << widthShift) - 2 << cellShift, plus origin at grid+0xf4/+0xf8), and emits it as a 4-corner quad at constant Z (grid+0xfc); writes count 0 instead when the clamped region is empty. Confirms the LOD field is literally a terrain draw radius in cells.

entries.name: Terrain_DrawCellQuad
entries.description: Draws one terrain cell. The caller (Terrain_DrawCellRowRun / Terrain_DrawCellColumnRun) hands it a vertex block already carrying the quad's four camera-space corner positions, in the order (cellX,cellY), (cellX,cellY+1), (cellX+1,cellY+1), (cellX+1,cellY); this fetches the matching four cells at grid[0xec] + index*0x10 (16 bytes/cell) and adds each corner's projected raw height byte (cell[0], via 00495240 against the grid+0xd0 projection state). It re-derives the diagonal split here from the projected corners rather than reading cell[+0xf]: z0+z2 == z1+z3 emits one 4-vertex quad, < 0 splits along corner 0-2, > 0 along corner 1-3. Texture comes from Terrain_ResolveCellTexture(&mat0[cell[0xf] >> 2], cellX, cellY, uvOut), whose four UV pairs are handed to the vertices by index in all three branches -- the fact that pins the corner-to-UV mapping. Each triangle's shade byte is cell[+0xd] (near) / cell[+0xe] (far) and its backface test uses the normals at cell[+0x1] / cell[+0x7] via Terrain_FaceVisibilityTest. Fog: installs the visibility range grid[0x10c] << grid[0x108] via Raster_SetVisibilityRange, then Raster_SetDepthFadeFromDistance(min of the four corners' component 1) -- component 1 is the view-space DEPTH (Raster_PerspectiveDivide divides by it), so a whole cell is fogged from its NEAREST corner's depth, not per pixel and not from a radial distance. Ends by calling Terrain_DrawCellObjects for the cell.
entries.source: docs/retail/formats/terrain-texturing.md, 'Which quad corner takes which UV'
entries.signature: void __cdecl Terrain_DrawCellQuad(int cellX, int cellY, void *grid, int *vertexBlock)
