entries.name: TSDetailPart_SetSizeScale
entries.description: (scale): writes g_TSDetailPartSizeScaleQ10 (004a1034), the Q10 factor TSDetailPart_Render applies to projected size. No caller found by es2_xref. es2_xref finds two references to g_TSDetailPartSizeScaleQ10 (004a1034): this write (004768a3) and TSDetailPart_Render's read (00476928). The VSHELL copy is 004221cd, which writes 004719c8.

entries.name: TSDetailPart_SetBias
entries.description: One-line setter for g_TSDetailPartBias, the starting level index TSDetailPart_Render walks up from, and its only writer. Every caller is a draw slot bracketing its render with a push and a restore to 0: Structure_DrawWithDetailBias, Flyer_Draw, Debris_Draw and WeaponMount_RenderWithDetailBias.

entries.name: TSDetailPart_Render
entries.description: Detail-level selection. size = (radius << DAT_006c60ac) / max(Math_FastMagnitude3D(viewOffset) - radius, 1); t = Math_Q10Multiply(g_TSDetailPartSizeScaleQ10, size); i starts at the STRUCTURE DETAIL bias g_TSDetailPartBias and advances while details[i] < t; renders parts[min(i - bias, count-1)]. Thresholds are ascending and index-aligned with Parts, so part 0 is the coarsest and the last is the finest; bias 0 is MAXIMUM.

entries.name: TSBSPPart_Ctor
entries.description: The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's TSBSPPart_Ctor (004222c9), the TSBSPPart constructor: identical decompiles once the vtable labels are set aside.

entries.name: TSBSPPart_Dtor
entries.description: The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's TSBSPPart_Dtor (004222fa).
entries.source: es2_naming.py diff DBSIM 004769d4 VSHELL 004222fa: differs only in callee labels and decompiler typing; RTTI TSBSPPart vtable slot

entries.name: TSBSPPart_RenderNode
entries.description: Walks a TSBSPPart's BSP tree from one node, back-to-front. Nodes are 14 bytes at part+0x18 (int16 normal triple, int32 coeff, front int16, back int16) with a parallel per-node transform id at part+0x1c (-1 = untransformed). A front/back value below zero draws nothing; with bit 0x4000 set it names child (value & 0x3fff) and renders it through vtable +0x1c; otherwise it is another node index. A child no node reaches is never drawn -- the Parts array is a pool the tree indexes, not a draw list.

entries.name: TSBSPPart_Render
entries.description: The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's TSBSPPart_Render (0042286d).
entries.source: es2_naming.py diff DBSIM 00476b0c VSHELL 0042286d: differs only in callee labels and decompiler typing; RTTI TSBSPPart vtable slot

entries.name: TSTransformState_StaticInit
entries.description: Static initialiser (_INIT_ entry at 004a7bb2, pointer at 004a7bb4): Rtl_VectorNew(&g_TSTransformStates (006b7bf4), 0x110, 0x34, 1, TSTransformState_Ctor), 52 TSTransformStates, the count its debug string 'TSTransformState[52]' (00476c05) names. TSTransformState_StaticDtor deletes them.

entries.name: TSTransformState_StaticDtor
entries.description: Exit routine (_EXIT_ entry at 004a7c6c, pointer at 004a7c6e), frameless: Rtl_VectorDelete(&g_TSTransformStates (006b7bf4), 0x110, 0x34, 1, TSTransformState_Dtor). Identical after normalisation to VSHELL's 00422902.

entries.name: TSTransformState_Ctor
entries.description: TSTransformState constructor, and the element constructor TSTransformState_StaticInit passes Rtl_VectorNew (stored pointer at 00476b75): (state) Rtl_VectorNew of ten 0x16-byte TSContexts at +0x34 with TSContext_Ctor, increments *Rtl_DtorCountPtr and returns state. The LEAs of +0x14 and +0x28 are leftovers of inlined empty member constructors. The 0x110 bytes are the slot Raster_SaveState fills: 0x34 bytes of transform state, then a 0x16-byte model-space light copy per TSContext.

entries.name: TSTransformState_Dtor
entries.description: TSTransformState's destructor, the dtor its class record (0x110 bytes, at 00476c53) names: (state, flags): when state is not null, decrements *Rtl_DtorCountPtr, Rtl_VectorDelete of the ten 0x16-byte TSContexts at +0x34 with TSContext_Dtor, then Mem_Delete when flags bit 0 is set. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's TSTransformState_Dtor (00422978).

entries.name: Memory_Ctor
entries.description: The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's 004077ac, identical after normalisation: (pool) zeroes a src\mymem.cpp Memory object's base +0, byte size +4, free-list head +8 and free bytes +0xc, leaving +0x10 (the lowest free count). Mem_StaticInit runs it on g_SimPool before Heap_InitInBuffer gives the pool its buffer.

entries.name: Heap_InitInBuffer
entries.description: (heap, size, block): heap+0 and +8 = block, +4 = size, +0xc and +0x10 = size & ~7; the block's first dword 0, second size & ~7, and the tag 'KLBF' (0x46424c4b) at block+8. Sim_Run sets up 006bb37c over the 0xb0000 bytes at 00604f88 with it when CockpitArt_LoadOnDemand is set.

entries.name: Memory_IsAllocatedBlock
entries.description: Returns 1 when ptr (header at ptr-8) lies inside the pool's [base, base+size) and its header holds 'KLBA' (0x41424c4b). The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's Memory_IsAllocatedBlock.

entries.name: Memory_IsBlockHeader
entries.description: Returns 1 when a header address lies in [base, base+size-0x10] and is tagged either as a free block ('KLBF' at +8) or an allocated one ('KLBA' at +0). Memory_CheckOverrun calls it. Identical to VSHELL's Memory_IsBlockHeader (00407831) after normalisation.

entries.name: Memory_CheckOverrun
entries.description: The 'Block overrun' check: fails when Memory_IsAllocatedBlock fails; passes when the block ends exactly at base + [pool+4]*8; otherwise returns Memory_IsBlockHeader of the block's own header (ptr-8). The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's Memory_CheckOverrun (00407870), whose description covers what the test does and does not inspect.

entries.name: Memory_LargestFreeBlock
entries.description: Returns the size of the largest block on the pool's free list minus 0x6c, clamped to 0. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's Memory_LargestFreeBlock.

entries.name: Memory_Alloc
entries.description: First-fit allocation from a src\mymem.cpp pool (pool, size, trackLow): the same algorithm and 'KLBA'/'KLBF' block tags as VSHELL's Memory_Alloc, with the asserts compiled out. Mem_New and Mem_NewArray use it on the pool at 006bb37c.

entries.name: Memory_Free
entries.description: Returns a block to a src\mymem.cpp pool: adds its size to the pool's free bytes, writes 'KLBF' at the caller's data start (block +8), and links the block into the free list in address order. When it merges into the free block below it, it writes 0 over that tag; when the free block above merges in, it clears that block's tag. VSHELL's Memory_Free without the asserts. Mem_Delete calls it.

entries.name: Memory_Realloc
entries.description: The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's Memory_Realloc (00407be9) without its two asserts ('Bad pointer', 'Block overrun'): (pool, ptr, newSize). newSize 0 frees (Memory_Free) and returns 0. Rounds to (newSize + 15) & ~7. Shrinking gives the tail to a following free block (relinked through Memory_PrevLinkedHeader), or splits it off as a block freed through Memory_Free when over 0x10 bytes, else moves (Memory_Alloc, memcpy, Memory_Free). Growing takes the room from a following free block large enough, else moves. Updates the free bytes +0xc and the lowest-free mark +0x10. No caller found by es2_xref.

entries.name: Memory_DrawUsageMap
entries.description: The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's Memory_DrawUsageMap (00407ea3), identical after normalisation: (pool, x, y, cols, rows) gives each of cols * rows cells an equal share of pool+4 (the byte size of the first argument), walks g_SimPool (006bb37c) with Memory_BlockIterBegin/Next, and prints one character per cell with Mono_Printf('%c' at 004a10fc) at (x + col, y + row): 07 for 0 percent allocated, B1 under 50, B2 under 100, DB at 100. No caller found by es2_xref.

entries.name: Memory_PrevLinkedHeader
entries.description: The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's Memory_PrevLinkedHeader (00407fe6) without its asserts: (pool, freeBlock) returns 0 when freeBlock is the free-list head (pool+8), else walks the list and returns the entry whose link (+0) is freeBlock, or 0 at the end of the list. Memory_Realloc calls it twice (0047704a, 00477144).

entries.name: Memory_BlockIterBegin
entries.description: The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's Memory_BlockIterBegin (00408089): (iter, pool) sets iter[0] = pool and iter[1] = the pool base (the first block header). Memory_DrawUsageMap calls it.

entries.name: Memory_BlockIterNext
entries.description: The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's Memory_BlockIterNext (0040809d): (iter) returns 0 when iter[1] is 0; otherwise advances iter[1] by the current header's size (+4), clears it once it reaches base + size, and returns it. Memory_DrawUsageMap calls it.

entries.name: maybe_Memory_OperatorNew
entries.description: The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's maybe_Memory_OperatorNew (004080d7): (size, pool) returns Memory_Alloc(pool, size, 1). The name assumes a class operator new(size_t, Memory*). No caller found by es2_xref.

entries.name: Mem_HeapAlloc
entries.description: calloc(1, size), adding the block's own recorded size to the heap byte count at 006bb390, which Mem_Delete subtracts from. The large-request path of Mem_New and Mem_NewArray, and what Arena_Push allocates an arena with. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's Mem_HeapAlloc; returns the calloc pointer in EAX (the decompile drops it).

entries.name: Mem_New
entries.description: The global operator new, the DBSIM copy of VSHELL's Mem_New. A size below the pool's free byte count (006bb388, pool 006bb37c + 0xc) and no larger than the pool's largest free block less 0x6c (00476dd0) is carved from the pool by Memory_Alloc; anything else goes to Mem_HeapAlloc. Both paths hand back zeroed memory, which is what settles what an uninitialised object field holds at construction. Mem_Delete is its pair; Mem_NewArray is the same with 8 bytes added.

entries.name: Mem_NewArray
entries.description: The global array operator new, the DBSIM copy of VSHELL's Mem_NewArray: Mem_New with 8 bytes added to the size. It returns the block start, so the 8 bytes are unused slack, not a header. Rtl_VectorNew allocates through it and callers pass count * element size; Mem_DeleteArray is its pair. Also the fallback Arena_Alloc drops to when there is no arena or the arena is full.

entries.name: Mem_Delete
entries.description: The global operator delete, the DBSIM copy of VSHELL's Mem_Delete: a pointer for which Memory_IsAllocatedBlock holds on the pool at 006bb37c goes back to it through Memory_Free; anything else is _free'd and its size at p[-1] subtracted from the heap byte count at 006bb390. Pairs with Mem_New.

entries.name: Mem_DeleteArray
entries.description: The global array operator delete, the DBSIM copy of VSHELL's Mem_DeleteArray: body identical to Mem_Delete (a tagged block in the pool at 006bb37c goes back through Memory_Free, anything else is _free'd and its size at p[-1] subtracted from the heap byte count at 006bb390). Rtl_VectorDelete frees through it.

entries.name: Mem_StaticInit
entries.description: Static initialiser (_INIT_ entry at 004a7bb8, pointer at 004a7bba), frameless: Memory_Ctor(&g_SimPool (006bb37c)). Identical after normalisation to VSHELL's 00408232, which does the same to g_ShellPool.

entries.name: JoystickDevice_CtorBase
entries.description: (this, kind, ...): GL_ClaimGlobal(this, kind, this); when this is the instance claimed for kind (006c5f38[kind]), Joystick_Enumerate(this, kind); then sets the resolution field +0x16 to 7. JoystickDevice_Ctor runs it.

entries.name: DVJoystick_Dtor
entries.description: DVJoystick's destructor, the dtor its class record (RTTI 'DVJoystick', 0x1f bytes, at 0045c597) names: (this, flags) decrements *Rtl_DtorCountPtr; when GL global slot +0x18 (006c5f38 + index*4, the GL_ClaimGlobal table) is set, DVJoystick_Shutdown(this) and clears the slot; then Mem_Delete when flags bit 0 is set. VSHELL's DVJoystick_Dtor (004057b8) reads its index at +0x68 and asserts on a clear slot.

entries.name: Joystick_Enumerate
entries.description: joyGetDevCapsA over joystick ids 0 and 1 only, into JOYCAPS blocks at DAT_006bb3fc (stride 0x194), stamping each MMRESULT at DAT_006bb724; then one joyGetPosEx per device. Sets each JOYINFOEX's dwSize to 0x34 and dwFlags to 0xccf -- X, Y, Z, R, POV, BUTTONS, CENTERED, USEDEADZONE. U and V are never requested.

entries.name: DVJoystick_Shutdown
entries.description: (this): clears bit 0 of the joystick's first dword. DVJoystick_Dtor calls it. Byte-identical to VSHELL's DVJoystick_Shutdown (0040591c).

entries.name: Joystick_Poll
entries.description: Polls both sticks with joyGetPosEx and packs the 0x12-byte device reading. Stick 0's X and Y always; its Z as the throttle and R as the rudder when JOYCAPS_HASZ/HASR, else stick 1's X and Y. dwPOV is matched against exactly 0/18000/27000/9000 into bits 0-3 of one byte -- no diagonal matches. Stick 1's button mask is OR'd in shifted left by stick 0's wMaxButtons.

entries.name: Joystick_NormaliseAxes
entries.description: Maps each of the four raw joyGetPosEx axes onto a signed byte: (raw << 8) / 0xffff - 0x80, giving -0x80..+0x80. Joystick_ReadWithResponse takes the width as 1 << the resolution field +0x16, which JoystickDevice_CtorBase sets to 7. No JOYCAPS min/max is consulted -- the game leans entirely on Windows' own calibration.

entries.name: Joystick_ReadAxisSigns
entries.description: (device, out): returns 0 when bit 0 of the device's first byte is clear. Otherwise Joystick_NormaliseAxes into the device's four axes (+4..+0x10), replaces each with its sign (-1, 0 or +1), copies the four axes and the int16 at +0x14 to out and returns 1. Joystick_ReadWithResponse reads response mode 2 through it, and its deadzone step then zeroes every axis.

entries.name: Input_QueryCapabilities
entries.description: Rebuilds the eight-byte joystick capability block at 006bb72c on every call, zeroing it first, and returns it. +0 is 2 when DAT_006bb728 is zero and 1 otherwise, so never 0; +2 is the button count, DAT_006bb438 + DAT_006bb5cc clamped to 8; +4 is 1 unless the device flag word 006bb45c has bit 0 clear and DAT_006bb728 is non-zero, and +5 likewise with bit 1; +6 is the flag word's bit 4 as it stands, 0 or 0x10. ControlsPanel_Run greys its rows against it (read).

entries.name: DVKeyboard_AtExitNoOp
entries.description: A single RET in bytes Ghidra left undefined between Input_QueryCapabilities and DVKeyboard_AssertHookNoOp. KeyboardDriver_Ctor registers it with _atexit (PUSH 0x477890 at 004778c9). VSHELL's DVKeyboard_Ctor registers its counterpart 0040456c, also a single RET.

entries.name: DVKeyboard_AssertHookNoOp
entries.description: Empty body. KeyboardDriver_Ctor registers it with Assert_AddHook (PUSH 0x477894 at 004778d4), as VSHELL's DVKeyboard_Ctor registers 0040456d.

entries.name: KeyboardDriver_Ctor
entries.description: (this, arg): GL_ClaimGlobal(this, 1, this); when this is the claimed keyboard instance (006c5f3c) runs KeyboardDriver_Init (00477940) and, if that succeeds, registers atexit DVKeyboard_AtExitNoOp (00477890), Assert hook DVKeyboard_AssertHookNoOp (00477894) and a KeyListener_Register subscription with callback KeyListener_NoOp (00477970). KeyboardInputDevice_Ctor runs it.

entries.name: DVKeyboard_Dtor
entries.description: DVKeyboard's destructor, the dtor its class record (RTTI 'DVKeyboard', 4 bytes, at 0045b9e8) names: (this, flags) decrements *Rtl_DtorCountPtr; when the claimed keyboard (GL global 1, 006c5f3c) is set, DVKeyboard_Shutdown and clears it; then Mem_Delete when flags bit 0 is set. IMKeyboard's destructor 0045c03c calls it with flags 0.

entries.name: KeyboardDriver_Init
entries.description: (this): WndProcHook_Register(00477ae0), then returns bit 0 of this+0. KeyboardDriver_Ctor runs it for the claimed keyboard instance and goes on only when it returns non-zero.

entries.name: DVKeyboard_Shutdown
entries.description: WndProcHook_Unregister(Key_WndProcHook), returns 0. DVKeyboard_Dtor calls it. VSHELL's DVKeyboard_Shutdown (00404670) only returns 0.

entries.name: KeyListener_NoOp
entries.description: Returns 0, so a code it is offered stays unconsumed. KeyboardDriver_Ctor registers it with KeyListener_Register and an empty code list (stored pointer at 004778e8); Input_BuildSourceTable registers it with KeyListener_RegisterCopy and codes 0049eae4 (stored pointer at 0045a62a). The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's KeyListener_NoOp (00404677).

entries.name: DVKeyboard_ReturnZero
entries.description: Returns 0. KeyboardInputDevice_SetReadMode (0045c148) calls it with (keyboard, arg), ignores the answer, then stores arg at keyboard+9; es2_xref finds that one call. It sits at the position of VSHELL's 0040467e (also a return 0) in the dv_ky.cpp block.

entries.name: DVKeyboard_StubReturnZero1
entries.description: Returns 0. No caller found by es2_xref. Number 1 of six such stubs after DVKeyboard_ReturnZero in the dv_ky.cpp block (the sixth is DVKeyboard_StubReturnZero6 (004779a8)). VSHELL's block has six stubs in the same position that report an assert at src\dv_ky.cpp and return 0; this one sits where VSHELL's 00404685 (line 0xbf) does.

entries.name: DVKeyboard_StubReturnZero2
entries.description: Returns 0. No caller found by es2_xref. Number 2 of six such stubs after DVKeyboard_ReturnZero in the dv_ky.cpp block (the sixth is DVKeyboard_StubReturnZero6 (004779a8)). VSHELL's block has six stubs in the same position that report an assert at src\dv_ky.cpp and return 0; this one sits where VSHELL's 004046af (line 0xc4) does.

entries.name: DVKeyboard_StubReturnZero3
entries.description: Returns 0. No caller found by es2_xref. Number 3 of six such stubs after DVKeyboard_ReturnZero in the dv_ky.cpp block (the sixth is DVKeyboard_StubReturnZero6 (004779a8)). VSHELL's block has six stubs in the same position that report an assert at src\dv_ky.cpp and return 0; this one sits where VSHELL's 004046d9 (line 0xc9) does.

entries.name: DVKeyboard_StubReturnZero4
entries.description: Returns 0. No caller found by es2_xref. Number 4 of six such stubs after DVKeyboard_ReturnZero in the dv_ky.cpp block (the sixth is DVKeyboard_StubReturnZero6 (004779a8)). VSHELL's block has six stubs in the same position that report an assert at src\dv_ky.cpp and return 0; this one sits where VSHELL's 00404703 (line 0xd0) does.

entries.name: DVKeyboard_StubReturnZero5
entries.description: Returns 0. No caller found by es2_xref. Number 5 of six such stubs after DVKeyboard_ReturnZero in the dv_ky.cpp block (the sixth is DVKeyboard_StubReturnZero6 (004779a8)). VSHELL's block has six stubs in the same position that report an assert at src\dv_ky.cpp and return 0; this one sits where VSHELL's 0040472d (line 0xd5) does.

entries.name: DVKeyboard_StubReturnZero6
entries.description: Its whole body is XOR EAX,EAX; RET: returns 0. The last of the six 7-byte return-0 stubs DVKeyboard_StubReturnZero1 (00477980)-004779a8 between DVKeyboard_Shutdown and Keyboard_FlushKeys in the dv_ky.cpp block; VSHELL has six stubs at the same place in its dv_ky.cpp block (00404685-00404757) that each raise a severity-4 assert at src\dv_ky.cpp lines 0xbf-0xda, so this is the sixth (line 0xda) with the assert compiled out. No caller found by es2_xref.
entries.source: DBSIM decompile and disassembly at 004779a8; VSHELL 00404757

entries.name: Keyboard_FlushKeys
entries.description: (keyboard): empties KeyEventRing (read index 006bb938 = write index 006bb934) and clears bit 1 (keys pending) of the keyboard object's flags. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's Keyboard_FlushKeys.

entries.name: Keyboard_PopKey
entries.description: (keyboard): pops the next 16-bit code off KeyEventRing (read index 006bb938, write index 006bb934) and returns it, 0 when the ring is empty; clears bit 1 (keys pending) of the keyboard object's flags when it empties the ring. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's Keyboard_PopKey.

entries.name: KeyListener_Register
entries.description: Appends to the ten-slot {enabled, wantedCodes, callback} keyboard subscriber table at 006bb93c that Key_WndProcHook walks. wantedCodes is a NUL-terminated list of the low bytes (scancodes) that subscriber wants; the first callback to return 1 consumes the code.

entries.name: KeyListener_UnregisterCallback
entries.description: (keyboard, callback), the first argument ignored: clears the enabled word of every enabled slot of KeyListenerTable (006bb93c, ten 12-byte {enabled, wantedCodes, callback} slots) whose callback (+8) equals callback; returns 1. No caller found by es2_xref. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's 004047ff (identical decompile).
entries.source: DBSIM decompile and disassembly at 00477a44; VSHELL 004047ff

entries.name: KeyListener_RegisterCopy
entries.description: A byte-identical copy of KeyListener_Register (00477a0c) at a different address: appends {1, wantedCodes, callback} to KeyListenerTable. Input_BuildSourceTable registers callback 00477970 with wanted codes 0049eae4 through it.

entries.name: KeyListener_Unregister
entries.description: (keyboard, callback, wantedCodes), the first argument ignored: clears the enabled word of the first enabled KeyListenerTable slot (KeyListenerTable (006bb93c)) whose callback (+8) and wantedCodes (+4) both match, returning 1; returns 0 when all ten slots fail to match. KeyListener_Register's inverse. No caller found by es2_xref. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's 0040485e (identical decompile).
entries.source: DBSIM decompile and disassembly at 00477aa8; VSHELL 0040485e

entries.name: Key_WndProcHook
entries.description: The keyboard filter in the same ten-slot table ahead of MainWndProc as Mouse_WndProcHook. Catches WM_KEYDOWN/UP (0x100/0x101) and WM_SYSKEYDOWN/UP (0x104/0x105), translates the virtual key through the 223-entry scancode table at 004a1104, ORs in 0x800 for Shift, 0x200 for Alt, 0x400 for Ctrl and 0x80 for a key-up, then offers the code to the ten subscribers at 006bb93c; whatever none of them claims goes into the 256-entry ring at 006bb734.

entries.name: Raster_BuildEdgeTables
entries.description: (count, vertices, flags): turns a clipped ring of 7-dword screen vertices {x, y, depth, u, v, w, shade} into per-row edge entries. Drops repeated points (fewer than 3 left gives 0 rows); walks forward from the top vertex (smallest y, rightmost) into the right-edge table at 006bbe14 and backward from the top-leftmost one into the left-edge table at 006c0914, until each reaches the bottom y. Each 10-dword row entry: +0 x, +4 depth (flag 8), +8/+0xc u and v (flag 1), +0x14 shade (flag 4); flag 2 makes u and v 64-bit (high dwords at +0x20/+0x24, shifted by 10 instead of 8) and adds w at +0x10 and a quadratic fit of u/w and v/w through the edge's ends and middle at +0x18/+0x1c. Returns 006c5414 = {first row (clamped to ctx+0x214), row count, left table, right table}.
entries.source: DBSIM decompile at 00477c3c; table roles from Raster_DrawPolygon's use (+8 start x, +0xc end x)

entries.name: RasterEdgeTables_StaticInit
entries.description: Static initialiser (Borland _INIT_ entry 004a7bbe, priority 0x20): Rtl_VectorNew over RasterRightEdgeTable (006bbe14) and RasterLeftEdgeTable (006c0914), each 0x1e0 (480) elements of 0x28 bytes, with the element constructor RasterEdgeRow_ElementCtor (00478513). Raster_BuildEdgeTables writes one 0x28-byte row per screen line into them.

entries.name: RasterEdgeRow_ElementCtor
entries.description: (row): returns its argument -- the per-element constructor RasterEdgeTables_StaticInit passes to Rtl_VectorNew for the two 480-row, 0x28-byte edge tables (pointer stored at 004784dd and 004784f8).

entries.name: ObjectPool_QueueForDelete
entries.description: Appends an object to a deferred-delete queue (pointer array at queue+0, int16 count at queue+4), used with g_FlatObjDeleteQueue and the other pools' queues. Nothing is destructed here, and the append does not test the capacity at queue+6.

entries.name: ObjectPool_FlushDeleteQueue
entries.description: Drains the queue ObjectPool_QueueForDelete fills: destructs each entry through its vtable +0x08, returns it to the pool, then zeroes the count.

entries.name: Stub_ReturnZero
entries.description: Returns 0. Vtable +0x0c of every simulation-object, projectile, effect and FlatObj table, and of the table at 00498064; what the slot is for is not established.

entries.name: Drawable_GetRadiusZero
entries.description: DRAWABLE vtable +0x10, kept by MAT_OBJ, REG_OBJ, TINY_OBJ, their TS_ variants, LightSource, SMOKE and DummyDrawable: returns 0. TS_OBJ and everything below it install SimObject_GetShapeRadius in the slot.

entries.name: Drawable_Dtor
entries.description: DRAWABLE vtable +0x08 (004a14bc, RTTI 'DRAWABLE', 0xc bytes): the deleting destructor, (this, flags). One RTL destructor-count decrement, reinstalls DRAWABLE's table, and Mem_Deletes this on flags bit 0.

entries.name: ANSequence_NextFrame
entries.description: Plain ANSequence vtable +0x20: frame >= frameCount-1 ? frame : frame+1, i.e. CLAMPS rather than wrapping. That clamp is the only way a one-shot's end is observable, because the end-of-sequence test everywhere is frame == nextFrame. Every retail chassis carries exactly one non-cyclic sequence and its chassis record's death-animation id names it. Args derived from disassembly: [EBP+8] sequence, [EBP+0xc] frame.

entries.name: ANSequence_PrevFrame
entries.description: Plain ANSequence vtable +0x24: frame != 0 ? frame-1 : 0, i.e. holds at the first frame. Args derived from disassembly: only [EBP+0xc] is read, the sequence pointer being unused on this arm.

entries.name: ANSequence_FrameShortOfTarget
entries.description: ANSequence vtable +0x28 (004a6864), (seq, frame, target, flag): 1 when frame < target, or frame == target and flag is 0; otherwise 0. AnimThread_FindTransition asks it of a transition's destination sequence, for forward play, with the thread's +0x1c as the flag. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's 0046301c.

entries.name: ANSequence_FrameShortOfTargetBackward
entries.description: ANSequence vtable +0x2c (004a6864), ANSequence_FrameShortOfTarget's mirror for backward play: 1 when frame > target, or frame == target and flag is 0. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's 00463048.

entries.name: ANCyclicSequence_NextFrame
entries.description: ANCyclicSequence vtable +0x20: frame < frameCount-1 ? frame+1 : 0, i.e. wraps. Args derived from disassembly: [EBP+8] sequence, [EBP+0xc] frame, plain RET.

entries.name: ANCyclicSequence_PrevFrame
entries.description: ANCyclicSequence vtable +0x24: frame != 0 ? frame-1 : frameCount-1, i.e. wraps. Args derived from disassembly: [EBP+8] sequence, [EBP+0xc] frame.

entries.name: ANCyclicSequence_FrameShortOfTarget_Always
entries.description: ANCyclicSequence vtable +0x28 (004a6828): returns 1 in AX. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's 004630b0.

entries.name: ANCyclicSequence_FrameShortOfTargetBackward_Always
entries.description: ANCyclicSequence vtable +0x2c (004a6828): returns 1 in AX. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's 004630bc.

entries.name: ShapeInst_Construct
entries.description: TSShapeInstance constructor. Reads the node count from shape->animList+0x16 into shapeInst+0xc, then allocates the three per-node arrays ONCE: dirty flags at +0xe, local transforms at +0x12 (stride 0xc) and world transforms at +0x16 (stride 0x20). Seeds the locals from the anim list's default transforms and calls ShapeInst_BuildWorldTransforms. Nothing reallocates these, so an instance stays sized and numbered by the shape it was built with -- root 0 for a machine -- whatever root Shape_DrawAtDetailLevel later swaps in.

entries.name: ANShapeInstance_Dtor
entries.description: The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's ANShapeInstance_Dtor (004631bc).
entries.source: es2_naming.py diff DBSIM 00478850 VSHELL 004631bc: differs only in callee labels and decompiler typing; RTTI ANShapeInstance vtable slot

entries.name: ShapeInst_CountThreads
entries.description: (shapeInst): returns how many of the ten thread slots from shapeInst+0x1a are filled, counting up to the first null.

entries.name: ShapeInst_SortThreadsByPriority
entries.description: (shapeInst): bubble-sorts the thread slots at shapeInst+0x1a ascending by AnimThread_SequencePriority, swapping only on strictly greater, so equal priorities keep registration order. ShapeInst_RegisterThread runs it on every registration and AnimThread_StepAll after every advance; since ShapeInst_EvalAllNodeLocals runs last-to-first, the lowest priority wins a node two threads cover.

entries.name: ShapeInst_RegisterThread
entries.description: (shapeInst, thread): stores thread in the first empty of the ten slots at shapeInst+0x1a and re-sorts them with ShapeInst_SortThreadsByPriority; returns 1, or 0 when all ten are taken. ShapeInst_AddThread registers through it.

entries.name: ShapeInst_RemoveThread
entries.description: (shapeInst, thread): finds thread in the ten slots at shapeInst+0x1a that ShapeInst_RegisterThread fills, shifts the slots after it down by one and zeroes the tenth; returns 1, or 0 when thread is not registered. Does not free the thread.

entries.name: AnimThread_StepAll
entries.description: Advances every thread on the shape instance by the timestep (AnimThread_Advance, 00479614), last slot first over ShapeInst_CountThreads slots, then re-sorts the slots with ShapeInst_SortThreadsByPriority. Then, if a first thread exists, writes its ramped root transform (AnimThread_ReadRootTransform, 00478fa8) into the leading slot of the world-transform array at shapeInst+0x16 -- the first thread after the sort, which is not always the one ShapeInst_SeedRootTransform seeded before the advance.

entries.name: ShapeInst_EvalAllNodeLocals
entries.description: Runs AnimThread_EvalNodeLocals (004799a4) over every thread the shape instance holds (thread pointers from shapeInst+0x1a upward), passing the local-transform array (shapeInst+0x12) and the dirty-flag array (shapeInst+0xe). The loop runs last-to-first and AnimThread_EvalNodeLocals overwrites each covered node's local transform unconditionally, so the first slot's write is the one left standing for a node several threads cover -- and the slots are kept in ascending sequence priority by ShapeInst_SortThreadsByPriority. See docs/retail/formats/dts-node-posing.md, 'Several threads on one shape'.

entries.name: ShapeInst_ReadRootTransform
entries.description: (shapeInst, out): AnimThread_ReadRootTransform of the first thread into out, or the identity transform (0x4000 on the diagonal) when the instance has none.

entries.name: ShapeInst_SeedRootTransform
entries.description: (shapeInst, transform): when the instance has a thread, AnimThread_WriteRootTransform(first thread, transform) and copies the 0x20-byte transform into world slot 0 (shapeInst+0x16). The first thread is the first after ShapeInst_SortThreadsByPriority. SimObject_ApplyRootMotion seeds identity through it before stepping.

entries.name: ShapeInst_ComposeChildTransform
entries.description: Same expansion as ShapeInst_ExpandRootTransform, then concatenates the result onto the parent's world transform (Transform_Concat) into the destination slot.

entries.name: ShapeInst_ExpandRootTransform
entries.description: Expands one 12-byte local transform into a 0x20-byte world transform with no parent: BuildEulerRotationMatrixQ14 over the three leading shorts, and the trailing three shorts widened to the ints at +0x14/+0x18/+0x1c. Confirms the 0xc-byte local record layout is [eulerX, eulerY, eulerZ, x, y, z] as shorts.

entries.name: ShapeInst_BuildWorldTransforms
entries.description: Composes the per-node WORLD transform array (shapeInst+0x16, stride 0x20, indexed by transform id) that everything else reads -- e.g. Mech_TargetRelativeToPilot (0041ef14) and the cockpit eye. Walks the relation list (pairs of shorts at animList+0xc, count at animList+10): parent == -1 goes through ShapeInst_ExpandRootTransform (00478b10), otherwise ShapeInst_ComposeChildTransform (00478ab8) against the parent's already-built world transform. Dirty-flag driven off shapeInst+0xe (bit 0 = local changed, bit 1 = world rebuilt, so children follow), and memsets the flag array when done.

entries.name: ShapeInstance_StepAnimation
entries.description: Advance threads, evaluate keyframes into per-node local transforms, rebuild world transforms. In call order: AnimThread_StepAll (004789a0) then ShapeInst_EvalAllNodeLocals (004789f4, which runs AnimThread_EvalNodeLocals per thread) then ShapeInst_BuildWorldTransforms (00478b58). The keyframe interpolation is the middle step, so poses are re-blended every time this is called. Cadence: the sole caller is SimObject_ApplyRootMotion (0040250c), which Mech_IntegrateMotion runs once per sim tick -- poses are evaluated per TICK, not per rendered frame. DBSIM has no separate render rate to be per-frame at: Time_BeginSimTick spin-waits the whole loop to 40 ms (25 Hz), so tick and frame are the same thing in the original. A port with a fixed 25 Hz tick matches vanilla pose cadence exactly, however fast it renders.

entries.name: ShapeInst_PushModelTransform
entries.description: (shapeInst, scratch, root): saves g_ModelTransformPtr, Transform_Concat(root, saved, scratch), installs scratch with Raster_SetModelTransform and returns the saved pointer. ANShapeInstance_Render brackets TSShapeInstance_Render with it and ShapeInst_PopModelTransform. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's ShapeInst_PushModelTransform (004635a4).

entries.name: ShapeInst_PopModelTransform
entries.description: (shapeInst, saved): Raster_SetModelTransform(saved) when saved is non-null. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's ShapeInst_PopModelTransform (004635d0).

entries.name: ANShapeInstance_Render
entries.description: The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's ANShapeInstance_Render (004635e4). It differs from VSHELL's: VSHELL runs Transform_Ctor on the local transform first and reads the shape through TSShapeInstance_GetShape; DBSIM's makes no Transform_Ctor call and reads the shape at instance +4 inline.
entries.source: es2_naming.py diff DBSIM 00478c98 VSHELL 004635e4: differs as described; RTTI ANShapeInstance vtable slot

entries.name: ANShape_Render
entries.description: The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's ANShape_Render (00463630).
entries.source: es2_naming.py diff DBSIM 00478cd8 VSHELL 00463630: identical after normalisation; RTTI ANShape vtable slot

entries.name: ShapeInst_StaticInit
entries.description: Static initialiser (Borland _INIT_ entry 004a7bc4, priority 0x20) of the shape-instance block (ShapeInst_*, ANShapeInstance_*): a single RET. The ANShapeInstance class record follows it at 00478ce1.

entries.name: AnimThread_Ctor
entries.description: (thread, animList): stores animList at +0, AnimThread_SetSequence(thread, 0, 0, 0), zeroes the 0x20 bytes at +0x2e and stores 0x4000 in the int16s at +0x2e, +0x34 and +0x3e. Returns thread. ShapeInst_AddThread builds each 0x52-byte thread with it.

entries.name: AnimThread_SequencePriority
entries.description: (thread): returns the int16 at +6 of the sequence the thread is playing (shape->sequences[thread+4]) -- the field after the tick count and before the ground-movement flag at +8, the file's 'priority'.
entries.source: DBSIM disassembly at 00478d80; ANSequence file layout

entries.name: AnimThread_ElapsedTicks
entries.description: (thread): the ticks played into the current sequence: walks from frame 0 with the sequence's (animList+6 table, index thread+4) vtable +0x20 next-frame step until it reaches the current frame (+6), summing each passed frame's duration (int16 +0 of its 6-byte record in the sequence's +0xc table), and returns that sum plus the intra-frame offset (int16 +0x1c). No caller found by es2_xref. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's AnimThread_ElapsedTicks (00464a58), identical after normalisation.
entries.source: DBSIM decompile and disassembly at 00478d98; es2_naming diff with VSHELL 00464a58

entries.name: AnimThread_LoadFrameGroundMovement
entries.description: Called on every animation frame advance. If the sequence ground-movement flag is set, loads Transforms[transformIndices[frame * numParts]] -- part index 0, the root node -- into the thread ground translation (+0x22/24/26) and rotation (+0x28/2a/2c) and sets the ground-move flag at +0x20.

entries.name: AnimThread_CommitGroundMovement
entries.description: On frame exit, folds the completed frame full ground transform into the thread stored transform.

entries.name: AnimThread_UncommitGroundMovement
entries.description: Inverse of AnimThread_CommitGroundMovement, for backward playback.

entries.name: AnimThread_ReadRootTransform
entries.description: Returns scale(groundTransform, thread[0x1c]/thread[0x1e]) composed onto the thread stored transform, where the fraction is intra-frame accumulator over frame duration. Inverse of AnimThread_WriteRootTransform.

entries.name: AnimThread_WriteRootTransform
entries.description: Stores inverse(scale(groundTransform, frac)) composed with the incoming transform. Paired with AnimThread_ReadRootTransform so that seeding identity and reading back yields the exact per-tick root-motion delta.

entries.name: AnimThread_SetSequence
entries.description: (thread, sequence, frame, offset): cuts a thread straight to a sequence and frame, abandoning any target. Stores the sequence at +4 and +8 and the frame at +6, the sequence's vtable +0x20 answer for the frame at +0xa, the intra-frame offset at +0x1c and the frame's duration from the sequence's 6-byte frame table (+0xc) at +0x1e, loads the frame's ground movement (AnimThread_LoadFrameGroundMovement), then clears the target (+0x16 and +0x18 = -1, +0x1a = 0), sets +0xc to -1 and +0x50 to 1. AnimThread_SeekToPosition, ShapeInst_AddThread and the locomotion ticks call it.

entries.name: AnimThread_SeekToPosition
entries.description: Parks a thread at a Q14 fraction of a sequence instead of playing through it: sums the sequence's frame durations, scales the position by Q14 x (total - 1) (Math_Q14Multiply), walks the frames subtracting durations, and installs the resulting frame + intra-frame offset with AnimThread_SetSequence (004791a0). The only caller pair is the two torso ticks, which pass (unsigned)angle >> 2 -- this is how a turret angle becomes a pose. See docs/retail/simulation/torso-aim.md.

entries.name: AnimThread_FindTransition
entries.description: (thread): walks the current sequence's (+4) frames from the current frame (+6) when playing backward (rate +0x4e < 0) or the next frame (+0xa) otherwise, stepping with the sequence's vtable +0x24 (previous) or +0x20 (next) until it laps, and scans each frame's transitions (8-byte records at anim +0x1e, a frame's first index and count in the sequence's 6-byte per-frame table at +0xc) for one whose destination (+2) is the target sequence (+0x16). A match is armed: duration (+0) to +0x12, the target to +0xe, destination frame (+4) to +0x10, transform index (+6) to +0x14. With no target frame (+0x18 == -1) that is final; otherwise the destination sequence's vtable +0x2c (backward) or +0x28 (forward) is asked, with (destination frame, target frame, +0x1c), whether it lands on the near side of the target, and the scan continues when it does not. Leaves the scan frame (+0xc) at -1 when nothing qualifies. AnimThread_SetTarget calls it.
entries.source: DBSIM decompile at 004792c8; ported as AnimationThread.FindTransition

entries.name: AnimThread_SetTarget
entries.description: Asks playback to reach a sequence via whatever transition leads there rather than snapping to it: writes thread+0x16/+0x18/+0x1a, clears the at-target bit and runs AnimThread_FindTransition to find the transition. frame -1 means any frame will do; flags bit 0 stops playback dead on arrival. This, not AnimThread_SetSequence, is how the death fall is started, so sweeping the latter's call sites alone does not enumerate what plays a sequence. Args derived from disassembly: four pushes with ADD ESP,0x10 at 00416db5.
entries.signature: void __cdecl AnimThread_SetTarget(void *thread, short sequence, short frame, short flags)

entries.name: AnimThread_SetPlaybackRate
entries.description: Writes the playback rate to thread+0x4e; restarts the sequence when the sign flips.

entries.name: AnimThread_Advance
entries.description: Advances one animation thread by dt * thread[0x4e] >> 8, crossing frames forward or backward and driving the ground-movement load and commit hooks.

entries.name: AnimThread_EvalNodeLocals
entries.description: The keyframe interpolator. For each animated column of the playing sequence, reads the transform-pool index at (sequence, frame) and at (nextSequence, nextFrame); if the two indices match, copies the 12-byte local transform straight; otherwise calls Anim_BlendKeyframeTransforms (00492600) with a Q10 interpolant of ((frameAccumulator * 0x400 + frameDuration/2) / frameDuration) -- the SAME elapsed-frame fraction AnimThread_ReadRootScaled already ramps root motion by. Writes into the shape instance's per-node local array (shapeInst+0x12, stride 0xc, indexed by transform id) and sets that node's dirty byte in shapeInst+0xe. Columns whose part id is 0 are skipped entirely, so transform 0 keeps its default and never takes an animated pose. Thread field offsets confirmed here: +4 sequence, +6 frame, +8 nextSequence, +10 nextFrame, +0x1c frameAccumulator, +0x1e frameDuration.

entries.name: Assert_Ctor
entries.description: (assert): Assert_Emit(0, 1, 0, 0, 0), counts the object live and returns it. The static initialiser 00479c40 builds the assert logger 006c574c with it. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's Assert_Ctor (0044de50).

entries.name: Assert_Dtor
entries.description: The assert logger's destructor, the dtor its class record (RTTI 'Assert', 1 byte, at 00479c80) names: (logger, flags) decrements *Rtl_DtorCountPtr, Assert_Emit(1, 1, 0, 0, null), then Mem_Delete when flags bit 0 is set. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's Assert_Dtor (0044de78), whose description covers the Assert_Emit call.

entries.name: Assert_RunHooks
entries.description: Calls each hook on the list at 006c575c with the severity. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's Assert_RunHooks.

entries.name: Assert_Report
entries.description: The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's Assert_Report: (logger, severity, condition, file, line, message). Severities 4-6 run the hooks (Assert_RunHooks), emit (Assert_Emit), call Assert_Emit again with severity 1 (which has no case and prints nothing), call 00464fc8 and MainWindow_KillTimer, PostQuitMessage(0) and _exit(1); lower severities only emit.

entries.name: Assert_AddHook
entries.description: Pushes a callback onto the assert hook list at 006c575c; aborts with an assert_abort_notify message if the allocation fails. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's Assert_AddHook.

entries.name: maybe_Assert_GetCheckCount
entries.description: Frameless getter: MOV EAX,[006c5750]; RET -- the dword at g_AssertLogger+4. VSHELL has the same getter at the same place after Assert_AddHook (0044df84), reading its Assert_CheckCount (g_AssertLogger+4). No reference found by es2_xref.

entries.name: maybe_Assert_GetBreakRequested
entries.description: Frameless getter: MOV EAX,[006c5754]; RET -- the dword at g_AssertLogger+8. VSHELL has the same getter after Assert_AddHook (0044df8c), reading its maybe_Assert_BreakRequested (g_AssertLogger+8). No reference found by es2_xref.

entries.name: Assert_StaticInit
entries.description: Static initialiser (Borland _INIT_ entry 004a7bca, priority 0x20): Assert_Ctor(g_AssertLogger 006c574c) inside an exception frame. Assert_StaticDtor is its _EXIT_ counterpart. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's Assert_StaticInit (0044df94); es2_naming diff differs in the logger's label alone.

entries.name: Assert_StaticDtor
entries.description: Assert_StaticInit's _EXIT_ routine (Borland _EXIT_ entry 004a7c72): Assert_Dtor(g_AssertLogger 006c574c, 2).

entries.name: Assert_Format
entries.description: (buffer, severity, file, line, message): formats 'Assert::<severity name>: Line <line> in "<file>"' with the severity-name table at 004a160c, then appends ': <message>' when there is one. Assert_Emit builds its line with it.

entries.name: Assert_SetLogDir
entries.description: (dir): copies dir into 006c5760, the directory Assert_LogPath puts in front of the log name, and returns that buffer. Sim_Run calls it with 004d2840.

entries.name: Assert_LogPath
entries.description: Builds the assert log's path in 006c5860: the directory string at 006c5760 followed by the log name. Returns it. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's Assert_LogPath.

entries.name: Assert_AppendToLog
entries.description: (text): opens Assert_LogPath() with _open(0x901, 0x180) = O_WRONLY|O_CREAT|O_APPEND, aborting on failure; while 004a1628 is set it first writes an 80-byte line of dashes and clears the flag; then writes the text and CR LF and closes. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's Assert_AppendToLog.

entries.name: Assert_Emit
entries.description: Formats and outputs one assert by severity (the DBSIM copy of VSHELL's Assert_Emit): 2 prints the message, 3 counts (006c58b0) and shows the formatted line in a MessageBoxA titled 'Error', 4 prints it and shows the box, 5 prefixes 'Internal Error: Please call Sierra...' and shows the box, 6 prints the break notice. 3-5 call 004668b0 first.

entries.name: ClassItem_RegisterBucket
entries.description: (entries, count): appends an {entries, count} bucket to the registry ClassItem_FindHandler searches (006c58b8, count 004a16a8), unless count is 0. Light_ResetSystem registers g_TSObjectTypeRegistry with it; GL_RegisterClassItems and AN_RegisterClassItems register the tables at GL_ClassItemTable and AN_ClassItemTable.

entries.name: ClassItem_RegisterProbeBucket
entries.description: (entries, count): when count is non-zero, appends {entries, count} to ClassItem_ProbeBuckets (006c5958, count ClassItem_ProbeBucketCount 004a16ac), the bucket list ClassItem_TryEveryLoader walks, after raising ClassItem_ProbeHeaderSize (004a16b0) over the 12-byte {id, loadFn, headerSize} entries: for i = count-1 down to 0 it compares the dword at entries + i*12 - 4 (the previous entry's +8, and for i = 0 the dword before the table) with the running value (unsigned) and, when larger, stores entry i's +8. No caller found by es2_xref. VSHELL's 00403bc6 is the same routine compiled differently.
entries.source: DBSIM decompile and disassembly at 00479fdc; es2_naming diff with VSHELL 00403bc6

entries.name: ClassItem_LoadResource
entries.description: Generic polymorphic resource loader entry point (stream, mode). Reads an 8-byte type tag via ClassItem_ReadTypeTag, looks up a handler via ClassItem_FindHandler, calls its loadFn.

entries.name: ClassItem_StoreItem
entries.description: (item, stream, mode): writes one class item. Points ClassItem_CurrentFrame at a frame on its stack (restoring the previous one on exit). When the item's stream size (its vtable +4) is 0 and the stream's GetCapabilities(3) (vtable +0xc) returns 0, wraps the stream in a local BuffWStream (BuffWStream_CtorOnTarget(local, stream, 0, 0)) and writes through it: ClassItem_OpenItemForWrite(buffer, item tag from vtable slot 0, size), the item's write slot (vtable +0x10)(item, buffer, mode), ClassItem_CloseItemForWrite(buffer), BuffWStream_Dtor(local, 2). Otherwise runs the same three steps on the stream directly. Callers found by es2_xref: GLBitmapArray_WriteToStream, GLCursor_WriteToStream, TSGroup_WriteToStream, TSPartList_WriteToStream, ANAnimList_WriteToStream, ANShape_WriteToStream. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's ClassItem_StoreItem (00403cad).
entries.source: DBSIM decompile at 0047a0a0; es2_naming diff with VSHELL 00403cad

entries.name: Arena_AllocDup
entries.description: Second emitted copy of Arena_Alloc (0047a1bc), same code: (size, arena) bump-allocates from {base, limit, cursor}, falling back to Mem_NewArray with no arena or no room. The 3Space shape readers call this copy (GridShape_ReadFromStream, TSShape_ReadFromStream, TSPartList_ReadFromStream, ShapeInstance_CtorCellFrames), as VSHELL's shape constructors call its Arena_Alloc (00403dc4).

entries.name: Arena_Alloc
entries.description: Bump-allocates from the {base, limit, cursor} arena it is handed: advances the cursor and returns base + old cursor, with NO zeroing of its own. A null or exhausted arena falls back to Mem_NewArray. Every weapon mount comes from here, out of the arena MechLoadout_ConstructWeaponMounts pushes -- and that arena is calloc'd, so a mount block is zero however it was served.

entries.name: ClassItem_PeekTypeTag
entries.description: (stream, tag[2]): saves the stream position (vtable +4), reads the 8-byte class type tag into tag (-1, 0 beforehand), and when no handler is registered for it (ClassItem_FindHandler) and 004a16ac is set, copies it to 006c59a8 and reads the rest of the header into 006c59b0 (ClassItem_TryEveryLoader). Seeks back to the saved position unless the status is 2 (end of data), then runs 0047a768 on the stream.

entries.name: ClassItem_Skip
entries.description: (stream): reads a class item's 8-byte type tag and seeks past its body, the size in the tag's second dword rounded up to an even length, then runs 0047a768 on the stream. Shape_LoadAllRoots and BaseType_ResolveShape skip items with it.

entries.name: ArenaStack_Push
entries.description: (a, b, c): increments the depth 004a16d8, stores the three dwords in the 12-byte entry at 006c59ec + depth*12 and points the current-arena pointer 006c58b4 at it. Arena_Push calls it.

entries.name: ArenaStack_PushAlloc
entries.description: (size): carves size bytes from the current arena (006c58b4) with Arena_AllocDup, increments the depth 004a16d8, stores {block, size, 0} in the 12-byte entry at 006c59ec + depth*12, points 006c58b4 at it and returns block -- a sub-arena pushed inside the current one. ArenaStack_Pop undoes the push. No caller found by es2_xref.

entries.name: ArenaStack_Pop
entries.description: Decrements the depth 004a16d8 and points 006c58b4 back at the entry below. Arena_Pop calls it.

entries.name: ClassItem_FindHandler
entries.description: Searches a registry of (idArray, count) bucket pairs for a matching type tag, returns a 12-byte {id, loadFn, extra} descriptor.

entries.name: ClassItem_TryEveryLoader
entries.description: (stream, tag): walks the 004a16ac registry buckets at 006c5958 ({entries, count}) and calls each 12-byte {id, loadFn, extra} entry's loadFn with (006c59a8, tag, stream), returning 1 at the first that returns nonzero and 0 when none does. ClassItem_PeekTypeTag and ClassItem_ReadTypeTag fall back to it for a tag no handler is registered for.

entries.name: ClassItem_TagTotalSize
entries.description: (tag): an item's total length from its 8-byte class type tag: the size dword at +4 as it is when the high nibble of byte 3 is set, else size + 8 (the tag itself) rounded up to an even length. WeaponModels_LoadShapeChunks steps through chunks with it.

entries.name: ClassItem_ItemTotalSize
entries.description: (item): the bytes the item occupies in a stream with its 8-byte type tag: builds {tag = vtable slot 0, size = vtable slot +4} and returns ClassItem_TagTotalSize of it, or 0 when the item's stream size is 0. Callers found by es2_naming.py callers: the GetStreamSize methods of GLBitmapArray, GLCursor, TSGroup, TSPartList, ANAnimList and ANShape. Identical to VSHELL's ClassItem_ItemTotalSize (004040e9) after normalisation.

entries.name: ClassItem_DebugPrintType
entries.description: The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's VshellClassItem_DebugPrintType (00404120).
entries.source: es2_naming.py diff DBSIM 0047a488 VSHELL 00404120: differs only in callee labels and decompiler typing; RTTI GLRegion vtable slot

entries.name: ClassItem_OpenItemForWrite
entries.description: (stream, typeId, size): fills the frame at ClassItem_CurrentFrame for writing: typeId at +0, the stream position (vtable +4) at +4, that position plus ClassItem_TagTotalSize({typeId, size}) as the end at +8, and the byte +0xc set when size is even. Unless the high nibble of the tag's byte 3 is set, writes the 8-byte tag {typeId, size} through the stream's write slot (vtable +0x14). ClassItem_StoreItem calls it twice. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's ClassItem_OpenItemForWrite (00404208).
entries.source: DBSIM decompile at 0047a52c; es2_naming diff with VSHELL 00404208

entries.name: ClassItem_ReadTypeTag
entries.description: Reads the 8-byte type tag from a resource stream, called by ClassItem_LoadResource.

entries.name: ClassItem_CloseItemForWrite
entries.description: (stream): closes the frame at ClassItem_CurrentFrame after writing, unless the high nibble of the tag's byte 3 is set. For a frame opened with size 0 (end - start == 8) it measures the body written (position less end), adds it to the end, writes a 0 pad byte (Stream_WriteByte2) and bumps the end when that length is odd, seeks (vtable +8) to start + 4, writes the unpadded length with Stream_WriteDword and seeks back to the end. Otherwise writes a 0 pad byte when +0xc (even size) is clear. ClassItem_StoreItem calls it twice. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's ClassItem_CloseItemForWrite (00404392) without its assert and its overrun check.
entries.source: DBSIM decompile and disassembly at 0047a68c; es2_naming diff with VSHELL 00404392

entries.name: ClassItem_CloseItem
entries.description: (stream): reads one byte at a time with Stream_ReadByte until the stream position (vtable +4) reaches the end offset (+8) of the item frame ClassItem_CurrentFrame points at, or the stream status goes non-zero. ClassItem_LoadResource runs it after the item's loader, so an item whose loader read short still leaves the stream at its end. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's ClassItem_CloseItem (ClassItem::closeItem) without its assert and overrun report.

entries.name: Stream_GetStatus_Thunk
entries.description: Forwarder to Stream_GetStatus. ClassItem_PeekTypeTag and ClassItem_Skip end with it.

entries.name: Stream_BaseCtor
entries.description: StreamIO constructor (vtable 004a1700): installs the vtable and clears the status word at +4. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's Stream_BaseCtor.

entries.name: Stream_BaseDtor
entries.description: StreamIO destructor: restores vtable 004a1700, calls its close slot (+0x10), frees with Mem_Delete when flag & 1. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's Stream_BaseDtor.

Callers found by es2_xref: BuffWStream_Ctor, BuffWStream_CtorOnTarget. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's BuffWStream_InitBuffer (0044fcb8), identical after normalisation.

entries.name: BuffRStream_Ctor
entries.description: BuffRStream constructor (vtable 004a1af0, RTTI name 'BuffRStream', 0x21 bytes): (this, source, size, buffer) Stream_BaseCtor, installs the vtable, BuffRStream_InitBuffer(this, size, buffer) and BuffRStream_SetSource(this, source). The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's BuffRStream_Ctor.

entries.name: BuffRStream_InitBuffer
entries.description: (stream, size, buffer): clears +8, +0x10, +0x19 and +0x1d, stores size at +0xc, whether buffer is null at +0x18 (the stream owns it) and the buffer at +0x14, Mem_HeapAlloc(size) when none was passed. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's BuffRStream_InitBuffer.

entries.name: BuffRStream_SetSource

entries.name: BuffRStream_ReleaseSource
entries.description: (stream): when a source is attached (+8): calls the stream's own vtable +0x10, seeks the source (its vtable +8) to the position recorded at attach (+0x10) plus +0x1d, clears +8 and sets status 6. BuffRStream_SetSource runs it before attaching a different source. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's BuffRStream_ReleaseSource.

entries.name: BuffRStream_FillAt
entries.description: (stream, pos): seeks the source (+8, its vtable +8) to pos, returning BuffRStream_SyncStatus when the seek fails; reads a buffer's worth (+0xc) into the buffer +0x14 with Stream_ReadCopy3. A full read sets the filled count +0x19 to +0xc. A failed read with the source at end of data (status 2) keeps what came (source position less pos) as +0x19, or, when that is 0, sets status 2, clears +0x19 and returns 0; any other failure returns BuffRStream_SyncStatus. On success stores pos at +0x10, clears the cursor +0x1d and returns 1. Callers found by es2_xref: BuffRStream_SetPosition, BuffRStream_Read. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's BuffRStream_FillAt (004502bc).
entries.source: DBSIM decompile and disassembly at 0047c7b8; es2_naming diff with VSHELL 004502bc

entries.name: BuffRStream_SyncStatus
entries.description: (stream): sets the status word +4 to 6 (no source attached) when the source +8 is null, else to the source's Stream_GetStatus. Returns 0. BuffRStream_SetSource ends with it. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's BuffRStream_SyncStatus.

entries.name: Stream_ReadCopy3

entries.name: Volume_Ctor
entries.description: (volume): zeroes +0, +4, +0x24, +0x28 and +0x2c of the 0x30-byte volume. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's Volume_Ctor.

entries.name: Volume_Dtor
entries.description: (volume, flags): frees the arrays at +0x24, +0x28 and +0x2c, destroys the streams at +4 and +0 through their own destructors (flag 3), and frees the volume when flags bit 0 is set. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's Volume_Dtor.

entries.name: Volume_LoadVolume
entries.description: (path, mask, bufferSize): the DBSIM copy of VSHELL's Volume_LoadVolume without its asserts and without the revision check: it reads the revision byte after the 'VOL' signature and ignores it. Opens path as a FileRStream, checks the signature, reads the flags dword and returns null unless it shares a bit with mask; otherwise wraps the file in a BuffRStream of max(bufferSize, 0x80) bytes and builds the 0x30-byte volume (Volume_Ctor): file stream +0, buffered stream +4, name +8, header byte +0x1c, flags +0x20, directory names +0x24/+0x28 (count +0x1d) and 0x12-byte entries +0x2c (count +0x1e). Returns null after Volume_Dtor when the stream fails.
entries.source: DBSIM decompile and disassembly at 0047c9a4 (no compare after the 0047cf3a read at 0047cacd)

entries.name: Volume_FindEntry
entries.description: (volume, path, entryInfo): the DBSIM copy of VSHELL's Volume_FindEntry (0040279f), line for line: splits the path with Path_Split, matches the directory (+0x1d count, +0x24 names) and then the name and directory index against the 18-byte entries (+0x1e count, +0x2c table) case-insensitively, and on a hit seeks the volume's stream (+4) to the entry, reads its 9-byte prefix and fills entryInfo ([0] stream, [2] and [4] data offset, [5] compression type, [6] size). Returns 1 on a hit, 0 otherwise. VolumeGroup_FindEntry calls it per volume.
entries.source: DBSIM decompile at 0047ccec, diffed against VSHELL 0040279f

entries.name: Stream_ReadBytes
entries.description: (stream, count, dst): reads count bytes through the stream's read slot (vtable +0x18). Volume_LoadVolume reads the 3-byte signature with it; Stream_ReadBytes2 and Stream_ReadBytes3 are copies with the same body.

entries.name: Stream_ReadBytes2
entries.description: (stream, count, dst): reads count bytes through the stream's read slot (vtable +0x18); a second copy of Stream_ReadBytes. Volume_LoadVolume reads the revision byte with it.

entries.name: Stream_ReadDword
entries.description: (stream, dst): reads 4 bytes through the stream's read slot (vtable +0x18). Volume_LoadVolume reads the flags dword with it.

entries.name: Stream_ReadByte2

entries.name: Stream_ReadWord3
entries.description: (stream, dst): reads 2 bytes through the stream's read slot (vtable +0x18); a third copy of Stream_ReadWord.

entries.name: Stream_ReadBytes3
entries.description: (stream, count, dst): reads count bytes through the stream's read slot (vtable +0x18); a third copy of Stream_ReadBytes. Volume_LoadVolume reads the directory-name block with it.

entries.name: Stream_ReadDword2
entries.description: (stream, dst): reads 4 bytes through the stream's read slot (vtable +0x18); a second copy of Stream_ReadDword.

entries.name: Str_TrimLeft
entries.description: (s): skips the leading characters whose signed value is below 0x21 (control characters and space, and bytes 0x80-0xff, which MOVSX makes negative), stopping at the NUL, copies the rest down to s, terminates it and returns s. Str_TrimRight's counterpart beside it. No caller found by es2_xref.

entries.name: Str_TrimRight
entries.description: (s): cuts s after its last character above a space (code > 0x20), dropping trailing blanks and control characters; returns s. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's Str_TrimRight (00450428).

entries.name: Str_Concat4
entries.description: (a, b, c, d, out): concatenates the non-null strings a to d into out, or into the static buffer 006c5e2f when out is null, and returns it. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's Str_Concat4.

entries.name: Math_Atan2Bam
entries.description: atan2 in binary angles, arguments (x, y): 0 is +x and +y is a quarter turn, so in screen space 0 is right and a quarter turn is down. Octant-folded through the correction table at 004a1c4c. Answers 0 for (0, 0), and for any y of 0 with x positive. The result is masked to 14 bits and shifted left 2.

Callers found by es2_xref: Point3S_ExactDistanceBetween (0047d494), Point3S_DistanceBetween (0047d4d4) and Point3S_ChebyshevDistanceBetween (0047d514), each on a local copy of its first argument before Point3S_ExactMagnitude, Point3S_Magnitude and Point3S_ChebyshevMagnitude respectively.

entries.name: Point3I_ChebyshevMagnitude
