entries.name: Anim_BlendKeyframeTransforms
entries.description: Blends two 12-byte ANAnimList transform records (3 euler shorts then 3 translation shorts) by a Q10 factor (0x400 == fully the second). Rotation components take the SHORTEST ARC: the difference is biased by 0x10000 when it would go negative, subtracted, then folded back by 0x10000 when it exceeds 0x7fff -- the shortest signed 16-bit difference -- before the Q10 multiply and arithmetic >>10. Translation components are a plain truncating lerp on the 16-bit difference. All fixed point; no float anywhere.

entries.name: Math_NormalizeVec3ToLength
entries.description: Rescales an int Vec3 in place to the requested length and returns it. Zeroes all three when the magnitude is zero; otherwise scales each by Math_Q16Divide(length << 16, magnitude) NARROWED TO A SIGNED 16-BIT VALUE before the multiply, so a step over a short delta comes out shorter than asked for. Distinct from Math_NormalizeVec3ShortToLength (0046c138), which is the three-short form and halves until the magnitude fits first.

entries.name: Math_DivModShort
entries.description: (value int32, divisor int16): returns the int16 quotient value / divisor in the low word and the int16 remainder value % divisor in the high word of EAX (two IDIVs by the sign-extended divisor). No caller found by es2_xref.

entries.name: Math_DistanceBetweenPoints
entries.description: Distance between two int Vec3s: copies a to a stack temp, subtracts b, and returns Point3I_Magnitude -- the Vec3 form of Math_FastMagnitude3D -- so it carries that function's direction-dependent error (about 8% low to 8.7% high). The MFD TARGET range readout and BeamTracer_Ctor's chain node count both go through it.

entries.name: Math_GroundDistanceBetweenPoints
entries.description: Ground-plane distance between two int Vec3s: Vec2_Subtract then Vec2_Magnitude, returned in EAX, Z dropped entirely. Every range an AI steering decision is made on is this; the 3D Math_DistanceBetweenPoints gates only obstacle avoidance's machine sweep and following's standoff -- a waypoint on a hilltop is as near as one at its foot.

entries.name: Math_Atan2Guarded
entries.description: atan2 as a BAM angle, with the degenerate pair nudged onto an axis. ARGUMENT ORDER IS (x, y), NOT (y, x): it forwards to Math_Atan2Bam_Thunk(p1, p2) and sets p1 -- the X -- to 1 when both are zero. Both Math_HeadingToward and Math_EulerToward call it as (dx, dy). Getting this backwards mirrors a bearing about the 45-degree line and turns an elevation into a polar angle from +Z.

entries.name: Math_HeadingToward
entries.description: Ground-plane bearing from one position to another as a BAM angle: atan2(to.y - from.y, to.x - from.x) via Math_Atan2Guarded, minus a quarter turn, because the sim's forward axis is model Y and not model X. Call sites pass the destination first. DBSim_SpawnMissionObjects uses it to face a group along the first leg of its route when the group's block-11 record carries no heading ref.

entries.name: Math_ElevationAngle
entries.description: (a, b): Math_Atan2Guarded(Math_FastMagnitude2D_Thunk(a.x - b.x, a.y - b.y), a.z - b.z) on int32 triples, returned in AX. Flyer_AttackRun passes its aim point and the flyer's position (+0x26) and feeds the result to Flyer_PitchCommand.

entries.name: Math_EulerToward
entries.description: Math_EulerToward(out, from, to), d = from - to: euler[2] = Math_Atan2Guarded(dx, dy) - 0x4000, euler[1] = 0, euler[0] = Math_Atan2Guarded(Math_FastMagnitude2D(dx, dy), dz). Math_Atan2Guarded takes (x, y), so euler[2] is the ground bearing and euler[0] is an ELEVATION above the horizon, not a polar angle from +Z. The quarter-turn subtraction is because the simulation's forward axis is model Y. Same helper and same argument order as Math_HeadingToward.

entries.name: Math_OffsetPointByBearing
entries.description: (point, bearing, distance): offsets an int Vec3's x and y by distance along a BAM bearing, the bearing quarter-turned back because the sim's forward axis is model Y, adding Math_ScaleByCos(distance, bearing + 0x4000) to x and Math_ScaleBySin(distance, bearing + 0x4000) to y and returning the point; z is left alone. The offset is 16-bit: both helpers take the distance's low word and return a sign-extended int16, so a distance past +/-32767 wraps. GroundVehicle_DriveToPoint depends on the wrap.

entries.name: Vec2_Subtract
entries.description: In-place 2D vector subtract: a->x -= b->x, a->y -= b->y. Confirms the HUD's waypoint/contact distances are ground-plane distances, Z ignored.

entries.name: Vec2_Magnitude
entries.description: Thin wrapper: Math_FastMagnitude2D(v->x, v->y) via Math_FastMagnitude2D_Thunk.

entries.name: Vec3_Subtract
entries.description: (a, b): subtracts b from a in place, z first and then x and y through Vec2_Subtract; returns a.

entries.name: Point3I_Magnitude
entries.description: Returns Math_FastMagnitude3D of an int32 point's three components (through Math_FastMagnitude3D_Thunk; the decompile drops the return value).

entries.name: Math_FastMagnitude2D_Thunk
entries.description: Forwards (dx, dy) to Math_FastMagnitude2D and returns its result. Vec2_Magnitude and Math_EulerToward call it.

entries.name: Math_FastMagnitude3D_Thunk
entries.description: One-line forwarder to Math_FastMagnitude3D(x, y, z).

entries.name: Math_Atan2Bam_Thunk
entries.description: One-line forwarder to Math_Atan2Bam with the same arguments. Math_Atan2Guarded calls it.

entries.name: Math_CosBam_Thunk
entries.description: (angle): Math_CosBam(angle), returned in AX.

entries.name: Math_Q14Multiply_Thunk
entries.description: (a, b): Math_Q14Multiply on int16 arguments -- a sign-extended from its low word (MOVSX EDX,word ptr), b passed as AX -- returning Math_Q14Multiply's EAX.

entries.name: Math_DivInt
entries.description: (a, b): a / b, signed. Math_NormalizeVec3ToLength calls it.

entries.name: Math_ScaleByCos
entries.description: (length, angle): Math_Q14Multiply_Thunk(length, Math_CosBam_Thunk(angle)) as a sign-extended int16 (MOVSX EAX,AX). The length is passed on as the low word of EDX, so only its low 16 bits count. Math_OffsetPointByBearing calls it.

entries.name: Math_ScaleBySin
entries.description: (length, angle): Math_Q14Multiply_Thunk(length, Math_SinBam(angle)) as a sign-extended int16 (MOVSX EAX,AX). The length is passed on as the low word of EDX, so only its low 16 bits count. Math_OffsetPointByBearing calls it.

entries.name: Math_SinBam
entries.description: (angle): Math_CosBam(angle - 0x4000), i.e. the sine in Q14, returned in AX.

entries.name: Str_ReplaceFirst
entries.description: (s, find, replace): replaces the first occurrence of the character find in s with replace (strchr) and returns s.

entries.name: Path_WithExtension
entries.description: (path, extension): copies path into the static buffer 006cbc90, cuts it at the first '.' (Str_ReplaceFirst), then appends '.' and the extension.

entries.name: ResourcePath_BuildFolderName
entries.description: The shared folder\name resource-path builder: ResourcePath_BuildFolderName(name, folder) writes 'folder\\name' into a shared static buffer (&DAT_006cbcae) via Path_WithExtension(name) + strcat('\\') + strcat(folder). Confirmed by tracing its two operands against known-good results (e.g. ResourcePath_BuildFolderName(hercName, "vue") and the folder-name pointer table at CockpitDpl_ResourceFolderNames).

entries.name: NameList_Split
entries.description: (buffer, out): walks the NUL-terminated names in buffer until one starts with a '\n' byte, storing each name's address in out when out is non-null, and returns the count (EAX = EDI; the decompile drops it). LoadNameList splits the .NAM file with it.

entries.name: VolFile_GetSize
entries.description: (path): opens path as a VolRStream (loose file or volume entry) and returns VolRStream_GetSize, or 0 when the open fails. LoadNameList sizes the .NAM file with it.

entries.name: LoadNameList
entries.description: Loads a nam\<name>.NAM list -- a flat run of NUL-terminated ASCII names indexed by type number -- with a capacity bound as the second argument. Called with ('mechs', 0x55) into the mech name table DAT_004a9de4 that MechType_InitOne indexes, and with ('flyers', 0x22) into DAT_004a9e74. These are the tables that turn script.dat block 7's and block 8's type numbers into resource base names; MECHS.NAM ships 21 names and FLYERS.NAM 3.

entries.name: maybe_Math_RandomNoOp
entries.description: Empty body (PUSH EBP / MOV EBP,ESP / POP EBP / RET). It sits between LoadNameList and Math_RandomSeed, whose module ends with the same empty bodies Math_RandomSeedNoOp and Math_RandomSeedAndSkipNoOp. No caller found by es2_xref.

entries.name: Math_RandomSeed
entries.description: Seeds one Math_RandomNext state block: the cursors at +0x70/+0x71 to the literals 0x18 and 0x37, then a memmove of 112 bytes (56 int16) from the static table at 004a6958. The function it calls afterwards, 00492e3c, is an empty stub -- no clock and no entropy reaches the generator. Called for both 0x4d261d and 0x4d268f from Main_StaticInit (0045cad8), and by Math_RandomSeedAndSkip.

entries.name: Math_RandomSeedAndSkip
entries.description: (state, count). Seeds the given generator block with Math_RandomSeed, calls the empty stub 00492e41, then draws and discards count values with Math_RandomNext; count is a signed 16-bit value, so a count of zero or less discards none. es2_xref.py finds no reference to it anywhere in the image. See docs/retail/simulation/random-generator.md.

entries.name: Math_RandomNext
entries.description: The game's pseudo-random generator: an additive lagged Fibonacci generator over a 56-entry (0x38) table of shorts with two rotating byte cursors at state+0x70 and state+0x71. Each call does table[i] += table[j]; returns the new table[i] in the low 16 bits; then advances both cursors modulo 56. Callers pass the state block address (0x4d261d) and mask the result -- & 0xfff for the terrain material roll in TerrainZone_PopulateFromBitmap and for the explosion's ~51% per-component roll in Mech_ApplyExplosiveDamage. Seeded only by Math_RandomSeed (00492d7c), from a static table; there is no entropy input anywhere, so DBSIM's simulation replays identically on every run.

entries.name: Math_RandomBelow
entries.description: A draw in [0, bound): (Math_RandomNext() & 0x7fff) % bound. The mask drops the sign bit rather than taking an absolute value, so the distribution is the low fifteen bits'. Used by Component_SpillIntoDependents' weighted pick.

entries.name: Math_RandomSeedNoOp
entries.description: Empty body. Math_RandomSeed's last call.

entries.name: Math_RandomSeedAndSkipNoOp
entries.description: Empty body. Math_RandomSeedAndSkip calls it after Math_RandomSeed, before the discarded draws.

entries.name: Ovl_ReadFile
entries.description: (dst, size, count, path): opens path with VolRStream_CtorFromPath, asserting (OVL.CPP line 0x15) on a bad stream status, reads size * count bytes into dst with VolRStream_Read, asserting (line 0x17) when that fails, and closes it. MechType_InitOne reads the 0xd8-byte type record and the 0x36-byte block with it; FlyerType_LoadResources its 0x2e-byte stats.

entries.name: Stream_GetStatus
entries.description: Returns a stream's status word at +4. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's Stream_GetStatus.

entries.description: The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's Poly_ScanConvertEitherWinding (00465d39), byte-identical; see that entry.

entries.name: ViewFrustum_DefaultCtor
entries.description: (frustum): ViewFrustum_Ctor without its far and margin arguments: maybe_Point3I_Ctor on the position at +0xc, Rtl_VectorNew of the six 0x10-byte planes from +0x18 (Plane_Ctor), then 0 at +0 (margin) and +4 (far) and -1 at +8 (every plane enabled); returns frustum. No caller found by es2_xref.

entries.name: ViewFrustum_Ctor
entries.description: (frustum, far, margin): constructs the position at +0xc and the six 0x10-byte planes from +0x18 (Plane_Ctor), stores far at +4, margin at +0 and -1 (every plane enabled) at +8. Terrain_SetupVisibleRegion builds one with far = grid+0x10c << cellShift and margin = 1.5 cells.

entries.name: ViewFrustum_Build
entries.description: (frustum, view, far, margin): the six planes of the view's frustum, each built in view axes (across, depth, up), rotated by the view's euler matrix and handed to Plane_FromPointNormal. With F = far, M = margin, s = the view's perspective shift (+0x1a), and from the render context (+0x16) the rect +0x210..+0x21c (w, h) and the pair +0x220/+0x224 (-cx, -cy): near (+0x18) through (0,-M,0), normal (0,F,0); far (+0x28) through (0,F,0), normal -(0,F,0); top (+0x38) through (0,0,M), normal (0, cy*F>>s, -F); bottom (+0x48) through -(0,0,M), normal (0,(h-cy)*F>>s, F); left (+0x58) through -(M,0,0), normal (F, cx*F>>s, 0); right (+0x68) through (M,0,0), normal (-F,(w-cx)*F>>s, 0). The position (+0xc) is the view's.

entries.name: ViewFrustum_ClipPolygon
entries.description: (frustum, poly, out) -> bool: ViewFrustum_ClipGroundPolygon without the Z shift, with the planes as built.

entries.name: ViewFrustum_ClipGroundPolygon
entries.description: (frustum, poly, lowZ, highZ, out) -> bool: copies the six planes, shifting each non-vertical one (Plane_IsVertical) along Z by lowZ when its Z component is <= 0 and by -highZ when positive (Plane_ShiftAlongZ); moves poly to the eye (Poly3_SubtractOffset), cuts it with Poly_SplitByPlane keeping the front against the enabled planes in the order left, right, top, bottom, far, near, and moves the result back (Poly3_AddOffset). Returns whether any points are left. Terrain_SetupVisibleRegion clips the draw square with it, passing grid+0x110 and grid+0x114.

entries.name: Poly3_SubtractOffset
entries.description: (in, offset, out): out = in with offset subtracted from each int32 {x, y, z} point; count copied.

entries.name: Poly3_AddOffset
entries.description: (in, offset, out): out = in with offset added to each int32 {x, y, z} point; count copied.

entries.name: Transform_Ctor
entries.description: Constructs a transform: Transform_CtorRotation on it (which returns its argument) and maybe_Point3I_Ctor on its translation at +0x14. Returns it.

entries.name: Rtl_ReturnArgCopy2
entries.description: Returns its argument unchanged (MOV EAX,[EBP+8]; the decompile drops it) -- a third copy of Rtl_ReturnArg. Transform_Ctor and Bitmap_BlitRotatedScaled call it.

entries.name: View_GetPosition
entries.description: (view) -> view + 4, the view's int32 position.

entries.name: View_GetPerspectiveShift
entries.description: (view) -> the dword at view + 0x1a, the perspective shift.

entries.name: View_GetRenderContext
entries.description: (view) -> the dword at view + 0x16, the view's render context.

entries.name: View_BuildTransform
entries.description: (view, out): Transform_SetEulerAndTranslation(out, view + 0x10, view + 4).

entries.name: Transform_CtorRotation
entries.description: (transform): returns Rtl_ReturnArgCopy2(transform), its argument; constructs nothing. Transform_Ctor runs it on the transform before constructing the translation at +0x14.

entries.name: Transform_SetEulerAndTranslation
entries.description: (out, euler, position): writes position into the transform's translation (+0x14..+0x1c) and builds the rotation from the euler triple with BuildEulerRotationMatrixQ14.

entries.name: Point3I_Negate
entries.description: (p): negates Z, then X and Y through Point3I_NegateXY.

entries.name: BuildEulerRotationMatrixQ14_Thunk
entries.description: (matrix, euler): BuildEulerRotationMatrixQ14(euler, matrix), the arguments exchanged.

entries.name: Point3I_NegateXY
entries.description: (p): negates X and Y.

entries.name: Plane_Ctor
entries.description: maybe_Point3I_Ctor on the plane's normal, which it starts with; returns it. ViewFrustum_Ctor and ViewFrustum_ClipGroundPolygon build their six planes with it.

entries.name: Dword_Swap
entries.description: (a, b): exchanges the dwords at a and b. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's Dword_Swap; every direct caller swaps the in and out point-list pointers after a Poly_SplitByPlane pass.

entries.name: Plane_IsVertical
entries.description: (plane) -> 1 when the normal's Z is 0 and X, Y are not both 0; 0 otherwise.

entries.name: Plane_ShiftAlongZ
entries.description: (plane, v): plane.d -= v * plane.nz.

entries.name: HeightOffsetTable_Ctor
entries.description: VectorTable constructor (vtables ClassItem 004a6a08, TSBase 004a6a2c, then VectorTable 004a6a58; RTTI name 'VectorTable', 0x1c bytes): (table, count) stores count at +0xc, base 0 at +8 and step 100 at +4, a count-byte computed-flag array at +0x10, count int32 triples at +0x14 and eight at +0x18. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's HeightOffsetTable_Ctor; HeightGrid_Constructor's table at +0xd0.
entries.source: DBSIM decompile at 0049515c; RTTI at vtable-0xc

entries.name: HeightOffsetTable_SetScale
entries.description: (table, base, step): stores base at table+8 and step at table+4. TerrainZone_LoadHeightmap, TerrainZone_PopulateFromBitmap and Terrain_SetupVisibleRegion call it on HeightGrid+0xd0 with the grid's height base (+0x110) and height scale (+0x118).

entries.name: HeightOffsetTable_Reset
entries.description: (table): memsets the per-height computed flags (table+0x10, length table+0xc) to 0 and writes the view-space image of the up vector (0, 0, 0x10000) under g_ModelToView into the vector table+0x18 points at, via Transform_RotatePoint_Thunk. Called on HeightGrid+0xd0 after each HeightOffsetTable_SetScale.

entries.name: HeightOffsetTable_Get
entries.description: (table, rawHeight): returns the 12-byte view-space offset of a raw height byte at table+0x14 + rawHeight*12. Filled on first use after HeightOffsetTable_Reset (flag byte table+0x10[rawHeight]): each component of the up vector at *(table+0x18) times rawHeight*step(+4) + base(+8), through Math_Q16Multiply. entries.name: Eh_InitExceptBlock
entries.description: Borland C++ exception-frame prologue, the DBSIM copy of VSHELL's Eh_InitExceptBlock (0046b234): builds the frame's registration record (handler 0049672c, the frame descriptor passed in EAX, the live-destructor count from [006cbf74]) and links it into the FS:[0] SEH chain. Functions that construct objects with destructors call it first, which is why it has 258 call sites.

entries.name: Rtl_DefaultTerminate
entries.description: The RTL's default terminate handler, which Rtl_ExceptInit stores at +8 of the exception block: calls _abort (004967c8) and returns.

entries.name: Rtl_SetTerminate
entries.description: Borland RTL set_terminate: (handler): returns the terminate handler at +8 of the thread's exception block (FS:[4] - 8) and stores handler there when it is not null. es2_xref finds no reference to it. Byte-identical to VSHELL's 0046b27a.

entries.name: Rtl_Terminate
entries.description: Borland RTL terminate: _flushall, calls the exception block's terminate handler (+8), then _abort. Byte-identical to VSHELL's 0046b29f.

entries.name: Rtl_DefaultUnexpected
entries.description: The RTL's default unexpected handler, which Rtl_ExceptInit stores at +0xc of the exception block: calls Rtl_Terminate.

entries.name: Rtl_SetUnexpected
entries.description: Borland RTL set_unexpected: (handler): returns the unexpected handler at +0xc of the thread's exception block (FS:[4] - 8) and stores handler there when it is not null. es2_xref finds no reference to it. Byte-identical to VSHELL's 0046b2f5.

entries.name: Rtl_GetPolymorphicDtorCount
entries.description: Borland RTL helper, the DBSIM copy of VSHELL's Rtl_GetPolymorphicDtorCount: (object, vptrOffset) returns the destructor count in the dynamic type's typeinfo (+0x20), found through vptr[-4] and the typeinfo pointer at vptr-0xc; 0 for a null object. Every polymorphic delete adds it to [006cbf74] before calling the virtual destructor with flag 3.

entries.name: Rtl_ExceptInit
entries.description: Borland RTL exception setup: (block): with block null, takes the exception-DLL info from the module's own __GetExceptDLLinfo export when 00497058 is set and the magic lies in 0x82727349-0x82727359, else from Rtl_GetExceptDllInfoInternal; with a block, points its +8 and +0xc at the RTL's default handlers 00496288 and 00496303. Stores the block at FS:[4] - 8, clears FS:[4] - 4 and the block's +4, and for a null block sets Rtl_DtorCountPtr to FS:[4] - 4. Byte-identical to VSHELL's Rtl_ExceptInit (0046b34d).

entries.name: Rtl_GetExceptDllInfoInternal
entries.description: Borland RTL: (info): stores (the thread's exception block at FS:[4] - 8) + 0x24 at 004a7924 and fills info with the magic 0x82727349 and the address 004a7908. Rtl_ExceptInit calls it. Byte-identical to VSHELL's Rtl_GetExceptDllInfoInternal (0046b40a).

entries.name: maybe_Rtl_MathErr
entries.description: (e): for e+0 == 4 zeroes the double at +0x18 and returns 1; for 5 returns 1; otherwise 0. The startup data block at the start of DATA stores it at 00497048, beside WinMain's pointer (00497044) and maybe_Rtl_MathErrL's (0049704c). The offsets and type codes are those of Borland's struct _exception {type, name, arg1, arg2, retval} with UNDERFLOW 4 and TLOSS 5, read as the RTL's default _matherr. Byte-identical after normalisation to VSHELL's 0046b438.

entries.name: maybe_Rtl_MathErrL
entries.description: (e): for e+0 == 4 zeroes the 10 bytes at +0x1c..+0x25 and returns 1; for 5 returns 1; otherwise 0. Stored at 0049704c beside maybe_Rtl_MathErr. The offsets are Borland's struct _exceptionl with long double fields (retval at +0x1c), read as the RTL's default _matherrl. Byte-identical after normalisation to VSHELL's 0046b464.

entries.name: Rtl_VectorDelete
entries.description: Borland RTL _vector_delete_ (named by its own error string 'Illegal mode in _vector_delete_' at 004a79fc), the DBSIM copy of VSHELL's Rtl_VectorDelete: (array, elemSize, count, mode, dtor). Takes the count from array[-1] when mode & 0x10, runs dtor(elem, 2) on each element from last to first under the mode & 7 calling convention, then frees the block with Mem_DeleteArray when mode & 8 and returns 0; otherwise returns the block start.

entries.name: Rtl_VectorDeleteCounted
entries.description: (array, dtorLevels, elemSize, count, mode, dtor): returns 0 for a null array; otherwise takes the count from array[-1] when mode & 0x10, adds count * dtorLevels to the live-destructor count at FS:[4] - 4 (the dword Rtl_DtorCountPtr points at), and returns Rtl_VectorDelete(array, elemSize, count, mode, dtor). Mechs_FreeAllTypes passes (DAT_004a9de8, 0x29, 0x21e, 0, 0x19, MECH_TYPE_DATA_Dtor (00420867)).

entries.name: Rtl_VectorNew
entries.description: Borland RTL _vector_new_ (named by its own error string 'Illegal mode in _vector_new_' at 004a7a1c), the DBSIM copy of VSHELL's Rtl_VectorNew: when passed no memory, allocates elemSize*count bytes with Mem_NewArray (plus a 4-byte count prefix when mode bit 0x10 is set), then runs the element constructor once per element at elemSize stride. Worth having named because it appears in the middle of data-structure loaders -- e.g. the HeightGrid cell array allocation in TerrainZone_PopulateFromBitmap -- where it can otherwise be mistaken for domain logic.

entries.name: Rtl_PureVirtualCalled
entries.description: Borland's pure-virtual handler: pushes "Pure virtual function called" (004a7a3c) and calls __ErrorExit (import thunk 004966a8). Fills every abstract slot -- 24 vtables in DBSIM hold it.

entries.name: g_ShapeDetailSizeScaleQ10
entries.description: Q10 factor the projected size is scaled by before the threshold comparison in Shape_DrawAtDetailLevel. Written by ShapeDetail_ApplyHercDetailSetting from g_HercDetailScaleValues, which holds 2000 for all five settings; the image's own initialiser leaves it at Q10 one (1024).

entries.name: g_ShapeDetailBias
entries.description: Shape_DrawAtDetailLevel's starting root index -- the floor on how fine any machine is drawn. Written by ShapeDetail_ApplyHercDetailSetting from g_HercDetailBiasValues {4,3,2,1,0} indexed by the HERC DETAIL preference byte DAT_004d1fc5, so setting 0 is the crudest and 4 the finest. Zero in the image; the runtime value is the load-bearing one.

entries.name: g_BaseDeathStageCount
entries.description: How many stages each of the four structure death sequences runs: 8, 6, 6, 2. The last of five parallel four-entry tables indexed by a BASES.DAT component record's +4; the others are the collapse explosion type (004973fc), the hold after it (00497404), whether that explosion goes off at the object's origin (0049740c), and the smoke explosion type (00497414).

entries.name: Light_PersistentCount
entries.description: Entry count of Light_PersistentList (004a9690).

entries.name: BeamQuadIndexOffsets
entries.description: Four INT16s {1, 0, 1, 2}, the per-corner offsets Beam_LoadResourceTables adds when building BeamQuadIndexTable. Element size is set by the builder's own 'word ptr [ECX*2 + 0x498640]'; read as bytes the quads collapse to a degenerate edge.

entries.name: CollisionTable_Count
entries.description: int16: the number of 6-byte collision model entries CollisionTable_Reserve has handed out.

entries.name: DmgTable_Count
entries.description: int16: the number of 12-byte .DMG component tables DmgTable_Reserve has handed out, one per mech and flyer type.

entries.name: maybe_ComponentDependencyList
entries.description: Dependency list walked by Component_DestroyAndCascade to find and destroy dependent components.

entries.name: MissileAmmoNameTable
entries.description: 4 char* indexed by a PROJ.DAT Missile record's subtype id: SARH, ARH, ARM, EO. Read only by WeaponMount_GetDisplayName, with no bounds check -- MISSL (id 21, subtype 4) reads one past the end.

entries.name: WeaponMountNameTable
entries.description: 33 char* in weapon-id order -- the simulator's own weapon names, walked by Weapons_LoadResourceTables into each WeaponMountTemplate's +0x52. NOT the SHELL0/GAM/WEAPONS.DAT catalog's names: id 7 is 'EMP' here and 'EMPC' there, id 30 'SHIELD' vs 'SHLD'. Ids 13-16 hold bare round counts ('6','8','10','24') because a launcher never prints this name.

entries.name: ElfMountVtable
entries.description: The ELF/ELF2 weapon-mount vtable. MechLoadout_ConstructWeaponMounts's case for weapon ids 6 and 22 runs WeaponMount_CtorEnergy and then overwrites the object's vtable pointer with this, so an ELF is an energy mount with five slots replaced: +0x28 ElfMount_FireDispatch, +0x2c ElfMount_CanFire, +0x30 ElfMount_TriggerHeld, +0x34 ElfMount_SpinUpAndChargeTick, +0x5c WeaponMount_EnergyIsSpent. The charge, power-level, wake, priority and gauge slots are NOT replaced, so an ELF carries and charges an ordinary capacitor and prints an ordinary bar.

entries.name: BehaviourStateTable
entries.description: The 22 AI behaviour state descriptors, 0x3e stride, zero-filled in the image and built at startup as C++ statics from BehaviourSlotBlocks. Descriptor layout: +0x00 name pointer into BehaviourStateNames, +0x04 a dwell time in MILLISECONDS before the state reassesses (50000 for combat states, 10 -- under one tick -- for the rest), +0x08 sixteen one-byte flags expanded from a 16-bit mask by Behaviour_ExpandFlagBits, bit 0 suppressing the dwell countdown, +0x18/+0x24/+0x30 the think/move/reassess triples, +0x3c a short of 0 or 3. 004993a4 + 22*0x3e lands exactly on BehaviourSlotBlocks, which is what fixes the count at 22. States 0/1/2 are 'deciding'/'player'/'player fly', the three Mech_Constructor installs.

entries.name: BehaviourSlotBlocks
entries.description: 22 unmarked 0x24-stride blocks of pointer-to-member-function triples {func, thisDelta, vtableIndex}, the source the AI behaviour state descriptors at BehaviourStateTable are built from at startup. Slot +0x00 is the state's think function, +0x0c its move, +0x18 its reassess; the static initialiser at 00413ed4 copies them to descriptor +0x18/+0x24/+0x30 respectively. 18 of the 22 move slots hold Mech_MovementTick (0041a360) -- those are the 18 states sharing the walk move, not one entry per mech type; 00499928 is block 1's move slot, and the blocks start at 004998f8. Full layout in docs/retail/simulation/ai-dispatch.md.

entries.name: FlyerBehaviourSlots
entries.description: The flyer behaviour class' three pointer-to-member-function triples, each {func, thisDelta, vtableIndex}: +0x00 the slot the dispatcher at 00415b38 reads (0041c194), +0x0c the per-tick move (Razor_MovementTick), +0x18 empty. The walker set is the identically shaped block at 0049991c, whose move slot is Mech_MovementTick. Mech_Constructor picks between three behaviour instances by (is this the local player, does the type record set the flyer flag), so Razor_MovementTick runs for the player's RAZOR alone.

entries.name: BehaviourStateNames
entries.description: 22 packed NUL-terminated AI behaviour state names, the game's own, in table order: deciding, player, player fly, attacking, flanking, facing off, attacking base, attacking flyer, patrolling, travelling, following, bulldog travel, search/destroy, sleeping, skirting, guarding, driving off en, ramming, fleeing, in limbo, dead, disabled. Each descriptor's +0x00 points at its entry. No xrefs -- reached as base + offset by the static initialiser.

entries.name: FlyerBehaviourStateTable
entries.description: The Flyer class' seven behaviour descriptors, stride 0x3c. Zero-filled in the image and built by Flyer_BuildStateTable (00414c68). Two bytes shorter than the mech table's 0x3e because a flyer descriptor carries no OBJECTIVE: string index. Order: deciding, attacking, patrolling, search and destroy, sleeping, scouting, dead.

entries.name: FlyerBehaviourSlotBlocks
entries.description: Seven 0x24-byte source blocks, one per flyer behaviour state, holding the think/move/reassess member-function triples Flyer_BuildStateTable copies into each descriptor's +0x18..+0x3b.

entries.name: FlyerBehaviourStateNames
entries.description: Seven packed NUL-terminated names for the flyer behaviour states, the game's own: deciding, attacking, patrolling, search and destroy, sleeping, scouting, dead.

entries.name: DevKeys_MoveStepTable
entries.description: Nine int16 move steps for commands 0x602-0x60a (Ctrl+Alt+1-9): 500, 1000, 1500, 2000, 3000, 4500, 6000, 7500, 9000. Mech_HandleCommand indexes it as 0049941c + command*2.

entries.name: DevKeys_TurnStepTable
entries.description: Nine int16 turn steps for commands 0x602-0x60a, the same values as DevKeys_MoveStepTable. Mech_HandleCommand indexes it as 0049942e + command*2.

entries.name: SlideDamageScaleByDifficulty
entries.description: short[4] {400, 800, 1200, 1600} -- scale on the damage Mech_CollisionTest deals the player for a long downhill slide, indexed by MissionDifficulty.

entries.name: TargetingPodComponentRotation
entries.description: The seven component slots [Tab] cycles a HERC target through: 0, 4, 5, 7, 8, 9, 10. Read only by Mech_NextTargetableComponent, twice. Seven of the machine's twenty-nine slots, across both the chassis band and the systems band of Mech_AiSelectAimComponent's table.

entries.name: ThrottleLeverMode
entries.description: Joystick throttle-lever mode: 0 = no lever (keyboard/plain stick), +1 = lever present, -1 = lever present with its sense inverted. Set by Input_SetThrottleLeverMode, which writes 1 only when the input config reports a throttle control AND the preferences page assigns it to THROTTLE rather than TURRET, and 0 otherwise; the key command (Sim_PollPlayerInput case 5) and the cockpit slider commit (ThrottleSlider_OnValue) only flip between +1 and -1 and are gated on that same pair. Not a forward/reverse gear selector, which is the obvious reading of the +1/-1 values: DBSIM has no gear. In Mech_ApplyThrottleInput it gates two things: the absolute-lever read (|axis-0x100|*2, deadbanded below 100) and the throttle clamp, which spans the full +/-0x400 at 0 and closes to one side of zero otherwise. That is why holding the keyboard throttle down walks a HERC through zero into reverse.

entries.name: AirframeContactImpactFx
entries.description: A PROJ.DAT-shaped 12-entry ImpactFX table held in the image rather than in a file, used for airframe contacts alone: shield {11,11,11,11}, ground and armour both {0,1,4,5}. Statically initialised, and pointed at by AirframeContactShot+0x0a.

entries.name: AirframeContactShot
entries.description: The shot record Razor_MovementTick reuses for every airframe contact, refilled per probe. +0x00 pointer to a stack ray {transform*, length = airspeed, clearance}, +0x04 armour damage (Q10 of airspeed for a ground contact, a flat 1000 or 5000 for an object one), +0x06 shield damage, always 8000, +0x08 splash 0, +0x0a AirframeContactImpactFx, +0x0e attacker = NULL so a collision is nobody's kill, +0x14 the aircraft itself, which is Sim_RaycastObjectList's second exclusion.

entries.name: LockTone_PhaseSounded
entries.description: Mech_LockTonePlay's blink latch: set once the lock tone has sounded for the current phase of the 0x40-coarse-tick cadence, cleared when that bit goes low, so the tone plays once per phase rather than every tick.

entries.name: LockTone_WasLocked
entries.description: Mech_LockTonePlay's edge latch: set while a lock is held, so that losing it plays trgunloc (0x16) exactly once. The branch that consumes it returns before the target-changed test, which is why switching target while locked plays the loss tone and not the acquisition blip.

entries.name: FlatObj_Vtable
entries.description: Vtable of class FlatObj (Borland RTTI at 0041bcf6: 'FlatObj', 0x41 bytes). Five slots: FlatObj_Draw, SimObject_GetPosition, FlatObj_Destruct, Stub_ReturnZero, SimObject_GetShapeRadius -- no tick, so a FlatObj is static unless its owner moves it. Every spawner writes type 9 at obj+0x04, the tag ObjList_DrawCellObjects draws on the spot with the ramp row count zeroed.

entries.name: AiAimScatterByDifficulty
entries.description: short[4] {1000, 800, 400, 200} -- how far Ai_FireAtPoint throws a Cybrid machine's aim off, indexed by MissionDifficulty.

entries.name: g_ShapeDetailThresholds
entries.description: The LOD root threshold table, seven int32s {75, 60, 45, 25, 18, 12, 6} in projected pixels. MechType_InitOne writes this one address into EVERY mech type record's detail struct at +0xe2, so it is a single global table and not per-chassis data. Descending, so Shape_DrawAtDetailLevel advances while the shape is SMALLER than the entry -- the opposite sense to TSDetailPart_Render's ascending per-part table.

entries.name: g_MechTextureGroupNames
entries.description: 7-entry array of pointers to the literal strings 'light'/'medium'/'heavy'/'enemy'/'apocatex'/'razortex'/'newhercs' (the strings themselves start at 0049a437, 0x0049a37c holds an 8th unrelated pointer -- not part of this array, unresearched). Confirmed dead in DBSIM.EXE's own code (zero xrefs to the array base or any individual string, checked both via ReferenceManager and a full-binary decompiled-text scan) -- DBSIM does NOT read this table at runtime to pick a mech's DBA. The real runtime mechanism is MechType_TextureGroupIndex (see that entry) feeding g_MechTextureGroupSlots directly; this string table is very likely leftover linked-in rodata from the same shared ThreeSpace source file, present in the binary but never actually executed. Byte-verified against the 7-name set in docs/retail/formats/dts-texture-binding.md.

entries.name: s_mforms_0049a46b
entries.description: String literal 'mforms', mechsys.cpp's dat\MFORMS.DAT resource name (joined with the 'dat' folder prefix by ResourcePath_BuildFolderName in Mech_LoadResources). Sits in a literal pool alongside other mechsys.cpp string constants (difficulty names, texture-bank names) immediately followed by the source-file name 'mechsys.cpp' itself -- typical MSVC layout for a translation unit's string constants. No Reference object existed to this address before Mech_LoadResources was manually disassembled, because that function itself was never auto-analyzed; found by raw byte-scanning every initialized memory block for the literal ASCII bytes.

entries.name: DamageScaleBySide0Difficulty
entries.description: short[4] {3500, 2800, 2100, 1400} -- Q10 damage factor Damage_ScaleByDifficulty applies to a shot fired by side 0, indexed by MissionDifficulty.

entries.name: DamageScaleByCybridDifficulty
entries.description: short[4] {300, 600, 800, 1000} -- the same factor for a shot fired by any other side.

entries.name: GridShape_ClassItemEntry
entries.description: One ClassItem registry entry {0x02bc0001, GridShape_Construct, 'GridShape' (0049aa88)}, registered by GridShape_RegisterClassItem.

entries.name: g_TerrainDrawGrid
entries.description: The zone's HeightGrid as Terrain_LoadZone constructs it (the HeightGrid_Constructor result stored through ESI at 004279ec). Scene_DrawTerrain passes it to Terrain_DrawVisibleCells.

CellWalk_Polygon's second walk-direction flag: 1 in the image, which with maybe_g_DepthBufferEnabled == 0 selects the far-to-near walk. es2_xref finds one reference, the read in CellWalk_Polygon. VSHELL's counterpart is 00471884.

entries.name: g_UnusedTerrainTypeNames
entries.description: A 3-entry pointer table to the literal strings 'urban', 'waste', 'ruins' (at 0049ab82/0049ab88/0049ab8e); the 4th slot is not a pointer, so the table is exactly 3 long. Found via string xref while hunting terrain texture selection. DEAD DATA -- ES2FindAddressRefs on this address returns zero references anywhere in DBSIM, the third confirmed instance of this binary's dead-table pattern after g_MechTextureGroupNames and the RTTI type-name strings. Recorded so a future session does not re-derive it as a live terrain-type selector; note also that only URBAN.DBA exists in retail data (no WASTE/RUINS).

entries.name: ZoneFilenameTemplate
entries.description: Literal string 'zoneXXXX' -- template overwritten in place by _itoa(zoneIndex) to build each zone's base filename (e.g. 'zone504'). Confirmed against real filenames in ES2/VOL/ZONES.VOL (ZONE504.DAT, ZONE504.DBA, etc.).

entries.name: maybe_DbaFolderPrefix
entries.description: Literal string 'dba' -- used as a folder prefix when building the per-zone heightmap bitmap path ('dba\zoneNNNN.dba'). Confirmed the target files exist for real (ES2/VOL/ZONES.VOL/DBA/ZONE*.DBA) but the exact path-join semantics of ResourcePath_BuildFolderName weren't independently proven beyond this.

entries.name: ObjList_SortNodes
entries.description: Pointer to the 0x1d-byte depth-sort tree nodes ObjList_AllocSortNodes allocates (512 from ObjList_LoadResources); its first node is the tree root ObjList_SortTreeAddOthers inserts under.

entries.name: CockpitViewShakeArmed
entries.description: Set by CockpitView_SetShakeBand and tested first by CockpitView_StepShake, which does nothing until a band has been seeded.

entries.name: CockpitShakeReseedAfterSlide
entries.description: Byte. Set by CockpitView_ApplyViewState when a view change clears an armed shake band, cleared on a change to view 4; while set, CockpitView_StepViewTransition ends every slide with CockpitView_SetShakeBand(10).

entries.name: CockpitPaletteSingleton
entries.description: Pointer to the currently-loaded cockpit-family palette object. First loaded lazily (guarded by == 0) as the literal resource 'dpl\\cockpit' (s_cockpit_0049ae69 + CockpitDpl_ResourceFolderNames[0]="dpl", via ResourcePath_BuildFolderName + ClassItem_LoadTaggedResource) -- confirms DBSIM loads COCKPIT.DPL by a plain literal name, not a derived/offset one, and the real retail file ES2/VOL/simvol0/dpl/COCKPIT.DPL exists under exactly that name. Later swapped to 'dpl\\impactcp' (IMPACTCP.DPL, also a real retail file) as a second, smaller damage/impact-flash palette, whose colors get copied into a 24-entry sub-range of the global active display palette (Palette_InstallRange(0x2a, 0x18, ...)) rather than replacing CockpitPaletteSingleton wholesale. No index-remap/offset was found anywhere in this load path -- decoding a real .HB0 through COCKPIT.DPL with a direct, unmodified index lookup produces a correct, recognizable cockpit image (visually verified against APOCA.HB0/SAMSON.HB0).

entries.name: CockpitOverride_Index
entries.description: int16, the -C name's index in the 13-name table at 0049ac64, written by CmdLine_SetCockpitOverride. The cockpit view manager stores it at +0x27 in place of the machine's when CockpitOverride_Name is set.

entries.name: CockpitOverride_Name
entries.description: char*, the -C name, null unless CmdLine_SetCockpitOverride matched one. Replaces the herc name the cockpit view manager and the canopy-crack art take from the machine.

entries.name: g_TheaterHzline
entries.description: Pointer to the theater's hzline, the sky backdrop. World_LoadTheater stores it (Hzline_Ctor) and fills it from the .WLD's first eight int16s; Scene_DrawTerrainPass reads it once a frame. Every access in 0049aee0-0049aef8 is by absolute address.

entries.name: World_FlatSetSelector
entries.description: int16 read by World_LoadTheater as the tenth int16 of wld\world<N>.wld (byte 18) and passed to FlatObj_LoadResources: 0 loads the 'flat' set, nonzero 'flat2'. All ten retail files hold 1, and only FLAT2.DTS/FLAT2.DBA ship.

entries.name: ImpactPaletteObject
entries.description: The theater's impact palette, loaded by World_LoadTheater (0042e010) from the third trailing string of wld/WORLD<n>.WLD -- IMPACT0.DPL through IMPACT9.DPL. Its only readers are the three Palette_*Impact functions that flash it during the cockpit damage shake.

entries.name: ActivePaletteObject
entries.description: The live palette object. Field +8 is its 256 x 4-byte entry array (the array every Palette_* helper indexes). Installed by Palette_LoadAndActivate from dpl\\world<N>; DAT_0049b028/0x2c/0x30 are its dirty min/max/valid triple and DAT_0049b024 the last-uploaded object.

entries.name: g_ShadeRamps
entries.description: Pointer to 0x81 8-byte ramp records {int16 *indices; int16 count}, allocated (0x408 bytes) by Palette_LoadResources, which also gives each record a 0x102-byte index array. Palette_SetRampsToRange and Palette_SetRampsToRangeList fill records and hand them to Raster_SetColourRamps (00486d04), which copies them into the raster's ramp table at g_RasterColourRamps (004a4fbd); Palette_ReadShadeRampRanges (004304dc) reads them back.

entries.name: StepKickCurve
entries.description: int16[10] {1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 5, 4, 3, 2, 1}: the step kick's offsets over its 0x3c coarse ticks, read by Cockpit_StepKickTick.

entries.name: PowerUp_RowArmDelays
entries.description: Ten shorts, 20, 40, ... 200: the coarse-tick delay after the power-up start past which Cockpit_PowerUpTick arms each weapon-row gauge in cockpit+0x70, indexed by .GAU weapon row. Read from the PE; the Ghidra listing leaves all but the first two undefined.

entries.name: Cockpit_ZeroOffset
entries.description: {int x, int y} = {0, 0}, set by CockpitView_StaticInit: the offset Widget_DrawToCockpit hands Region_CopyBetweenPages when its caller passes a null offset (MOV EDI,0x49b07e at 004313a2).

entries.name: CockpitViewInstance
entries.description: Singleton pointer to LocalPlayerMech's live cockpit/HUD view object (set once, guarded by == 0, in ColorSchemePanels_LoadAll/00431098). Directly embeds each GAU widget as a live sub-object at a fixed struct offset matching GAUFile.cs's own documented field order: a 10-slot weapon-button array at +0x1c (matches GAU's 10 weapon hardpoint slots), then single widgets at +0x1e1/+0x1e5/+0x1e9/+0x1ed/+0x1f1/+0x1f5/+0x1f9/+0x20b (chain/link/autotrack/energy-meter-family offsets), each paint-dispatched via its own vtable call. Read throughout the cockpit/HUD call graph (Player_PerFrameCockpitUpdate, Sim_RenderFrame, Gau_BuildCockpitWidgets, Gau_RovingGunsightWidget, Hud_UpdateWaypointIndicator, ~90 more sites) but never seen holding the HB0/HB2 background bitmap itself -- that field, and the exact function that blits the cockpit background art and composites the live 3D view into it, are not pinned to a specific offset or address (see docs/retail/formats/cockpit-views.md's open items). NOT the same object as maybe_MechInspectViewInstance (CockpitViewManagerInstance), a separate, much smaller (0x37-byte) object built by Sim_InitMissionSession right after this singleton is already in use.

entries.name: Cockpit_CursorImages
entries.description: The seven .DCI cursors ColorSchemePanels_LoadAll loads, in name-table order: 0 cursor, 1 pcursor, 2 mcursor, 3 ncursor, 4 scursor, 5 ecursor, 6 wcursor. The cockpit's three cursor slots (view+0x232, +0x236, +0x23a) take their images from here.
entries.source: DBSIM decompile at 00431098; name table at 0049b150

entries.name: CockpitGauRecord
entries.description: Pointer to the current herc's loaded .GAU record (Gau_Load's 0x6a4-byte buffer, content offsets 1:1), stored by Gau_BuildCockpitWidgets (00431c27). Widget builders read rects from it by content offset; the pilot-port rect at +0x684 and the training lift at +0x680 are coordinate-shifted in place.

entries.name: ColorSchemePanels
entries.description: Base of the 18-element loaded-font array filled by ColorSchemePanels_LoadAll, in load order: 0 cpblue, 1 cpgreen, 2 cpred, 3 cpylw, 4 cpon, 5 cppress, 6 cpoff, 7 cpgrey, 8 cpblack, 9 cporange, 10 white, 11 gray, 12 dark, 13 green, 14 red, 15 hud1, 16 hud2, 17 hud3. Each entry is a .DFN/.HFN bitmap font (see docs/retail/formats/dfn-hfn-dci.md) stencilled in a single palette index, so a widget picks its text colour by picking which entry to hand the label constructor -- it never passes a colour. Consumers reach entries by absolute address: 0049b0d4 = 10 white (shield readouts, selected weapon name), 0049b0d8 = 11 gray, 0049b0dc = 12 dark, 0049b0ec = 16 hud2 (SPEED:/TIME: captions), 0049b0f0 = 17 hud3 (their values).

entries.name: HitShakeEndTick
entries.description: The Time_GetCoarseTicks value at which the cockpit damage shake ends -- set to now + 0x3c (60 units, 0.96 s) by Cockpit_StartHitShake. Zero means no shake is running.

entries.name: HitShakeNextToggleTick
entries.description: The Time_GetCoarseTicks value at which the damage shake next flips the impact palette, pushed to now + rand%10 each time it fires.

entries.name: Cockpit_CursorsLive
entries.description: Byte Sim_InitMissionSession sets once the cockpit is up. Cockpit_PickEdgeCursor, Cockpit_UpdateEdgeCursor, Cockpit_SetForwardCursor and Cockpit_SetOffForwardCursor do nothing while it is clear.
entries.source: DBSIM decompile at 004614fc and its four readers

entries.name: StepKickStartTick
entries.description: The Time_GetCoarseTicks value Cockpit_StartStepKick restarted the kick at; Cockpit_StepKickTick indexes StepKickCurve from it.

entries.name: StepKickEndTick
entries.description: The Time_GetCoarseTicks value the step kick ends at, start + 0x3c; 0 while none runs.

entries.name: MfdStatusLabelTables
entries.description: Three parallel int16[5] tables for the MFD status screen's labels: 0049bd84 x0 (6 for all five), 0049bd8e y0 (16, 23, 32, 40, 49), 0049bd98 font selector (0,1,0,1,1) into {ColorSchemePanels[10] WHITE, [14] RED}. All in GAU units relative to the inset screen origin; each label is 6 units tall and runs right to the wireframe viewport's left edge at 45. See docs/retail/formats/mfd.md.

entries.name: Hud_BitmapBank
entries.description: The 'hud' bitmap bank, loaded once by Gau_RovingGunsightWidget (from the panel-mode-3 folder in that mode). Its frame pointers are at +8: frame 14 is the ATT plate, frames 15-18 the RAZOR's altitude scale.

entries.name: MfdMapScreen_ViewAngles
entries.description: int16 triple {0xc000, 0, 0} set by MfdMapScreen_StaticInit. MfdMapScreen_Ctor passes its address to the nav map's view constructor (PUSH 0x49c454 at 00440577) and MfdMapScreen_Paint copies the first int16 into its camera block (004406c2).

entries.name: WeaponGauge_WipeFirstFrames
entries.description: Two shorts {1, 9}: the first WPN_DMG frame of each of the weapon row's two sensor-dropout sequences. WeaponGauge_Ctor steps each to its partner in 0049c4cc ({9, 1}), one frame per coarse tick.

entries.name: ChainCountCaptions
entries.description: Three 4-byte inline strings 'I', 'II', 'III' indexed by chain count, read by ConsoleButton_Paint.

entries.name: ShieldRingColors
entries.description: Six bytes of 6-bit colour channels for the shield meter's ring ramp: base R,G,B at +0..+2 = (25,59,23) and bright R,G,B at +3..+5 = (59,59,23). Read only by ShieldsGauge_UpdateRingPalette. Channel order matches the .DPL entry layout, byte 0 = R.

entries.name: MfdButtonRects
entries.description: Four parallel int16[13] tables giving the MFD's button rects in GAU units relative to the inset screen origin: 0049cacc x0, 0049cae6 y0, 0049cb00 x1, 0049cb1a y1. Indices 0-5 are the F-key mode column at x -16..-2 with a 10-unit pitch (negative because the column sits left of the inset), 6 is a degenerate zero rect, 7-12 the per-screen aux buttons. Every rect size matches a dba\MFD.DBA frame size exactly. See docs/retail/formats/mfd.md.

entries.name: MfdDropoutSetByCondition
entries.description: Five shorts [0, 1, 2, 2, 2]: which of the MFD's three sensor-dropout sets each condition 0-4 uses.

entries.name: MfdDropoutSequenceCounts
entries.description: Six shorts [3, 2, 3, 3, 6, 3], frame counts of the six MFD_DMG sequences whose frame lists sit at 0049cb4c-0049cb88 (six shorts each). MfdDisplay_Ctor builds only the first three, each held 4 ticks.

entries.name: g_MfdMissileCamSavedMode
entries.description: int16: the MFD mode MfdDisplay_SyncMissileCamMode saved before switching to the missile cam, and restores after (3 in the image).

entries.name: g_MfdMissileCamMode
entries.description: int16: 5 while MfdDisplay_SyncMissileCamMode's condition holds, -1 otherwise (-1 in the image). MfdDisplay_SetMode resets it to -1 whenever it runs with it set; MfdDisplay_Update also tests it.

entries.name: g_MfdMissileCamArmed
entries.description: byte: whether MfdDisplay_SyncMissileCamMode switches to the missile cam when its condition starts (1 in the image). MfdDisplay_SetMode clears it when it runs during the condition; MfdDisplay_SyncMissileCamMode sets it again.

entries.name: MfdButtonVisibility
entries.description: 6 rows x 13 bytes: which buttons each MFD mode shows. Indices 0-5 are 1 in every row; the aux columns give SELECT on modes 0 and 4, XMIT on 1, RANGE/TARGET/PASS/ACTIVE on 3, and none on 2 and 5. MfdDisplay_SetMode and MfdDisplay_Repaint address it as &table[mode][6], which the decompiler folds into DAT_0049cbde + mode*13. See docs/retail/formats/mfd.md.

entries.name: MfdDisplay_StaticRegionBuilt
entries.description: Byte guard of MfdDisplay_Ctor's function-local static MfdDisplay_StaticRegion (004d1d34): MfdDisplay_Ctor, finding it 0, installs GLRectangleRegionVtable at MfdDisplay_StaticRegion (004d1d34), zeroes 004d1d38 and increments the byte. MfdDisplay_StaticDtor tests it.

entries.name: HddStaticBank
entries.description: The 'static' sprite bank handle -- five 64x53 frames of video noise that HddGauge_PaintStatic cycles through a comm box whose pilot's comms are out. Ships in dba\ only.

entries.name: HddSpriteBank
entries.description: The 'hdd' sprite bank handle (hba\HDD.HBA or dba\HDD.DBA), 27 frames: 0-1 the XMIT/CANCEL plate unlit/lit, 2-4 the selected-order highlight bar, 5-12 the first arrow-button set, 13-20 the second, 21-24 the two map magnifiers, 25-26 the F7/F8 page buttons. Which arrow set a herc uses is its own .GAU block value at offset 0x5c.

entries.name: HddStaticFramePos
entries.description: int x, y: the point HddGauge_PaintStatic hands VideoMode_BlitRotated as a static frame's position; it adds DAT_004d25da/DAT_004d25de before the blit and subtracts them after. HddDisplay_StaticInit zeroes both.

entries.name: CommBox0PilotOverride
entries.description: int, the -t<n> command-line value. HddGauge_LoadPilotFrames takes it as squad comm box 0's pilot index when it is non-negative.

entries.name: HddPageWidgetVisibility
entries.description: 2 rows x 15 bytes, indexed [page][widget] by HddDisplay_SetPage. Page 0 shows widgets 0-7 and 13-14, page 1 only 0-5. Both rows hide the three comm boxes (10-12), which HddGauge_LoadPilotFrames re-enables per occupied squad slot.

entries.name: HddMapView_Angles
entries.description: int16[3] = (0xc000, 0, 0), set by HddCommandScreen_StaticInit: the angle triple HddCommandScreen_Ctor passes to View_Ctor for the command display's map view (PUSH 0x49d6c0 at 0044c4be). MfdMapScreen_Ctor passes the triple at MfdMapScreen_ViewAngles (0049c454), which MfdMapScreen_StaticInit (004407f0) sets to the same values.

entries.name: HddDamageColorIds
entries.description: Four COLORS.DAT logical colour ids -- 19, 9, 15, 12 -- that HddDamageScreen_Ctor resolves through HudColorTable in place to palette 16, 10, 13, 14 (black, red, yellow, green). Dead after that: 0049d9ec is materialised exactly once in the image, at 004507c9, which is the resolve loop itself, and nothing reads the resolved values. The damage rows take their colour from a ColorSchemePanels font picked by Damage_PickRegionTint's state instead. See docs/retail/formats/heads-down-display.md, Rejected readings.

entries.name: PanelAmbience_ColonOn
entries.description: Byte that every PanelAmbience_TickClock call toggles: the clock advances on the calls that set it to 1, and the colon label is texted while it is set.

entries.name: Widget_PressedIndex
entries.description: int16. Index into the cockpit-wide clickable list of the widget a mouse button is currently held down on, or -1 for none. One global for the whole cockpit, not per-panel. Set by Widget_OnMouseDown from its own hit test, read and acted on by Widget_TrackPressedWidget, cleared to -1 at the end of Widget_OnMouseUp. Its -1 guard is what makes Widget_TrackPressedWidget a no-op unless a button is held.

entries.name: Widget_DragCapture
entries.description: Set by Widget_OnMouseDown when the pressed widget's +0x1d flag is 1. While set, CockpitMouse_ProcessQueue routes every position change to the captured widget's drag slot (+0x18) WITHOUT hit-testing -- a drag follows the pointer off the widget and off the window -- and the release path reads the value (+0x10) and commits it (+8) instead of calling Widget_OnMouseUp, so a drag fires no click.

entries.name: CockpitMouse_DoubleClick
entries.description: Byte. The double-click flag: CockpitMouse_ProcessQueue clears it at the top of every record and sets it on a release edge whose timestamp is less than CockpitMouse_DoubleClickTicks after the same button's previous release (CockpitMouse_LastLeftRelease / _LastRightRelease), wherever that release landed. It stands until the next record, so a key-driven press in between still sees it. Read by MfdButton_OnClick (XMIT returns without transmitting), MfdFlashComm_HandleListClick (a double-click on the selected row presses XMIT and transmits) and HddCommandScreen_QueueListClick (copied to the screen's +0x15b, which gates the order list's XMIT shortcut).

entries.name: CockpitMouse_LastLeftRelease
entries.description: Timestamp of the left button's previous release, written by CockpitMouse_ProcessQueue on each left release edge after the double-click test reads it.

entries.name: CockpitMouse_LastRightRelease
entries.description: Timestamp of the right button's previous release; the right-button twin of CockpitMouse_LastLeftRelease.

entries.name: CornerFrame_Styles
entries.description: Pointer to the 0x40-byte style records CornerFrame_LoadStyles vector-news and reads (layout in CornerFrame_Draw). Grep of the disassembly finds no access outside CornerFrame_LoadStyles.

entries.name: ScreenshotCounter
entries.description: int: the number Screenshot_BuildPath appends to the base name; Screenshot_Save increments it after each capture.

entries.name: Prefs_Path
entries.description: char[0x100], the prefs.cfg path the option load and save open. Prefs_InitPathAndHandlers sets data\prefs.cfg under the base directory when it is empty; Sim_ParseCommandLine's tape-playback arm (-p) sets it first to the Config_BuildPath of prefs.cfg.

entries.name: VoiceArchivePresent
entries.description: Byte set once by Voice_ArchiveExists at Prefs_Init time: whether the localised simvoice archive is on disk. Zero in the image, so it looks like a dead constant in a static read -- it is not; Prefs_Init writes it. When clear, options 2 and 3 are forced to 0 and the preferences panel's PILOT MESSAGE and COMPUTER MESSAGE rows refuse every click.

entries.name: SimCommandMask
entries.description: 0x47ff. Input_BuildPlayerDevice ANDs the input block's head command word and every queued command code with this, which discards the 0x800 Shift bit Key_WndProcHook sets -- so a shifted key folds onto the plain one, in the cockpit and in the alert panels' loops, which read the same word.

entries.name: KeyjoyWantedCodes
entries.description: The 30-byte NUL-terminated wanted-code list Input_KeyjoyAxisKey is registered against: 47 48 49 4b 4d 4f 50 51 32 24 25 17 4a 4e 39, then the same fifteen with the key-up bit 0x80 set -- keypad, M, J, K, I and Space.

entries.name: SimCommandWantedCodes
entries.description: The 7-byte NUL-terminated wanted-code list SimCommandQueue_Push is registered against: 1c 0c 0d 1a 1b 4e 4a -- Enter, -, =, [, ] and the keypad +/-. These are the only scancodes that reach the command queue at 004d2148 directly rather than through the player input block.

entries.name: KeyboardAxisDiagonalFlags
entries.description: 8 bytes, 01 00 01 00 00 01 00 01: marks keyboard axis keys 0-7 that are diagonals (keypad 7, 9, 1, 3). In Input_BuildKeyboardAxes the first held diagonal zeroes the first pair, adds its own entry and ends the group.

entries.name: KeyboardAxisDeltas
entries.description: 28-byte table of signed (dx, dy) pairs for the fourteen keyboard axis keys, zero in the image and filled at startup by Input_InitKeyboardAxisTable; Input_BuildKeyboardAxes shifts each left 7 (+/-0x80).

entries.name: MonoComponentPanel_Labels
entries.description: 41 string pointers MonoComponentPanel_Init prints down the monochrome monitor: FRONT_COCKPIT, REAR_COCKPIT, LEFT_BRACKET, RIGHT_BRACKET, LEFT_SHOULDER, RIGHT_SHOULDER, CROTCH, LEFT_QUAD, RIGHT_QUAD, LEFT_SHIN, RIGHT_SHIN, LEFT_FOOT, RIGHT_FOOT, REAR LEFT/RIGHT QUAD, SHIN and FOOT, LEFT/RIGHT LEG SERVO, SENSORS, TARGETING COMPUTER, SHIELD GENERATOR, ENGINE, HYDRAULICS, STABILIZER, LIFE_SUPPORT, PILOT, REAR LEFT/RIGHT LEG SERVO, WEAPON 1 to WEAPON 10.

entries.name: g_HercDetailScaleKeys
entries.description: Five int16 lookup keys {0,1,2,3,4} ShapeDetail_ApplyHercDetailSetting walks with setting <= key to index g_HercDetailScaleValues. Identity, so a setting selects its own slot.

entries.name: g_HercDetailScaleValues
entries.description: Five int16 values for g_ShapeDetailSizeScaleQ10, one per HERC DETAIL setting: 2000 in every slot, so the setting does not in fact move this one.

entries.name: g_HercDetailBiasKeys
entries.description: Five int16 lookup keys {0,1,2,3,4} for the second table pair in ShapeDetail_ApplyHercDetailSetting. Identity, as g_HercDetailScaleKeys is.

entries.name: g_HercDetailBiasValues
entries.description: Five int16 values for g_ShapeDetailBias, one per HERC DETAIL setting: {4,3,2,1,0}. Setting 4 is the finest; setting 0 pins every machine to root 4 or coarser at any distance.

entries.name: g_HercDetailTSDetailBiasValues
entries.description: Five int16 values for g_TSDetailBiasFromHercDetail, one per HERC DETAIL setting: {2,2,1,1,0}. Written by the same pass that writes g_ShapeDetailBias.

entries.name: g_StructureDetailKeys
entries.description: Five int16 lookup keys StructureDetail_ApplySetting walks with setting <= key.

entries.name: g_StructureDetailValues
entries.description: Five int16 values StructureDetail_ApplySetting writes into both g_TSDetailBiasFromStructureDetail and DAT_004a9e48.

entries.name: LiftStart_FadeRemaining
entries.description: LiftStart_Rise's copy of Palette_StepCrossFade's return value, 1 in the image. The ride steps the fade only while this is nonzero, and nothing else reads or writes it (es2_xref.py: the two accesses at 0045dac1 and 0045dad8), so once a step returns 0 the fade is never stepped again.

entries.name: g_TexturedPolyUseBitmapBrush
entries.description: The DBSIM counterpart of VSHELL's g_TexturedPolyUseBitmapBrush (00471890), read by TSTexture4Poly_Render (x5) and TexPoly_Render (x1); getReferencesTo finds no write site, and it is 0 in the image, in an initialized DATA block. 0: TSTexture4Poly_Render takes the frame descriptor from g_CurrentShapeDbaContext[1] and draws through the fill g_TexturedPolyPerspective picks. Non-zero: it takes the frame's bitmap from the DBA's pointer list and fills the projected poly (Poly_ProjectShapeVertices, then Poly_ClipRingToNearPlaneWithUV when it returns 1) with a type-7 bitmap brush {7, count, uvs, bitmap, remap row} installed at the context's +0x22c, the UVs the bitmap's extent inset by 3 and the remap row ((DAT_004a5b1c - 1) * shade & ~0xff) + DAT_004a5b18, through PolyFill_FillThenOutline; the default brush 006c60d8 is restored after.

entries.name: maybe_g_DepthBufferEnabled
entries.description: Depth-buffer switch, read by every consumer as one. When non-zero: Raster_SetupTexturedSpan stores the view depth in vertex +8; Raster_DrawPolygon and Raster_DrawTexturedPolyNear run Raster_DepthTestSpan per row and, when ActiveScanlineClipSpans is set, draw its visible runs through the ...Clipped span routines; TSBSPPart_RenderNode draws the viewer's side of each splitting plane first instead of the far side; CellWalk_Polygon walks near to far. 0 in the image; es2_xref finds only reads (CMP). VSHELL's counterpart is 00471888.
entries.source: DBSIM decompile of Raster_SetupTexturedSpan, Raster_DrawPolygon, Raster_DrawTexturedPolyNear, TSBSPPart_RenderNode (00476a96) and CellWalk_Polygon (00471e90); es2_xref

entries.name: g_TexturedPolyPerspective
entries.description: Selects TSTexture4Poly_Render's textured fill: 0 calls Raster_SetupTexturedSpan, which maps u and v linearly in screen space, non-zero Raster_DrawTexturedPolyNear, which is perspective-correct. One read site (004753b7); es2_xref finds no other reference in DBSIM.EXE (the same scan finds the writer of the neighbouring g_PerspectiveUseQuadraticFit). 0 in the image, in an initialized DATA block. VSHELL's counterpart is 00471898.

entries.name: g_PerspectiveUseQuadraticFit
entries.description: When non-zero, Raster_DrawTexturedPolyNear takes each row's starting u and v, and its last partial run's end, from Raster_BuildEdgeTables' quadratic fit (edge +0x18/+0x1c) instead of dividing by 1/z; the run ends inside a row are divided either way. Terrain_DrawCellQuad sets it per cell to (nearest corner's view depth > 25000), the depth it passes Raster_SetDepthFadeFromDistance.
entries.source: DBSIM disassembly: writer 0046da89 in Terrain_DrawCellQuad, readers 00468c9d and 00468ed1 in Raster_DrawTexturedPolyNear

entries.name: DeathCamera_CountdownByClass
entries.description: int[2] by type record +0x50 (walker, RAZOR): 20000, 6000 -- the player-death camera's length in the timer unit, about 9.8 s and 2.9 s.

entries.name: DeathCamera_SteerByClass
entries.description: short[2] by type record +0x50 (walker, RAZOR): 50, 50 -- the steering axis the player-death camera hands Cam_Steer every tick.

entries.name: DeathCamera_ThrottleByClass
entries.description: short[2] by type record +0x50 (walker, RAZOR): -30, 30 -- the throttle axis it hands Cam_Steer: a pitch rate for the walker, a zoom rate for the RAZOR, whose trigger is set.

entries.name: DeathCamera_TriggerByClass
entries.description: short[2] by type record +0x50 (walker, RAZOR): 0, 1 -- the trigger it hands Cam_Steer, which tests the whole word.

entries.name: DeathCamera_PitchByClass
entries.description: short[2] by type record +0x50 (walker, RAZOR): 0x1f40, -0x1f40 -- the orbit pitch (CAM+0x26) the player-death camera's first call writes, with roll 0 in the same dword store.

entries.name: DeathCamera_HeadingByClass
entries.description: short[2] by type record +0x50 (walker, RAZOR): 0, 0 -- the orbit heading (CAM+0x2a) the player-death camera's first call writes, relative to the machine's own.

entries.name: DeathCamera_DistanceByClass
entries.description: int[2] by type record +0x50 (walker, RAZOR), stored to the word CAM+0x22: 2500, 7000 -- the orbit distance the player-death camera's first call writes.

entries.name: AlertPanel_EndsMissionButton
entries.description: Per alert status, the index of the button whose press ends the mission. The poll's and [Q]'s raises of the status alert compare the modal loop's return against this entry and nothing else decides it; the player-death camera's raise ends the mission whatever the answer. Entry 7 is 1 against a one-button panel, which is what makes the mission-boundary warning an acknowledgement rather than a choice.

entries.name: SfxManager
entries.description: The single SFX manager instance (0x4c bytes), or 0 when sound is off. Every Sound_* entry point tests it first.

entries.name: Sound_MusicEnabled
entries.description: Enable flag for catalog ids 0-9.

entries.name: Sound_EffectsEnabled
entries.description: Enable flag for catalog ids 10 and up.

entries.name: Music_CdTrack
entries.description: CD track number for the mission, written by Sim_InitMissionSession. 0 means use the (dead) digital music ids instead.

entries.name: Music_CdEnabled
entries.description: CD music enable byte, written by Sim_InitMissionSession (00461cb0); read by sfxWndProc before the loop restart and by Sound_SuspendAll.

entries.name: Music_SavedPosition
entries.description: TMSF position saved by Sound_SuspendAll for Music_ResumeAt.

entries.name: Sound_SpeechEnabled
entries.description: Enable flag for the five-slot speech channel; without it Voice_Acquire opens nothing.

entries.name: VolumeGroup_BufferSize
entries.description: The BuffRStream buffer size VolumeGroup_AddVolume hands Volume_LoadVolume for each volume file it opens. 0x400 in the image; VolumeGroup_Ctor stores 0x400 and VolumeGroup_SetBufferSize stores its clamped argument.
entries.source: DBSIM disassembly: writes at 00467ab0 and 00467b46, read at 00467e96

entries.name: AtlasPage_Root
entries.description: Pointer to the first 0x808-byte atlas page ('Sheet'), allocated and AtlasPage_Init'ed as page 0 by AtlasPage_StaticInit; AtlasPage_SetRootIndex writes its +0x804.

entries.name: ShadeRampTable
entries.description: 256-byte-aligned base of the theater's world<N>.rmp rows, set by ShadeRamp_Allocate and filled by World_LoadTheater. Raster_ShadeRampRow masks a row offset to 0x100 and adds it, which is why the alignment matters; the span routines 0046ac48 and 0046adad index it the same way.

entries.name: maybe_DatFolderPrefixPtr
entries.description: Pointer to the literal string 'dat' -- used as a folder prefix when building the per-zone header resource path ('dat\zoneNNNN', 16-byte header) and the shared material table path ('dat\mat0'). Confirmed both target files exist for real (ES2/VOL/ZONES.VOL/DAT/ZONE*.DAT, ES2/VOL/simvol0/dat/MAT0.DAT) but the exact path-join semantics of ResourcePath_BuildFolderName weren't independently proven beyond this.

entries.name: CockpitDpl_ResourceFolderNames
entries.description: A 12-entry constant pointer table of resource folder-name strings: dpl, gl, dmg, col, edg, dba, dci, dfn, gau, hfn, hdg, hba (0x4a0a14-0x4a0a43, pointing into a shared string pool at 0x4a0a44 that separately also holds wb/rb (fopen modes) and nam/dat/bnd/dts, those last four belonging to a different, not-yet-located table). Despite the name, this table is NOT cockpit-exclusive -- gau/dpl/dba/dci/dfn/hfn/hdg/hba are all mech-subsystem resource kinds reused site-wide; named for the first confirmed use found this session (index 0, "dpl", is PTR_DAT_004a0a14, used directly by the COCKPIT.DPL/IMPACTCP.DPL load calls -- see CockpitPaletteSingleton).

entries.name: ActiveHeightGrid
entries.description: Pointer to the currently-installed HeightGrid struct, confirmed set by Terrain_LoadZone.

entries.name: Mat0ResourceName
entries.description: Literal string 'mat0' -- resource name for the shared terrain-material table, combined with the 'dat' folder prefix to build 'dat\mat0'. Confirmed against the real retail file ES2/VOL/simvol0/dat/MAT0.DAT.

entries.name: DbaExtensionLiteral
entries.description: Literal string '.dba' -- checked via stricmp in TerrainZone_LoadHeightmap to pick the real-data (ClassItem bitmap) loading path over the ASCII fscanf fallback. Confirmed: every real zone heightmap in ES2/VOL/ZONES.VOL/DBA/ uses this extension.

entries.name: Avi_PlaybackDone
entries.description: Avi_Play's loop condition: cleared before MCI_PLAY, set by Avi_NotifyHook on a successful MCI notify or by Avi_Play itself on Esc or Space.

entries.name: Avi_MciDeviceId
entries.description: The MCI device id Avi_Play's MCI_OPEN returns; MCI_WINDOW, MCI_STATUS and MCI_PLAY go to it, and Avi_CloseMovie closes it.

entries.name: g_VolumeGroup
entries.description: Pointer to the simulation's VolumeGroup. VolRStream_SetGroup creates it, VolRStream_Open searches it and VolRStream_LoadVolume adds to it. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's g_VolumeGroup.

entries.name: Music_MciDeviceId
entries.description: MCI device id of the open cdaudio device, or -1 when closed.

entries.name: Sos_MasterVolume
entries.description: Master volume, 0-100 (100 in the image), multiplied into every voice volume by Sos_ApplyVolume. Sos_SetMasterVolume writes it; es2_xref.py finds no reference to that setter.

entries.name: Sos_LastError
entries.description: The last SOS error result the backend stored, e.g. Sos_ShutdownDrivers' driver uninit results; read by Sos_GetLastError.

entries.name: TSBounds_CachedViewWidth
entries.description: TSBounds_ScreenVisibility's cache key: the drawing-context width TSBounds_RadiusScale was last built for. -1 in the image.

entries.name: g_TSDetailPartSizeScaleQ10
entries.description: Q10 factor TSDetailPart_Render scales projected size by before comparing against the part's own Details table. 1024 (Q10 one) in the image.

entries.name: g_TSDetailPartBias
entries.description: The level index TSDetailPart_Render starts its walk from, and subtracts again when indexing Parts. Written only by TSDetailPart_SetBias, which every draw slot that cares brackets its render with. Zero -- maximum detail -- outside such a bracket.

entries.name: VkToScancode
entries.description: 223 int32 entries, indexed by Win32 virtual key code, giving the PC set-1 scancode that becomes the low byte of a DBSIM command code. VK_F1 -> 0x3b, VK_F11 -> 0x57, VK_P -> 0x19, VK_OEM_4 -> 0x1a, VK_TAB -> 0x0f. Zero means unmapped. Read only by Key_WndProcHook.

entries.name: ClassItem_ProbeBucketCount
entries.description: Number of buckets in ClassItem_ProbeBuckets (006c5958). ClassItem_RegisterProbeBucket increments it; ClassItem_PeekTypeTag and ClassItem_ReadTypeTag try the probe loaders for an unregistered tag when it is non-zero. Text search of the decompile dump finds its increment in ClassItem_RegisterProbeBucket and reads elsewhere.

entries.name: ClassItem_ProbeHeaderSize
entries.description: Header length, tag included, that ClassItem_PeekTypeTag and ClassItem_ReadTypeTag read before trying the probe loaders: they copy the 8-byte tag to ClassItem_ProbeHeader (006c59a8) and read this value less 8 more bytes (0 when it is 8 or less) into 006c59b0. ClassItem_RegisterProbeBucket raises it from its entries' +8.

entries.name: GL_ClassItemTable
entries.description: Nine 12-byte {type tag, load function, class name} class-item handlers, count at 004a2f3c: tags 0x280000 'Old GLBitmap', 0x28000e 'GLBitmap', 0x280001 'GLBitmapArray', 0x28000f 'GLPalette', 0x280003 'Old GLFont', 0x280005 'GLFont', 0x28000c 'GLRectangleRegion', 0x28000d 'GLEdgeTableRegion', 0x28000b 'GLCursor'. GL_RegisterClassItems registers it.

entries.name: g_RasterColourRamps
entries.description: Table of 8-byte records {int16 *entries at +0, int16 length at +4}, indexed by ramp number (the int16 at 004a4fc1 is record 0's length). Raster_SetColourRamps writes a run of records; Raster_FillContourPolygon reads entry (shade * length) >> 8 of the ramp a brush colour names, and the span and polygon fills index it the same way for a type-4 colour. The bytes are zero in the image.
entries.source: DBSIM disassembly at 00486d04; readers in the decompile at 004879c0 and the fills that MOV EDX,0x4a4fbd

entries.name: g_RasterRoutines
entries.description: 36 rasterizer function pointers, zero in the image and filled by RasterDriver_InstallRoutines. Slot 0 is the mode-0 flat span Raster_DrawPolygonDispatch calls, slot 1 the mode-6 span, slot 33 (004a5848) Raster_FillBitmapPolygon.

entries.name: g_RasterRoutines_RemapSpans
entries.description: Slot 1 of g_RasterRoutines. Driver 3 fills it with Driver3_RemapSpans. Raster_FillSpanList and Raster_DrawPolygonDispatch call it for a mode-6 brush.
entries.source: DBSIM driver-3 table entry 1 at 004a5888 and decompile reads of 004a57c8

entries.name: g_RasterRoutines_FillRect
entries.description: Slot 2 of g_RasterRoutines. Driver 3 fills it with Driver3_FillRect. Raster_FillRect calls it for a mode-0 brush.
entries.source: DBSIM driver-3 table entry 2 at 004a588c and decompile reads of 004a57cc

entries.name: g_RasterRoutines_RemapRect
entries.description: Slot 3 of g_RasterRoutines. Driver 3 fills it with Driver3_RemapRect. Raster_FillRect calls it for a mode-6 brush.
entries.source: DBSIM driver-3 table entry 3 at 004a5890 and decompile reads of 004a57d0

entries.name: g_RasterRoutines_GetPixel
entries.description: Slot 4 of g_RasterRoutines. Driver 3 fills it with Raster_GetPixel (0048a234). The object pick and the occlusion probe read their test pixels through it.
entries.source: DBSIM driver-3 table at 004a5894; disassembly at 0048a234

entries.name: g_RasterRoutines_PutPixel
entries.description: Slot 5 of g_RasterRoutines. Driver 3 fills it with Raster_PutPixel (0048a255).
entries.source: DBSIM driver-3 table at 004a5898; disassembly at 0048a255

entries.name: g_RasterRoutines_RemapPixel
entries.description: Slot 6 of g_RasterRoutines. Driver 3 fills it with Driver3_RemapPixel. Gfx_PlotPixel calls it for a mode-2 pen.
entries.source: DBSIM driver-3 table entry 6 at 004a589c and decompile reads of 004a57dc

entries.name: g_RasterRoutines_GetPalette
entries.description: Slot 14 of g_RasterRoutines, (first, count, entries): Screenshot_WritePal calls it with (0, 0x100, buffer). Driver 3's table (g_RasterRoutines_Driver3 + 0x38) holds Driver3_ReadPalette (004896bf), which waits for vertical retrace (port 0x3da bit 3), sets the DAC read index (0x3c7) to first and reads count R, G, B bytes from 0x3c9 into 4-byte entries, storing 1 in each entry's fourth byte.

entries.name: g_RasterRoutines_SetOrigin
entries.description: Slot 15 of g_RasterRoutines: driver 3 fills it with 00489802, which calls Display_SetOrigin(page, point).

entries.name: maybe_g_RasterRoutines_SetSourcePage
entries.description: Slot 16 of g_RasterRoutines, called with the render target's +0x38 whenever that is set (the source page of a page-to-page copy). Driver 3 fills it with the empty stub 004897f0.

entries.name: maybe_g_RasterRoutines_SetDrawPage
entries.description: Slot 17 of g_RasterRoutines, called with the render target's +0x3c (the draw page) whenever that is set. Driver 3 fills it with the empty stub 004897f6.

entries.name: maybe_g_RasterRoutines_SetVisiblePage
entries.description: Slot 18 of g_RasterRoutines, called with the render target's +0x34 (the visible page), which Sim_EndFrame's -b flip sets. Driver 3 fills it with the empty stub 004897fc.

entries.name: g_RasterRoutines_CopySpans
entries.description: Slot 19 of g_RasterRoutines. Driver 3 fills it with Driver3_CopySpans. Region_CopySpansBetweenPages and Region_CopyRectBetweenPages call it.
entries.source: DBSIM driver-3 table entry 19 at 004a58d0 and decompile reads of 004a5810

entries.name: g_RasterRoutines_CopyRect
entries.description: Slot 20 of g_RasterRoutines, Region_CopyRectBetweenPages's (and so Region_CopyBetweenPages's) rect copy. Driver 3 fills it with 0048a69b, which copies the rect from (rect - offset) to rect within the one back buffer, choosing the direction by the offset's sign, and returns at once on a zero offset.

entries.name: g_RasterRoutines_SpanRead
entries.description: Slot 21 of g_RasterRoutines. Driver 3 fills it with Driver3_SpanRead. Region_SaveSpans calls it.
entries.source: DBSIM driver-3 table entry 21 at 004a58d8 and decompile reads of 004a5818

entries.name: g_RasterRoutines_SpanCopy
entries.description: Slot 22 of g_RasterRoutines. Driver 3 fills it with Driver3_SpanCopy. Raster_SpanCopy calls it.
entries.source: DBSIM driver-3 table entry 22 at 004a58dc and decompile reads of 004a581c

entries.name: g_RasterRoutines_SpanCopyRegion
entries.description: Slot 23 of g_RasterRoutines. Driver 3 fills it with Driver3_SpanCopyRegion. Raster_SpanCopyRegion and SpanRegion_Restore call it.
entries.source: DBSIM driver-3 table entry 23 at 004a58e0 and decompile reads of 004a5820

entries.name: g_RasterRoutines_SpanFill
entries.description: Slot 24 of g_RasterRoutines. Driver 3 fills it with Driver3_SpanFill. Raster_SpanFill calls it.
entries.source: DBSIM driver-3 table entry 24 at 004a58e4 and decompile reads of 004a5824

entries.name: g_RasterRoutines_SpanFillRegion
entries.description: Slot 25 of g_RasterRoutines. Driver 3 fills it with Driver3_SpanFillRegion. Raster_SpanFillRegion calls it.
entries.source: DBSIM driver-3 table entry 25 at 004a58e8 and decompile reads of 004a5828

entries.name: g_RasterRoutines_Blit
entries.description: Slot 26 of g_RasterRoutines. Driver 3 fills it with Driver3_BlitClipped. Bitmap_BlitClipDispatch calls it for clip mode 0.
entries.source: DBSIM driver-3 table entry 26 at 004a58ec and decompile reads of 004a582c

entries.name: g_RasterRoutines_Grab
entries.description: Slot 27 of g_RasterRoutines. Driver 3 fills it with Driver3_GrabClipped. Bitmap_GrabClipDispatch calls it.
entries.source: DBSIM driver-3 table entry 27 at 004a58f0 and decompile reads of 004a5830

entries.name: g_RasterRoutines_BlitRegion
entries.description: Slot 28 of g_RasterRoutines. Driver 3 fills it with Driver3_BlitClippedRegion. Bitmap_BlitClipDispatch calls it for clip modes 1 and 2.
entries.source: DBSIM driver-3 table entry 28 at 004a58f4 and decompile reads of 004a5834

entries.name: g_RasterRoutines_BlitScaled
entries.description: Slot 29 of g_RasterRoutines. Driver 3 fills it with Driver3_BlitScaled. Bitmap_BlitScaledClipDispatch calls it.
entries.source: DBSIM driver-3 table entry 29 at 004a58f8 and decompile reads of 004a5838

entries.name: maybe_g_RasterRoutines_ShowCursor
entries.description: Slot 30 of g_RasterRoutines, called after a pointer move by Cursor_SyncPosition and after drawing on the -b paged path. Driver 3 fills it with Driver3_Slot30NoOp, which only saves and restores registers.

entries.name: maybe_g_RasterRoutines_HideCursor
entries.description: Slot 31 of g_RasterRoutines, the partner of slot 30 called before the same moves and draws. Driver 3 fills it with Driver3_Slot31NoOp, which only saves and restores registers.

entries.name: g_RasterRoutines_BitmapPolygon
entries.description: Slot 33 of g_RasterRoutines, which Raster_DrawPolygonDispatch calls for brush modes 5 and 7. Filled from driver 3's table with Raster_FillBitmapPolygon.

entries.name: g_RasterRoutines_DrawLine
entries.description: Slot 34 of g_RasterRoutines. Driver 3 fills it with Driver3_DrawLine. Raster_DrawLine calls it.
entries.source: DBSIM driver-3 table entry 34 at 004a590c and decompile reads of 004a584c

entries.name: g_RasterRoutines_ClearSurface
entries.description: Slot 35 of g_RasterRoutines. Driver 3 fills it with Driver3_ClearSurface. Sim_DeathFlash calls it twice.
