entries.source: DBSIM driver-3 table entry 35 at 004a5910 and decompile reads of 004a5850

entries.name: g_RasterRoutineCount
entries.description: 36: the number of dwords RasterDriver_InstallRoutines copies into g_RasterRoutines.

entries.name: g_RasterDriverTable
entries.description: {int id, void **table} pairs ending in id -1: {0, NULL}, {1, NULL}, {3, g_RasterRoutines_Driver3}. Searched by RasterDriver_FindRoutineTable.

entries.name: g_RasterRoutines_Driver3
entries.description: Driver 3's 36-entry routine table, the only one g_RasterDriverTable holds; slot 33 is Raster_FillBitmapPolygon (0048a818).

entries.name: g_DepthBufferFrameTag
entries.description: Byte tag DepthBuffer_ClearWrappedRows and DepthBuffer_ClearWrappedRowSpans decrement after resetting the rows r with (r + tag) & 0xff == 0 to 0xffffffff; Raster_DepthTestSpan's value carries (row + tag) in its top byte.

entries.name: g_DepthBufferWidth
entries.description: Width in pixels of g_DepthBuffer, stored by DepthBuffer_Alloc; the row stride of the helpers at DepthBuffer_ClearWrappedRows (0048b7f0)-0048b95c.

entries.name: g_DepthBufferHeight
entries.description: Height in rows of g_DepthBuffer, stored by DepthBuffer_Alloc; the row limit of the helpers at DepthBuffer_ClearWrappedRows (0048b7f0)-0048b95c.

entries.name: ActiveScanlineClipSpans
entries.description: Pointer to the current view's per-scanline visible-span table (built by ClipRegions_BuildScanlineSpans). The polygon rasterizer at 00468310 indexes it per row (row*8 -> {spanCount, spanPtr}) and skips rows whose span count is zero, so the 3D scene only ever paints through the canopy's cut-out. Set to 0 for view 4 (no cockpit, unclipped full screen).

entries.name: g_TSObjectTypeRegistry
entries.description: DBSIM's DTS node factory, the counterpart of VSHELL's 0047f258: 12-byte entries of {uint32 tag, constructorFnPtr, nameStringPtr} where tag is the on-disk chunk marker. Use it rather than structural resemblance to identify a DTS object's class -- structural resemblance misidentifies two poly renderers (see TSSolidPoly_Render 00474db4 and TSTexture4Poly_Render 00474e9c).

entries.name: AN_ClassItemTable
entries.description: Four 12-byte {type tag, load function, class name} class-item handlers, count at 004a68c4: tags 0x1e0001 'ANSequence', 0x1e0002 'ANAnimList', 0x1e0003 'ANShape', 0x1e0004 'ANCyclicSequence'. AN_RegisterClassItems registers it.

entries.name: Sos_BindRefCount
entries.description: Sos_BindLibrary's refcount. Nonzero means the SOS entry points are already bound, so repeated calls skip the LoadLibrary and the GetProcAddress walk.

entries.name: SosBindingTable
entries.description: 100 records of 0x24 bytes, terminated by a null destination: {void** destinationSlot; char exportName[0x20];}. SosApi_LoadDriver walks it to bind the SOS thunks at 00495xxx to the pointer slots at 006cbde4-006cbf70. This is how a thunk's slot address resolves to an export name.

entries.name: ChaseTrail_Positions
entries.description: 50 x 12 bytes: the player's position each frame, for the chase view.

entries.name: ChaseTrail_Rotations
entries.description: 50 x 6 bytes: the player's euler triple each frame.

entries.name: ChaseTrail_Lengths
entries.description: 50 ints: each frame's Math_IntegrateRateOverTick(0x400).

entries.name: ChaseTrail_Cursor
entries.description: The chase ring's next slot.

entries.name: SimObjectSave_AnimThreads
entries.description: Ten 0x52-byte ANThread records: the animation threads SimObject_PushTransform saves and SimObject_PopTransform restores. Vector-constructed by SimObject_StaticInit.

entries.name: SimObjectSave_NodeLocals
entries.description: Thirty 12-byte [euler, translation] local node records, the copy SimObject_PushTransform takes of the shape instance's array at +0x12 and SimObject_PopTransform writes back. Vector-constructed by SimObject_StaticInit.

entries.name: SimObjectSave_NodeTransforms
entries.description: Thirty 0x20-byte node transforms, the copy SimObject_PushTransform takes of the shape instance's array at +0x16 and SimObject_PopTransform writes back. Vector-constructed by SimObject_StaticInit.

entries.name: g_HulkShapes
entries.description: dgs\BHULKS.DGS, the wreck library a fallen structure is redrawn out of, indexed by its type's BASES.DAT +0x04. Base_LoadResources sizes it from the largest value any type states and binds BASETEX to every shape in it, whatever bank the standing building used. Retail: 16 wrecks.

entries.name: g_StructurePool
entries.description: The structure object pool Structure_InitPool builds (count entries of 0x26d bytes) and Base_Construct draws every structure class from; Sim_RaycastShapeList gathers hit candidates from it. Nulled by Base_StaticInit, flushed by Structure_FlushDeletes, deleted by Base_StaticDtor.

entries.name: g_StructureDeleteQueue
entries.description: Structure delete queue: an 8-byte list header (capacity 0x19 at +6, count at +4) over a 100-byte pointer array, built by Structure_InitPool and drained into g_StructurePool by Structure_FlushDeletes.

entries.name: g_TSDetailBiasFromStructureDetail
entries.description: TSDetailPart starting level derived from the STRUCTURE DETAIL setting, via g_StructureDetailValues. Structure_DrawWithDetailBias pushes it into g_TSDetailPartBias for the duration of every structure's draw -- the whole route from that preference to what is drawn.

entries.name: g_LcWeaponSlotCount
entries.description: int16 record count of dat\LC_WPNS.DAT, read by Base_LoadResources. Retail: 3.

entries.name: g_LcWeaponSlots
entries.description: Pointer to dat\LC_WPNS.DAT's 22-byte weapon slot records, allocated and filled by Base_LoadResources (null in the image). Base_TransportThinkTick is the only reader: per slot, pitch arc +0, yaw arc +2, range +4, muzzle offset +8 (three int32s), refire delay +0x14.

entries.name: g_DebrisStructure
entries.description: BASE_DEB, the structure debris database, loaded by Base_LoadResources and installed as the alternate by Base_ThrowDebris. Retail holds 8 groups over 33 shapes.

entries.name: EffectLightPool
entries.description: The effect-light handle pool LightManager_InitSubsystem builds; Explosion_Construct allocates from it, EffectLightPool_FlushDeletes drains its delete queue (004a9686), and 004078c8 zeroes it. Three entries of 0xe bytes (Pool_Init(pool, 3, 0xe)).

entries.name: Light_PersistentList
entries.description: Array of light pointers, count Light_PersistentCount (00497ae4). Light_AddPersistent appends, Light_RemovePersistent removes, Light_ReregisterPersistent re-registers each with Light_Register.

entries.name: g_ExplosionPool
entries.description: The impact-effect object pool (40 entries of 0x5b bytes), allocated from by every effect spawn site. A pool of its own, separate from the tracer and round pool g_ProjectilePool; Sim_MainTick walks it first in the effect-pool pass, ahead of the smoke, fire, debris, meteor and g_ProjectilePool pools.

entries.name: g_ExplosionDeleteQueue
entries.description: Impact-effect delete queue: an 8-byte list header (capacity 0x1e at +6, count at +4) over a 120-byte pointer array, built by Explosion_LoadResources, filled by Sim_MainTick through ObjectPool_QueueForDelete (which does not check the capacity) and drained into g_ExplosionPool by ExplosionPool_FlushDeletes.

entries.name: g_ExplosionTypeTable
entries.description: EXPLOS.DAT's second table: 0x28-byte effect type rows (22 in retail), indexed by the effect type ids a PROJ.DAT ImpactFX array holds. Row layout in docs/retail/simulation/impact-effects.md.

entries.name: g_ExplosionShapes
entries.description: Array of loaded EXPLOS.DTS root shapes (20 in retail), indexed by an EXPLOS.DAT type row's shape index. Every root is a TSCellAnimPart flipbook of TSBitmapParts.

entries.name: g_ExplosionShapeTable
entries.description: EXPLOS.DAT's first table: one 4-byte row per EXPLOS.DTS root, {int16 animSequence; int16 textureBankIndex}. The bank index selects which of the fifteen EXPLO<n> DBA banks Explosion_LoadResources binds to that shape.

entries.name: g_DebrisPool
entries.description: The debris object pool: 150 entries of 0x61 bytes. Walked by the same effect-pool pass of Sim_MainTick that carries tracers and travelling rounds, so nothing can shoot a piece of wreckage and nothing collides with one.

entries.name: g_DebrisAlternate
entries.description: The currently installed alternate debris database -- the high half of the group index space Debris_Resolve splits. Written immediately before a throw by whichever site is throwing: Mech_ComponentDamageWrite installs the machine's own chassis table (typeRecord+0x212), Base_ThrowDebris installs g_DebrisStructure, and a bursting piece re-installs the table it was itself thrown out of, captured at obj+0x5d.

entries.name: g_DebrisDefault
entries.description: DEF_DEB, the shared default database, and the low half of every debris group index. 12 bytes: {group* groups; int16 groupCount; TSShape** shapes; int16 shapeCount}. Retail holds 6 groups over 7 shapes, so indices 0-5 are the same wreckage whoever throws them.

entries.name: g_DebrisPitchMin
entries.description: Lowest launch pitch a thrown piece is drawn, BAM. 6000 (about 33 degrees) for a first throw; Debris_TickUpdate rewrites it to 3000 around a burst and restores it after, which is what makes second-generation debris scatter closer. g_DebrisPitchMax (004a96ea, 16000/8000) and g_DebrisSpeedScale (004a96ec, 420/320) are the other two.

entries.name: g_DebrisSpeedScale
entries.description: What a thrown piece's launch speed is shifted up ten and divided by the piece's own mass from -- 420 for a first throw and 320 for a burst. See g_DebrisPitchMin for the pair beside it.

entries.name: g_SmokeBallPool
entries.description: SMOKE_BALL object pool (200 entries of 0x4c bytes), built by SmokeBall_LoadResources. Flushed by SmokeBall_FlushDeletes.

entries.name: g_SmokeBallDeleteQueue
entries.description: SMOKE_BALL delete queue: an 8-byte list header (capacity 0x19 at +6, count at +4) over a 100-byte pointer array, built by SmokeBall_LoadResources and drained into g_SmokeBallPool by SmokeBall_FlushDeletes.

entries.name: g_SmokeShapes
entries.description: The smoke shape roots SmokeBall_LoadResources loads with Shape_LoadAllRoots; SmokeBall_Construct takes its shape from it by variant, and each root's DBA context points at g_SmokeTextures.

entries.name: g_SmokeTextures
entries.description: The smoke DBA bank SmokeBall_LoadResources loads with Resource_Load; its address is what every g_SmokeShapes root holds at +0x26.

entries.name: g_SmokePool
entries.description: SMOKE emitter pool (20 entries of 0x2a bytes), built by Smoke_LoadResources. Flushed by Smoke_FlushDeletes.

entries.name: g_SmokeDeleteQueue
entries.description: SMOKE delete queue: an 8-byte list header (capacity 0x19 at +6, count at +4) over a 100-byte pointer array, built by Smoke_LoadResources and drained into g_SmokePool by Smoke_FlushDeletes.

entries.name: g_FlatObjPool
entries.description: Pool of FlatObj ground shapes (Borland 'ObjPool<FlatObj>'): 150 entries of 0x41 bytes, built by FlatObj_LoadResources. Allocated from by Explosion_Construct (when the EXPLOS.DAT row's +0x04 is nonzero: shape 1, pointer kept at explosion+0x4f; no retail row sets it), Mech_Constructor (one per entry of the type record's byte list at +0x72, into the array at mech+0x238, count +0x23c) and Meteor_Tick (shape 3, at a group-carrying pod's landing site). None of the three checks the allocation. The only walk is Scene_SubmitFrameObjects' draw submit; nothing ticks a FlatObj.

entries.name: g_FlatObjDeleteQueue
entries.description: FlatObj delete queue: an 8-byte list header (capacity 0x19 at +6, count at +4) over a 100-byte pointer array, built by FlatObj_LoadResources and drained into g_FlatObjPool by Sim_FlushDeleteQueue.

entries.name: g_FlatShapes
entries.description: The flat set's shape roots, loaded by FlatObj_LoadResources from dts\flat or dts\flat2 through Shape_LoadAllRoots; count at 004a9720. Indexed by each FlatObj spawner for its shape.

entries.name: g_FlatShapeCount
entries.description: Number of roots in g_FlatShapes (int16).

entries.name: g_MeteorPool
entries.description: Object pool for METEOR (drop pod) instances, allocated by Meteor_LoadResources. Sim_MainTick walks it calling Meteor_Tick and queues anything that returns nonzero on g_MeteorDeleteQueue, which Meteor_FlushDeletes drains; Scene_SubmitFrameObjects and Group_DeploymentCheck are its other readers.

entries.name: g_MeteorDeleteQueue
entries.description: METEOR delete queue, the list Sim_MainTick queues a finished drop pod on; Meteor_FlushDeletes drains it into g_MeteorPool.

entries.name: g_ProjectilePool
entries.description: LoosePool<PROJECTILE>: 160 entries of 0x66 bytes, built by Projectile_LoadResources, the pool every rocket, bullet, beam tracer and grenade is allocated from. Flushed by Projectile_FlushDeletes, deleted by Projectile_StaticDtor.

entries.name: g_ProjectileDeleteQueue
entries.description: Projectile delete queue: an 8-byte list header (capacity 0x50 at +6, count at +4) over a 0x140-byte pointer array, built by Projectile_LoadResources and drained into g_ProjectilePool by Projectile_FlushDeletes.

entries.name: maybe_RocketTypeTable_Unguided
entries.description: dat/ROCKETS.DAT in memory, 14-byte stride, loaded by Rocket_LoadTypeTable_Unguided. Layout is NOT BULLETS.DAT's: +0x00 model id, +0x02 lifetime in ticks, +0x04 acceleration, +0x06 hit-test slack, +0x08 animation interval, +0x0a animation sequence, +0x0c sound id.

entries.name: maybe_RocketTypeTable_Unguided_Count
entries.description: Record count for maybe_RocketTypeTable_Unguided.

entries.name: g_GrenadeTypeTable
entries.description: Pointer to 8-byte grenade type records, indexed by subtype through Grenade_GetTypeRecord; Grenade_Construct takes the record's +0 as an index into g_GrenadeShapes. The module's loader is Grenade_LoadResourcesNoOp; no writer of this address found by es2_xref, whose sweep finds only the two reads at 0040ac2d and 0040ac42.

entries.name: g_GrenadeShapes
entries.description: Pointer to an array of grenade shape roots, indexed by a g_GrenadeTypeTable record's +0 in Grenade_Construct. No writer of this address found by es2_xref, whose sweep finds only the read at 0040ac57.

entries.name: BeamQuadIndexTable
entries.description: 120 int16 vertex indices built at startup by Beam_LoadResourceTables as (i>>1) + BeamQuadIndexOffsets[i&3]. BeamTracer_Draw points the shape renderer's index-list global at it and reads four entries from 4k for chain quad k, which works out to points[2k+1], points[2k], points[2k+2], points[2k+3] -- a wound quad spanning nodes k and k+1. 120 entries caps a chain at 30 quads; retail's longest ELF shot is 20.

entries.name: BeamAppearanceTable
entries.description: Pointer to the parsed dat\BEAM.DAT records, 6 bytes each, indexed by PROJ.DAT subtype id (not weapon id): {int16 halfWidth world units, int16 palette index, int16 BEAMTEX.DBA frame}. Retail has 10 records, frame 0 throughout. Only the width differs per weapon on the straight-beam path; the palette index is unread there and is the flat fill colour on the ELF/ELF2 jagged path.

entries.name: BeamTextureDescriptors
entries.description: Pointer to the BEAMTEX.DBA frame descriptors built by BitmapArray_PackToAtlas, 20 bytes each: {x0, y0, x1, y1, int16 atlasPageIndex}, plus a +0x12 short flagging a frame that contains palette index 0. Retail ships one frame, 128x25, every row a single repeated palette index forming a symmetric cross-section (11 at the edges, ramp 84..95 to the middle).

entries.name: Collision_NodeToMuzzleTransform
entries.description: Pointer to the node-to-muzzle-space transform of the node being tested: Mech_ComponentGeometryTest_Candidate points it at its own stack copy (the candidate's frame for an object-frame node, otherwise the node's posed transform concatenated with it) before walking the node's clusters, whose centres Collision_ClusterBoundTest and Collision_ClusterSphereTest move through it. Left pointing at that stack frame afterwards.

entries.name: CollisionTable_Array
entries.description: Pointer to CollisionTable_Count 6-byte collision models. Collision_RegisterObject loads entry 004987de (then increments it) with Collision_LoadRecordArray.

entries.name: DmgTable_Array
entries.description: Pointer to DmgTable_Count 12-byte entries. Damage_LoadMechDmgFile fills entry 00498854 (then increments it) with HercPiece_LoadTable.

entries.name: g_TSDetailBiasFromHercDetail
entries.description: TSDetailPart starting level derived from the HERC DETAIL setting, via g_HercDetailTSDetailBiasValues. Read by WeaponMount_RenderWithDetailBias and WeaponMount_Destroy, each pushing it into g_TSDetailPartBias around a draw.

entries.name: GunLayout_Table
entries.description: Pointer to the gun-layout table of 6-byte {int16 count, record*} entries, GunLayout_Count (004a996c) long. GunLayout_AllocTable allocates it; GunLayout_GetBySlot indexes it.

entries.name: GunLayout_Count
entries.description: Entry count of GunLayout_Table (004a9968).

entries.name: WeaponMountTemplate_Table
entries.description: Pointer to the WEAPONS.DAT mount-template array (0x58-byte records, count WeaponMountTemplate_Count) Weapons_LoadResourceTables allocates with WeaponMountTemplate_ElementCtor; WeaponMountTemplate_GetByWeaponId indexes it.

entries.name: WeaponMountTemplate_Count
entries.description: int16 record count of WeaponMountTemplate_Table, read from WEAPONS.DAT's leading UINT16 by Weapons_LoadResourceTables.

entries.name: ProjDat_RecordTable
entries.description: PROJ.DAT's in-memory record table, 36 bytes/record, keyed by (category, subtypeId). Verified byte-exact against the real retail ES2/VOL/simvol0/dat/PROJ.DAT (27 records) -- independently converges with the pre-existing C# ProjectileData.cs field layout.

entries.name: maybe_GlobalLiveObjectList
entries.description: Global live-object list walked by Sim_RaycastObjectList and Damage_ExplosiveBlastSweep. Shared with confirmed objlist.cpp functions, not proven by a direct assert-string tie to Sim_RaycastObjectList itself.

entries.name: EnemySighted_CalledInLatch
entries.description: Byte array indexed by an object's live-list slot (obj+0x4b): the player's group has had its chance to call that enemy in. Set by Mech_AiEnemySighted -- always by the player's own machine, by a squadmate only for an enemy that passes the callout's tests -- and never cleared; es2_xref finds its three references, all in that function.

entries.name: EnemySighted_CalloutRateLimit
entries.description: CountdownTimer record (counter the short at 004a9be9) rate-limiting the enemy-detected squad callout. Mech_AiEnemySighted steps it once per call from any machine but the player's and re-arms it to 10000 on each callout.

entries.name: GlobalMechList
entries.description: Global list of live mechs, walked once per tick by Sim_MainTick (calling Mech_PerTickSystemsUpdate per live, non-removed, non-dead mech).

entries.name: g_MechDeleteQueue
entries.description: The mech pool's deferred-delete queue, set by DBSim_LoadScriptDat (004251fe) and drained by Mech_FlushDeletes each frame.

entries.name: Mech_DrawEnabled
entries.description: int16: Mech_Draw splices and draws a machine while it is non-zero and returns at once while it is 0. Mech_ResetMissionGlobals sets it to 1 at every mission start; an absolute-address search of the disassembly finds those two references.

entries.name: PlayerMech
entries.description: The player-controlled mech. Distinct from LocalPlayerMech (004d256a, the camera subject). Used for team comparisons, scoring, and to skip Mech_AiObstacleAvoidance for the player.

entries.name: DevKeys_MoveStep
entries.description: int16 step Mech_HandleCommand's developer move commands move the machine by; Ctrl+Alt+1-9 load it from DevKeys_MoveStepTable, Mech_ResetMissionGlobals from that table's entry 3 (2000).

entries.name: DevKeys_TurnStep
entries.description: int16 angle step Mech_HandleCommand's developer turn commands add to or subtract from the yaw; loaded like DevKeys_MoveStep from DevKeys_TurnStepTable.

entries.name: g_MechFormationTable
entries.description: The mech formation-offset table pointer Formation_GetSlotOffset (004205cc) reads. Written by Mech_LoadResources (0041fdb0), which sets it (`g_MechFormationTable = extraout_EAX_00;`) immediately after Rtl_VectorNew allocates count*28 bytes and before the file's formation data is read into that buffer). Sits in a tight cluster of mech-subsystem globals: DAT_004a9de4 (mech name table, LoadNameList's target) / DAT_004a9dec (formation count) / this pointer / DAT_004a9df4 (cached object-pool handle, maybe_MechTypeSlot_Allocate).

entries.name: g_MechTextureGroupSlots
entries.description: 8-byte-stride array, one slot per texture group (light/medium/heavy/enemy/apocatex/razortex/newhercs -- see g_MechTextureGroupNames, though this array is populated independently of that dead string table; the loader that fills each slot from a real .DBA is not traced). MechType_InitOne (0041a8) writes '&g_MechTextureGroupSlots + textureGroupIndex*8' directly into every mesh sub-component's TSShapeInstance+0x26 (the confirmed bound-active-DBA field from docs/retail/formats/dts-texture-binding.md's VSHELL RE) at mech-spawn time -- this is the actual, confirmed, executed mech-to-texture-atlas binding mechanism in DBSIM.EXE.

entries.name: g_FlyerPool
entries.description: ObjPool<FLYER>: Pool_Init'd with 0x291-byte elements (the FLYER record length) by DBSim_LoadScriptDat (stored at 00425247); nulled by Flyer_RegisterSubsystem, freed by Flyer_StaticDtor, flushed by Flyer_FlushDeletes.

entries.name: g_FlyerDeleteQueue
entries.description: The flyer pool's deferred-delete queue: an 8-byte {entries, int16 count, int16 capacity 0x19} block DBSim_LoadScriptDat allocates (stored at 00425299); Flyer_FlushDeletes drains it.

entries.name: MissionGroups
entries.description: {record pointer, int16 count at 004a9e88}: the mission's 0x7a-byte group records, allocated by MissionGroups_Allocate and filled by DBSim_BuildGroupRecord from script.dat block 11. Mission_ResolveRefByKind indexes it for kind 0; Sim_MainTick, Actions_EvaluateTriggers, DBSim_SpawnMissionObjects and Group_NoRivalOrderOnSubject walk it.

entries.name: ActionTimer_Count
entries.description: int16 count of script.dat block-6 action timers, read by DBSim_LoadScriptDat; ActionTimers_Tick walks that many.

entries.name: ActionTimer_Array
entries.description: Pointer to the 0x31-byte block-6 action-timer records DBSim_LoadScriptDat allocates with ActionTimer_ElementCtor and ActionTimers_Tick steps.

entries.name: ScriptDatHeader
entries.description: The 20 bytes DBSim_LoadScriptDat reads out of data\script.dat in one call: theater, zone, mode flag, objective type, the two cheat flags, the difficulty and the theater variant.

entries.name: MissionModeFlag
entries.description: script.dat header +0x04. The writer emits 1 and DBSim_LoadScriptDat stores 0 over it before any reader runs, so the two cheat flags beside it are always read on their live arm.

entries.name: ScriptDatTrainingMission
entries.description: script.dat header +0x08. The training mission number, 0 for anything that is not one. DBSim_LoadScriptDat only stores it; every reader takes the copy at TrainingMissionNumber (004aa7ac). Set by the .MSN header patch (VSHELL DAT_0048544e).

entries.name: UnlimitedAmmoFlag
entries.description: script.dat header +0x0a. 1 = the practice missions screen's Unlimited setting; refunds weapon energy in WeaponMounts_ArbitrateEnergy and ammunition via WeaponMounts_FireTrigger's free-shot flag. Gated on MissionModeFlag being 0.

entries.name: PlayerInvulnerableFlag
entries.description: script.dat header +0x0c. 1 = the practice missions screen's Invulnerable setting; Sim_DamageToPlayerDisabled returns true and the player's component damage is skipped.

entries.name: MissionDifficulty
entries.description: script.dat header +0x0e. The mission difficulty, 0-3 (ROOKIE/REGULAR/VETERAN/ELITE). Written only by the header read in DBSim_LoadScriptDat; four readers -- Damage_ScaleByDifficulty, Ai_FireAtPoint, Mech_CollisionTest and Sim_DamageToPlayerDisabled.

entries.name: MissionPollTimer
entries.description: CountdownTimer record: the objective poll's interval. Mission_PollStatus passes this base to Math_CountdownTimerTick each tick and evaluates the status only when the counter (MissionPollTimer_Count, +1) reaches 0, or when the player is outside the mission box.

entries.name: MissionPollTimer_Count
entries.description: Short counter of MissionPollTimer (+1 of the record), stepped through the record base by Math_CountdownTimerTick, so it has no absolute-address reader. Re-armed to 10000 by Mission_PollStatus when the answer is not worth raising; Ai_ChooseWeapon raises it to at least 1000 when a machine runs out of weapons, deferring the next poll.

entries.name: MissionAlertTimer
entries.description: CountdownTimer record: how long an alert-worthy status must stand before Mission_PollStatus hands it up. Ticked through this base every poll.

entries.name: MissionAlertTimer_Count
entries.description: Short counter of MissionAlertTimer (+1 of the record). Armed to 10000 by Mission_PollStatus when MissionAlertArmed is first raised, and read directly there.

entries.name: MissionAlertArmed
entries.description: Short latch: MissionAlertTimer has been armed. Set by Mission_PollStatus with the arm; cleared by Sim_DispatchCommand's [Q] case after its status alert closes (00460585), so the next alert-worthy status waits the full delay again.

entries.name: Mission_Box
entries.description: The mission box, four int32s {x0, y0, x1, y1} at 004aa6c4..004aa6d0. DBSim_LoadScriptDat resets it to an inverted box and grows it over block 1's coordinates as it reads them; Mission_IsOutsideBox tests positions against it, and the HDD map is framed by it.

entries.name: g_MissionStrings
entries.description: The data\mission.str string table: StringTable_Ctor'd by World_StaticInit, loaded by DBSim_LoadScriptDat (StringTable_Load, then StringTable_LoadGroup of up to 0x32 lines into g_MissionStringLines), destroyed by World_StaticDtor.

entries.name: g_MissionStringLines
entries.description: Up to 0x32 line pointers into g_MissionStrings, filled by DBSim_LoadScriptDat's StringTable_LoadGroup; the mission's text refs index it.

entries.name: TrainingMissionNumber
entries.description: Copy of ScriptDatTrainingMission taken at the end of DBSim_LoadScriptDat (00425321), and the one every reader takes. Read at 00431cda (nonzero builds the 0x4ef-byte training port and raises its .GAU rect by the offset-1664 training lift), 00431dab (the COMMAND<n>.STR digit, whatever its value), 004368fb (the TM<n>_ digit and the PILOT MESSAGE voice gate) and 00461c8f (no CD music when nonzero). TRAIN1-TRAIN4 set 1-4.

entries.name: TerrainTexturingEnabled
entries.description: Prefs option 8, TERRAIN TEXTURE. Written by Prefs_ApplyTerrainTextureOption and by Terrain_LoadZone from the option byte; read by Terrain_DrawCellQuad, which picks the textured span writers on 1 and the flat ones on 0. MfdMissileViewScreen_Paint saves, zeroes and restores it around the MISSILE CAM screen's own terrain pass, so that view is never textured.

entries.name: RaycastShapeMinDistance
entries.description: int. Sim_RaycastShapeVolume lowers it to an object's centre distance from the ray origin when that is smaller, and sets it to 0 when the object is within the ray's reach. RaycastShapeMinDistance_Clear zeroes it; Sim_RaycastObjectList reads it through RaycastShapeMinDistance_Get into 004aaaf0 and 004aaaec.

entries.name: g_TerrainHitPseudoObject
entries.description: Static stand-in object Sim_RaycastTerrain reports as the thing a ground-clipped ray struck, with the hit point stored at its +0x1a/+0x1e/+0x22. INERT: the fields are written there and never read; only its address is used, as the non-null struck-object value that reaches Mech_AiOnLineOfFireBlocked, which ignores its argument. The terrain impact effect does NOT come from it -- Sim_RaycastObjectList spawns that itself, see docs/retail/simulation/impact-effects.md.

entries.name: CockpitViewManagerPublished
entries.description: A second global holding CockpitViewManagerInstance (004d2544), published at the tail of CockpitViewManager_LoadViews through the setter at 00429810 and read back through the accessor at 00429820. Same object, same fields: +0x14 is the current view index, which is what MessagePort_Show tests when it refuses to draw a line in view 4.

entries.name: CockpitVueRecords
entries.description: Four 32-byte view records, vector-constructed by CockpitViewManager_StaticInit; CockpitViewManager_LoadViews stores this address at the manager's +4 and reads vue\<herc>'s records into it.

entries.name: ExternalView_DefaultRect
entries.description: The default 3D rect and offset pair (6 dwords) CockpitViewManager_Ctor builds; ExternalView_ResetRect copies it back to ExternalView_Rect.

entries.name: ExternalView_Rect
entries.description: The external view's (view manager view 4) 3D rect {x0, y0, x1, y1} followed by the offset pair at 004cfad4/004cfad8 that goes to the render context's +0x220/+0x224. Copied from ExternalView_DefaultRect by CockpitViewManager_Ctor and ExternalView_ResetRect, set by ExternalView_SetRect, and installed by CockpitView_ApplyViewState.

entries.name: CockpitView_KickOffset
entries.description: The step-kick offset CockpitView_SetKickOffset last added to the render context's +0x224, so the next call can take it out.

entries.name: WorldShades_TypeTable
entries.description: Pointer to SHADES.DAT's per-type-tag 5-byte records {byte count, pointer to count {shade ramp, column} byte pairs}, built by World_LoadShades and indexed by WorldShades_ApplyForObject with obj+4.

entries.name: WorldShades_DistanceOffsets
entries.description: Two int32 distance offsets read from the .WLD after the ramp section (-10000 and -10000 in retail files): WorldShades_DistanceBand adds [0] for a type-5 object under 5000 shape radius and [1] at or above it; WorldShades_IsBeyondLastBand also adds [0] for tag 8.

entries.name: WorldShades_LevelRanges
entries.description: {int16 start, int16 count} palette index ranges, 004cfd62 levels per column for 004cfd60 columns, which World_LoadTheater interpolates from the .WLD's two ramp tables with Palette_InterpolateIndexRanges; WorldShades_ApplyForObject indexes column * 004cfd62 + band.

entries.name: WorldShades_BlendRanges
entries.description: One {int16 start, int16 count} range per band (004cfd62 of them), interpolated by World_LoadTheater from the .WLD's two 4-byte extra entries; WorldShades_ApplyForObject's blend path builds its second segment from it.

entries.name: WorldShades_BandsTagged
entries.description: Pointer to the .WLD's first int32 distance-threshold table (count int16 004cfd5c), read by World_LoadTheater; WorldShades_DistanceBand and WorldShades_IsBeyondLastBand use it for a non-zero type tag. Retail: 16 entries, 60000 to 126000 in steps of 4400.

entries.name: WorldShades_BandsTag0
entries.description: Pointer to the .WLD's second int32 distance-threshold table (count int16 004cfd5e), read by World_LoadTheater; used for type tag 0. Equal to WorldShades_BandsTagged in retail files.

entries.name: g_SquadmateMachines
entries.description: Up to three machine pointers, the player's squadmates by slot: filled at mission start by Cockpit_LoadSquadmatePilots, and indexed by slot in Squad_SendOrderToSlot, Squad_IndexOf, HddDisplay_SelectPilot, HddDisplay_HandleWidgetPress, HddGauge_LoadPilotFrames, HddGauge_PaintIdle and HddCommandScreen_DrawMap.

entries.name: PilotStringTables
entries.description: Three 16-byte StringTables ('Strings[3]'), one per comm-box slot: SystemMessages_Index(port, 2, slot, bank) loads str\PILOT<bank>.STR into entry slot. Built by MessagePort_StaticInit.

entries.name: CommandStringTable
entries.description: StringTable for str\COMMAND<n>.STR, loaded by SystemMessages_Index mode 1. Built by MessagePort_StaticInit.

entries.name: SystemStringTable
entries.description: StringTable for str\SYSTEM.STR, loaded by SystemMessages_Index mode 0. Built by MessagePort_StaticInit.

entries.name: SimStringTable
entries.description: StringTable that SimStrings_LoadAll loads str\STRINGS0.STR into (StringTable_Load at 004375a6) before registering its groups. Built by SimStrings_StaticInit.

entries.name: ConsoleButtonCaptions
entries.description: 4-entry .bss pointer array (STRINGS0.STR group 4: 'I', 'LINK', 'TRACK', ''), filled by SimStrings_LoadAll and read by ConsoleButton_Paint, indexed by the console button's own kind field. Entry 0 ('I') is unused by that reader -- the chain button gets its numerals from the separate ChainCountCaptions table instead.

entries.name: MfdCaptionTable
entries.description: 13 pointers into STRINGS0.STR group 5, filled at runtime by SimStrings_LoadAll (BSS, zero in the image). Entries 0-5 are the MFD's six screen titles (STATUS, FLASH COMM, NAV MAP, SCANNER, TARGET, MISSILE CAM) and 6-12 its aux button captions (MODE, SELECT, RANGE, TARGET, XMIT, PASS, ACTIVE). Indexed by mode for the title and by button index for captions. See docs/retail/formats/mfd.md.

entries.name: SquadCallsignStrings
entries.description: STRINGS0.STR group 7, three string pointers RED 1, RED 2, RED 3 (SimStrings_LoadAll registers it with count 3 at 00437633). Squad_CallsignOf indexes it by squadmate slot.

entries.name: MfdStatusConditionStrings
entries.description: 5 pointers into STRINGS0.STR group 28 -- OK, SHIELDS DN, INT DAMAGE, CRITICAL, DESTROYED -- filled at runtime by SimStrings_LoadAll. Indexed by condition state for the MFD status screen's fourth label in MfdStatusScreen_SetCondition. This, not the similar-looking group 10 at DAT_004d1440, is the live table. See docs/retail/formats/mfd.md.

entries.name: WeaponIconSizes
entries.description: 28 {int width, int height} pairs, vector-constructed by PaperDoll_StaticInit; PaperDoll_InitTables reads pdg\WEAPONS.PDG's pairs into it, shifted by VideoMode_X/YCoordShift.

entries.name: maybe_MfdMissileView_ClipRegion
entries.description: A global GLRectangleRegion (0x18 bytes) constructed by MfdMissileView_StaticInit. MfdMissileViewScreen_Ctor fills its rect (004d1ab8..004d1ac4) and stores 004d1ab4 at 004d18b0 beside a 1 at 004d18ac; the clip role is read from that pairing, not from a reader of 004d18b0.

entries.name: MfdScannerRanges
entries.description: Three int32 scanner ranges -- 50000, 100000, 200000 world units = 300, 600, 1200 m at the game 1000 units = 6 m scale. MfdDisplay_Ctor writes all three as literals and inits the zoom field at +0xc5 to 2; 1200 m matches the RNG: readout in the retail scanner screenshot. The last entry is also read directly by the target filter TargetSelect_CanTarget as its radar-visibility range. See docs/retail/formats/mfd-scanner.md.

entries.name: MfdDisplay_StaticRegion
entries.description: Function-local static GLRectangleRegion of MfdDisplay_Ctor, constructed once under MfdDisplay_StaticRegionBuilt. Every MfdDisplay_Ctor then copies the display's rect (+0xeb..+0xf7) into its rect at 004d1d3c..004d1d48, and stores 1 at display+0x104 and 004d1d38 (region+4) at display+0x108.

entries.name: HddMapTerrainRaster
entries.description: GLBitmap (0x1a bytes): the command map's terrain raster. HddCommandScreen_StaticInit constructs it and HddCommandScreen_StaticDtor destroys it; HddMap_BuildTerrainRaster fills it and HddMap_DrawTerrain blits it.

entries.name: PanelAmbience_ClockDigits
entries.description: char[8]: the minutes at +0/+1 (NUL at +2), the seconds at +3/+4 (+5 zero in .bss) and ':' at +6 (NUL at +7). PanelAmbience_Ctor sets '00', '00' and ':'; PanelAmbience_TickClock carries the digits; PanelAmbience_FormatClock joins them.

entries.name: PanelAmbience_ClockText
entries.description: char buffer PanelAmbience_FormatClock builds 'MM:SS' in and returns.

entries.name: CockpitMouseLive
entries.description: Gates CockpitMouse_OnEvent: with this byte clear the listener queues nothing, which is how a replaying .TAP tape owns the cockpit mouse queue. Set again when the tape ends.

entries.name: CockpitMouse_DoubleClickTicks
entries.description: The double-click window, 0x1e coarse ticks (480 ms), set by CockpitMouse_Init: a release less than this after the same button's previous one sets CockpitMouse_DoubleClick. It gates nothing else: Widget_OnMouseUp runs on every release, however long the button was held. Shares its literal with the listener's event mask, an unrelated field.

entries.name: CornerFrame_StyleCount
entries.description: int16: the style count CornerFrame_LoadStyles reads first from its file. Grep of the disassembly finds no access outside CornerFrame_LoadStyles.

entries.name: ScreenshotBitmap
entries.description: GLBitmap (0x1a bytes) Screenshot_Save captures the screen into; its bitmap header starts at 004d1ec0 (height 004d1ec0, width 004d1ec2, format 004d1ec4, size 004d1ec6, pixels 004d1eca). Screenshot_StaticInit constructs it and Screenshot_StaticDtor destroys it.

entries.name: ScreenshotPath
entries.description: char buffer Screenshot_BuildPath writes the .SCR and .PAL file names into.

entries.name: AlertPanel_NextPresentTicks
entries.description: Coarse tick count at which AlertPanel_Present next calls Display_Present on the scroll-window path; it then moves it on by 004d1ee4. AlertPanel_ResetPresentTimer sets it to now.

entries.name: Alert_FillBrush
entries.description: {int mode, int colour} fill brush (004d1efc, 004d1f00) that AlertPanel_CtorBase points each panel's GLViewport (+0x48) brush slot at: panel+0x274, the viewport's +0x22c (MOV at 00454278). Alert_StaticInit zeroes the mode. Grep of the disassembly finds no other access to 004d1efc or 004d1f00.

entries.name: SimOptions
entries.description: Base of the simulator's 0x36-byte option array -- data\prefs.cfg read straight over it by Prefs_LoadOptions with no parse, so an option's index is its byte offset. Prefs_SetOption indexes it, the shadow copy of the outgoing value goes to 004d2028 and the per-option handler table is 004d2060. Options 0-3 and 7-11 are the preferences panel's nine rows, 13-24 the controls panel's twelve walking a HERC and 25-36 the same twelve flying the RAZOR. The two message modes are entries 2 and 3 of it; it is not a four-byte array of message-channel modes.

entries.name: PilotMessageMode
entries.description: SimOptions[2]: the PILOT MESSAGE preference, gating the pilot/squad port's two halves. 0 text only, 1 voice only, 2 both -- three settings, so the row offers no OFF.

entries.name: ComputerMessageMode
entries.description: SimOptions[3]: the COMPUTER MESSAGE preference, gating the computer ticker's two halves. Same three values as PilotMessageMode.

entries.name: Sound_DetailSetting
entries.description: An options-screen 0-2 value the play-request gate scales against: Sound_ConsumeRequest computes its interval as (2 - this) * the catalog row's attribute byte 3 (play requests per play), so 2 zeroes the interval and lets every call through while 0 doubles the authored divisor. Also read by an options-screen label (PreferencesPanel_RefreshRow case 8) and by Base_DeathSequenceTick and Debris_TickUpdate.

entries.name: Prefs_OptionHandlers
entries.description: 0x36 dwords, one per SimOptions byte: the per-option change handlers Prefs_Init registers (indices 0, 1, 2, 8 and 0x0e). Zeroed by Prefs_InitPathAndHandlers first.

entries.name: PrefsInitInProgress
entries.description: Raised for the duration of Prefs_Init and read by the MUSIC and SOUNDS handlers, which skip their mute/unmute call while it is up -- so loading the file cannot drive the mixer before the sound system is built. Four references in the image: those two reads, and Prefs_Init's own set and clear.

entries.name: PlayerInputBlock
entries.description: The global player input block Input_BuildPlayerDevice fills each frame and returns. Head word is the frame's command code, which Sim_PollPlayerInput dispatches first thing; the four axes follow at +0x0e. A .TAP frame record is a snapshot of its first sixteen bytes.

entries.name: Input_CursorPos
entries.description: The cursor position Input_BuildPlayerDevice keeps: from Cursor_GetPosition, or from the mouse record it pushes on CockpitMouseQueue_Push. Input_GetCursorPos returns its address.

entries.name: Input_DeviceTable
entries.description: Nine pointers, indexed by device kind (0-3 used: 1 keyboard, 2 mouse, 3 joystick), each to the InputDevice sub-object InputDevice_Register was given -- not the object base, which is why Input_GetDevice and Input_GetMouseDevice subtract the sub-object's offset. The enabled bytes per kind follow at 004d2510.

entries.name: MonoComponentPanel_Block
entries.description: The block MonoComponentPanel_Init was given; its 41 int16 values start at +2. The cursor handlers bound the cursor by +2 and +0x52.

entries.name: MonoComponentPanel_Cursor
entries.description: Pointer to the int16 value the mono component panel's cursor is on; MonoComponentPanel_IncreaseValue and MonoComponentPanel_DecreaseValue step it by 0x20.

entries.name: MonoComponentPanel_LabelColumn
entries.description: int16 monochrome-monitor column of the current label column (2, then +0x28 per column); the '>' marker goes one column left of it.

entries.name: MonoComponentPanel_Row
entries.description: int16 monochrome-monitor row of the mono component panel's cursor, 1 to 0x16.

entries.name: MonoComponentPanel_ValueColumn
entries.description: int16 monochrome-monitor column the current column's values print at (0x1e, then +0x28 per column).

entries.name: CockpitViewManagerInstance
entries.description: Result of CockpitViewManager_Ctor, constructed in Sim_InitMissionSession. The player's cockpit view-state object (current view, pending view command, the 4 canopy bitmaps / clip blocks / span tables, and the CockpitView widget tree). Distinct from, and the owner of, CockpitViewInstance (CockpitViewInstance).

entries.name: CmdLineSwitch_S
entries.description: Byte +0x0b of the 004d2540 block. Zeroed by Main_StaticInit; set to 1 by Sim_ParseCommandLine's -S case (0045e886) for any -S argument other than exactly -SPRUNKNOWN, which instead toggles DAT_0049ef60. Its only reader is Sim_InitMissionSession (004619c3/004619e8, through EDI = block base), which picks a page count from it -- 1/0 under VideoMode_PanelMode 1, 2/0 on the -b paged path, 0 otherwise -- and stores it to stack slots [EBP-0xa4]/[EBP-0xa0] that no instruction in the function reads back. So in the shipped build the switch has no effect. The counts are the page numbers CockpitView_ProcessViewCommand's paged glance gate waits for, and the next instruction (004619f7) tests Display_UseScrollWindow with nothing branching on it; see cockpit-views.md Open. Scan: every one of the 18 functions that holds the block base, via es2_fieldscan +0xb.

entries.name: Sim_RenderContext
entries.description: Pointer to the 0x239-byte GLViewport render context Sim_CreateRenderContext builds. Sim_RenderFrame adds CockpitView_GetShakeOffset's pair to its +0x220/+0x224 for the frame and takes it off again.

entries.name: TapePlayback
entries.description: Non-zero while a .TAP input tape is being replayed. Set by Sim_ParseCommandLine's -p and -D, cleared when the tape runs short or a recorded Ctrl+E (command 0x412) stops it.

entries.name: TapeRecording
entries.description: Non-zero while input is being recorded to a .TAP tape. Set by Sim_ParseCommandLine's -r once the bundle has been written.

entries.name: TapeStem
entries.description: The tape name from the command line, before the tap extension is forced onto it.

entries.name: TapeFile
entries.description: The open tape's FILE*. Held for the whole mission on playback; the recording path reopens the tape in append mode every frame instead.

entries.name: LocalPlayerMech
entries.description: Confirmed global pointer to 'this instance's own locally-piloted mech' -- set in the level-init function by scanning the mech list for the one with the locally-simulated flag set.

entries.name: ViewObjectPtr
entries.description: Pointer to the active view object; its +4 is the camera position triple. Simulation code reads it directly for two audio range gates -- Mech_PlaceLegsOnGround tests a machine against it before playing a footfall, and Rocket_TickUpdate tests each round against it for the missile-inbound warning -- so the camera position is an input to the simulation, not only to the renderer.

entries.name: ViewChain_View
entries.description: Word, block 004d2540+0x32: the view the game is in -- 1 free camera, 2 cockpit, 3 outside, 4 chase. Starts at 2.

entries.name: InputDrivesCamera
entries.description: Word, block 004d2540+0x34. Set: the controls steer a camera, not the machine -- every reader tests it together with the missile-camera flag 004d25aa. Input_BuildPlayerDevice re-points the axis sources (+0x22/+0x26 to +0x0e/+0x10), Sim_PollPlayerInput reads the camera axes and skips Mech_PlayerFireTick, Mech_ApplyThrottleInput ignores the lever, ViewChain_DrawCaption picks label 2 rather than 3 from the table at 004d1724. Writers: ViewChain_Apply (0045de14) on every change of view and, in the outside view on the player, from the preference 004d259c ([Enter]/[Tab] in view 4); ViewChain_ViewObject (0045df18), 1 for any object but the player and 004d259c for the player; the developer keys Ctrl+T (0x414), which toggles it, and Ctrl+N/P (0x431/0x419), which set it.

entries.name: g_CenterTurretMode
entries.description: Latched by scancode 0x0e ([Backspace]) and by the expiry of the timer at mech+0x31b; cleared by scancode 0x2b (Center Body) and by Sim_PollPlayerInput the moment either turret axis is non-zero. While set, the player's turret block runs Mech_CenterTorsoTick instead of the two torso ticks.

entries.name: ViewChain_CameraControlPreferred
entries.description: Word, starts 1: whether the outside view on the player puts the controls on the camera. [Enter]/[Tab] in view 4 flip it.

entries.name: ViewChain_PendingView
entries.description: Word: the view ViewChain_Apply moves to on the view manager's next step. Starts at 2.

entries.name: ViewChain_Chosen
entries.description: The object the outside view opens on: the player at mission start, then whatever [N] or [Ctrl+N]/[Ctrl+P] chose.

entries.name: ViewChain_CaptionFrames
entries.description: Frames ViewChain_Apply draws the caption on: reloaded to 2.

entries.name: DemoMode
entries.description: Set by Sim_ParseCommandLine's -D in addition to TapePlayback. It arms the abort: any command code off the tape, and Input_KeyjoyAxisKey's first axis key, raise DemoAbort.

entries.name: DemoAbort
entries.description: Raised when a demo-mode replay should end -- by a keypress, by a command on the tape, by the tape running out or by WM_CLOSE. StatusAlertPanel_RunModal reads it to leave the mission.

entries.name: ViewChain_FollowChosen
entries.description: Set by [Ctrl+F], cleared by [V] and both joystick view actions: the cockpit the chain returns to rides 004d25a0's eye.

entries.name: VideoMode_PanelMode
entries.description: Three-valued panel/display mode selector at +0x7b of the 0xc3-byte video-mode block at 004d2540. Retail stores only 0 (Main_StaticInit, and VideoMode_Configure mode 0) and 3 (VideoMode_Configure modes 1 and 2+). 3 selects the 640-wide art set: .HFN fonts, hba\ sprite banks, the hb0/hb1/hb2 canopy folders (via CockpitCanopy_LoadViewBitmap) and the hd0-hd3 clip files. 1 is a scrapped display mode that nothing stores but 17 sites test for: glances turn the camera -/+0x3600 (CockpitView_ProcessViewCommand), Sim_EndFrame switches to an off-screen render target at block+0xac around the view transition, and the transition copies the whole 320x480 canvas. See docs/retail/formats/cockpit-views.md, 'Panel mode 1'.

entries.name: maybe_CockpitLayoutMode
entries.description: Alternate cockpit layout selector at +0x7c of the video-mode block at 004d2540, and zero in every run found: its only write is Main_StaticInit's (memset, then a 0 store through EBX). All 23 absolute occurrences of 004d25bc are MOVSX reads, and over the 18 functions that hold the block base (in a register or as a pushed argument) es2_fieldscan finds only one other access to +0x7c, a read in Sim_InitMissionSession. Both branches the readers test for are therefore unreachable. Value 1 would make view 0 also blit the view-1 (heads-down) bitmap at y+0xc5 and disable view 1 as a standalone view, and it is defective besides -- its second load reuses the unmodified local folder buffer and corrupts the global 'dba' literal. Value 2 would route blits through Bitmap_BlitClipped and put the view origin in DAT_004d25da/de instead of DAT_004cfa24/28; the only stores to DAT_004d25da/de (CockpitView_SetView, 0042a1d8/0042a1e1) are on that path, so the offset Widget_OnMouseDown and Widget_OnMouseUp add from them is always zero.

entries.name: VideoMode_XCoordShift
entries.description: Per-axis resolution shift for hardcoded widget coordinates: the exe writes them as `value << (VideoMode_XCoordShift & 0x1f)`. 0 in the 320-wide mode, 1 in the 640-wide one, so every .GAU coordinate is doubled in the 640-wide mode. VideoMode_YCoordShift is the Y counterpart.

entries.name: VideoMode_YCoordShift
entries.description: Y-axis counterpart of VideoMode_XCoordShift.

entries.name: VideoMode_BackBufferWidth
entries.description: Back-buffer width set by VideoMode_Configure: 640 in mode 0, 1280 in modes 1/2, twice the viewport. Screen_ResetBackBufferGlobals copies it to 004d30c4 for the DIB; Screen_PresentFrame uses it as the source row stride.

entries.name: VideoMode_BackBufferHeight
entries.description: Back-buffer height set by VideoMode_Configure: 480 in mode 0, 960 in modes 1/2, twice the viewport. Screen_PresentFrame clamps its row count against it.

entries.name: CockpitCanvasWidth
entries.description: Width of the virtual cockpit canvas the .GAU widget rects are authored in: 320 in mode 0, 640 in modes 1/2 (paired with CockpitCanvasHeight at 004d25d6 = 480 / 960). The canvas is TALLER than the 3D viewport (004d25c2/c6 = 320x240 / 640x480) because view 1's .VUE origin is (0,237): canvas rows 0-239 are the forward cockpit and rows 237-476 are the heads-down display. Views 2 and 3 sit at canvas x +320 and -320. This is why .GAU's addressable Y range runs past 240.

entries.name: Display_UseScrollWindow
entries.description: Word at +0xaa of the 004d2540 block. Nonzero (Main_StaticInit and every VideoMode_Configure branch store 1): the scroll-window path, which presents Display_Present once a frame and moves the window over the back buffer for view changes. Zero (Sim_ParseCommandLine's -b, which runs after VideoMode_Configure): a page-flipping path whose page hooks are empty stubs in driver 3, so no mission frame is presented, and whose CockpitView_ProcessViewCommand calls Vga_WaitVerticalRetrace (IN from port 0x3DA) every frame. Readers: see cockpit-views.md 'The -b paged path'; the 18 block-base holders add three reads in Sim_InitMissionSession.

entries.name: VideoMode_UseHiResBanks
entries.description: Nonzero selects the 640-wide `hba` sprite banks, zero selects the 320-wide `dba` ones. Read directly by every HUD bank constructor. A parallel flag VideoMode_PanelMode == 3 drives the same choice for sysbuttn/throttle/icons and for .hfn over .dfn.

entries.name: PilotingRazor
entries.description: Byte set by DBSim_LoadScriptDat as (playerMechType == 8), the RAZOR. It selects the controls panel's flight half -- title and all four axis word sets -- the flight per-button action table at 0049e681, and, through ControlsOptionBase, the second twelve-byte binding block in prefs.cfg.

entries.name: Music_TrackSelect
entries.description: The -R command-line switch's value, parsed with atol at 0045e824. Sim_InitMissionSession derives the mission's CD track from it as value % 5 + 2, so 0-4 select tracks 2-6 and an absent switch leaves every mission on track 2.

entries.name: ControlsOptionBase
entries.description: Which SimOptions index the controls panel's twelve options start at: 0x0d walking and 0x19 flying. Sim_InitMissionSession sets it from PilotingRazor after DBSim_LoadScriptDat, and PreferencesManager_Reset starts it on 0x0d. The two blocks are independent, so a binding made in a walker does not disturb the RAZOR's.

entries.name: Sim_FrameCount
entries.description: Dword: frames run, incremented by the main loop (Sim_Run) after each one. CHASE VIEW waits for it to pass 0x31.

entries.name: CockpitArt_LoadOnDemand
entries.description: When non-zero, canopy view bitmaps are loaded on entering a view and freed on leaving it instead of all being loaded up front in CockpitViewManager_LoadViews. A low-memory path.

entries.name: ViewChain_Viewed
entries.description: The object the view was last moved to (ViewChain_ViewObject). The developer keys' Ctrl+Alt+D hits it and their move keys move it.

entries.name: ViewChain_SquadCameras
entries.description: One CAM pointer per member of the player's group, built by Sim_InitMissionSession.

entries.name: DemoTape_NameTable
entries.description: StringTable DemoTape_PickRandom constructs on first use (guard byte 0049f05a) and loads from tapes\demolist.str (0049f23a, through Path_PrefixBaseDir) with StringTable_LoadFromStream; StringTable_LoadGroup puts up to 0x14 names at 004d2778 and their count at 004d2774. ViewChain_StaticDtor destroys it.

entries.name: ViewChain_SpareCamera
entries.description: The CAM used once every squad camera views something else.

entries.name: DriveCfg_Directory
entries.description: The directory string Sim_Run reads out of data\drive.cfg at startup. DriveCfg_PrefixPath puts it in front of a path.

entries.name: DeathCamera_Countdown
entries.description: LongCountdownTimer record, its int counter at 004d2add: the player-death camera's time left. ViewChain_PlayerDeathCamera arms it from DeathCamera_CountdownByClass on its first call and steps it with Timer_CountDown on every call.

entries.name: DeathCamera_Started
entries.description: Dword: the player-death camera has had its first call. Set and tested only by ViewChain_PlayerDeathCamera (es2_xref: its two operands), zero from the image's BSS clear.

entries.name: g_CenterBodyMode
entries.description: The counterpart of g_CenterTurretMode for scancode 0x2b ('\', Center Body): while set, Sim_PollPlayerInput steers the machine onto the turret's centreline instead of taking the throttle/steer axes, using the target heading cached in g_CenterBodyTargetHeading (004d2af8). Cleared only by its own convergence test or by [Backspace]; steering and the turret axes do not cancel it.

entries.name: g_CenterBodyTargetHeading
entries.description: Short. Latched by scancode 0x2b to (mech+0x10) - Mech_GetTorsoTwistAngle() -- the world direction the turret is pointing in at the moment Center Body is pressed. While g_CenterBodyMode is set, both the substituted steering command and the substituted turret twist command are errors measured against this one number.

entries.name: SoundCatalog_Names
entries.description: 57 pointers to the catalog's .wav filenames, into the loaded SOUNDS.STR buffer.

entries.name: SoundCatalog_Attributes
entries.description: 57 pointers to the catalog's attribute blobs, into the loaded SOUNDS.STR buffer. Byte 0 loop count (0 = forever), 1 volume 0-100, 2 preload, 3 throttle divisor, 4 rolloff start / 1024 world units (0xff gives 5), 5 cutoff / 1024 world units (0xff gives 100), 6 variation count, 7 resume flag, 8 category volume percent, 9 throttle counter. Bytes 7-9 are runtime-only and overlap the next entry's header in the file buffer, which is inert because every pointer is collected before the first write.

entries.name: SoundCatalog_StringTable
entries.description: The StringTable SoundCatalog_Load fills from the language's sounds.str (Language_StringFilePath('sounds', ...), StringTable_Load) and walks with StringTable_ReadNext. Sound_StaticInit constructs it, Sound_StaticDtor destroys it.

entries.name: SoundCatalog_Voices
entries.description: 57 SFX voice handles, one per catalog id. Index 10 (004d2d24) is where the effects half starts.

entries.name: SoundCatalog_Count
entries.description: Number of catalog entries actually opened.

entries.name: VoiceSlots
entries.description: Pointer to the five 0x42-byte speech channel records Sound_Init vector-constructs (Rtl_VectorNew(0, 0x42, 5, 1, VoiceSlot_ElementCtor), stored at 00462368). Record layout: +0x00 SFX voice handle, +0x04 next script event time, +0x08 current portrait frame (-1 = finished), +0x0a script cursor, +0x0e wav name, +0x2f this slot's 100-byte .SNC buffer, +0x33 name pointer for the by-name lookup, +0x37 last-use tick for LRU, +0x3b in-use, +0x3c owning catalog id, +0x3e SFX voice handle.

entries.name: SncEventQueue
entries.description: Global .SNC timer queue: 8-byte {uint32 time, void *slot} entries, count at 0049f97c, drained by Snc_ServiceQueue.

entries.name: Display_ScreenRect
entries.description: int[4] {x0, y0, x1, y1}: the viewport's rect on screen, {0, 0, w-1, h-1}, set by driver 3's surface setup Driver3_OpenDisplay. Display_Present's destination rect.

entries.name: Display_OriginX
entries.description: x of the viewport window's top-left in the back buffer, with Display_OriginY at 004d30a0. Written only by Display_SetOrigin and zeroed by driver 3's surface setup Driver3_OpenDisplay. Display_Present passes it to Screen_PresentFrame as the source point.

entries.name: Display_OriginY
entries.description: y of the viewport window's top-left in the back buffer; see Display_OriginX.

entries.name: BackBuffer_Pixels
entries.description: Pixel bits of the back-buffer DIB section Screen_CreateBackBuffer creates (CreateDIBSection), stored into the BMP_8 descriptor as its pixel pointer. Everything DBSIM draws lands here; Screen_PresentFrame copies from it.

entries.name: MainWindow_Handle
entries.description: The simulator's HWND: MainWindow_Create stores CreateWindowExA's result here, and ShowWindow, UpdateWindow, GetClientRect, BeginPaint, GetWindowRect and KillTimer all take it.
entries.source: DBSIM disassembly at 00465187 and its 28 readers

entries.name: Win_PumpCursor
entries.description: HCURSOR. Win_PumpMessages calls SetCursor with it whenever no message is waiting and it is non-null. Win_SetPumpCursor stores it.

entries.name: Screen_SoftwareCursor
entries.description: The cursor bitmap Screen_PresentFrame blits at GetCursorPos() in fullscreen when nonzero. Written only by Screen_SetSoftwareCursor.
entries.source: DBSIM disassembly: one store at 0046551a, readers at 00465666, 004656ae, 00466824, 0046688a

entries.name: SimTickDelta
entries.description: Global simulation timestep, Q8 with 1.0 = 125 ms: Time_InitSimClock sets 0x100 and Time_BeginSimTick recomputes it every frame, except during tape playback, when Sim_MainTick copies each frame record's delta into it instead; the time module's integrate, countdown and count-up helpers read it.

entries.name: HudColorTable
entries.description: 27 int16 palette indices, loaded from dat\COLORS.DAT (54-byte payload) by HudColor_LoadResources (00467a60), which passes 0x4d3c00 to Ovl_ReadFile as the destination. HUD data files carry small logical colour ids rather than palette indices; those are resolved through this table once at load time, in place (arr[i] = table[arr[i]]). Read at 16 distinct offsets by ~60 functions. Verified: HDD ids 19/9/15/12 resolve to palette 16/10/13/14 = black/red/yellow/green, matching retail HDD screenshots.

entries.name: Raster_VertexBuffer
entries.description: Ten 0x28-byte vertex records Raster_StaticInit builds and the textured polygon fills (Raster_SetupTexturedSpan, Raster_DrawTexturedPolyNear, maybe_Raster_DrawTexturedPolyW) write per vertex: +0 screen x, +4 screen y, +8 depth, +0xc u, +0x10 v, +0x18 ramp row, +0x1c view-space position (3 ints); maybe_Raster_DrawTexturedPolyW also writes +0x14.

entries.name: maybe_g_BitmapAtlasCache
entries.description: The shared runtime texture atlas: 256x256 pages that BitmapArray_PackToAtlas (00469f38) packs each loaded .DBA's frames into through Bitmap_PlaceInAtlasPage (00469d10), which spills into an overflow bank (param_1[0x200]/[0x201]) when a row is full, and records one 20-byte descriptor per frame. It lies in the DATA section's 2,245,120-byte zero-fill tail (DBSIM.EXE is 724,512 bytes on disk), so it is not a static table: it holds nothing until a loader fills it. Packer callers: Base_LoadResources, FlatObj_LoadResources, Weapons_LoadResourceTables, Terrain_BindTextureBank, Bullet_LoadResources (0040ade0) and Beam_LoadResourceTables (0040b6e0), each loading the .DBA through Resource_Load (0045cdd8). A textured span addresses it as (page << 16 | pixel), the page taken from the frame descriptor's +0x10. See docs/retail/formats/dts-texture-binding.md.

entries.name: maybe_ShadeRamp_Bitmap
entries.description: A GLBitmap (0x1a bytes) ShadeRamp_StaticInit constructs and ShadeRamp_StaticDtor destroys; ShadeRamp_Free clears the dword at its +0xe (006b4f96).

entries.name: ShadeRamp_Allocation
entries.description: The (rows + 1) * 0x100-byte Mem_NewArray block ShadeRamp_Allocate stores; ShadeRampTable is its next 256-byte boundary. ShadeRamp_Free deletes it.

entries.name: g_FireShapes
entries.description: The four dts\FIRE.DTS roots, each a flipbook of billboards. dat\FIRE.DAT -- a 4-byte count header and then one byte per shape -- names the bank each takes; retail is [0, 0, 0, 1] over fire0/fire1, and the roots hold 24, 24, 24 and 27 frames.

entries.name: g_FirePool
entries.description: The burning-object effect pool: ten entries. FireEffect_AcquireSlot never refuses a new fire -- with all ten busy it evicts the one with the fewest loops left.

entries.name: g_TerrainViewerPos
entries.description: int32 {x, y, z} (006b4fc8/cc/d0): the view's position, copied by Terrain_SetupVisibleRegion. Terrain_FaceVisibilityTest measures from it, Terrain_BuildDrawRegionQuad centres the draw square on it, and HeightGrid_PickDrawCell takes the viewer's cell from it.

entries.name: g_TerrainViewerCellX
entries.description: The view's cell X, set by Terrain_DrawVisibleCells for the walk; with g_TerrainViewerCellY (006b4fd8) it is the walk's centre.

entries.name: g_TerrainViewerCellY
entries.description: The view's cell Y; see g_TerrainViewerCellX.

entries.name: g_TerrainViewerCellPending
entries.description: Byte: the viewer's cell's pending-object count at the start of the walk. The run callbacks clear it when a run covers that cell; if still set after the walk, Terrain_DrawVisibleCells draws that cell's objects then.

entries.name: Terrain_CellCorners
entries.description: Four 0xc-byte Point3I that Terrain_StaticInit builds and Terrain_DrawCellRowRun (0046dce1) and Terrain_DrawCellColumnRun (0046dead) load as the cell's corner block before Terrain_DrawCellQuad.

entries.name: HGrid_SpanFirstRow
entries.description: First row HGrid_RowSpans holds a span for; HGrid_SpanAddCell lowers it. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's HGrid_SpanFirstRow (0048a438).

entries.name: HGrid_SpanLastRow
entries.description: Last row HGrid_RowSpans holds a span for; HGrid_SpanAddCell raises it. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's HGrid_SpanLastRow (0048a43c).

entries.name: HGrid_RowSpans
entries.description: Per-row cell spans, int16 {minX, maxX} each, that HGrid_SpanAddCell widens. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's HGrid_RowSpans (0048a440).

entries.name: Avi_MovieWindow
entries.description: The movie's window handle, from Avi_Play's MCI_STATUS item MCI_DGV_STATUS_HWND; Avi_MoveWindow moves it.

entries.name: Music_NotifyWindow
entries.description: The window handle Sos_InitBackend was given, used as MCI_PLAY's dwCallback so MM_MCINOTIFY reaches sfxWndProc when a track ends.

entries.name: Music_TrackLength
entries.description: The MSF length Music_GetTrackLength last returned, reused as the MCI_TO of the next play.

entries.name: Sos_DriverHandle
entries.description: int16 SOS driver handle. 00473da0 passes its address to 00495963 as an out-parameter; Sos_StopAllSamples, Sos_StartSample and Sos_StopSample receive it as driverHandle, the latter two through Sos_GetDriverHandle.

entries.name: g_ShapeNodeWorldTransforms
entries.description: Pointer to the currently bound shape instance's per-node WORLD transform array (shapeInst+0x16, stride 0x20, indexed by transform id -- the array ShapeInst_BuildWorldTransforms fills). Written only by ShapeInst_BindNodeTransformArray (00475fd8); read by ShapeNode_InstallTransform (00476030) and by TSBSPPart_RenderNode.

entries.name: g_CellAnimFrames
entries.description: Pointer to the currently-drawing shape instance's per-sequence cell-animation frame array (one ushort per sequence). Saved/swapped/restored around a shape's draw alongside g_CurrentShapeDbaContext; TSCellAnimPart_Render indexes it by the part's animSequence (+0x16).

entries.name: g_TSTransformStates
entries.description: 52 TSTransformStates of 0x110 bytes, built by TSTransformState_StaticInit and deleted by TSTransformState_StaticDtor: the Raster_SaveState / Raster_RestoreState slots of a shape draw. ShapeInst_BindNodeTransformArray saves the object's base state into slot 0 (00475ff8); ShapeNode_InstallTransform saves the state after composing transform id into slot id + 1 and restores slot 0 or slot id + 1 (00476048, 004760dc, 004760fb). Slot 0's +0x20 (g_ShapeObjectModelTransformPtr (006b7c14)) is the model transform pointer Raster_SaveState copies from g_ModelTransformPtr.

entries.name: g_ShapeObjectModelTransformPtr
entries.description: +0x20 of slot 0 of g_TSTransformStates (006b7bf4): the model-transform pointer Raster_SaveState records when ShapeInst_BindNodeTransformArray saves the renderer state into slot 0 as it binds a shape instance (PUSH 0x6b7bf4 at 00475ff8), i.e. the transform the object itself was drawn with. ShapeNode_InstallTransform concatenates each node's world transform with it and installs the result through Raster_SetModelTransform, which applies the view itself.

entries.name: g_ShapeNodeTransformCacheFlags
entries.description: 0x32-byte per-node 'already composed for this shape' flag block, cleared by ShapeInst_BindNodeTransformArray. Byte 0 is set as a bound marker; the per-node flags ShapeNode_InstallTransform tests start at 006bb335 and are indexed by transform id.

entries.name: TSBounds_RadiusScale
entries.description: 0x1000000 / Math_CosBam(Math_Atan2Bam(1 << DAT_006c60ac, width)), rebuilt by TSBounds_ScreenVisibility whenever the width differs from TSBounds_CachedViewWidth; multiplies the bounding radius before projection.

entries.name: g_SimPool
entries.description: The src\mymem.cpp Memory pool behind Mem_New, Mem_NewArray, Mem_Delete and Mem_DeleteArray, DBSIM's counterpart of VSHELL's g_ShellPool: +0 base, +4 byte size, +8 free-list head, +0xc free bytes (006bb388, Mem_New's size test), +0x10 lowest free bytes. Mem_StaticInit zeroes it through Memory_Ctor; 0045f326 gives it 0xb0000 bytes at 0x4d4f88 + 0x130000 through Heap_InitInBuffer; Memory_DrawUsageMap walks it.

entries.name: KeyEventRing
entries.description: 256 int16 entries, head at 006bb934 and tail at 006bb938. Key_WndProcHook pushes any command code no KeyListenerTable subscriber consumed; Input_ReadDeviceEvent pops.

entries.name: KeyListenerTable
entries.description: Ten {enabled, wantedCodes, callback} triples, the keyboard twin of the mouse-listener table at DAT_006c5f5c. Key_WndProcHook walks it; KeyListener_Register appends.

entries.name: RasterRightEdgeTable
entries.description: 480 (0x1e0) rows of 0x28 bytes (10 dwords), one per screen line from the polygon's top, built by RasterEdgeTables_StaticInit. Raster_BuildEdgeTables fills it on its first (forward) edge walk and returns it at 006c5420 of its result block; RasterLeftEdgeTable (006c0914) follows it directly.

entries.name: RasterLeftEdgeTable
entries.description: 480 (0x1e0) rows of 0x28 bytes, one per screen line from the polygon's top, built by RasterEdgeTables_StaticInit. Raster_BuildEdgeTables fills it on its second (backward) edge walk and returns it at 006c541c of its result block.

entries.name: g_AssertLogger
entries.description: The simulator's assert logger, built by Assert_StaticInit with Assert_Ctor and destroyed by Assert_StaticDtor; 44 of the 45 Assert_Report lines in the decompile dump pass it first (the 45th is Assert_Report's own definition). +0x10 (006c575c) is the hook list Assert_AddHook pushes onto; +4 and +8 are read by the getters maybe_Assert_GetCheckCount (00479c30) and maybe_Assert_GetBreakRequested (00479c38). The DBSIM counterpart of VSHELL's g_AssertLogger (0048dc24).
entries.source: DBSIM decompile of 00479c40, 00479c70 and the Assert_Report call sites

entries.name: ClassItem_ProbeBuckets
entries.description: Array of 8-byte {entries, count} buckets of 12-byte {id, loadFn, headerSize} class-item entries that ClassItem_TryEveryLoader offers an unrecognised item to; ClassItem_RegisterProbeBucket appends, ClassItem_ProbeBucketCount (004a16ac) counts them.

entries.name: ClassItem_ProbeHeader
entries.description: Buffer holding an unrecognised class item's 8-byte type tag followed by up to ClassItem_ProbeHeaderSize - 8 further header bytes (from 006c59b0), filled by ClassItem_PeekTypeTag and ClassItem_ReadTypeTag; ClassItem_TryEveryLoader passes it as the first argument of each probe entry's loadFn.

entries.name: ClassItem_CurrentFrame
entries.description: Pointer to the frame of the class item being read: {+0 type tag, +4 start position, +8 end position, +0xc byte}. ClassItem_LoadResource and 0047a0a0 point it at a frame on their own stack and restore the previous one on exit; ClassItem_ReadTypeTag fills it, ClassItem_CloseItem reads the end.

entries.name: Mouse_State
entries.description: {int32 x, int32 y, uint16 buttons} at 006c5fd4/006c5fd8/006c5fdc. Mouse_DispatchEvent fills x and y from the event's low and high words scaled by Math_Q16Multiply with 004a2de4/004a2de8, and buttons bit 0 and bit 1 from the event's bits 0 and 1, then passes it to each matching listener; MouseDriver_GetState returns its address; MouseState_StaticInit constructs it.
entries.source: DBSIM decompile of Mouse_DispatchEvent, MouseDriver_GetState and 004809cc

entries.name: Bitmap_UseCallerScratch
entries.description: Flag Bitmap_SetScratchOverride sets. While it is non-zero Bitmap_UnpackToScratch returns 0 without unpacking, and Bitmap_Blit, Bitmap_BlitRect, Bitmap_BlitScaled and Bitmap_BlitRotatedUnpacked skip the Mem_Delete of Bitmap_UnpackScratch after a packed-bitmap blit.
entries.source: DBSIM decompile: 004817ec and the readers of 006c5ff8

entries.name: Bitmap_UnpackScratch
entries.description: The unpacked-pixel buffer a packed bitmap is blitted from: Bitmap_UnpackToScratch allocates it with Mem_NewArray and fills it, or Bitmap_SetScratchOverride stores a caller's buffer. Bitmap_Blit, Bitmap_BlitRect, Bitmap_BlitScaled and Bitmap_BlitRotatedUnpacked substitute it for the bitmap's data pointer +0xe during the blit.

entries.name: g_DepthBuffer
entries.description: The depth buffer: g_DepthBufferWidth * g_DepthBufferHeight dwords, allocated and zeroed by DepthBuffer_Alloc. Raster_DrawPolygon's depth path hands rows of it to Raster_DepthTestSpan.

entries.name: g_ModelToView
entries.description: The current model-to-view transform (0x20 bytes), built by Raster_SetModelTransform and reinstated by Raster_RestoreState.

entries.name: g_ViewToModel
entries.description: The inverse of g_ModelToView.

entries.name: g_ModelTransformPtr
entries.description: Pointer to the installed model transform (the identity at 006c6080 when null is installed).

entries.name: g_EyeInModelSpace
entries.description: The viewpoint in the current model's space (int32 x, y, z at 006c60a0-a8): the origin through g_ViewToModel. Its length is the node's distance from the camera, which the 3Space detail-level pick measures.

entries.name: PolyFill_LineBrush
entries.description: The poly renderers' line brush {+0 mode, +4 colour (006c60d4)}, constructed by LineBrush_Ctor in Raster_StaticInit and installed at the render context's +0x228. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's PolyFill_LineBrush.

entries.name: PolyFill_FillBrush
entries.description: The poly renderers' fill brush {+0 mode, +4 colour (006c60dc), +8, +0xc}, constructed by FillBrush_Ctor in Raster_StaticInit and installed at the render context's +0x22c; the flat renderers set its mode to 0 before PolyFill_FillThenOutline. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's PolyFill_FillBrush.

entries.name: g_CurrentShapeDbaContext
entries.description: The bound DBA the poly renderers read. Four stores: ConfigPart_Render saves it, installs its object's +0x10 shape instance's +0x26 -- the same field as VSHELL's TSShapeInstance+0x26 bound DBA -- around a TSGroup_BindNodeTransform/TSPartList_Render render, and restores it; TSBase_SetActiveBitmapArray sets it to its argument; TexPoly_DrawAtPoints (0042fa18) installs its own this+0x1a. g_CurrentShapeDbaContext[1] is the shape's bound DBA's 20-byte-stride frame-descriptor table, DBSIM's counterpart of VSHELL's g_ActiveBitmapArray[1]. TSTexture4Poly_Render (00474e9c) fetches a frame descriptor at g_CurrentShapeDbaContext[1] + frontValue*0x14 and takes its +0x10 (F4) as the atlas page (maybe_g_BitmapAtlasCache, 004d4f88) the fill samples. See docs/retail/formats/dts-texture-binding.md.

entries.name: Poly_ViewCache
entries.description: 1000 int32 {x, y, z} view-space points (12 bytes each), built by Raster_StaticInit; the projectors store each vertex's transformed point here and the near-plane clips interpolate from it. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's Poly_ViewCache.

entries.name: Poly_ScreenCache
entries.description: 1000 int32 {x, y} projected screen points (8 bytes each), built by Raster_StaticInit; the projectors memoise each vertex's screen point here. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's Poly_ScreenCache.

entries.name: Poly_ScreenPoints
entries.description: The screen-point list: 0x20 int32 {x, y} pairs built by Raster_StaticInit, count at 006cbc86; Poly_ProjectIndexedVertices, Poly_ProjectShapeVertices and the near-plane clips fill it. The DBSIM copy of VSHELL's Poly_ScreenPoints.

entries.name: Sos_UsingSos9503
entries.description: int16: Sos_BindLibrary sets 1 when it loads sos9503.dll (GetVersion below 0x80000000, or a major version above 3) and 0 when it loads sos32s03.dll. Five of the import wrappers special-case it.

entries.name: Rtl_DtorCountPtr
entries.description: Pointer to the Borland exception handler's live-destructor count, the dword just below the stack top in the thread block (FS:[4] - 4), stored by the entry point (0040103f) and by the RTL's thread setup (004963f6). Every constructor level adds one to *it and every destructor level takes one off. VSHELL's counterpart is 005ddec0.
